leads.title: Elisha heals Jericho's water; the bears of Bethel ↔ The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God's power to make water sweet or bitter [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3); Bitter water made drinkable by throwing in a piece of wood God shows the leader (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.3.

Only in Elisha heals Jericho's water; the bears of Bethel: Small boys jeer 'Go up, baldhead!'; the prophet curses them and two she-bears maul forty-two of them; Prophet throws salt from a new bowl into the spring and heals the deadly, miscarriage-causing water 'to this day'.

Only in The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat: The damned eat of Zaqqum to fill their bellies and drink boiling water like thirst-crazed camels (al-him); A noble Quran in a hidden Book which none touch but the purified; The 'hospitality' (nuzul) of the deniers is boiling water and roasting in hell; The damned had lived in luxury and persisted in the great sin (al-hinth al-'azim); 'I swear by the positions (setting-places) of the stars, a mighty oath if you knew'; Have you seen the water you drink? Did you send it down from the rain-clouds? We could make it bitter (ujaj); For those brought near: rest (rawh), fragrance (rayhan) and a garden of bliss; The Companions of the Left are in scorching wind (samum), boiling water and the shade of black smoke (yahmum), neither cool nor kind; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; Fire kindled from a tree that God made grow [divergence between the texts]; The scripture exists with God in the 'Mother of the Book' (umm al-kitab), a heavenly archetype; and 7 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping (weight 6.7); A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king (weight 6.7); Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die' (weight 6.7); Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward) (weight 6.7); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life (weight 6.3); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz (weight 6.3); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3); At a leader's command the sun and moon stand still until the battle is won (weight 6.0). Pair score 51.6.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys: The king proudly shows foreign envoys all his treasures, prompting a prophecy of their loss; A king receives a foreign ruler's envoys and gift [contrast between the texts]; King accepts doom for his descendants, glad there will be peace and truth in his own days; Prophecy that the king's descendants will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon; King makes a pool and conduit to bring water into the city; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm: Speaker laments that in the noon of his days he must go to the gates of Sheol, deprived of the rest of his years; A psalm-like 'writing' (mikhtav) of the king composed when he was sick and recovered; My dwelling is pulled up like a shepherd's tent; I have rolled up my life like a weaver, he cuts me off from the loom; In distress the sufferer chirps like a swift or crane and moans like a dove; God has cast all the speaker's sins behind his back and held back his soul from the pit of destruction; The dead cannot praise God: no wonders for the dead, no hesed in the grave, no faithfulness in Abaddon; A dying person's plea to God for more life, and God's answer [contrast between the texts]; On that day neither wealth nor sons avail, only one who comes to God with a sound heart; Bequest (wasiyya) to parents and kin prescribed for one who leaves wealth; altering it is a sin; Death or Sheol has gates (sha'arei mavet).

leads.title: Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A king receives a foreign ruler's envoys and gift [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys: The king proudly shows foreign envoys all his treasures, prompting a prophecy of their loss; A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king; Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward); Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die'; King accepts doom for his descendants, glad there will be peace and truth in his own days; Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping; Prophecy that the king's descendants will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon; King makes a pool and conduit to bring water into the city; In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life; In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life [contrast between the texts]; As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant; and 1 more.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 22 more.

وَإِنِّى مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِم بِهَدِيَّةٍ فَنَاظِرَةٌۢ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

leads.title: Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys ↔ Al-Munafiqun: false testimony, propped-up timbers, 'the mightier will expel the meaner', and the deathbed plea for delay
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life (weight 6.3); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3). Pair score 12.6.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys: The king proudly shows foreign envoys all his treasures, prompting a prophecy of their loss; A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king; Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward); A king receives a foreign ruler's envoys and gift [contrast between the texts]; Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die'; King accepts doom for his descendants, glad there will be peace and truth in his own days; Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping; Prophecy that the king's descendants will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon; King makes a pool and conduit to bring water into the city; As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant; At a leader's command the sun and moon stand still until the battle is won.

Only in Al-Munafiqun: false testimony, propped-up timbers, 'the mightier will expel the meaner', and the deathbed plea for delay: Spend before death comes and one says 'My Lord, if only you would delay me a little, I would give charity'; God delays no soul when its term comes; It is the same whether the prophet asks forgiveness for the hypocrites or not; God will not forgive them; The hypocrites testify 'You are God's messenger'; God knows he is, and testifies that the hypocrites are liars; The hypocrites say 'When we return to Medina the mightier will expel the meaner from it'; but might belongs to God, his messenger and the believers; Let not your wealth and children divert you from God's remembrance; The hypocrites' bodies impress and their speech is heard, but they are like propped-up timbers, thinking every cry is against them; The hypocrites take their oaths as a shield (junna) and will swear falsely even to God at the resurrection; When you eat and are full, beware lest you forget God; God forbids the prophet to pray or intercede for the people, for he will not hear; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; God opens his good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain.

leads.title: Josiah's temple repair, the finding of the book and Huldah's oracle ↔ Temple repair, finding of the book of the Torah, Huldah's oracle and covenant
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Royal officials consult a woman prophet on behalf of the king (weight 6.7); A lost book of the law is found in the temple during repairs (weight 6.7); Because the king humbled himself, he will die in peace and not see the coming disaster (weight 6.7); Workmen handling sacred funds are not audited because they deal faithfully (weight 6.3); Men tear their garments in grief or dismay (weight 4.9). Pair score 31.3.

Only in Josiah's temple repair, the finding of the book and Huldah's oracle: A newly found sacred book is read aloud before the king, who tears his clothes; The king organizes the collection of silver for repairing the temple; A child of eight to twelve years becomes king.

Only in Temple repair, finding of the book of the Torah, Huldah's oracle and covenant: Prophet announces that the curses written in the found book will come upon the land; King stands at his place and makes the covenant before God; Levites skilled in music oversee the burden-bearers and workmen; The scribe reads the found book aloud before the king; Money collected by the Levites is given to the workmen to repair the temple; The book of the covenant is read aloud to the people; King and people enter a covenant to seek or serve YHWH in a public ceremony.

leads.title: Josiah's covenant, purge of the cults and Passover; death at Megiddo ↔ The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations
leads.summary: 1 shared motif, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot) (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Josiah's covenant, purge of the cults and Passover; death at Megiddo: Idolatrous cult objects are burned and their dust carried away or thrown on graves; Despite the righteous king's reform, God does not turn from his anger over a predecessor's sins; Horses dedicated to the sun at the temple entrance and chariots of the sun burned; The high places Solomon built on the 'mount of destruction' (Mount of Olives) for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom; The righteous king is killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necho; Priests of the high places are slaughtered on their own altars; An old prophecy (naming the future king) is fulfilled generations later; The bones of a prophet are left undisturbed when other graves are desecrated; Priests of the high places may not serve at the altar but eat unleavened bread among their brothers; The Tophet in the valley of Ben-hinnom is defiled so no one may burn children to Molech; A Passover such as had not been kept since the days of the judges; Women weave 'houses' (garments, hangings) for Asherah in the temple precinct; and 11 more.

Only in The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations: God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently; God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage; Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?'; What God does after creating in six days [divergence between the texts]; God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness; God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; God set constellations (buruj) in the sky and adorned it for beholders; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them; God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers; A solid firmament (raqia) separates upper waters from lower waters; and 6 more.

leads.title: Jehoram's campaign against Mesha of Moab ↔ Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay'
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not cut down fruit trees during a siege: is the tree of the field a man? (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Jehoram's campaign against Mesha of Moab: Besieged king offers his firstborn heir as a burnt offering on the city wall, and 'great wrath' falls on Israel, who withdraw; Prophet calls for a musician; as he plays, the hand of YHWH comes upon him; Prophet says he would not even look at the wicked king were it not for the righteous ally; Invaders fell every good tree, stop every spring and ruin every good field with stones; Allied kings on a seven-day detour run out of water for army and beasts and despair; A sheep-breeding vassal king pays tribute of a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams; At sunrise the water looks red as blood; the enemy thinks the kings have slain each other and rushes to plunder; Dry wadi fills with water though no wind or rain is seen; Standard regnal formula: age at accession, length of reign, mother's name, evaluation, burial, successor; Nations burn their sons and daughters in fire to their gods.

Only in Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay': The expelled demolish their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers; Had God not decreed exile (jala') for them, he would have punished them in this world; God expelled the unbelieving People of the Book (the Banu Nadir) from their homes at 'the first gathering' (li-awwal al-hashr); Whatever palm trees (lina) you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave; Later believers pray: forgive us and our brethren who preceded us in faith, and put no rancor in our hearts; Whether the enemy's trees may be cut down in a siege [contrast between the texts]; How spoil taken from the enemy is distributed [divergence between the texts]; Fay' (booty gained without cavalry or camels) goes to God, the messenger, kin, orphans, the poor and the wayfarer, so wealth does not circulate only among the rich; They thought their fortresses would protect them from God, but God came from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts; The poor emigrants and the hosts who prefer others over themselves even in need; whoever is saved from his own greed succeeds; Cities 'great and fortified up to heaven'; Spoils divided half to warriors, half to community, with a levy for God; and 2 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: King tears his clothes: 'Am I God, to kill and to make alive?' (weight 6.7); Jesus heals the born-blind and the leper and raises the dead by God's leave (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.7.

Only in Naaman healed of leprosy; Gehazi's greed: Prophet sends word to wash seven times in the Jordan; the foreigner is cured; A captive Israelite servant girl tells her foreign mistress that the prophet in Samaria could cure her master; Convert asks pardon in advance for bowing in the temple of Rimmon when his master leans on his arm; Proud foreigner is angry that the prophet did not come out and wave his hand, preferring the rivers of his own land; Prophet's servant runs after the healed man and lies to obtain silver and garments; Healed flesh is restored like the flesh of a little boy; A great foreign general, mighty warrior and favorite of his king, is a leper; The healed man's leprosy clings to the greedy servant and his descendants forever, white as snow; Prophet reveals clairvoyance: 'Did not my heart go with you when the man turned from his chariot?'; Prophet refuses any gift for the healing; Convert takes two mule-loads of Israel's earth to worship YHWH on in a foreign land; One forced to disbelieve while his heart is firm in faith is excused; and 6 more.

matches.note: Verdict, recognition and outcome. Sam: David burns with anger, ben-māweṯ hā-ʾîš, fourfold restitution; Nathan: ʾattâ hā-ʾîš; David: ḥāṭāʾṯî la-YHWH; pardon with a penalty, gam ha-bbēn ha-yyillôḏ ləḵā môṯ yāmûṯ, and the sword never leaves his house (12:10). Q: a calm verdict, la-qad ẓalamaka bi-suʾāli naʿjatika ilā niʿājihi; no 'you are the man'. David himself perceives (ẓanna Dāwūdu annamā fatannāhu) that it was a test, fa-staghfara rabbahu wa-kharra rākiʿan wa-anāb, and then fa-ghafarnā lahu dhālika wa-inna lahu ʿindanā la-zulfā wa-ḥusna maʾāb. Full forgiveness and honour, with no dead child and no curse on the house. The sin (Uriah, Bathsheba, 2 Sam 12:9) is never named.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God strengthened David's kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive judgment (fasl al-khitab) (weight 6.7); A prophet tells a case as if real; the king condemns the offender and is told 'You are the man' (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in The wise woman of Tekoa wins Absalom's return: A returned exile may not see the king's face; The king guesses who is behind a petitioner's speech; An only heir called 'my remaining ember' that kinsmen would quench; Mortality likened to water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered up; A woman disguised as a long-mourning widow petitions the king with an invented case; Oath that not one hair of the person shall fall to the ground; A brother kills his brother in the first murder; A person praised as 'good (or wise) as an angel of God'; A wise woman intercepts an avenging warrior with gifts and speech and averts bloodshed; The 'redeemer of blood' (go'el ha-dam) kills the murderer.

Only in David's mountains, the two litigants and the ninety-nine ewes: Two litigants scale the wall of David's prayer-chamber (mihrab) and frighten him; A man with ninety-nine ewes demands his brother's single ewe and overpowers him in argument; A case about a ewe is brought to David for judgment [divergence between the texts]; 'O David, we made you a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; judge between people with truth and do not follow desire'; David realizes he was being tested, asks forgiveness, falls down bowing and turns in repentance; David's repentance and what follows it [divergence between the texts]; A man with many sheep takes another's only ewe [divergence between the texts]; Shall God treat believers like those who spread corruption, the godfearing like the wicked?; The king confesses 'I have sinned' and the prophet announces forgiveness with a remaining penalty; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The prophet's wives are the mothers of the believers and may not be married after him (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Sheba's revolt, Joab's murder of Amasa, and the wise woman of Abel: A city proverbially famed as the place to ask counsel, 'a mother in Israel'; A corpse wallowing in blood on the road halts the army until it is covered with a garment; Townspeople throw the rebel's head over the wall to end a siege; A man grasps his victim's beard to kiss him and stabs him; Concubines violated by the usurper are kept shut up in 'living widowhood' until death; Besiegers pile up a siege ramp against a city's wall; A man is drawn aside 'to speak privately' and stabbed in the belly; A commander blows the shofar to halt the pursuit or end the fighting; Secession cry: 'What portion have we in David? To your tents, O Israel!'; A wise woman intercepts an avenging warrior with gifts and speech and averts bloodshed.

Only in Divorce before consummation; the prophet's marriages; the curtain and the cloaks: A wife divorced before consummation owes no waiting period ('idda); give her a gift and release her gracefully; Enter the prophet's houses only when invited to a meal and leave after; ask his wives from behind a curtain (hijab); Special marriage rules for the prophet: lawful wives, captives, named cousins who emigrated, and a woman who gives herself; afterwards no more wives; God and his angels bless (yusalluna 'ala) the prophet; believers are told to bless him and greet him with peace; How a husband sends away a divorced wife (document, gift, waiting period) [divergence between the texts]; Limits on how many wives the leader may take [contrast between the texts]; Limits on how many wives the leader may take [divergence between the texts]; What a woman's veil or cloak signals to men who see her [contrast between the texts]; Believing women are to draw their outer cloaks (jalabib) over themselves so they are recognized and not harmed; The way (sunna) of God with those who passed before: you will find no change in God's way; King must not multiply horses, wives or silver and gold, nor return the people to Egypt.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The prophet is sent as witness, bearer of good tidings and warner (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Four descendants of the Rapha slain: A variant tradition attributes the killing of Goliath to another hero; The king called 'the lamp of Israel' that must not be quenched; Giant's bronze armor and weaver's-beam spear described with weights; A giant with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot; The army forbids the king to go into battle because he is worth ten thousand; Ancient giant or Rephaite peoples (Rephaim, Zuzim, Emim, Horites) defeated.

Only in Zayd's wife, the seal of the prophets, and the prophet as a lamp: The greeting of the righteous in the hereafter is 'Peace' (salam); Adopted sons are not one's sons; call them by their fathers' names, or as brothers in religion and clients; God and his angels bless (yusalluna 'ala) the prophet; believers are told to bless him and greet him with peace; A ruler or prophet marries the wife of a man under him [contrast between the texts]; Whether a man may marry his son's (or adopted son's) wife [divergence between the texts]; Muhammad is not the father of any of your men but the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets (khatam al-nabiyyin); After Zayd ends his marriage, God marries his former wife to the prophet so believers may marry the ex-wives of adopted sons; Glorify God in the evening, morning, afternoon and noon (set times of praise or prayer); The way (sunna) of God with those who passed before: you will find no change in God's way; God brings believers out of darknesses into light; false gods lead others from light into darkness.

leads.title: David's song of deliverance (= Psalm 18) ↔ Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany
leads.summary: 16 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: God trains the king's hands for war so his arms bend a bow of bronze (weight 6.7); God hears the cry from his (heavenly) temple (weight 6.7); God shows steadfast love to his anointed and his seed forever (weight 6.7); God rides on a cherub and flies on the wings of the wind (weight 6.7); 'By my God I leap over a wall' (weight 6.7); God reaches from on high and draws the sufferer out of many waters (weight 6.7); Smoke rises from God's nostrils and devouring fire from his mouth (weight 6.7); Enemies beaten fine as dust and trampled like mire of the streets (weight 6.7); God rewards the speaker according to his righteousness and clean hands (weight 6.7); Foreigners come cringing and trembling to submit to the king (weight 6.7); God shows himself loyal to the loyal and crooked to the crooked (weight 6.7); God is called the speaker's lamp who lights his darkness (weight 6.3); God makes the speaker's feet like hinds' feet and sets him on the heights (weight 6.3); The psalmist is engulfed by breakers of death and cords of Sheol (weight 6.3); God shoots his arrows at the people or enemies (weight 5.6); At God's coming the earth quakes, heavens drip and mountains flow (weight 5.2). Pair score 103.2.

Only in David's song of deliverance (= Psalm 18): Leader and people sing a victory song after the enemy's destruction; Theophany with thunder, lightning, thick cloud and a loud trumpet; God called the Rock (tsur).

Only in Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany: God makes darkness his hiding place and dark waters and clouds his canopy; The king gives thanks for God's deliverance from all his enemies (song also in 2 Sam 22); At God's rebuke the channels of the sea are seen and the foundations of the world laid bare; 'Who is God except YHWH, and who is a rock besides our God?'; God answers the distressed when he calls and removes the evil; God's words are pure, silver refined in a furnace, purified seven times; God addressed with a string of protective epithets: rock, fortress, deliverer, shield, horn of salvation, stronghold; God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven; Thunder is the roaring voice of God; On that day a great earthquake shakes the land; fish, birds, beasts, creeping things and all humans quake before God, mountains are thrown down and every wall falls; Superscription sets the psalm in a specific episode of David's life.

Only in The last words of David: A just ruler is like the morning sun on a cloudless day; Poem opening with 'Oracle (ne'um) of the man...' formula; The spirit of God speaks through the king's tongue; The wicked are thorns that cannot be handled and are burned; God has made an everlasting covenant with the king's house.

passages.text: הָל֞וֹךְ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֶל דָּוִ֗ד כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׁלֹ֕שׁ אָנֹכִ֖י נוֹטֵ֣ל עָלֶ֑יךָ בְּחַר לְךָ֥ אַֽחַת מֵהֶ֖ם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה לָּֽךְ

וַיָּבֹא גָ֥ד אֶל דָּוִ֖ד וַיַּגֶּד ל֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֡וֹ הֲתָב֣וֹא לְךָ֣ שֶֽׁבַע שָׁנִ֣ים רָעָ֣ב בְּאַרְצֶ֡ךָ אִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳ֠דָשִׁים נֻסְךָ֨ לִפְנֵֽי צָרֶ֜יךָ וְה֣וּא רֹדְפֶ֗ךָ וְאִם הֱ֠יוֹת שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת יָמִ֥ים דֶּ֨בֶר֙ בְּאַרְצֶ֔ךָ עַתָּה֙ דַּ֣ע וּרְאֵ֔ה מָה אָשִׁ֥יב שֹׁלְחִ֖י דָּבָֽר
וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל גָּ֖ד צַר לִ֣י מְאֹ֑ד נִפְּלָה נָּ֤א בְיַד יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי רַבִּ֣ים רחמו רַֽחֲמָ֔יו וּבְיַד אָדָ֖ם אַל אֶפֹּֽלָה

וַיָּ֥בֹא גָ֖ד אֶל דָּוִ֑יד וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֛וֹ כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה קַבֶּל לָֽךְ

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The believers' pride in their great numbers avails nothing and the earth grows narrow for them (Hunayn) (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in David's census, the plague, and Araunah's threshing floor: Itinerary of census-takers around the land's borders; The king's heart strikes him after a sin; God halts the destroying angel at a specific spot: 'Enough, stay your hand'; The commander objects to the king's census; Counting the people requires a ransom for each life to avert plague; A prophet offers the king a choice among three punishments; God himself incites a person to an evil act; The king refuses a free gift of land for an altar and pays its price; King asks that punishment fall on him and his house rather than on the innocent 'sheep'; Census totals given tribe by tribe; Exact number of dead in a divine plague is given; A threshing floor where the plague was stopped becomes the site of the altar and temple; and 1 more.

Only in Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya: People of the Book who do not follow the true religion are fought until they pay the jizya, subdued; Polytheists are impure (najas) and may not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year; No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter the sanctuary; Gatekeepers stationed so that no one unclean enters the temple; Those counted impure are kept out of the sanctuary [divergence between the texts]; A large army must not claim the victory for itself [divergence between the texts]; City accepting peace becomes forced labor; one resisting has its males killed; God supports the prophet with hosts (junud) the believers did not see; God reinforces the believers in battle with a thousand (or more) angels; God sends down his sakina (tranquility, cf. shekhinah) on the prophet and believers.

leads.summary: 9 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The king's son, not the king, will build the house for God's name (weight 6.7); God promises to make the chosen one's name great (weight 6.7); Israel is the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem for himself (weight 6.7); Prayer of humility: 'Who am I and what is my house?' (weight 6.7); God has never dwelt in a house but moved from tent to tent (weight 6.7); A prophet approves a plan, then is corrected by a revelation that night (weight 6.7); God took the ruler from following the sheep (weight 6.7); God declares the king his son: 'I will be his father and he my son' (weight 6.0); God promises David's house and throne will endure forever (weight 5.8). Pair score 58.6.

Only in Nathan's oracle of the eternal house of David and David's prayer: God's steadfast love will not be withdrawn from the heir as it was from the previous king; The king, living in a cedar palace, proposes to build a house for God; Obscure phrase 'this is the torah of man (adam)'; Wordplay on 'house' as temple and as dynasty; God disciplines Israel as a man disciplines his son; Whether God has, begets or takes sons or other offspring [contrast between the texts]; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts]; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'.

Only in Nathan's oracle of an eternal house and David's prayer: Pun on 'house': the king would build God a house; God will build the king a house (dynasty); Revelation described as God 'uncovering the ear' of his servant; The king lives in a cedar house while the ark of God remains under curtains; 'There is none like you and no God beside you'; Chronicles differs in a specific detail from its parallel in Samuel–Kings.

leads.title: Nathan's oracle of the eternal house of David and David's prayer ↔ Pure religion; no son for God; creation from one soul in three darknesses

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether God has, begets or takes sons or other offspring [contrast between the texts] (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Nathan's oracle of the eternal house of David and David's prayer: God's steadfast love will not be withdrawn from the heir as it was from the previous king; The king, living in a cedar palace, proposes to build a house for God; Obscure phrase 'this is the torah of man (adam)'; Wordplay on 'house' as temple and as dynasty; God has never dwelt in a house but moved from tent to tent; God promises to make the chosen one's name great; Israel is the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem for himself; A prophet approves a plan, then is corrected by a revelation that night; God took the ruler from following the sheep; The king's son, not the king, will build the house for God's name; Prayer of humility: 'Who am I and what is my house?'; God disciplines Israel as a man disciplines his son; and 4 more.

Only in Pure religion; no son for God; creation from one soul in three darknesses: God sent down for you eight pairs of livestock; Idolaters say 'we worship them only that they may bring us near to God'; Had God wished to take a son he would have chosen from what he creates whatever he willed; glory be to him, the One; God creates you in your mothers' bellies creation after creation in three darknesses; God wraps (yukawwir) the night around the day and the day around the night; Was not God's earth wide enough for you to emigrate (hijra) in it?; How God made the human mate, and for what purpose [divergence between the texts]; The believers' sides forsake their beds as they call on their Lord in fear and hope (night vigil); First woman made from the man's rib or side while he sleeps; God formed the kidneys and wove (knit) the speaker in his mother's womb; No burdened soul bears another's burden; even a relative will not carry any of it; Sun and moon are subjected, each running to an appointed term; and 2 more.

matches.label: God as maker or lord of named stars
matches.note: God as lord of a named star, with a different star. Amos: ʿōśēh ḵîmâ û-ḵəsîl ... YHWH šəmô (maker of the Pleiades and Orion). Quran: wa-annahu huwa rabbu sh-shiʿrā (he is the Lord of Sirius). In both the star is claimed for the one God. Amos names constellations without known cult; the Quran names a star worshipped in Arabia, so the claim is also polemical.

leads.title: The Lord at the altar, no escape, the sieve, and the fallen booth of David ↔ Passing the regions of heaven, the rose-red sky, forelocks and feet, and the two pairs of gardens with secluded maidens
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: O company of jinn and men, pass beyond the regions of the heavens and earth if you can; you cannot without authority; flames and molten brass will be sent on you (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The Lord at the altar, no escape, the sieve, and the fallen booth of David: In that day God will raise up the fallen booth (sukkah) of David and repair its breaches; God builds his upper chambers (ma'alot) in the heavens and founds his vault (aguddah) on the earth; 'Are you not like the Cushites to me, O Israel?'; The prophet sees the Lord standing by the altar commanding 'Strike the capitals so the thresholds shake'; All the nations over whom God's name is called will be possessed; God will plant them on their land and they will never again be uprooted; God brought up Israel from Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor and Aram from Kir; The plowman will overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes the sower; God commands the serpent at the bottom of the sea to bite those who hide there; God will shake Israel among the nations as grain is shaken in a sieve, yet no pebble will fall to the ground; The whole land heaves and sinks like the Nile of Egypt; In that day the mountains drip sweet wine and the hills flow with milk; and 3 more.

Only in Passing the regions of heaven, the rose-red sky, forelocks and feet, and the two pairs of gardens with secluded maidens: The damned go round between Gehenna and seething boiling water; Reclining on green cushions (rafraf) and beautiful 'abqari carpets; Houris secluded in pavilions/tents (khiyam); 'Is the reward of excellence anything but excellence?'; When the sky is split open and becomes rose-red like (red) leather/oil dregs; For whoever fears the standing before his Lord there are two gardens, with branches, two flowing springs and every fruit in pairs; Below those, two further gardens, dark green (mudhammatan), with gushing springs, fruit, palms and pomegranates; 'We shall attend to you, O two weighty ones (al-thaqalan)'; Doxology: 'Blessed be the name of your Lord, possessor of majesty and honor'; Reclining on couches lined with brocade, with the fruit of the gardens hanging near; The text addresses jinn and humans together in the dual ('you two', al-thaqalan, 'the two weighty ones'); The guilty are known by their marks and seized by the forelocks and the feet; and 5 more.

leads.title: The vision by the Tigris and the angelic princes of the nations ↔ Polemic with the People of the Book
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The angel Michael is named [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Michael, 'one of the chief princes', the great prince who stands over Israel (weight 6.3). Pair score 12.6.

Only in The vision by the Tigris and the angelic princes of the nations: The angel was opposed twenty-one days by the 'prince of the kingdom of Persia' until Michael came to help; A figure in human likeness touches the seer's lips so he can speak; What is inscribed in the 'book of truth' is revealed; The seer's companions do not see the vision but are seized with terror and flee; A man clothed in linen with a gold belt, body like chrysolite, face like lightning, eyes like torches, limbs like burnished bronze; The seer mourns three weeks, eating no delicacies, meat or wine and not anointing himself; Nations have heavenly 'princes' (patron angels): the prince of Persia, prince of Greece, and Michael 'your prince'; The seer receives a vision standing by the great river Tigris (Hiddeqel); The seer is addressed as 'greatly beloved' (ish hamudot); The seer falls into a deep sleep on his face; the angel touches him and sets him on his feet; Elyon divided the nations by the number of the sons of Israel/God; Jacob is YHWH's portion.

Only in Polemic with the People of the Book: The love of the calf was made to sink (be drunk) into their hearts; If the next world is yours alone, wish for death: they never will; Enmity to Gabriel and Michael (Mikal) equated with enmity to God; Gabriel (Jibril) brings down the revelation upon the prophet's heart; Some wish to be granted a life of a thousand years; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Claim that the fire will touch them only for a few numbered days, rebutted; The idol is burned, ground to powder, scattered on water and the people made to drink it; Israel at the mountain says 'we hear and we disobey' (sami'na wa-'asayna); Woe to those who write the book with their own hands and say it is from God, for a small price; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; and 15 more.

leads.title: Nebuchadnezzar demands his dream be told; the mystery revealed to Daniel ↔ Owner of sovereignty
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God changes times and seasons, deposes kings and sets up kings (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Nebuchadnezzar demands his dream be told; the mystery revealed to Daniel: The magicians say only the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh, could reveal such a thing; The king demands that his experts tell him the dream itself as well as its meaning, on pain of death; God knows what is in darkness and light dwells with him; A hidden mystery (raz) is revealed to the seer in a night vision; The enraged king orders all the wise men of the capital killed; Threat that offenders will be torn limb from limb and their houses made a dunghill; Courtiers address the ruler 'O king, live forever'; The king's experts cannot interpret the dream.

Only in Owner of sovereignty: On the day each soul finds what good and evil it did present before it, wishing a far distance from its evil; Believers may not take unbelievers as allies, unless guarding against them (tuqat); God warns you of himself (yuhadhdhirukum allahu nafsahu); God makes night enter day and day night, brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living; O God, owner of sovereignty, you give it to whom you will and take it from whom you will; you exalt and abase; God gives justice to the poor and seats kings (or the lowly) on the throne; The Most High rules the kingdom of men, gives it to whom he wills and sets over it the lowliest of men; God provides for whom he wills without reckoning (bi-ghayri hisab); Hymn of reversals: the barren bears seven, the mighty broken, the poor raised from the dung-heap.

matches.note: Cognate pair of titles: Dan 6:27 dî hûʾ ʾĕlāhāʾ ḥayyāʾ wĕ-qayyām lĕ-ʿālmîn 'the living God, enduring forever'; Q 2:255 allāhu lā ilāha illā huwa l-ḥayyu l-qayyūm. Only in The four beasts, the Ancient of Days and one like a son of man: Thrones are set and the Ancient of Days sits, his garment white as snow and his hair like pure wool; The seer asks one of the attendants or an angel, who explains the vision to him; A bear raised on one side with three ribs in its mouth is told 'Arise, devour much flesh'; The arch-enemy beast is slain and its body given over to burning fire; A heavenly figure or the holy ones are given everlasting dominion, glory and kingdom which all peoples serve; God's throne is flames of fire with wheels of burning fire; Four great beasts rise from the sea, each different, symbolizing successive kingdoms; A leopard with four wings and four heads is given dominion; The four winds of heaven stir up the great sea, out of which monstrous beasts arise; The holy ones of the Most High (qaddishe 'elyonin) receive and possess the kingdom forever; The horn makes war against the holy ones and prevails until the Ancient of Days comes; A little horn with human eyes and a mouth speaking great things uproots three horns; and 14 more.

Only in Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book: God's book speaks against them with truth: 'We used to have transcribed (nastansikh) all that you did'; What God's heavenly book records: names or deeds [divergence between the texts]; Deniers of resurrection say there is only our first death and challenge the prophet to bring back their fathers; To God belongs the grandeur (kibriya') in the heavens and the earth; Whether death is the end: asked, held by sceptics, or answered by resurrection [response between the texts]; Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; The prophet's mission and the hearers' closed ears, eyes and hearts: caused, sealed, or beyond his cure [divergence between the texts]; God forgets the damned today as they forgot the meeting of this day; Do evildoers think God will make them equal to the righteous in life and in death?; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Dhu l-Qarnayn ('the two-horned') is given power on earth and a way to everything (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The ram, the he-goat and the little horn; Gabriel explains: A king 'fierce of face' and understanding riddles arises, destroys the holy people, and is broken without human hand; Desolation reckoned as 2,300 evenings and mornings before the sanctuary is restored; A small horn grows up to the host of heaven, casts down some of the stars and tramples them; The tyrant magnifies himself against the Prince of the host / Prince of princes; A two-horned ram (Media-Persia) is trampled by a he-goat with one great horn (Greece) coming from the west without touching the ground; The seer is exhausted and sick for days after the vision; The seer finds himself in a vision at Susa the citadel by the river Ulai; The vision concerns the time of the end (et qets); The great horn breaks at its height and four horns arise toward the four winds (the successor kingdoms); A heavenly being or the seer asks 'Until when (ad matai)?' the desolation will last; The seer falls into a deep sleep on his face; the angel touches him and sets him on his feet; The seer is told to shut up and seal the vision/book until the end; and 3 more.

matches.label: Dhu l-Qarnayn ('the two-horned') is given power on earth and a way to everything
matches.note: hāʾayil ʾăšer-rāʾîtā baʿal haqqərānāyim malkê māday ûpārās, a two-horned ram pushing west, north and south, wəʾên maṣṣîl miyyādô; Dhū l-Qarnayn ('the possessor of the two horns') given power on earth and a way to everything, who travels west and east. The epithet is the same, baʿal haqqərānāyim / dhū l-qarnayn. In Dan it is the Persian empire, broken by the goat-king of Yāwān (Greece); in Q a just, God-guided ruler (usually identified with Alexander).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Open your hand wide to the poor brother; do not harden your heart or shut your hand (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Release of debts, release of Hebrew slaves, firstlings: Base thought refusing a loan as the release year nears; the poor man cries to God against you; There will be no poor among you, yet the poor will never cease from the land; Seventh-year release (shemittah) of debts owed by a fellow Israelite; Slave who loves his master has his ear pierced with an awl at the door and serves forever; Firstborn male of herd and flock consecrated to God, not worked or shorn; Debts of a foreigner may still be exacted though a brother's are released; Freed slave must not be sent away empty-handed but furnished from flock, threshing floor and winepress; Blood is the life; do not eat it but pour it on the ground like water; Whether obligations differ toward insiders and outsiders [response between the texts]; Firstborn male of herd and flock consecrated to God, not worked or shorn [contrast between the texts]; Hebrew slaves are released in the seventh year; Relief of debtors: release or respite [divergence between the texts]; and 2 more.

Only in Hypocrites who mock and the destroyed peoples: Hypocrites fear a surah will be revealed exposing what is in their hearts; Hypocrites mock the prophet as 'all ear' (udhun), credulous; Like a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows is a man who deceives his neighbor and says 'I was only joking'; God's good pleasure (ridwan) is greater than the gardens of Eden; 'Hate evil, love good, establish justice in the gate; perhaps God will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph'; Hypocrite men and women enjoin wrong and forbid right and close their hands; The 'overturned cities' (al-mu'tafikat), Lot's towns; God forgets the damned today as they forgot the meeting of this day; Roll call of destroyed peoples: Noah's, Ad, Thamud, Abraham's people, Midian and the overturned cities; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

leads.title: Passover, Weeks, Booths; judges; no Asherah ↔ Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy (weight 6.7); Who must make pilgrimage to the sanctuary, and how often [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Three annual pilgrimage festivals when every male appears before God (weight 5.3). Pair score 18.3.

Only in Passover, Weeks, Booths; judges; no Asherah: Unleavened bread, bread of affliction, because you left Egypt in haste; Justice, justice shall you pursue; No Asherah tree planted beside God's altar and no standing stone; Passover in the month of Aviv, at evening, at the chosen place; Feast of Weeks counted seven weeks from the first sickle in the standing grain; Seven full weeks (fifty days) counted from the sheaf offering to the new grain offering; Appoint judges and officers in every town to judge righteously; Passover offering boiled (bishalta) and eaten, flock or herd; Rejoice before God with sons, daughters, slaves and the Levite; Feast of Booths seven days after gathering threshing floor and winepress; you shall be only joyful; What is slaughtered on stone altars (nuṣub/anṣāb) is forbidden; the stones are abomination; Seven-day festival of dwelling in booths recalling the wilderness; and 3 more.

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts]; A place recognized as the house of God and gate of heaven; Who chose or founded the single sanctuary of sacrifice, and when [divergence between the texts]; and 4 more.

matches.label: Limits on how many wives the leader may take
matches.note: A limit on the leader's wives. Deut: wə-lōʾ yarbeh-lô nāšîm wə-lōʾ yāsûr ləḇāḇô, a general cap on number, for fear his heart turns. Q: first an enumerated permission (innā aḥlalnā laka azwājaka ... khāliṣatan laka min dūni l-muʾminīn), then a freeze: lā yaḥillu laka n-nisāʾu min baʿdu wa-lā an tabaddala bihinna min azwājin wa-law aʿjabaka ḥusnuhunna. Deut does not let the number grow; the Quran grants a special privilege and then closes it.

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى فَٱكْتُبُوهُ وَلْيَكْتُب بَّيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌۢ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَلَا يَأْبَ كَاتِبٌ أَن يَكْتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ فَلْيَكْتُبْ وَلْيُمْلِلِ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلْيَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُۥ وَلَا يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْـًٔا فَإِن كَانَ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُۥ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱسْتَشْهِدُوا۟ شَهِيدَيْنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمْ فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَٱمْرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ وَلَا يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُوا۟ وَلَا تَسْـَٔمُوٓا۟ أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أَوْ كَبِيرًا إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلِهِۦ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَٰدَةِ وَأَدْنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَرْتَابُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا وَأَشْهِدُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُمْ وَلَا يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلَا شَهِيدٌ وَإِن تَفْعَلُوا۟ فَإِنَّهُۥ فُسُوقٌۢ بِكُمْ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

matches.label: False witness receives the punishment he plotted for his brother
matches.note: fa-jlidūhum thamānīna jaldatan wa-lā taqbalū lahum shahādatan abadan ~ wə-hinnēh ʿēd šeqer ... wa-ʿăśîtem lô kaʾăšer zāmam laʿăśôt lə-ʾāḥîw: the false accuser is punished. Deut gives him the penalty he intended (talion); the Quran sets a fixed flogging, disqualifies him as a witness, and leaves room for repentance (illā lladhīna tābū, 24:5).

matches.label: Men leave the battle line to go home, and how that is judged
matches.note: Going home from the battle line. Deut grants it as a right: mî-hā-ʾîš ʾăšer bānâ ḇayiṯ-ḥāḏāš ... yēlēḵ wə-yāšōḇ lə-ḇêṯô ... mî-hā-ʾîš ha-yyārēʾ wə-raḵ ha-llēḇāḇ yēlēḵ wə-yāšōḇ lə-ḇêṯô. The Quran condemns the same plea: yastaʾdhinu farīqun minhumu n-nabiyya yaqūlūna inna buyūtanā ʿawratun wa-mā hiya bi-ʿawratin in yurīdūna illā firārā. The exempted house and the fainthearted of Deut are the hypocrites of the Quran.

وَإِذْ قَالَت طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنْهُمْ يَٰٓأَهْلَ يَثْرِبَ لَا مُقَامَ لَكُمْ فَٱرْجِعُوا۟ وَيَسْتَـْٔذِنُ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُمُ ٱلنَّبِىَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنَا عَوْرَةٌ وَمَا هِىَ بِعَوْرَةٍ إِن يُرِيدُونَ إِلَّا فِرَارًا
وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِم مِّنْ أَقْطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُئِلُوا۟ ٱلْفِتْنَةَ لَءَاتَوْهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُوا۟ بِهَآ إِلَّا يَسِيرًا

وَأَنزَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَٰهَرُوهُم مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مِن صَيَاصِيهِمْ وَقَذَفَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعْبَ فَرِيقًا تَقْتُلُونَ وَتَأْسِرُونَ فَرِيقًا

No offer of peace beforehand, but no killing of all males afterwards.

Deuteronomy exempts by circumstance of property and family: mî hā-ʾîš ʾăšer bānâ ḇayiṯ ḥāḏāš ... nāṭaʿ kerem ... ʾēraś ʾiššâ wə-lōʾ ləqāḥāh yēlēḵ wə-yāšōḇ lə-ḇêṯô. matches.note: Both remove a rebellious son for his parents' sake. Deut: after the fact and in public, bēn sôrēr ûmôreh ... ûrgāmuhû kol-ʾanšê ʿîrô, at the parents' own complaint. Q: a hidden pre-emptive killing by God's servant of a boy who has done nothing yet, fa-khashīnā an yurhiqahumā ṭughyānan wa-kufrā, which Moses protests as nafsan zakiyyatan bi-ghayri nafs. God then gives the parents a better child.

וּ֠רְגָמֻהוּ כָּל אַנְשֵׁ֨י עִיר֤וֹ בָֽאֲבָנִים֙ וָמֵ֔ת וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִשְׁמְע֥וּ וְיִרָֽאוּ

matches.note: Deut 21:1, 3 kî yimmāṣēʾ ḥālāl ... lōʾ nôdaʿ mî hikkāhû ... ʿeglat bāqār ʾăšer lōʾ ʿubbad bāh ʾăšer lōʾ māšĕkâ bĕ-ʿōl: an unsolved killing and an unworked heifer; Q 2:71-72 lā dhalūlun tuthīru l-arḍa ... wa-idh qataltum nafsan fa-ddāraʾtum fīhā: a heifer not used for ploughing and a killing over which people dispute. The ending is reversed: in Deut the killer stays unknown, the neck is broken (wĕ-ʿārĕpû) and the elders declare yādênû lōʾ šāpĕkû ʾet ha-ddām ha-zzeh, the blood atoned; in the Quran the cow is slaughtered (fa-dhabaḥūhā) and God brings out what was hidden (wa-llāhu mukhrijun mā kuntum taktumūn): the dead man is revived and the killer known.

matches.note: Deut 21:15 kî tihyênā lĕ-ʾîš šĕtê nāšîm hā-ʾaḥat ʾăhûbâ wĕ-hā-ʾaḥat śĕnûʾâ: a man with two wives, one loved and one hated, must still be fair to the hated wife's son; Q 4:3 fa-nkiḥū mā ṭāba lakum mina n-nisāʾi mathnā wa-thulātha wa-rubāʿa fa-in khiftum allā taʿdilū fa-wāḥidatan: marry two, three or four, but only one if you fear you cannot be just. matches.label: The penalty for falsely accusing a woman of unchastity
matches.note: Punishing the false accuser of a woman: Deut 22:18-19 the husband who brought out an evil name (hôṣîʾ šēm rāʿ) is chastised (wə-yissərû ʾōtô), fined a hundred silver and may never divorce her; Q 24:4 anyone who accuses chaste women (al-muḥṣanāt) without four witnesses gets eighty lashes, and his testimony is never accepted again. In the Quran the husband's case goes to the oath procedure of 24:6-9.

فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُوا۟ فَأْذَنُوا۟ بِحَرْبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَإِن تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُءُوسُ أَمْوَٰلِكُمْ لَا تَظْلِمُونَ وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَذَرُوا۟ مَا بَقِىَ مِنَ ٱلرِّبَوٰٓا۟ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

matches.label: How a husband divorces his wife
matches.note: Deut 24:1 kî māṣāʾ bāh ʿerwat dābār wĕ-kātab lāh sēper kĕrîtut wĕ-nātan bĕ-yādāh wĕ-šillĕḥāh: divorce for 'some indecency', by a written bill handed to her; Q 2:228-229 wa-l-muṭallaqātu yatarabbaṣna bi-anfusihinna thalāthata qurūʾin ... aṭ-ṭalāqu marratāni fa-imsākun bi-maʿrūfin aw tasrīḥun bi-iḥsān: no grounds and no document named; a waiting period of three menstrual cycles, the husband's right to take her back within it, and a limit of two revocable divorces. šillaḥ / sarraḥa, both 'send away'.

passages.text: כִּֽי יִקַּ֥ח אִ֛ישׁ אִשָּׁ֖ה וּבְעָלָ֑הּ וְהָיָ֞ה אִם לֹ֧א תִמְצָא חֵ֣ן בְּעֵינָ֗יו כִּי מָ֤צָא בָהּ֙ עֶרְוַ֣ת דָּבָ֔ר וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּיתֽוֹ

وَٱلْمُطَلَّقَٰتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ ثَلَٰثَةَ قُرُوٓءٍ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ إِنْ أَرَادُوٓا۟ إِصْلَٰحًا وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ

ٱلطَّلَٰقُ مَرَّتَانِ فَإِمْسَاكٌۢ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌۢ بِإِحْسَٰنٍ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَأْخُذُوا۟ مِمَّآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْـًٔا إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِۦ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ

matches.label: Whether a divorced wife may return to her first husband after another marriage
matches.note: Opposite rulings on the same case. Deut 24:4 lōʾ yûkal baʿlāh hā-rīšôn ʾăšer šillĕḥāh lāšûb lĕ-qaḥtāh ... ʾaḥărê ʾăšer huṭṭammāʾâ kî tôʿēbâ hîʾ: after she has been another man's wife the first husband may never take her back, it is an abomination; Q 2:230 fa-in ṭallaqahā fa-lā taḥillu lahu min baʿdu ḥattā tankiḥa zawjan ghayrahu fa-in ṭallaqahā fa-lā junāḥa ʿalayhimā an yatarājaʿā: after the third divorce she may return to the first husband only after marrying another. The intervening marriage that bars return in Deut is the condition for return in the Quran.

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لِيَسْتَـْٔذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُكُمْ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا۟ ٱلْحُلُمَ مِنكُمْ ثَلَٰثَ مَرَّٰتٍ مِّن قَبْلِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلْفَجْرِ وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيَابَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظَّهِيرَةِ وَمِنۢ بَعْدِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلْعِشَآءِ ثَلَٰثُ عَوْرَٰتٍ لَّكُمْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَا عَلَيْهِمْ جُنَاحٌۢ بَعْدَهُنَّ طَوَّٰفُونَ عَلَيْكُم بَعْضُكُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ

matches.label: Husband writes a bill of divorcement for 'some indecency' and sends her away
matches.note: Grounds and house reversed. Deut 24:1 kî māṣāʾ vāh ʿerwat dāvār we-kātav lāh sēfer kerîtut ... we-šillḥāh mi-bbêtô (he finds 'some indecency', writes a writ, sends her out of HIS house). Q 65:1 lā tukhrijūhunna min buyūtihinna wa-lā yakhrujna illā an yaʾtīna bi-fāḥishatin mubayyinatin: during the ʿidda the wife may not be put out of HER house, and 'flagrant indecency' is the only ground for eviction, not the ground for divorce. No written writ in the Quran; instead a counted waiting period (aḥṣū l-ʿidda).

passages.text: כִּֽי יִקַּ֥ח אִ֛ישׁ אִשָּׁ֖ה וּבְעָלָ֑הּ וְהָיָ֞ה אִם לֹ֧א תִמְצָא חֵ֣ן בְּעֵינָ֗יו כִּי מָ֤צָא בָהּ֙ עֶרְוַ֣ת דָּבָ֔ר וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּיתֽוֹ

matches.note: Return to the wife: Deut 24:4 lōʾ yûkal baʿlāh hā-riʾšôn ... lāšûv le-qaḥtāh (after she has married another, never; tôʿēvāh hîʾ). leads.title: Inscribed stones and altar on Ebal; the twelve curses ↔ Patience, Safa and Marwa, signs of creation
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Those who conceal the revealed signs are cursed by God and by all who curse (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Inscribed stones and altar on Ebal; the twelve curses: Curses on lying with father's wife, a beast, a sister, a mother-in-law; Cursed is he who misleads a blind man on the road; Levites pronounce twelve curses on secret crimes and all the people answer Amen; Six tribes stand on one mountain to bless, six on the other to curse; Large stones plastered with lime and inscribed with the whole Torah after crossing; Blessing pronounced on Mount Gerizim and curse on Mount Ebal; Altar of whole stones on which no iron tool is lifted; Do not move your neighbor's ancient boundary marker; Prohibition of carved images or likenesses of anything for worship; Promised land described as flowing with milk and honey.

Only in Patience, Safa and Marwa, signs of creation: On seeing the punishment, those followed disown their followers, who wish for a return to disown them in turn; Safa and Marwa are among God's waymarks; circuit between them permitted on pilgrimage; Formula of the afflicted: 'To God we belong and to him we return'; 'YHWH gave and YHWH has taken; blessed be the name of YHWH'; Those slain in God's way are not dead but alive, provided for with their Lord; God's test by loss of goods, lives and children [divergence between the texts]; God's covenant with Israel is as sure as the fixed order of sun, moon, stars and sea; Ships go to and fro on the great sea; Catalogue of signs: heavens and earth, alternation of night and day, ships, rain reviving dead earth, beasts, winds, clouds; Hear O Israel: YHWH our God, YHWH is one; Declaration that YHWH is God and there is no other besides him; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in The Song of Moses (Ha'azinu): Fire kindled in God's anger burns to the depths of Sheol and the foundations of the mountains; God like an eagle stirring its nest and bearing its young on its pinions; God refrains from annihilating Israel lest the enemy boast it was their own hand; God nursed Israel with honey from the rock and oil from flint; God will provoke Israel to jealousy with a no-people, a foolish nation; Jeshurun grew fat and kicked, forsaking the God who made him; Nations called to rejoice as God avenges his servants' blood and atones for his land; God as the Rock that bore you and the God who writhed in labor with you; Teaching falls like rain and distils like dew; Their vine is from the vine of Sodom; grapes of poison, wine of serpents' venom; God is the father who acquired, made and established his people; God raises his hand to heaven and swears: as I live forever; and 29 more.

Only in The bargain of lives for paradise; Abraham's prayer for his father: God has bought from the believers their lives and wealth for paradise; a promise in Torah, Gospel and Quran; Believers may not pray for forgiveness for polytheists, even close kin; Catalogue of believers: repenting, worshiping, praising, wandering/fasting (sa'ihun), bowing, prostrating, enjoining right; How Abraham parts from his father and his father's land or gods; Abraham prayed for his father's forgiveness only by a promise, and disowned him when he proved God's enemy; Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols [divergence between the texts]; Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols.

sides.note: The same sequence: no other god, no killing, no adultery, no false witness: lā yadʿūna maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhara wa-lā yaqtulūna n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi wa-lā yaznūna ... lā yashhadūna z-zūra ~ lōʾ yihyeh ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāf ... lōʾ taʿăneh və-rēʿăkā ʿēd šāqer. Changes: the absolute lōʾ tirṣāḥ gets an exception ('except by right', illā bi-l-ḥaqq); theft is left out; the commands become a description of the righteous (alladhīna lā ...), followed by doubled punishment and an exception for those who repent (25:69-70).

sides.note: A short list of apodictic prohibitions, the women's pledge as a small decalogue. Exodus: lōʾ yihyeh ləḵā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāp̄ lōʾ tiḡnōḇ lōʾ ṯaʿăneh ḇə-rēʿăḵā ʿēḏ šāqer. leads.title: Superscription, 'vapor of vapors' and the endless cycles of nature ↔ Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The sun runs to its resting place (mustaqarr) (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Superscription, 'vapor of vapors' and the endless cycles of nature: Endless cycles: the sun rises and pants back to its place, the wind circles, rivers run to the sea which is never full; All things are wearisome; the eye is not sated with seeing nor the ear filled with hearing; A generation goes and a generation comes, but the earth stands forever; There is no remembrance of former people nor will there be of those yet to come; What has been is what will be; there is nothing new under the sun; The speaker Qohelet ('the assembler') is presented as son of David and king over Israel in Jerusalem (royal fiction); What profit (yitron) has a man from all his toil under the sun?; 'Hevel havalim': vapor of vapors, all is vapor (vanity, futility, transience).

Only in Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship: The night is a sign: God strips (naslakh) the day from it and they are in darkness; A sign: God carried their offspring in the laden ship, and made for them similar things to ride; God measured stations (manazil) for the moon until it returns like an old dried palm-stalk; Asked to spend, unbelievers retort 'shall we feed one whom God could feed if he willed?'; God made the flood ship (or its survivors) a sign for all the worlds; The hero is saved with those with him in the laden ark (al-fulk al-mashḥūn); The sun comes forth like a bridegroom from his chamber and rejoices like a strong man to run his course; God made the sun a radiance and the moon a light with measured stations, to count years and reckoning; Sun and moon each swim in an orbit (falak); God created humans (and things) in pairs, male and female; Scoffers ask the prophet to hasten the punishment; it is held back only by an appointed term and will come suddenly; Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons; and 1 more.

Only in Cast your bread upon the waters; rejoice in youth: As you do not know the way of the wind (or spirit), or how bones grow in the womb of the pregnant, so you do not know the work of God; Send out your bread on the face of the waters, for after many days you will find it; Give a portion to seven or even to eight, for you do not know what disaster may come; Light is sweet and it is pleasant for the eyes to see the sun; Rejoice, young man, in your youth and walk in the ways of your heart, but know that for all these God will bring you into judgment; In the morning sow your seed and in the evening do not withhold your hand, for you do not know which will prosper; If clouds are full they empty rain; where the tree falls, north or south, there it lies; He who watches the wind will not sow, and he who regards the clouds will not reap; Youth and the dawn of life (shaharut, 'blackness of hair') are vapor; Graded numerical saying: 'Three things... and four...' (x / x+1).

Only in God's signs, the inexhaustible words, and the five things only God knows: Creating and resurrecting all of you is for God like a single soul; Waves overwhelm the ship like canopies (zulal); If all trees were pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas, were ink, God's words would not be exhausted; The religion of the fathers invoked, held to or renounced [contrast between the texts]; Whoever rejects false gods (taghut) and believes in God grasps the firmest handhold that never breaks; On the Day no parent can avail his child, nor child his parent; Only God knows when the mountain goats and hinds give birth and counts their months; Seafarers cry to God in a storm; what they do once rescued [divergence between the texts]; Sailors in a storm call on God sincerely, vow thanks, and transgress once saved; Rejecters reply 'we follow what we found our fathers upon'; Sun and moon are subjected, each running to an appointed term; God makes the night pass into the day and the day into the night; and 1 more.

leads.title: Bureaucratic oppression, the love of money and wealth that perishes ↔ Rivalry, time and the slanderer
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Riches kept by their owner to his hurt, lost in a bad venture, so that his son has nothing in hand (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Bureaucratic oppression, the love of money and wealth that perishes: He will not much remember the days of his life because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart; When goods increase, those who eat them increase; the owner only sees them with his eyes; The profit of the land is for all; a king is for (served by) the cultivated field; Sweet is the sleep of the laborer whether he eats little or much, but the surfeit of the rich will not let him sleep; He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance with income; If you see oppression of the poor in a province, do not be amazed: a high one watches over a high one, and higher ones over them; 'Naked I came from my mother's womb and naked I shall return there'; What profit (yitron) has a man from all his toil under the sun?; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

Only in Rivalry, time and the slanderer: Knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin) and the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin): you will see hell; God's kindled fire rises over the hearts and is closed over them in extended columns; Oath by time or the afternoon (al-'asr): humankind is in loss; Rivalry in piling up (al-takathur) distracts people until they visit the graves; they will be asked about the pleasures; A fire is closed over the damned (mu'sada); Hell given proper names: Laza (scalp-stripper), Saqar (scorcher, leaves nothing), al-Hutama (the crusher), Hawiya (the abyss); Do not go about as a talebearer among your people; Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal; Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' (wa ma adraka ma) introducing an eschatological term.

Only in Wealth unenjoyed, the stillborn better off, desire unfilled: Whatever has come to be has already been named; man cannot dispute with one stronger than he; All man's toil is for his mouth, yet the appetite (nefesh) is never filled; Better the sight of the eyes than the wandering of desire; A man with a hundred children and long life who is unsatisfied and has no burial: the stillborn (nefel) is better off than he; Even if he lived a thousand years twice and saw no good, do not all go to one place?; God gives a man riches, possessions and honor but not the power to enjoy them; a stranger enjoys them; Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; Sufferer wishes he had died in the womb or been a hidden stillborn; Human days on earth are a shadow.

Only in Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing): Do not be quick to anger, for anger lodges in the bosom of fools; Do not say 'Why were the former days better than these?', for it is not from wisdom you ask this; The end of a thing is better than its beginning; patience is better than pride; Like the crackling of thorns (sirim) under a pot (sir), so is the laughter of the fool; In the day of prosperity be joyful, in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other; A good name is better than good oil (shem / shemen), and the day of death than the day of birth; Better to go to the house of mourning than to the house of feasting, for that is the end of all men; the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; Oppression makes a wise man foolish and a bribe destroys the heart; Vexation is better than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made glad; Consider the work of God: who can make straight what he has made crooked?; Wisdom is a shelter (shade) as money is a shelter; wisdom gives life to its possessor; A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, favor rather than silver and gold; and 1 more.

Only in Those who stayed behind, the exempt, and the Bedouin: The Bedouin (al-a'rab) are harder in unbelief and hypocrisy; Shirkers say 'do not go out in the heat'; hell's fire is hotter; Poor volunteers turn away weeping because the prophet has no mounts for them; Who is excused from going out to war [divergence between the texts]; Even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of joy is grief; The prophet must never pray over a dead hypocrite or stand at his grave; Catalogue of believers: repenting, worshiping, praising, wandering/fasting (sa'ihun), bowing, prostrating, enjoining right; God uses the unbelievers' wealth and children to punish them in this life; Hypocrites swear excuses and ask permission to stay behind from the campaign; Exemptions from war for a new house, unharvested vineyard, betrothed bride, or faintheartedness; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear.

leads.title: Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution ↔ The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: When the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, God is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back! (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution: Because sentence (pitgam) against an evil deed is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil; There are righteous men who receive what the wicked deserve and wicked who receive what the righteous deserve; No man has power over the wind (ruah) to restrain it, nor power over the day of death; there is no discharge in war; Keep the king's command because of the oath of God; who can say to him 'What are you doing?'; I saw the wicked buried with honor, going in and out of the holy place, and praised in the city where they did such things; Who is like the wise and knows the interpretation (pesher) of a thing? Wisdom makes his face shine; Man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun; even if the wise man claims to know, he cannot find it; For everything there is a season and a time for every matter under heaven (birth and death, planting and uprooting, etc.); Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; Wisdom or the fear of YHWH adds days and years of life; the years of the wicked are shortened; Human days on earth are a shadow; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

Only in The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat: The damned eat of Zaqqum to fill their bellies and drink boiling water like thirst-crazed camels (al-him); A noble Quran in a hidden Book which none touch but the purified; The 'hospitality' (nuzul) of the deniers is boiling water and roasting in hell; The damned had lived in luxury and persisted in the great sin (al-hinth al-'azim); 'I swear by the positions (setting-places) of the stars, a mighty oath if you knew'; Have you seen the water you drink? Did you send it down from the rain-clouds? We could make it bitter (ujaj); For those brought near: rest (rawh), fragrance (rayhan) and a garden of bliss; The Companions of the Left are in scorching wind (samum), boiling water and the shade of black smoke (yahmum), neither cool nor kind; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; Fire kindled from a tree that God made grow [divergence between the texts]; The scripture exists with God in the 'Mother of the Book' (umm al-kitab), a heavenly archetype; and 8 more.

leads.title: Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city ↔ Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city: Man does not know his time; like fish caught in a net and birds in a snare, people are trapped in an evil time; A great king besieges a small city; a poor wise man delivers it by his wisdom, yet no one remembers him; The race is not to the swift nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise; time and chance (pega') happen to all; Wisdom is better than might and weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good; A wise man scales the city of the mighty and brings down its trusted stronghold; 'Better is X than Y' comparative saying (tov ... min).

Only in Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book: God's book speaks against them with truth: 'We used to have transcribed (nastansikh) all that you did'; What God's heavenly book records: names or deeds [divergence between the texts]; Deniers of resurrection say there is only our first death and challenge the prophet to bring back their fathers; To God belongs the grandeur (kibriya') in the heavens and the earth; Whether death is the end: asked, held by sceptics, or answered by resurrection [response between the texts]; On the day of the Hour every community is seen kneeling (jathiya), each called to its book of deeds; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; The prophet's mission and the hearers' closed ears, eyes and hearts: caused, sealed, or beyond his cure [divergence between the texts]; God forgets the damned today as they forgot the meeting of this day; Do evildoers think God will make them equal to the righteous in life and in death?; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; and 2 more.
