leads.title: Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The queen consults her chiefs, who defer to her; she observes that kings who enter a town ruin it and humble its nobles (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal: Royal decree that every man shall rule in his own house; Merry with wine, the king orders the queen brought in her crown to show her beauty to his guests; A decree written into the laws of Persia and Media cannot be revoked; At the royal banquet drinking is by rule, no one compelled; The disobedient queen is deposed and her royalty given to 'another better than she'; The queen refuses to come at the king's command and the king is enraged; King holds a banquet showing his riches for 180 days; The queen holds a separate banquet for the women; Seven named eunuchs serve the king; Palace garden decorated with fine hangings, marble columns, gold and silver couches and mosaic pavement; Susa the citadel (Shushan ha-birah) as setting; Royal decree sent to each province in its own script and each people in its own language; and 2 more.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 22 more.

leads.title: The search for virgins, Esther made queen, and Mordecai foils the eunuchs' plot ↔ Two hearts, zihar, adopted sons, and the prophet's wives as mothers
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether an adopted or fostered child counts as one's own child [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in The search for virgins, Esther made queen, and Mordecai foils the eunuchs' plot: King grants the provinces a remission and gives gifts at the new queen's feast; Virgins gathered from all provinces so the king may choose a new queen; Hero's genealogy runs back to Kish the Benjaminite (Saul's father); Heroine at the foreign court hides her people and kindred on her guardian's orders; Convicted plotters against the king are hanged (impaled) on a tree; A courtier's service is recorded in the royal book of chronicles before the king; Heroine has a Hebrew name (Hadassah) and a foreign one (Esther); Two eunuch doorkeepers plot to kill the king; the hero learns of it and reports it; A royal eunuch keeps the harem and supplies the women's cosmetics; Hero's family was deported from Jerusalem with King Jeconiah; Heroine wins the favor of her guardian official, who gives her special treatment; Heroine asks for nothing beyond what the eunuch advises when she goes to the king; and 5 more.

Only in Two hearts, zihar, adopted sons, and the prophet's wives as mothers: God took a solemn covenant (mithaq) from the prophets: Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus son of Mary; Adopted sons are not one's sons; call them by their fathers' names, or as brothers in religion and clients; God has not put two hearts inside any man; Blood relatives are nearer to one another (in inheritance) in God's book; The prophet's wives are the mothers of the believers and may not be married after him; Zihar: a husband declaring his wife 'like my mother's back'; she is not his mother, the saying is false and abhorrent.

matches.note: Why Pharaoh oppresses: Exodus gives his fear that the people will grow and side with enemies (pen yirbeh ... wə-nôsaf gam hûʾ ʿal śōnʾênû); the Quran gives his arrogance (ʿalā fī l-arḍ) and division of the people into factions. evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: On the day believers' light runs before them and on their right hands (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Consecration of the firstborn, sign on hand and forehead, Joseph's bones, pillar of cloud and fire: The exodus month is Aviv, the month of ripening grain; Firstborn sons must be redeemed; God leads the people by a roundabout route so they will not see war and turn back; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken; The rite shall be a sign on your hand and a memorial between your eyes; Command to tell one's son and grandson of God's deeds in Egypt; A child asks the meaning of a rite and the parent recites the exodus story; Firstborn sons and animals belong to God; Hero makes them swear to carry his bones out of Egypt; Unleavened bread eaten for seven days; God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night; and 1 more.

Only in The believers' light, the hypocrites who would borrow it, and the wall with a gate; hearts hardened by long time: Believers must not be like those given the Book before, whose term grew long and whose hearts hardened; The hypocrites beg the believers 'Wait for us, that we may borrow some of your light' and are told 'Go back and seek light'; A wall with a gate is set between them: inside it mercy, outside it, facing, the punishment; The people's hearts are called hard (Arabic q-s-w, Hebrew q-sh-h), or God makes them so [contrast between the texts]; The people's hearts are called hard (Arabic q-s-w, Hebrew q-sh-h), or God makes them so [divergence between the texts]; No ransom (kofer) may be taken for a murderer's life; Each wrongdoer would ransom himself with all that is on earth, if he could; God will remove the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh and a new spirit; Who will lend God a goodly loan (qard hasan), that he may multiply it for him?; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

leads.title: The pursuit and the parting of the sea ↔ Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith
leads.summary: 4 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed, 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows (weight 6.7); Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites (weight 6.7); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 29.2.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 16 more.

Only in Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith: Only some youths (dhurriyya) of Moses' people believed him, fearing Pharaoh; As he drowns Pharaoh declares faith in the God of the Israelites, too late; Pharaoh's body is saved from the sea to be a sign for those after him; Moses prays God to obliterate Pharaoh's wealth and harden their hearts so they do not believe until they see punishment; Moses and Aaron are told to make their people's houses in Egypt a qibla (place/direction of prayer); God's instruction about the Israelites' houses in Egypt before the exodus [divergence between the texts]; Threatened believers say 'to our Lord we return' and pray for patience and to die as muslims; Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows [divergence between the texts]; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes; How Moses' own people in Egypt respond to his message [divergence between the texts]; The king confesses he has sinned and that God is righteous; Who causes Pharaoh's refusal: God hardening his heart, or Pharaoh and his people themselves; and 6 more.

matches.note: Why Pharaoh pursues: in Exod regret at losing the slave labour (mah-zōʾt ʿāśînû kî-šillaḥnû ʾet-yiśrāʾēl mēʿobdēnû); in Q aggression and enmity (fa-atbaʿahum firʿawnu wa-junūduhu baghyan wa-ʿadwan).

passages.text: וַיֻּגַּד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח הָעָ֑ם וַ֠יֵּהָפֵךְ לְבַ֨ב פַּרְעֹ֤ה וַעֲבָדָיו֙ אֶל הָעָ֔ם וַיֹּֽאמרוּ֙ מַה זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֔ינוּ כִּֽי שִׁלַּ֥חְנוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעָבְדֵֽנוּ

وَجَٰوَزْنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ بَغْيًا وَعَدْوًا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدْرَكَهُ ٱلْغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَامَنَتْ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓا۟ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

matches.label: What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea
matches.note: The drowned are seen as a sign afterwards: fa-l-yawma nunajjīka bi-badanika li-takūna li-man khalfaka āyatan vs wayyarʾ yiśrāʾēl ʾet-miṣrayim mēt ʿal-śᵉpat hayyām. Exod shows the Egyptian dead on the shore to Israel then; Q singles out Pharaoh's body, saved from the sea as a sign for later generations.

passages.text: וַיּ֨וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֜ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיַּ֤רְא יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵ֖ת עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּֽם
فَٱلْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنْ خَلْفَكَ ءَايَةً وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا لَغَٰفِلُونَ

matches.label: The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives
matches.note: wa-jāwaznā bi-banī isrāʾīla l-baḥra fa-atbaʿahum firʿawnu ... ḥattā idhā adrakahu l-gharaq vs wayyāšūbû hammayim wayᵉkassû ʾet-hārekeb ... lᵉkōl ḥêl parʿōh.

passages.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ הַמַּ֗יִם וַיְכַסּ֤וּ אֶת הָרֶ֨כֶב֙ וְאֶת הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים לְכֹל֙ חֵ֣יל פַּרְעֹ֔ה הַבָּאִ֥ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם בַּיָּ֑ם לֹֽא נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּהֶ֖ם עַד אֶחָֽד

وَجَٰوَزْنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ بَغْيًا وَعَدْوًا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدْرَكَهُ ٱلْغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَامَنَتْ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓا۟ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

matches.label: Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows
matches.note: At the sea the pursuers recognise Israel's God: wayyōʾmer miṣrayim ʾānûsāh mippᵉnê yiśrāʾēl kî YHWH nilḥām lāhem vs Pharaoh's āmantu annahu lā ilāha illā lladhī āmanat bihi banū isrāʾīl. Exod gives it to the Egyptians as a group, Q to Pharaoh alone. cf. Pirqe de-R. Eliezer 43 and Mekhilta (Pharaoh survives and repents), outside the canon.

passages.text: וַיָּ֗סַר אֵ֚ת אֹפַ֣ן מַרְכְּבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיְנַהֲגֵ֖הוּ בִּכְבֵדֻ֑ת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִצְרַ֗יִם אָנ֨וּסָה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה נִלְחָ֥ם לָהֶ֖ם בְּמִצְרָֽיִם

وَجَٰوَزْنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ بَغْيًا وَعَدْوًا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدْرَكَهُ ٱلْغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَامَنَتْ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓا۟ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

passages.text: וְחִזַּקְתִּ֣י אֶת לֵב פַּרְעֹה֮ וְרָדַ֣ף אַחֲרֵיהֶם֒ וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל חֵיל֔וֹ וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵֽן
וַיְחַזֵּ֣ק יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶת לֵ֤ב פַּרְעֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּרְדֹּ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יֹצְאִ֖ים בְּיָ֥ד רָמָֽה
וַאֲנִ֗י הִנְנִ֤י מְחַזֵּק֙ אֶת לֵ֣ב מִצְרַ֔יִם וְיָבֹ֖אוּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל חֵיל֔וֹ בְּרִכְבּ֖וֹ וּבְפָרָשָֽׁיו

وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ ءَاتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَأَهُۥ زِينَةً وَأَمْوَٰلًا فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِكَ رَبَّنَا ٱطْمِسْ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ وَٱشْدُدْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ

matches.note: Motive for the pursuit: Exodus gives Pharaoh's regret (mah zōʾt ʿāśînû kî šillaḥnû ʾet Yiśrāʾēl mēʿovdēnû) and God hardening his heart so he will pursue and God be glorified (wə-ḥizzaqtî ʾet lēv Parʿōh wə-rādaf ʾaḥărêhem wə-ʾikkāvədâ bə-Farʿōh); Q 26:52 says only that God warned Moses 'innakum muttabaʿūn', and 26:54-55 gives Pharaoh's contempt (la-shirdhimatun qalīlūna ... la-ghāʾiẓūn). There is no regret over losing slaves and no hardening.

passages.text: וְחִזַּקְתִּ֣י אֶת לֵב פַּרְעֹה֮ וְרָדַ֣ף אַחֲרֵיהֶם֒ וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל חֵיל֔וֹ וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵֽן
וַיֻּגַּד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח הָעָ֑ם וַ֠יֵּהָפֵךְ לְבַ֨ב פַּרְעֹ֤ה וַעֲבָדָיו֙ אֶל הָעָ֔ם וַיֹּֽאמרוּ֙ מַה זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֔ינוּ כִּֽי שִׁלַּ֥חְנוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעָבְדֵֽנוּ
וַיְחַזֵּ֣ק יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶת לֵ֤ב פַּרְעֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּרְדֹּ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יֹצְאִ֖ים בְּיָ֥ד רָמָֽה

matches.label: How the sea was split for the crossing

matches.label: Whether those who saw the sea miracle believed
matches.note: Ending of the sea story: Exod 14:31 wa-yyîrəʾû hā-ʿām ʾet YHWH wa-yyaʾămînû ba-YHWH û-və-Mōše ʿavdô, the people believe, and the Song follows (15:1). The Quran's refrain: inna fī dhālika la-āyatan wa-mā kāna aktharuhum muʾminīna, a sign, yet most of them did not believe. Faith at the sea becomes unbelief despite the sign, aimed at the Quran's own audience.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 4.5.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; and 20 more.

Only in Midian, Ad, Thamud, Korah, Pharaoh and Haman punished: The prophet Shu'ayb is sent to his kin, the people of Midian (Madyan); List of punishment types for the nations: stone-storm, the Shout, swallowing by the earth, drowning; How the people of Midian came to be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; God did not wrong them; they wronged themselves (refrain); Korah (Qarun), Pharaoh and Haman are grouped as arrogant opponents of Moses; Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings; God casts great hailstones from heaven, killing more than the sword; List of destroyed peoples or hosts (e.g. 'Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh) recalled as warning; The earth opens its mouth and swallows rebels alive into Sheol.

matches.label: What Moses does with the sea after the crossing
matches.note: What Moses does to the sea after crossing. Exodus: wa-yēṭ mōšeh ʾeṯ yāḏô ʿal hay-yām ... wə-yāšuḇû ham-mayim ʿal miṣrayim (he stretches out his hand again to bring the waters back). leads.finding: Moses helps the women at the water of Midian

units.title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry

matches.label: Moses helps the women at the water of Midian
matches.note: At the water of Midian: Exodus has seven daughters of the priest of Midian (šebaʿ bānôt) who draw water, shepherds who drive them off (wa-ygārəšûm), and Moses who rescues them (wa-yyôšiʿān) and waters their flock. The Quran has two women holding back their flock (imraʾatayni tadhūdāni) until the shepherds finish, explaining abūnā shaykhun kabīrun; Moses waters for them unasked, then withdraws to the shade and prays (rabbi innī limā anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqīr). There is no fight with the shepherds.

passages.text: וּלְכֹהֵ֥ן מִדְיָ֖ן שֶׁ֣בַע בָּנ֑וֹת וַתָּבֹ֣אנָה וַתִּדְלֶ֗נָה וַתְּמַלֶּ֨אנָה֙ אֶת הָ֣רְהָטִ֔ים לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת צֹ֥אן אֲבִיהֶֽן
וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ הָרֹעִ֖ים וַיְגָרְשׁ֑וּם וַיָּ֤קָם מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיּ֣וֹשִׁעָ֔ן וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת צֹאנָֽם

وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُمَا قَالَتَا لَا نَسْقِى حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ
فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ

matches.label: Moses' father-in-law in Midian
matches.note: The father: Exodus has a named priest, kōhēn Midyān and Rəʿûʾēl, who scolds his daughters for leaving the stranger and invites him to eat (qirʾen lô wə-yōʾkhal leḥem); the Quran has an unnamed 'very old man' (shaykhun kabīr), no priest, who sends a daughter to pay Moses his wage (li-yajziyaka ajra mā saqayta lanā) and reassures him: lā takhaf najawta mina l-qawmi ẓ-ẓālimīn.

matches.label: What the Midianite daughters do after Moses helps them
matches.note: The daughters' role: in Exodus they report together to their father, ʾîš Miṣrî hiṣṣîlānû mi-yyad hā-rōʿîm, 'an Egyptian man saved us' (Moses taken for an Egyptian); in the Quran one daughter walks shyly (tamshī ʿalā stiḥyāʾ) to invite him and then advises her father, istaʾjirhu inna khayra mani staʾjarta l-qawiyyu l-amīnu, 'hire him, the best one to hire is the strong and trustworthy'.

matches.label: The terms of Moses' marriage in Midian
matches.note: The marriage: Exodus has wa-yyôʾel Mōše lāševet ʾet hā-ʾîš wa-yyittēn ʾet Ṣippōrâ vittô lə-Mōše, a named bride and no terms; the Quran has an unnamed daughter given under a contract of service, ʿalā an taʾjuranī thamāniya ḥijajin fa-in atmamta ʿashran fa-min ʿindika, eight years or ten if he wishes, sworn before God (wa-llāhu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīl).

In Genesis the woman waters the stranger's animals as a sign; in the Quran the stranger waters the women's flock.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How Moses killed the Egyptian [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The retort Moses hears on the day after the killing [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand (weight 6.7); How Moses learns that his life is sought [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Kinsman rebuffs the hero: 'Who made you prince and judge over us?' (weight 6.7); How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Hero flees the king's death sentence to a foreign land (weight 5.8). Pair score 45.5.

Only in Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry: The foundling's weeping moves the finder to compassion; The hero's parents are introduced anonymously as a Levite man and a Levite woman; Mother sees that her newborn 'is good' (ki tov); Hero names his son for being a stranger in a foreign land; Infant adopted by a royal woman [divergence between the texts]; The groaning of the oppressed rises to God, who hears and remembers his covenant; Hero drives off shepherds and waters the flock of women at a well; What the Midianite daughters do after Moses helps them [divergence between the texts]; Moses helps the women at the water of Midian [divergence between the texts]; Moses' father-in-law in Midian [divergence between the texts]; Moses killed a man and God delivered him from distress, then tried him with trials [divergence between the texts]; Who decides that Moses be put on the water [divergence between the texts]; and 19 more.

Only in Moses kills the Egyptian, is warned, and flees toward Midian: Moses calls his killing 'the work of Satan' and asks forgiveness, which is granted; A man comes running from the far end of the city to warn the hero that the chiefs plot to kill him; When Moses reached his full strength God gave him judgment and knowledge; Moses killed a man and God delivered him from distress, then tried him with trials.

leads.finding: How Moses killed the Egyptian

units.title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry
Moses kills the Egyptian, is warned, and flees toward Midian

matches.label: How Moses killed the Egyptian
matches.note: The killing: Exodus has Moses see an Egyptian beating a Hebrew 'of his brothers', look this way and that and see no one (wa-yyifen kōh wā-khōh wa-yyarʾ kî ʾên ʾîš), strike him and hide him in the sand. The Quran has him find two men fighting, one of his party (shīʿa) and one of his enemy; at his kinsman's cry for help he strikes one blow and the man dies (fa-wakazahu Mūsā fa-qaḍā ʿalayhi). There is no looking around and no hiding of the body; the act is unpremeditated.

passages.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם וַיִּגְדַּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֶל אֶחָ֔יו וַיַּ֖רְא בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מַכֶּ֥ה אִישׁ עִבְרִ֖י מֵאֶחָֽיו
וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל

وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ مُّضِلٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged
matches.note: Moral verdict on the killing: Exodus passes none; Moses only fears exposure (wa-yyîrāʾ Mōše wa-yyōʾmar ʾākhēn nôdaʿ had-dāvār). The Quran has Moses judge it at once, hādhā min ʿamali sh-shayṭān ... rabbi innī ẓalamtu nafsī fa-ghfir lī, and God forgives him (fa-ghafara lahu), so Moses is a repentant penitent before he is a prophet.

passages.text: וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל
וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ הַלְהָרְגֵ֨נִי֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֑י וַיִּירָ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע הַדָּבָֽר

وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ مُّضِلٌّ مُّبِينٌ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى فَٱغْفِرْ لِى فَغَفَرَ لَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيرًا لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ

matches.label: The retort Moses hears on the day after the killing
matches.note: The second day: in Exodus two Hebrews (šənê ʾănāšîm ʿIvrîm) fight, Moses rebukes the guilty one, and that Hebrew retorts mî śāməkhā lə-ʾîš śar wə-šōfēṭ ʿālênû ha-lə-hārəgēnî ʾattâ ʾōmēr ka-ʾăšer hāragtā ʾet ham-Miṣrî. In the Quran the same kinsman again calls for help against an enemy, Moses calls the kinsman 'clearly misguided' (la-ghawiyyun mubīn), and as he moves to strike the enemy he hears a-turīdu an taqtulanī kamā qatalta nafsan bi-l-amsi in turīdu illā an takūna jabbāran fī l-arḍ. 'Prince and judge' becomes 'tyrant' (jabbār).

passages.text: וַיֵּצֵא֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהִנֵּ֛ה שְׁנֵֽי אֲנָשִׁ֥ים עִבְרִ֖ים נִצִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לָֽרָשָׁ֔ע לָ֥מָּה תַכֶּ֖ה רֵעֶֽךָ
וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ הַלְהָרְגֵ֨נִי֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֑י וַיִּירָ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע הַדָּבָֽר
فَأَصْبَحَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَنصَرَهُۥ بِٱلْأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُۥ قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّكَ لَغَوِىٌّ مُّبِينٌ

فَلَمَّآ أَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَبْطِشَ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ عَدُوٌّ لَّهُمَا قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِى كَمَا قَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۢا بِٱلْأَمْسِ إِن تُرِيدُ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ

matches.label: How Moses learns that his life is sought
matches.note: How the danger reaches Moses: Exodus has wa-yyišmaʿ Parʿōh ʾet had-dāvār haz-zeh wa-yvaqqēš lahărōg ʾet Mōše, Pharaoh himself; the Quran has the chiefs plotting (al-malaʾa yaʾtamirūna bika li-yaqtulūka) and an unnamed sympathizer running from the far end of the city to warn him (wa-jāʾa rajulun min aqṣā l-madīnati yasʿā).

passages.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לַהֲרֹ֣ג אֶת מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּבְרַ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ מִדְיָ֖ן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עַֽל הַבְּאֵֽר
وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌ مِّنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ فَٱخْرُجْ إِنِّى لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

matches.label: Hero flees the king's death sentence to a foreign land
matches.note: fa-kharaja minhā khāʾifan yataraqqabu ... wa-lammā tawajjaha tilqāʾa Madyana ~ wa-yyivraḥ Mōše mip-pənê Farʿōh wa-yyēšev bə-ʾereṣ Midyān: flight to Midian (Madyan / Midyān). The Quran adds two prayers (rabbi najjinī ... ʿasā rabbī an yahdiyanī sawāʾa s-sabīl).

passages.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לַהֲרֹ֣ג אֶת מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּבְרַ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ מִדְיָ֖ן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עַֽל הַבְּאֵֽר
فَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ قَالَ رَبِّ نَجِّنِى مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقَآءَ مَدْيَنَ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِى سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ

matches.label: Hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand

passages.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם וַיִּגְדַּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֶל אֶחָ֔יו וַיַּ֖רְא בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מַכֶּ֥ה אִישׁ עִבְרִ֖י מֵאֶחָֽיו
וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל

sides.note: buried in the sand after looking this way and that

passages.text: وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ مُّضِلٌّ مُّبِينٌ

sides.note: a single blow (wakazahu); no hiding of the body

leads.summary: 6 correspondences read side by side: 5 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Sister offers to find a nurse [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Who decides that Moses be put on the water [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Infant returned to his own mother to nurse [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Infant adopted by a royal woman [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Infant placed in a container and set on the water [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Infant's sister watches over him (weight 6.0); Infant adopted by a royal woman (weight 6.0); Sister offers to find a nurse (weight 5.8); Infant returned to his own mother to nurse (weight 5.8); Infant found by members of a royal household (weight 5.6); Infant placed in a container and set on the water (weight 5.6). Pair score 67.8.

Only in Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry: The foundling's weeping moves the finder to compassion; The hero's parents are introduced anonymously as a Levite man and a Levite woman; Mother sees that her newborn 'is good' (ki tov); Hero names his son for being a stranger in a foreign land; The groaning of the oppressed rises to God, who hears and remembers his covenant; Hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand; Hero drives off shepherds and waters the flock of women at a well; How Moses learns that his life is sought [divergence between the texts]; How Moses killed the Egyptian [divergence between the texts]; What the Midianite daughters do after Moses helps them [divergence between the texts]; Moses helps the women at the water of Midian [divergence between the texts]; Moses' father-in-law in Midian [divergence between the texts]; and 15 more.

Only in Pharaoh's oppression and the infant Moses on the water: Moses' mother's heart becomes empty and she nearly discloses him, but God steadies her heart; God wills to favor the oppressed and make them leaders (aʾimma) and inheritors; Pharaoh exalted himself and divided the land's people into factions, oppressing one group; The oppressor slaughters the sons and lets the women live; Why Pharaoh oppresses Israel [divergence between the texts]; Hāmān appears as Pharaoh's minister and partner; Infant refuses other wet nurses; Mother receives divine instruction about the infant; Foster parent says: perhaps he will benefit us, or we will take him as a son; God addresses the hero with 'Fear not' in a vision; Ruler orders the killing of male infants; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

leads.finding: Who decides that Moses be put on the water

units.title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry
Pharaoh's oppression and the infant Moses on the water

matches.label: Who decides that Moses be put on the water
matches.note: Who decides to put the child on the water: Exodus has the mother, on her own, hide him three months and, when she can hide him no longer (wə-lōʾ yākhlâ ʿôd haṣṣəfînô), make a papyrus basket sealed with pitch. In the Quran God inspires her (awḥaynā ilā ummi Mūsā): nurse him, cast him into the river when you fear, and 'we will return him to you and make him one of the messengers'. The rescue is announced in advance.

passages.text: וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֹתוֹ֙ כִּי ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַֽתִּצְפְּנֵ֖הוּ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יְרָחִֽים
וְלֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר
وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

matches.label: Infant placed in a container and set on the water
matches.note: fa-alqīhi fī l-yammi ~ wat-tāśem bas-sûf ʿal śəfat hay-yəʾōr: Exodus places him carefully among the reeds at the edge of the Nile (yəʾōr), in a basket (tēvat gōmeʾ) with bitumen and pitch; the Quran says 'cast him into the yamm', with no vessel in this passage, using the word that elsewhere names the sea where Pharaoh drowns.

passages.text: וְלֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר
وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

matches.label: Infant adopted by a royal woman
matches.note: Who finds and adopts him: Pharaoh's daughter (bat Parʿōh), bathing, sees the basket, has pity on the crying child, recognizes him as Hebrew (mī-yaldê hā-ʿIvrîm zeh) and later names him. In the Quran Pharaoh's household picks him up (iltaqaṭahu ālu Firʿawn), and Pharaoh's wife (imraʾat Firʿawn) pleads with Pharaoh: qurratu ʿaynin lī wa-laka lā taqtulūhu ʿasā an yanfaʿanā aw nattakhidhahu waladan. Daughter becomes wife, pity becomes intercession, and the Quran adds the divine irony 'so that he would be an enemy and a grief to them' (28:8).

passages.text: וַתֵּ֤רֶד בַּת פַּרְעֹה֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ עַל הַיְאֹ֔ר וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֥יהָ הֹלְכֹ֖ת עַל יַ֣ד הַיְאֹ֑ר וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֶת הַתֵּבָה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַסּ֔וּף וַתִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֶת אֲמָתָ֖הּ וַתִּקָּחֶֽהָ
וַתִּפְתַּח֙ וַתִּרְאֵ֣הוּ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וְהִנֵּה נַ֖עַר בֹּכֶ֑ה וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִיַּלְדֵ֥י הָֽעִבְרִ֖ים זֶֽה
וַיִגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֨הוּ֙ לְבַת פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מִן הַמַּ֖יִם מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ
فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ
وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّى وَلَكَ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

matches.label: Sister offers to find a nurse
matches.note: The sister's offer: Exodus has hăʾēlēkh wə-qārāʾtî lākh ʾiššâ mêneqet min hā-ʿIvriyyōt on her own initiative; the Quran first has God forbid the other wet-nurses to him (wa-ḥarramnā ʿalayhi l-marāḍiʿa min qablu), then the sister offers a household that will rear him. cf. b. Sotah 12b (Moses refuses Egyptian breasts), outside the HB.

passages.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲחֹתוֹ֮ אֶל בַּת פַּרְעֹה֒ הַאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְקָרָ֤אתִי לָךְ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה מֵינֶ֔קֶת מִ֖ן הָעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת וְתֵינִ֥ק לָ֖ךְ אֶת הַיָּֽלֶד
وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ

matches.label: Infant returned to his own mother to nurse
matches.note: Why the child goes back to his mother: Exodus has a paid arrangement with the princess, hêlîkhî ʾet hay-yeled haz-zeh wə-hênîqihû lî wa-ʾănî ʾettēn ʾet śəkhārēkh; the Quran has God keeping his promise, fa-radadnāhu ilā ummihi kay taqarra ʿaynuhā wa-lā taḥzana wa-li-taʿlama anna waʿda llāhi ḥaqqun. The Quran omits the naming and its etymology (Exod 2:10).

leads.title: Altar law ↔ Children of Adam - clothing, Satan's enmity, what God forbids
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Nakedness must be covered at the place of worship (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Altar law: Altar to be made of earth; God will come and bless in every place where he causes his name to be remembered; God declares that he spoke from heaven; No steps up to the altar, lest nakedness be exposed; Altar of whole stones on which no iron tool is lifted; Prohibition of carved images or likenesses of anything for worship.

Only in Children of Adam - clothing, Satan's enmity, what God forbids: Wear your adornment (clothing) at every place of prostration; Satan and his tribe see humans from where humans cannot see them; Satan pulled off the first couple's garments to show them their nakedness; Eat and drink but do not be excessive; God sends down clothing to cover nakedness, and the 'garment of piety' is better; God's adornments and good provisions are not forbidden to believers; Short list of what God truly forbids: indecencies open and hidden, sin, oppression, associating partners, false speech about God; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; Clothing at every altar or place of prostration; God makes garments of skin for the first couple; God makes garments of skin for the first couple [divergence between the texts]; Every nation has a fixed term that cannot be advanced or delayed by an hour; and 1 more.

leads.title: The Ten Words and the people's fear ↔ The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb
leads.summary: 11 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: People fear to hear God directly and ask the prophet to mediate (weight 6.3); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property (weight 5.8); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8); No other gods before YHWH (weight 5.8); Prohibition of carved images or likenesses of anything for worship (weight 5.6); Sabbath rest on the seventh day for all, including servants, animals and strangers (weight 5.6); God visits the fathers' sin on the third and fourth generation, but keeps steadfast love for thousands (weight 5.6); The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) (weight 5.4); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.3); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness (weight 5.1). Pair score 62.2.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; Do not take God's name in vain; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; and 3 more.

Only in The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb: The covenant is made with those alive today, not only with the fathers; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; Mountain burns with fire to the heart of heaven amid darkness and cloud; The people answer as one: all that YHWH has spoken we will do [response between the texts]; Who was present at the revelation on the mountain, and who knows it only by report [contrast between the texts]; God heard as a voice out of fire with no visible form; The people's answer to the covenant ('we hear ...') [response between the texts]; Sabbath grounded in the memory of slavery in Egypt; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left; God gives stone tablets he himself has written.

וַתֹּאמְר֗וּ הֵ֣ן הֶרְאָ֜נוּ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ אֶת כְּבֹד֣וֹ וְאֶת גָּדְל֔וֹ וְאֶת קֹל֥וֹ שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הָאֵ֑שׁ הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ רָאִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי יְדַבֵּ֧ר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת הָֽאָדָ֖ם וָחָֽי
וְעַתָּה֙ לָ֣מָּה נָמ֔וּת כִּ֣י תֹֽאכְלֵ֔נוּ הָאֵ֥שׁ הַגְּדֹלָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את אִם יֹסְפִ֣ים אֲנַ֗חְנוּ לִ֠שְׁמֹעַ אֶת ק֨וֹל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ ע֖וֹד וָמָֽתְנוּ

sides.note: Deut: kabbēd ʾet-ʾāvîkhā wə-ʾet-ʾimmekhā ... ləmaʿan yaʾărîkhūn yāmêkhā û-ləmaʿan yîṭav lākh ʿal-hā-ʾădāmāh. Q: wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan. 'Honour' becomes 'kindness', and the promise of long life in the land is dropped.

וְלֹ֥א תַחְמֹ֖ד אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֶ֑ךָ וְלֹ֨א תִתְאַוֶּ֜ה בֵּ֣ית רֵעֶ֗ךָ שָׂדֵ֜הוּ וְעַבְדּ֤וֹ וַאֲמָתוֹ֙ שׁוֹר֣וֹ וַחֲמֹר֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְרֵעֶֽךָ

sides.note: wife listed before house; 'field' added

passages.text: לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ
לֹ֖א תִּרְצָֽח
לֹ֖א תִּנְאָֽף

sides.note: The same sequence: no other god, no killing, no adultery, no false witness: lā yadʿūna maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhara wa-lā yaqtulūna n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi wa-lā yaznūna ... lā yashhadūna z-zūra ~ lōʾ yihyeh ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāf ... lōʾ taʿăneh və-rēʿăkā ʿēd šāqer. Changes: the absolute lōʾ tirṣāḥ gets an exception ('except by right', illā bi-l-ḥaqq); theft is left out; the commands become a description of the righteous (alladhīna lā ...), followed by doubled punishment and an exception for those who repent (25:69-70).

passages.text: לֹ֖א תִּרְצָֽח
וְלֹ֖א תִּנְאָֽף
וְלֹֽא תַעֲנֶ֥ה בְרֵֽעֲךָ֖ עֵ֥ד שָֽׁוְא

sides.note: Deut: lōʾ tirṣāḥ; wə-lōʾ tinʾāf; wə-lōʾ-taʿăneh və-rēʿăkhā ʿēd šāwʾ, absolute. Q qualifies and widens: wa-lā taqtulū l-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi (with an exception); wa-lā taqrabū l-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara minhā wa-mā baṭana (all indecency, not only adultery); wa-idhā qultum fa-ʿdilū wa-law kāna dhā qurbā (just speech even against kin). Theft is absent.

לֹא יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ

לֹֽא תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֣א תָעָבְדֵ֑ם כִּ֣י אָֽנֹכִ֞י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֵ֣ל קַנָּ֔א פֹּ֠קֵד עֲוֺ֨ן אָבֹ֧ת עַל בָּנִ֛ים עַל שִׁלֵּשִׁ֥ים וְעַל רִבֵּעִ֖ים לְשֹׂנְאָֽי

passages.text: (20:8) זָכ֛וֹר אֶת י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת לְקַדְּשֽׁוֹ (20:9) שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּֽעֲבֹ֔ד וְעָשִׂ֖יתָ כָּל מְלַאכְתֶּֽךָ (20:10) וְי֨וֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽ֣א תַעֲשֶׂ֨ה כָל מְלָאכָ֜ה אַתָּ֣ה וּבִנְךָֽ֣ וּבִתֶּ֗ךָ עַבְדְּךָ֤ וַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙ וּבְהֶמְתֶּ֔ךָ וְגֵרְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ (20:11) כִּ֣י שֵֽׁשֶׁת יָמִים֩ עָשָׂ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה אֶת הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת הַיָּם֙ וְאֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר בָּ֔ם וַיָּ֖נַח בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑י עַל כֵּ֗ן בֵּרַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת וַֽיְקַדְּשֵֽׁהוּ

matches.label: No other gods before YHWH
matches.note: lōʾ yihyeh-ləkā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ʿal-pānāy; lā tajʿal maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhar: same first commandment ('other gods' / 'another god'). The frame changes: Exod opens with the exodus, ʾăšer hôṣēʾtîkā mēʾereṣ miṣrayim; Q frames the code with the command at both ends (17:22, 17:39) and with no history of Israel, wa-qaḍā rabbuka. Q's code also has no Sabbath, no images clause and no coveting.

matches.label: The Ten Commandments (Decalogue)
matches.note: A recited list of commandments compared item by item. Kept: no other gods (allā tushrikū bihi shayʾan = lōʾ yihyeh-ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm), parents, killing, sexual sin, false speech. Omitted: the Sabbath (zākhôr ʾet-yôm haš-šabbāt) and coveting; the image ban is folded into 'associate nothing'. Added: allā taqtulū awlādakum min imlāqin, the orphan's property, full measure and weight, keeping God's covenant. The prologue ʾānōkhî YHWH ʾĕlōhêkhā ʾăšer hôṣēʾtîkhā mē-ʾereṣ miṣrayim becomes qul taʿālaw atlu mā ḥarrama rabbukum, without the Exodus.

לֹ֖א תִּנְאָֽף

sides.note: The same sequence: no other god, no killing, no adultery, no false witness: lā yadʿūna maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhara wa-lā yaqtulūna n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi wa-lā yaznūna ... lā yashhadūna z-zūra ~ lōʾ yihyeh ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāf ... lōʾ taʿăneh və-rēʿăkā ʿēd šāqer. Changes: the absolute lōʾ tirṣāḥ gets an exception ('except by right', illā bi-l-ḥaqq); theft is left out; the commands become a description of the righteous (alladhīna lā ...), followed by doubled punishment and an exception for those who repent (25:69-70).

passages.text: قُلْ تَعَالَوْا۟ أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا۟ بِهِۦ شَيْـًٔا وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا وَلَا تَقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَوْلَٰدَكُم مِّنْ إِمْلَٰقٍ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ ٱلْفَوَٰحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكُمْ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ

وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ مَالَ ٱلْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَأَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَإِذَا قُلْتُمْ فَٱعْدِلُوا۟ وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰ وَبِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْفُوا۟ ذَٰلِكُمْ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ

sides.note: Deut: lōʾ tirṣāḥ; wə-lōʾ tinʾāf; wə-lōʾ-taʿăneh və-rēʿăkhā ʿēd šāwʾ, absolute. Q qualifies and widens: wa-lā taqtulū l-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi (with an exception); wa-lā taqrabū l-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara minhā wa-mā baṭana (all indecency, not only adultery); wa-idhā qultum fa-ʿdilū wa-law kāna dhā qurbā (just speech even against kin). Theft is absent.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether guilt passes from parents to their descendants [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; Do not take God's name in vain; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

Only in Tenfold reward; my life and death for God; no bearer bears another's burden: On the day some of the signs come, faith not believed before will not avail; My prayer, my rites, my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds; God made you successors (khalāʾif) on the earth and raised some above others in rank to test you; The Prophet is commanded to be the first of those who submit (awwal al-muslimīn); God multiplies a good deed (tenfold) while an evil deed is requited only by its like; Those who split their religion into sects, each party exulting in what it has; 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's; Follow the religion (milla) of Abraham the ḥanīf, who was no idolater; Fathers not put to death for children nor children for fathers; Each person dies for his own sin.

matches.label: Whether guilt passes from parents to their descendants
matches.note: Two points. (1) Exod: pōqēd ʿăwōn ʾāvōt ʿal-bānîm ʿal-šillēšîm wə-ʿal-ribbēʿîm, guilt carried across generations; Q 6:164 lā taziru wāziratun wizra ukhrā, no one bears another's burden. (2) Both make reward larger than punishment: Exod ʿōśeh ḥesed lā-ʾălāfîm against three or four generations; Q man jāʾa bi-l-ḥasanati fa-lahu ʿashru amthālihā wa-man jāʾa bi-l-sayyiʾati fa-lā yujzā illā mithlahā.

matches.note: A short list of apodictic prohibitions, the women's pledge as a small decalogue. Exodus: lōʾ yihyeh ləḵā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāp̄ lōʾ tiḡnōḇ lōʾ ṯaʿăneh ḇə-rēʿăḵā ʿēḏ šāqer. Quran: ʿalā an lā yushrikna bi-llāhi shayʾan wa-lā yasriqna wa-lā yaznīna wa-lā yaqtulna awlādahunna wa-lā yaʾtīna bi-buhtānin yaftarīnahu bayna aydīhinna wa-arjulihinna wa-lā yaʿṣīnaka fī maʿrūf. The same order of other gods, theft, adultery, killing and false speech, but addressed to women as a pledge (bayʿa) to the Prophet: murder narrowed to infanticide, false witness to a slander 'between their hands and feet' (false paternity, in tafsir), obedience to the Prophet added; no Sabbath, parents or coveting.

matches.label: What or whom the visionaries saw: God himself or his messenger
matches.note: What was seen. Exodus says plainly that the elders saw God: wa-yyirʾû ʾēṯ ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl wə-ṯaḥaṯ raḡlâw kə-maʿăśēh liḇnaṯ has-sappîr ... wa-yyeḥĕzû ʾeṯ hā-ʾĕlōhîm wa-yyōʾḵəlû wa-yyištû. The Quran leaves the object unnamed: mā kadhaba l-fuʾādu mā raʾā; wa-la-qad raʾāhu nazlatan ukhrā (he saw him at another descent), and the exegetes dispute whether 'him' is God or Gabriel. Exodus' open sight of God has no plain counterpart in the Quran.

leads.title: Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days ↔ Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God sends down his sakina (tranquility, cf. shekhinah) on the prophet and believers (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days: The cloud covers the mountain six days and God calls on the seventh; God's glory appears as a devouring fire; Joshua serves as Moses' attendant; Aaron and Hur left in charge while Moses is on the mountain; Moses leaves a deputy (Aaron, with or without Hur) with the people while he is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; Moses' set period on the mountain is forty (days and nights, or nights) [divergence between the texts]; A prophet spends forty days and forty nights in a set period; God gives stone tablets he himself has written.

Only in Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya: People of the Book who do not follow the true religion are fought until they pay the jizya, subdued; Polytheists are impure (najas) and may not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year; No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter the sanctuary; Gatekeepers stationed so that no one unclean enters the temple; Those counted impure are kept out of the sanctuary [divergence between the texts]; A large army must not claim the victory for itself [divergence between the texts]; City accepting peace becomes forced labor; one resisting has its males killed; The believers' pride in their great numbers avails nothing and the earth grows narrow for them (Hunayn); God supports the prophet with hosts (junud) the believers did not see; God reinforces the believers in battle with a thousand (or more) angels.

passages.text: (25:23) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ שֻׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:24) וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ לּ֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:25) וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ לּ֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ זֵר זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב (25:26) וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וְנָתַתָּ֙ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו (25:27) לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת לְבָתִּ֣ים לְבַדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (25:28) וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְנִשָּׂא בָ֖ם אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (25:29) וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ קְּעָרֹתָ֜יו וְכַפֹּתָ֗יו וּקְשׂוֹתָיו֙ וּמְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם (25:30) וְנָתַתָּ֧ עַֽל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֛ן לֶ֥חֶם פָּנִ֖ים לְפָנַ֥י תָּמִֽיד

passages.text: (37:10) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (37:11) וַיְצַ֥ף אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (37:12) וַיַּ֨עַשׂ ל֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וַיַּ֧עַשׂ זֵר זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב (37:13) וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו (37:14) לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת הָי֖וּ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת בָּתִּים֙ לַבַּדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (37:15) וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (37:16) וַיַּ֜עַשׂ אֶֽת הַכֵּלִ֣ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֗ן אֶת קְעָרֹתָ֤יו וְאֶת כַּפֹּתָיו֙ וְאֵת֙ מְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו וְאֶת הַקְּשָׂוֺ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֖ב טָהֽוֹר

matches.label: A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups

passages.text: (25:31) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מְנֹרַ֖ת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה תֵּעָשֶׂ֤ה הַמְּנוֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יִהְיֽוּ (25:32) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (25:33) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בַּקָּנֶ֥ה הָאֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (25:34) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (25:35) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (25:36) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה יִהְי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (25:37) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱלָה֙ אֶת נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔יהָ וְהֵאִ֖יר עַל עֵ֥בֶר פָּנֶֽיהָ (25:38) וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (25:39) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

sides.note: almond-blossom cups, knobs and flowers; one talent of pure gold

passages.text: (37:17) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַמְּנֹרָ֖ה זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה עָשָׂ֤ה אֶת הַמְּנֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה הָיֽוּ (37:18) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (37:19) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (37:20) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁ֨קָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (37:21) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּֽחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנָּה (37:22) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה הָי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:23) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:24) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר עָשָׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל כֵּלֶֽיהָ

passages.text: (25:10) וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֲר֖וֹן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:11) וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתוֹ֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ תְּצַפֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ עָלָ֛יו זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:12) וְיָצַ֣קְתָּ לּ֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב וְנָ֣תַתָּ֔ה עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּעֹ֔ת עַל צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית (25:13) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בַדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב (25:14) וְהֵֽבֵאתָ֤ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֥את אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן בָּהֶֽם (25:15) בְּטַבְּעֹת֙ הָאָרֹ֔ן יִהְי֖וּ הַבַּדִּ֑ים לֹ֥א יָסֻ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ (25:16) וְנָתַתָּ֖ אֶל הָאָרֹ֑ן אֵ֚ת הָעֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ

(37:1) וַיַּ֧עַשׂ בְּצַלְאֵ֛ל אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (37:2) וַיְצַפֵּ֛הוּ זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר מִבַּ֣יִת וּמִח֑וּץ וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (37:3) וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּע֔וֹת עַל צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית (37:4) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בַּדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב (37:5) וַיָּבֵ֤א אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הָאָרֹֽן
וַיַּ֧עַשׂ בְּצַלְאֵ֛ל אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ

passages.text: וְעָשִׂ֛יתָ שְׁנַ֥יִם כְּרֻבִ֖ים זָהָ֑ב מִקְשָׁה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם מִשְּׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת
וַ֠עֲשֵׂה כְּר֨וּב אֶחָ֤ד מִקָּצָה֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וּכְרוּב אֶחָ֥ד מִקָּצָ֖ה מִזֶּ֑ה מִן הַכַּפֹּ֛רֶת תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֶת הַכְּרֻבִ֖ים עַל שְׁנֵ֥י קְצוֹתָֽיו
וְהָי֣וּ הַכְּרֻבִים֩ פֹּרְשֵׂ֨י כְנָפַ֜יִם לְמַ֗עְלָה סֹכְכִ֤ים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ עַל הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת וּפְנֵיהֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶל אָחִ֑יו אֶל הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת יִהְי֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הַכְּרֻבִֽים

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles (weight 5.6). Pair score 12.3.

Only in Contribution for the sanctuary; ark, cover, table and lampstand: A cult object is hammered from a single piece of gold; A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark; List of precious materials for the sanctuary: metals, dyed yarns, linen, skins, wood, oil, spices, gems; God's voice speaks to Moses from above the ark cover between the two cherubim; The ark's carrying poles must never be removed; God will dwell in the midst of the people in a sanctuary; Exact dimensions in cubits are given for a sacred object of the sanctuary; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); Materials for the sanctuary come from the free-will gifts of all whose heart moves them; A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups; A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God; The tablets of the testimony are placed inside the ark; and 2 more.

Only in Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath): The ark (tabut) returns, carried by angels, containing tranquility (sakina) and relics left by the family of Moses and Aaron; David kills Jalut (Goliath) and is given kingship and wisdom; Were it not for God checking people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted; 'How many a small band has overcome a large one by God's leave'; God chose the king and increased him in knowledge and stature, though he lacked wealth; The people object that the chosen king has no wealth and they have more right to kingship; Before battle the army is tested at a river: whoever drinks is not with the leader, except a handful scooped by hand; What the ark contains [contrast between the texts]; David kills the Philistine giant [divergence between the texts]; A giant taunts Israel and is killed by a hero; A jar of manna preserved before the testimony for future generations; Objection raised against the newly chosen king [divergence between the texts]; and 9 more.

Only in Tabernacle curtains, frames and veil: The lampstand stands on the south side and the table on the north; The innermost room, the holy of holies, holds the ark; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

Only in Bezalel appointed; too many gifts; making of the curtains and frames: God gives the master craftsmen the ability to teach others; The people bring more than enough and must be told to stop giving; God calls a master craftsman by name for the sacred work; A second craftsman from the tribe of Dan assists the master craftsman; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; God fills craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom for sacred work.

passages.text: (26:15) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּ֖ים עֹמְדִֽים (26:16) עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ וְאַמָּה֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (26:17) שְׁתֵּ֣י יָד֗וֹת לַקֶּ֨רֶשׁ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד מְשֻׁלָּבֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל אֲחֹתָ֑הּ כֵּ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל קַרְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן (26:18) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֶשְׂרִ֣ים קֶ֔רֶשׁ לִפְאַ֖ת נֶ֥גְבָּה תֵימָֽנָה (26:19) וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אַדְנֵי כֶ֔סֶף תַּעֲשֶׂ֕ה תַּ֖חַת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ שְׁנֵ֨י אֲדָנִ֜ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֤רֶשׁ הָאֶחָד֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י יְדֹתָ֔יו וּשְׁנֵ֧י אֲדָנִ֛ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י יְדֹתָֽיו (26:20) וּלְצֶ֧לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית לִפְאַ֣ת צָפ֑וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֖ים קָֽרֶשׁ (26:21) וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּ֑סֶף שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (26:22) וּֽלְיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יָ֑מָּה תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שִׁשָּׁ֥ה קְרָשִֽׁים (26:23) וּשְׁנֵ֤י קְרָשִׁים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לִמְקֻצְעֹ֖ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן בַּיַּרְכָתָֽיִם (26:24) וְיִֽהְי֣וּ תֹֽאֲמִים֮ מִלְּמַטָּה֒ וְיַחְדָּ֗ו יִהְי֤וּ תַמִּים֙ עַל רֹאשׁ֔וֹ אֶל הַטַּבַּ֖עַת הָאֶחָ֑ת כֵּ֚ן יִהְיֶ֣ה לִשְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם לִשְׁנֵ֥י הַמִּקְצֹעֹ֖ת יִהְיֽוּ (26:25) וְהָיוּ֙ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה קְרָשִׁ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אֲדָנִ֑ים שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The priest carries Israel's names before God as a memorial (weight 6.7); The robe's neck opening is bound so it will not tear (weight 6.7); The names of the twelve tribes are engraved like seals on gemstones (weight 6.7); The priest's robe has gold bells and pomegranates on its hem so he does not die (weight 6.7); The ephod, a woven priestly garment with shoulder pieces (weight 6.3); Priests wear linen breeches to cover their nakedness, on pain of death (weight 6.3); The breastpiece of judgment set with twelve gems in four rows (weight 6.3); A gold plate engraved 'Holy to YHWH' on the priest's forehead (weight 6.0). Only in The high priest's vestments: Aaron and his sons are designated as priests; Priestly garments are made for glory and beauty; Priests are installed by anointing and 'filling the hand'; Urim and Thummim placed in the breastpiece for divine decision; God fills craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom for sacred work.

Only in The vestments made; the work completed and blessed: Gold is beaten into sheets and cut into threads for weaving; The leader sees the finished work and blesses the workers; Completion of the sanctuary is narrated in the language of the completion of creation; The refrain 'as YHWH commanded Moses' recurs in a sevenfold pattern; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim.

leads.title: Ordination of the priests ↔ Moses ordains Aaron and his sons
leads.summary: 10 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Ordination of priests lasts seven days (weight 6.7); Blood and anointing oil are sprinkled on the priests and their garments (weight 6.7); Anointing oil is poured on the head of the priest (weight 6.7); Portions are waved before God as a wave offering (weight 6.3); Sacred meat left over until morning is burned (weight 6.3); Blood is daubed on the right earlobe, thumb and big toe (weight 6.3); Priests are washed with water at the entrance before ordination (weight 6.3); Blood is put on the horns of the altar with the finger and poured at its base (weight 5.8); The flesh, skin and dung of the sin offering are burned outside the camp (weight 5.8); The offerer lays his hand on the head of the animal (weight 5.8). Pair score 62.5.

Only in Ordination of the priests: A basket of unleavened bread, oiled cakes and wafers is offered; An outsider may not eat holy food; The high priest's vestments pass to his successor, who wears them seven days; The breast and the right thigh are the priests' portion; Sacrificial animals must be without blemish; Whatever touches the most holy altar or holy things becomes holy; An offering by fire is a pleasing odor to God; The fat, the two kidneys and the lobe of the liver are burned on the altar; The fat tail of the sheep is offered.

Only in Moses ordains Aaron and his sons: Moses himself performs the priestly rites at the ordination; The whole congregation is assembled at the tent entrance to witness a rite; Anointing makes the tent and its furnishings holy; The refrain 'as YHWH commanded Moses' recurs in a sevenfold pattern; The ephod, a woven priestly garment with shoulder pieces; Urim and Thummim placed in the breastpiece for divine decision; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; A gold plate engraved 'Holy to YHWH' on the priest's forehead; A ritual action is performed seven times.

leads.title: The burning bush and the divine name ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 3 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: What Moses asks Pharaoh to allow [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh (weight 6.7); The departing slaves ask their neighbors for silver, gold and clothing and so plunder their oppressors (weight 5.8); God identifies himself as God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (weight 5.6). Pair score 31.4.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Formulaic list of the Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Perizzite, Hivite and Jebusite; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy) [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; How the sea was split for the crossing [divergence between the texts]; and 38 more.

matches.label: The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh
matches.note: The divine title before Pharaoh: YHWH ʾĕlōhê hā-ʿivriyyîm niqrâ ʿālênû (Exod 3:18, also 5:3) ~ innā rasūlu rabbi l-ʿālamīna, and when Pharaoh asks 'and what is the Lord of the worlds?', Moses answers rabbu s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi wa-mā baynahumā ... rabbu l-mashriqi wa-l-maghribi. The god of one people becomes the Lord of the cosmos.

matches.label: Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story
matches.note: 'God of your fathers' changes addressee. Exod 3:15, said to Israel: YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾăvōtêkem ʾĕlōhê ʾAvrāhām ʾĕlōhê Yiṣḥāq wē-ʾlōhê Yaʿăqōv. Q 26:26, said to Pharaoh and his court: rabbukum wa-rabbu ābāʾikumu l-awwalīna, 'your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers'. The God of Israel's ancestors becomes the Lord of the Egyptians' ancestors too.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed (weight 6.0). Pair score 19.4.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; Formulaic list of the Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Perizzite, Hivite and Jebusite; and 15 more.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts]; Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts]; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign; A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff; and 4 more.

leads.finding: Why Moses approaches the fire

units.title: The burning bush and the divine name

matches.label: Why Moses approaches the fire
matches.note: Why Moses goes to the fire: Exodus has him alone with Jethro's flock at Horeb, turning aside to see the great sight (ʾāsurâ nāʾ wə-ʾerʾeh ʾet ham-marʾeh hag-gādōl haz-zeh); the Quran has him traveling with his family (qāla Mūsā li-ahlihi), going to bring back news or a burning brand 'that you may warm yourselves'. The Quran names neither flock, mountain nor Jethro.

passages.text: וּמֹשֶׁ֗ה הָיָ֥ה רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת צֹ֛אן יִתְר֥וֹ חֹתְנ֖וֹ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִדְיָ֑ן וַיִּנְהַ֤ג אֶת הַצֹּאן֙ אַחַ֣ר הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֛א אֶל הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים חֹרֵֽבָה
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה אָסֻֽרָה נָּ֣א וְאֶרְאֶ֔ה אֶת הַמַּרְאֶ֥ה הַגָּדֹ֖ל הַזֶּ֑ה מַדּ֖וּעַ לֹא יִבְעַ֥ר הַסְּנֶֽה
إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَهْلِهِۦٓ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا سَـَٔاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُم بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ

matches.label: How God names himself to Moses from the fire
matches.note: God's self-identification from the fire: Exodus has ʾānōkhî ʾĕlōhê ʾāvîkā ʾĕlōhê ʾAvrāhām ʾĕlōhê Yiṣḥāq wē-ʾlōhê Yaʿăqōv, then ʾehyeh ʾăšer ʾehyeh; the Quran has yā Mūsā innahu ana llāhu l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu, preceded by subḥāna llāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīna. The God of the fathers becomes the Lord of the worlds, and the name-riddle becomes 'Allāh'. The Quran also leaves out the sandals and Moses hiding his face (Exod 3:5-6).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אָנֹכִי֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב וַיַּסְתֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ פָּנָ֔יו כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔א מֵהַבִּ֖יט אֶל הָאֱלֹהִֽים
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶֽהְיֶ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶֽהְיֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כֹּ֤ה תֹאמַר֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶֽהְיֶ֖ה שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֲלֵיכֶֽם
فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا نُودِىَ أَنۢ بُورِكَ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

matches.label: God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed
matches.note: innī ānastu nāran ... fa-lammā jāʾahā nūdiya an būrika man fī n-nāri wa-man ḥawlahā ~ wa-yyērāʾ malʾakh YHWH ʾēlāyw bə-labbat ʾēš mit-tôkh has-səneh ... wa-yyiqrāʾ ʾēlāyw ʾĕlōhîm mit-tôkh has-səneh: Moses approaches a fire and is called from within it. The Quran does not mention the bush (only 'who is in the fire and around it'), nor the bush not being consumed.

passages.text: וַ֠יֵּרָא מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהֹוָ֥ה אֵלָ֛יו בְּלַבַּת אֵ֖שׁ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַסְּנֶ֑ה וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַסְּנֶה֙ בֹּעֵ֣ר בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְהַסְּנֶ֖ה אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אֻכָּֽל

matches.note: Place and occasion of the call: Exodus has Moses shepherding Jethro's flock 'behind the wilderness' to Horeb, the mountain of God, a place of holy ground (ʾadmat qōdeš hûʾ), where he must take off his sandals. There are no flock and no sandals; the holy ground becomes a blessed spot.

matches.note: Purpose of the mission changed: Exod 3:10 lekāh we-ʾešlāḥăkā ʾel parʿōh we-hôṣēʾ ʾet ʿammî venê Yiśrāʾēl (to free Israel); 3:18 YHWH ʾĕlōhê hā-ʿIvriyyîm niqrāh ʿālênû. leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A bronze laver where priests wash hands and feet before service, lest they die [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A bronze laver where priests wash hands and feet before service, lest they die (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.7.

Only in Incense altar, half-shekel ransom and bronze laver: Once a year atonement is made on the altar's horns with blood; Atonement money funds the sanctuary as a memorial before God; Incense is burned every morning and evening; Unauthorized ('strange') incense or offerings are forbidden on the altar; Counting the people requires a ransom for each life to avert plague; Every adult man pays half a shekel; the rich no more, the poor no less; A small gold-plated altar for burning incense before the veil.

Only in Ablution, the covenant 'we hear and obey', and justice despite hatred: Before prayer wash the face, hands to the elbows, wipe the head and wash feet to the ankles; God restrained a people who meant to stretch out their hands against the believers; Bathing in water after sexual emission or intercourse; One in major impurity (junub) must bathe before prayer, except a traveller passing through; Without water, purify with clean earth (tayammum), wiping face and hands; Let not hatred of a people move you to injustice; be just; The people answer as one: all that YHWH has spoken we will do.

matches.label: Whether God rested, or could tire, after creating heaven and earth
matches.note: kî šēšeṯ yāmîm ʿāśâ YHWH ʾeṯ haš-šāmayim wə-ʾeṯ hā-ʾāreṣ û-ḇay-yôm haš-šəḇîʿî šāḇaṯ wa-yyinnāp̄aš (he rested and caught his breath) vs. a-wa-lam yaraw anna llāha lladhī khalaqa s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa wa-lam yaʿya bi-khalqihinna bi-qādirin ʿalā an yuḥyiya l-mawtā (he was not wearied by creating them). The Quran's denial of weariness answers the anthropomorphic wa-yyinnāp̄aš, and uses it as proof that God can raise the dead. See also Q 50:38.

leads.title: Bezalel and Oholiab; Sabbath as sign; the tablets ↔ Nearer than the jugular vein; the two recorders; driver and witness; Gehenna says 'Is there more?'; creation in six days without weariness
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 answers the other.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether God rested, or could tire, after creating heaven and earth [response between the texts] (weight 6.3); God rested and was refreshed on the seventh day (weight 6.3). Pair score 12.6.

Only in Bezalel and Oholiab; Sabbath as sign; the tablets: God calls a master craftsman by name for the sacred work; Whoever works on the Sabbath shall be put to death; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; Those who violate the Sabbath are punished (executed, cut off, cursed or transformed) [divergence between the texts]; Tablets written by the finger of God; A second craftsman from the tribe of Dan assists the master craftsman; The Sabbath is an everlasting sign of the covenant between God and Israel; God fills craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom for sacred work; Punishment of those who break the Sabbath [divergence between the texts]; God gives stone tablets he himself has written.

Only in Nearer than the jugular vein; the two recorders; driver and witness; Gehenna says 'Is there more?'; creation in six days without weariness: On the day the caller calls from a place near at hand, and they hear the Cry (al-sayha): the day of coming forth; The damned man's companion (qarin) disputes before God: 'Our Lord, I did not make him transgress'; The earth splits open from them and they hasten forth to the gathering; 'Enter it in peace': the day of eternity; they have what they wish and more (mazid) with God; The Garden is brought near to the God-fearing, not far off; God created the heavens and earth in six days and no weariness (lughub) touched him; Every soul comes with a driver (sa'iq) and a witness (shahid); The stupor (sakra) of death comes with the truth: 'this is what you tried to avoid'; Two receivers sit on the right and the left recording every word a person utters; At judgment the covering is removed from a person and his sight that day is sharp as iron; Four things are never satisfied: Sheol, the barren womb, earth not filled with water, and fire that never says 'Enough'; God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near [divergence between the texts]; and 12 more.

matches.label: Whether God rested, or could tire, after creating heaven and earth
matches.note: The clearest rebuttal of a HB statement in this chunk. Exodus: kî šēšeṯ yāmîm ʿāśâ YHWH ʾeṯ haš-šāmayim wə-ʾeṯ hā-ʾāreṣ û-ḇay-yôm haš-šəḇîʿî šāḇaṯ wa-yyinnāp̄aš. Quran: wa-la-qad khalaqnā s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa wa-mā baynahumā fī sittati ayyāmin wa-mā massanā min lughūb. Same six days (šēšeṯ yāmîm / sittati ayyām) and the same heavens and earth, but instead of 'he rested and caught his breath' the Quran has 'no weariness touched us'. The next verse turns from rest to praise: fa-ṣbir ... wa-sabbiḥ bi-ḥamdi rabbik (50:39).
