leads.title: The golden calf ↔ Exodus, the calf and the wilderness
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in The golden calf: Aaron builds an altar before the calf and proclaims a feast to YHWH; Intercessor reminds God of his oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; The people eat, drink and rise up to revel before the idol; The prophet's delay on the mountain makes the people lose faith; Whether the calf is a god that leads the people [response between the texts]; The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Israel asks its leader to make them a god [divergence between the texts]; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment [divergence between the texts]; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf [divergence between the texts]; Aaron's standing before God [divergence between the texts]; Who makes the golden calf and from what [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word; Ruler orders the killing of male infants [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

matches.note: Who makes the calf: Exod 32:4 wa-yyiqqaḥ mi-yyādām wa-yyāṣar ʾōtô ba-ḥereṭ wa-yyaʿăśēhû ʿēgel massēkâ: Aaron fashions it, and the people hail it ʾēlleh ʾĕlōhêkā yiśrāʾēl ʾăšer heʿĕlûkā; Q 2:51 thumma ttakhadhtumu l-ʿijla min baʿdihi wa-antum ẓālimūn: 'you took the calf', the whole people, with Aaron unnamed and no acclamation of the calf as the god of the exodus.

matches.label: A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf
matches.note: Who makes the calf. Exod: Aaron, at the people's demand, qûm ʿăśēh-lānû ʾĕlōhîm ... pārəqû nizmê hazzāhāb ... wayyiṣar ʾōtô baḥereṭ wayyaʿăśēhû ʿēgel massēkâ. Q: al-Sāmirī, wa-aḍallahumu s-Sāmiriyy ... fa-kadhālika alqā s-Sāmiriyyu fa-akhraja lahum ʿijlan jasadan lahu khuwār. Aaron is cleared and a new agent is brought in, who gives his own motive: baṣurtu bi-mā lam yabṣurū bihi fa-qabaḍtu qabḍatan min athari r-rasūl.

passages.text: וַיַּ֣רְא הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי בֹשֵׁ֥שׁ מֹשֶׁ֖ה לָרֶ֣דֶת מִן הָהָ֑ר וַיִּקָּהֵ֨ל הָעָ֜ם עַֽל אַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ ק֣וּם עֲשֵׂה לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵֽלְכוּ֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ כִּי זֶ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֨נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְנוּ מֶה הָ֥יָה לֽוֹ
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אַהֲרֹ֔ן פָּֽרְקוּ֙ נִזְמֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י נְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם בְּנֵיכֶ֖ם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָבִ֖יאוּ אֵלָֽי
וַיִּקַּ֣ח מִיָּדָ֗ם וַיָּ֤צַר אֹתוֹ֙ בַּחֶ֔רֶט וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם
قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِىَ

matches.label: Aaron warns the people against the calf; they refuse to stop until Moses returns
matches.note: Reversal. Exod: Aaron builds the altar before the calf and proclaims ḥag laYHWH māḥār. Q: Aaron warns them, yā qawmi innamā futintum bihi wa-inna rabbakumu r-Raḥmānu fa-ttabiʿūnī, and the people refuse, lan nabraḥa ʿalayhi ʿākifīna ḥattā yarjiʿa ilaynā Mūsā.

passages.text: וַיַּ֣רְא אַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לְפָנָ֑יו וַיִּקְרָ֤א אַֽהֲרֹן֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר חַ֥ג לַיהוָ֖ה מָחָֽר
وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَٰرُونُ مِن قَبْلُ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى وَأَطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرِى
قَالُوا۟ لَن نَّبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ

matches.label: The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt
matches.note: ʾēlleh ʾĕlōhêkā yiśrāʾēl ʾăšer heʿĕlûkā mēʾereṣ miṣrāyim; hādhā ilāhukum wa-ilāhu Mūsā fa-nasiya. Exod has a plural 'gods' credited with the exodus; Q has 'your god and Moses' god, whom he forgot', making Moses' absence on the mountain into forgetfulness.

matches.label: God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment
matches.note: God tells Moses on the mountain what the people have done. Exod: lek-rēd kî šiḥēt ʿamməkā ... wəʿattâ hannîḥâ llî wəyiḥar-ʾappî bāhem waʾăkallēm, and Moses intercedes, lāmmâ YHWH yeḥĕreh ʾappəkā. Q: God asks mā aʿjalaka ʿan qawmika and says fa-innā qad fatannā qawmaka, the people tested by God himself. There is no threat to destroy them and no intercession.

leads.title: The golden calf ↔ The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: If God willed he could remove you and bring a new creation (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in The golden calf: Aaron builds an altar before the calf and proclaims a feast to YHWH; Intercessor reminds God of his oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; The people eat, drink and rise up to revel before the idol; The prophet's delay on the mountain makes the people lose faith; Whether the calf is a god that leads the people [response between the texts]; The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Israel asks its leader to make them a god [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment [divergence between the texts]; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

Only in The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas: God made the angels messengers with wings in twos, threes and fours, adding to creation what he wills; To God ascends the good word, and righteous deeds raise it up; Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy; he calls his party to the blaze; The false gods do not own even the thin skin of a date-stone (qitmir); they cannot hear prayer and will disown it at the Resurrection; The form, faces and number of wings of heavenly beings [divergence between the texts]; Each cherub or living creature has four faces (human, lion, ox/cherub, eagle), four wings and human hands under the wings; What God opens no one can shut, and what he withholds no one can release; What happens where fresh and salt water meet [divergence between the texts]; God began man's creation from clay, then made his progeny from an extract of a despised fluid, then shaped him and breathed of his spirit; No one is granted long life or has his life shortened except it is in a Book; The life of this world is only amusement and play (lahw wa-la'ib); the abode of the hereafter is the true life; Sun and moon are subjected, each running to an appointed term; and 6 more.

matches.label: If God willed he could remove you and bring a new creation
matches.note: wə-yiḥar-ʾappî ḇāhem wa-ʾăḵallēm wə-ʾeʿĕśeh ʾôṯəḵā lə-ḡôy gāḏôl vs. in yashaʾ yudhhibkum wa-yaʾti bi-khalqin jadīdin wa-mā dhālika ʿalā llāhi bi-ʿazīz: God can do away with a people and start again. evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Aaron's standing before God [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The golden calf: Aaron builds an altar before the calf and proclaims a feast to YHWH; Intercessor reminds God of his oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; The people eat, drink and rise up to revel before the idol; The prophet's delay on the mountain makes the people lose faith; Whether the calf is a god that leads the people [response between the texts]; The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Israel asks its leader to make them a god [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment [divergence between the texts]; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

leads.title: The golden calf ↔ The lowing calf and the seventy
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 answers the other.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether the calf is a god that leads the people [response between the texts] (weight 6.7); Who makes the golden calf and from what [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A golden calf is made from the people's gold earrings (weight 6.3). Pair score 19.7.

Only in The golden calf: Aaron builds an altar before the calf and proclaims a feast to YHWH; Intercessor reminds God of his oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; The people eat, drink and rise up to revel before the idol; The prophet's delay on the mountain makes the people lose faith; The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Israel asks its leader to make them a god [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment [divergence between the texts]; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf [divergence between the texts]; Aaron's standing before God [divergence between the texts]; and 6 more.

Only in The lowing calf and the seventy: Aaron pleads 'son of my mother, the people overpowered me and almost killed me'; The angry prophet seizes his brother by the head (and beard), dragging him; The seventy chosen men are seized by a tremor at the appointed meeting; When his anger subsides the prophet takes up the cast-down tablets again, their text intact; Aaron answers Moses' rebuke over the calf [divergence between the texts]; The people exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox that eats grass; God declares he will be gracious to whom he will be gracious; Moses intercedes for Aaron, with whom God was angry enough to destroy him; God's mercy encompasses all things; Moses includes himself with the guilty people in his plea after the calf [divergence between the texts]; Moses prays for Aaron after the calf [divergence between the texts]; Moses 'stood in the breach' (pérets) before God to turn back his wrath from destroying the people; and 13 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How the calf-worshippers are punished [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Aaron answers Moses' rebuke over the calf [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Moses includes himself with the guilty people in his plea after the calf [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The prophet breaks the tablets in anger at the idolatry (weight 6.3); The idol calf is a body that makes a lowing sound (khuwar) (weight 6.3); What becomes of the first tablets after the calf: broken and replaced, or cast down and taken up again [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8). Pair score 38.4.

Only in Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer: Aaron excuses himself: the people pressed him and the calf came out of the fire; The people run wild and become a derision to their enemies; God strikes the people with plague for idolatry; The prophet asks to be blotted from God's book if the people are not forgiven; The noise of the idolatrous revelry is mistaken for the sound of battle; The tablets are written on both sides by God; The leader calls 'Who is for YHWH? To me!' and a group rallies; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream [divergence between the texts]; The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast [divergence between the texts]; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; God erases what he wills and confirms, and with him is the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab); God sends an angel ahead of Israel who bears God's name; and 11 more.

Only in The lowing calf and the seventy: Aaron pleads 'son of my mother, the people overpowered me and almost killed me'; The angry prophet seizes his brother by the head (and beard), dragging him; The seventy chosen men are seized by a tremor at the appointed meeting; When his anger subsides the prophet takes up the cast-down tablets again, their text intact; Whether the calf is a god that leads the people [response between the texts]; The people exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox that eats grass; God declares he will be gracious to whom he will be gracious; Moses intercedes for Aaron, with whom God was angry enough to destroy him; God's mercy encompasses all things; Moses prays for Aaron after the calf [divergence between the texts]; Moses 'stood in the breach' (pérets) before God to turn back his wrath from destroying the people; After the calf the people mourn or repent of what they did [divergence between the texts]; and 10 more.

matches.label: What becomes of the first tablets after the calf: broken and replaced, or cast down and taken up again
matches.note: Moses returns angry: rajaʿa ... ghaḍbāna asifan; wa-alqā l-alwāḥa vs wayyiḥar ʾap mōšeh wayyašlēk miyyādāw ʾet-hallūḥōt wayšabbēr ʾōtām taḥat hāhār. Q has only 'cast down' (alqā), never 'broke' (Hebrew šibbēr).

passages.text: וַֽיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרַב֙ אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת הָעֵ֖גֶל וּמְחֹלֹ֑ת וַיִּֽחַר אַ֣ף מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֤ךְ מידו מִיָּדָיו֙ אֶת הַלֻּחֹ֔ת וַיְשַׁבֵּ֥ר אֹתָ֖ם תַּ֥חַת הָהָֽר

وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ غَضْبَٰنَ أَسِفًا قَالَ بِئْسَمَا خَلَفْتُمُونِى مِنۢ بَعْدِىٓ أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَلْقَى ٱلْأَلْوَاحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِ قَالَ ٱبْنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱسْتَضْعَفُونِى وَكَادُوا۟ يَقْتُلُونَنِى فَلَا تُشْمِتْ بِىَ ٱلْأَعْدَآءَ وَلَا تَجْعَلْنِى مَعَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

matches.label: Aaron answers Moses' rebuke over the calf
matches.note: Moses confronts Aaron, who blames the people: qāla bna umma inna l-qawma staḍʿafūnī wa-kādū yaqtulūnanī vs ʾal-yiḥar ʾap ʾădōnî ʾattāh yādaʿtā ʾet-hāʿām kî bᵉraʿ hûʾ. Changed: in Exod Aaron made the calf and admits throwing the gold into the fire; in Q he is not its maker and pleads that he was overpowered and nearly killed. He also calls Moses 'son of my mother' instead of ʾădōnî 'my lord'; Q adds the violence (akhadha bi-raʾsi akhīhi yajurruhu ilayhi).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֔ן מֶֽה עָשָׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי הֵבֵ֥אתָ עָלָ֖יו חֲטָאָ֥ה גְדֹלָֽה
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַהֲרֹ֔ן אַל יִ֥חַר אַ֖ף אֲדֹנִ֑י אַתָּה֙ יָדַ֣עְתָּ אֶת הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י בְרָ֖ע הֽוּא
וָאֹמַ֤ר לָהֶם֙ לְמִ֣י זָהָ֔ב הִתְפָּרָ֖קוּ וַיִּתְּנוּ לִ֑י וָאַשְׁלִכֵ֣הוּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וַיֵּצֵ֖א הָעֵ֥גֶל הַזֶּֽה

وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ غَضْبَٰنَ أَسِفًا قَالَ بِئْسَمَا خَلَفْتُمُونِى مِنۢ بَعْدِىٓ أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَلْقَى ٱلْأَلْوَاحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِ قَالَ ٱبْنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱسْتَضْعَفُونِى وَكَادُوا۟ يَقْتُلُونَنِى فَلَا تُشْمِتْ بِىَ ٱلْأَعْدَآءَ وَلَا تَجْعَلْنِى مَعَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

matches.label: How the calf-worshippers are punished
matches.note: Punishment for the calf: sa-yanāluhum ghaḍabun min rabbihim wa-dhillatun fī l-ḥayāti d-dunyā vs the Levites' killing of about 3,000 (kišlōšet ʾalpê ʾîš), the deferred visitation (ûbᵉyôm poqdî ûpāqadtî) and the plague (wayyiggōp YHWH ʾet-hāʿām). Q leaves out the Levite slaughter and gives wrath and humiliation in this life.

passages.text: וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ בְנֵֽי לֵוִ֖י כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּפֹּ֤ל מִן הָעָם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כִּשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֖י אִֽישׁ
וְעַתָּ֞ה לֵ֣ךְ נְחֵ֣ה אֶת הָעָ֗ם אֶ֤ל אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ לָ֔ךְ הִנֵּ֥ה מַלְאָכִ֖י יֵלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וּבְי֣וֹם פָּקְדִ֔י וּפָקַדְתִּ֥י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם חַטָּאתָֽם
וַיִּגֹּ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה אֶת הָעָ֑ם עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֶת הָעֵ֔גֶל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה אַהֲרֹֽן
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ ٱلْعِجْلَ سَيَنَالُهُمْ غَضَبٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَذِلَّةٌ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُفْتَرِينَ

matches.label: Moses includes himself with the guilty people in his plea after the calf
matches.note: Moses joins himself to the guilty: in Exod in punishment (wᵉʾim-ʾayin mᵉḥēnî nāʾ missiprᵉkā), answered by mî ʾăšer ḥāṭāʾ-lî ʾemḥennû missiprî; in Q in forgiveness (ighfir lī wa-li-akhī; fa-ghfir lanā wa-rḥamnā), answered by inna rabbaka min baʿdihā la-ghafūrun raḥīm for those who repent.

passages.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה אִם תִּשָּׂ֣א חַטָּאתָ֑ם וְאִם אַ֕יִן מְחֵ֣נִי נָ֔א מִֽסִּפְרְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּתָֽבְתָּ
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֑ה מִ֚י אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָֽטָא לִ֔י אֶמְחֶ֖נּוּ מִסִּפְרִֽי
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِأَخِى وَأَدْخِلْنَا فِى رَحْمَتِكَ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
وَٱلَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا۟ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ ثُمَّ تَابُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِهَا وَءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ

وَٱخْتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوْمَهُۥ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا لِّمِيقَٰتِنَا فَلَمَّآ أَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلرَّجْفَةُ قَالَ رَبِّ لَوْ شِئْتَ أَهْلَكْتَهُم مِّن قَبْلُ وَإِيَّٰىَ أَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَّآ إِنْ هِىَ إِلَّا فِتْنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِهَا مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَهْدِى مَن تَشَآءُ أَنتَ وَلِيُّنَا فَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا وَٱرْحَمْنَا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْغَٰفِرِينَ

matches.label: The idol calf is a body that makes a lowing sound (khuwar)
matches.note: The calf as if alive: ʿijlan jasadan lahu khuwārun (a body that lows) vs Aaron's wāʾašlikēhû bāʾēš wayyēṣēʾ hāʿēgel hazzeh ('I threw it in the fire and out came this calf'). cf. Pirqe de-R. Eliezer 45 (the calf comes out lowing), outside the canon.

passages.text: וָאֹמַ֤ר לָהֶם֙ לְמִ֣י זָהָ֔ב הִתְפָּרָ֖קוּ וַיִּתְּנוּ לִ֑י וָאַשְׁלִכֵ֣הוּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וַיֵּצֵ֖א הָעֵ֥גֶל הַזֶּֽה
وَٱتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ مُوسَىٰ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌ أَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّهُۥ لَا يُكَلِّمُهُمْ وَلَا يَهْدِيهِمْ سَبِيلًا ٱتَّخَذُوهُ وَكَانُوا۟ ظَٰلِمِينَ

matches.label: The prophet breaks the tablets in anger at the idolatry

وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ غَضْبَٰنَ أَسِفًا قَالَ بِئْسَمَا خَلَفْتُمُونِى مِنۢ بَعْدِىٓ أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَلْقَى ٱلْأَلْوَاحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِ قَالَ ٱبْنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱسْتَضْعَفُونِى وَكَادُوا۟ يَقْتُلُونَنِى فَلَا تُشْمِتْ بِىَ ٱلْأَعْدَآءَ وَلَا تَجْعَلْنِى مَعَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

sides.note: cast down (alqa), not said to break

leads.title: Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer ↔ Who maintains the mosques; God above family
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The Levites kill idolaters including their own kin and are consecrated for it (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer: Aaron excuses himself: the people pressed him and the calf came out of the fire; The people run wild and become a derision to their enemies; God strikes the people with plague for idolatry; The prophet asks to be blotted from God's book if the people are not forgiven; The noise of the idolatrous revelry is mistaken for the sound of battle; The tablets are written on both sides by God; The leader calls 'Who is for YHWH? To me!' and a group rallies; Aaron answers Moses' rebuke over the calf [divergence between the texts]; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream [divergence between the texts]; The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast [divergence between the texts]; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; God erases what he wills and confirms, and with him is the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab); and 16 more.

Only in Who maintains the mosques; God above family: Giving water to pilgrims and tending the Sacred Mosque are not equal to faith and striving; God's good pleasure (ridwan) is greater than the gardens of Eden; Levi says to father and mother 'I do not see you' and disregards his brothers and children for God's covenant; Do not take fathers or brothers as allies against faith; love of God must outweigh family, wealth, trade and homes; Only those who believe, pray and give alms may maintain God's places of worship; To obey is better than sacrifice; Entrance liturgy: 'Who may dwell on your holy mountain?' answered by a list of ethical qualifications.

leads.finding: The Levites kill idolaters including their own kin and are consecrated for it

units.title: Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer
Who maintains the mosques; God above family

matches.label: The Levites kill idolaters including their own kin and are consecrated for it
matches.note: Taking God's side against one's own kin: kî ʾîš bibnô ûbᵉʾāḥîw (Levites consecrated for it) vs lā tattakhidhū ābāʾakum wa-ikhwānakum awliyāʾa. Q does not ask for violence against kin, only refusal of their alliance.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה מִלְא֨וּ יֶדְכֶ֤ם הַיּוֹם֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ בִּבְנ֖וֹ וּבְאָחִ֑יו וְלָתֵ֧ת עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם הַיּ֖וֹם בְּרָכָֽה

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَتَّخِذُوٓا۟ ءَابَآءَكُمْ وَإِخْوَٰنَكُمْ أَوْلِيَآءَ إِنِ ٱسْتَحَبُّوا۟ ٱلْكُفْرَ عَلَى ٱلْإِيمَٰنِ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهُم مِّنكُمْ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ

leads.title: Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back ↔ Moses and the servant of God at the meeting of the two seas (Surah 18:60-82)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses travels with his young servant (fata) (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back: God refuses to go among the people lest he consume them on the way; Joshua, the young attendant, never leaves the tent; God tells the prophet: I know you by name and you have found favor; The people strip off their ornaments in mourning or penitence; The people stand at their tent doors and bow as the prophet goes to meet God; A tent of meeting pitched outside the camp where all who seek God go; God's own Presence (face) will go with the people; God declares he will be gracious to whom he will be gracious; Moses asks to see God, his glory or God himself [divergence between the texts]; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy); After the calf the people mourn or repent of what they did [divergence between the texts]; The prophet asks to see God's glory; and 10 more.

Only in Moses and the servant of God at the meeting of the two seas (Surah 18:60-82): A boy is killed lest he burden his believing parents with rebellion; God will give them a better child; The travelers' provision fish comes to life and slips away into the sea at the destined place; A forgetting is blamed on Satan; The sage explains the hidden reasons for his shocking acts; Moses vows to travel until he reaches the meeting of the two seas; A wall shelters a treasure belonging to two orphans until they come of age; Realizing the sign, the travelers retrace their footsteps; The travelers rest at a rock where the sign occurs; The sage kills a boy they meet; The sage repairs a wall about to collapse in the inhospitable town without payment; The sage holes the boat that carries them; A servant of God given mercy and knowledge from God's presence (ilm ladunni); and 6 more.

units.title: Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back

matches.label: Moses travels with his young servant (fata)

matches.label: No human can see God's face and live
matches.note: In the same chapter Exodus itself limits the vision: lōʾ yirʾanî hā-ʾāḏām wā-ḥāy; God covers Moses with his palm (wə-śakkōṯî ḵappî ʿāleḵā) and lets him see only his back (ʾăḥōrāy) while pānay lōʾ yērāʾû. The Quran's 'from behind a veil' (min warāʾi ḥijāb) agrees with this limit, against Exod 33:11 and Num 12:8. cf. b. Yevamot 49b on Moses' clear aspaqlaria.

leads.title: Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back ↔ Splitter of seed and dawn; stars for navigation; do not revile their gods
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: No human can see God's face and live (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back: God refuses to go among the people lest he consume them on the way; Joshua, the young attendant, never leaves the tent; God tells the prophet: I know you by name and you have found favor; The people strip off their ornaments in mourning or penitence; The people stand at their tent doors and bow as the prophet goes to meet God; A tent of meeting pitched outside the camp where all who seek God go; God's own Presence (face) will go with the people; God declares he will be gracious to whom he will be gracious; Moses asks to see God, his glory or God himself [divergence between the texts]; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy); Moses travels with his young servant (fata); After the calf the people mourn or repent of what they did [divergence between the texts]; and 10 more.

Only in Splitter of seed and dawn; stars for navigation; do not revile their gods: Do not revile those they invoke besides God, lest they revile God in ignorance; They made the jinn partners of God, though he created them; Humans have a lodging place and a repository (mustaqarr wa-mustawdaʿ); Opponents say to the Prophet 'you have studied' (darasta); Rain brings forth vegetation: clustered grain, hanging date clusters, vineyards, olives and pomegranates; God is the splitter of the dawn (fāliq al-iṣbāḥ); night for rest; God splits the grain and the date-stone; Vision does not grasp him, but he grasps all vision; Do not revile God or curse a ruler of your people; God has taken neither consort (sahiba) nor child; God made the stars for guidance in the darknesses of land and sea; God brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living; and 5 more.

matches.note: The people's remorse: wa-lammā suqiṭa fī aydīhim ... qālū la-in lam yarḥamnā rabbunā wa-yaghfir lanā vs wayyitʾabbālû wᵉlōʾ šātû ʾîš ʿedyô ʿālāyw. Pair score 32.8.

Only in Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back: God refuses to go among the people lest he consume them on the way; Joshua, the young attendant, never leaves the tent; God tells the prophet: I know you by name and you have found favor; The people strip off their ornaments in mourning or penitence; The people stand at their tent doors and bow as the prophet goes to meet God; A tent of meeting pitched outside the camp where all who seek God go; God's own Presence (face) will go with the people; God declares he will be gracious to whom he will be gracious; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy); Moses travels with his young servant (fata); After the calf the people mourn or repent of what they did [divergence between the texts]; God hides the prophet in a cleft of the rock, covers him with his hand, and lets him see only his back; and 6 more.

Only in Forty nights, the request to see God and the tablets: When God manifests himself to the mountain it is crushed to dust; The prophet falls down unconscious at the theophany and repents on waking; The tablets contain an exhortation and an explanation of all things; The appointed time on the mountain is thirty nights completed with ten more, making forty; Aaron and Hur left in charge while Moses is on the mountain; What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts]; Moses leaves a deputy (Aaron, with or without Hur) with the people while he is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; Moses' set period on the mountain is forty (days and nights, or nights) [divergence between the texts]; A mountain is shattered when God passes by or manifests himself [divergence between the texts]; Seeing God or breaking through to him brings death; A prophet spends forty days and forty nights in a set period; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear; and 2 more.

matches.label: What happens after God refuses to be seen by Moses
matches.note: After the refusal God points Moses to the rock or mountain: wa-lākini nẓur ilā l-jabali fa-ini staqarra makānahu fa-sawfa tarānī vs hinnēh māqôm ʾittî wᵉniṣṣabtā ʿal-haṣṣûr. leads.title: Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back ↔ The call to go forth; the second of two in the cave
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God's own Presence (face) will go with the people (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back: God refuses to go among the people lest he consume them on the way; Joshua, the young attendant, never leaves the tent; God tells the prophet: I know you by name and you have found favor; The people strip off their ornaments in mourning or penitence; The people stand at their tent doors and bow as the prophet goes to meet God; A tent of meeting pitched outside the camp where all who seek God go; God declares he will be gracious to whom he will be gracious; Moses asks to see God, his glory or God himself [divergence between the texts]; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy); Moses travels with his young servant (fata); After the calf the people mourn or repent of what they did [divergence between the texts]; The prophet asks to see God's glory; and 10 more.

Only in The call to go forth; the second of two in the cave: God threatens to destroy a people and put another in its place [divergence between the texts]; Sign: the young woman ('almah) is pregnant and will bear a son and call his name Immanuel ('God with us'); A poem lists the tribes, praising those who fought and shaming those who stayed home; The prophet is 'the second of two' hiding in the cave, telling his companion 'do not grieve, God is with us'; God supports the prophet with hosts (junud) the believers did not see; The oppressed people hide in caves, dens and mountain strongholds; God sends down his sakina (tranquility, cf. shekhinah) on the prophet and believers; If God wills he takes you away and brings another people in your place.

leads.title: New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue ↔ New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How often and when pilgrimage is made [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Three annual pilgrimage festivals when every male appears before God (weight 5.3). Pair score 11.6.

Only in New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue: God promises no one will covet the land while the men go up on pilgrimage; The Sabbath must be kept even in plowing and harvest time; Call to the People of the Book to a common word: worship none but God and take none as lords besides him; What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts]; Israel must tear down the standing stones of the Canaanite gods; A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken; God passes by and proclaims his name and attributes of mercy; A boundary is set round the holy mountain; whoever touches it dies; Whether one person (kin, descendants) bears another's sin [contrast between the texts]; Make no covenant with the inhabitants or their gods, who would be a snare; Do not offer sacrificial blood with leavened bread; fat not left until morning; No one shall appear before God empty-handed; and 20 more.

Only in New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites: When you pour down from Arafat, remember God at the Sacred Monument (al-Mash'ar al-Haram); Take provision, but the best provision is God-consciousness (taqwa); Remember God on the counted days; no sin whether one hastens in two days or delays; Piety is not entering houses from their backs but from their doors; Fight in God's way those who fight you, but do not transgress; Prayer 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the next, and guard us from the fire'; Complete the pilgrimage (hajj) and visitation (umra) for God; Do not fight at the Sacred Mosque unless they fight you there; No sexual talk, wickedness or quarreling during the pilgrimage; Remember God as you remember your fathers, or more; The sacred month for the sacred month; violations are subject to retaliation; Do not shave heads until the sacrificial offering (hady) reaches its place; and 9 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Three annual pilgrimage festivals when every male appears before God (weight 5.3). Pair score 5.3.

Only in New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue: God promises no one will covet the land while the men go up on pilgrimage; The Sabbath must be kept even in plowing and harvest time; Call to the People of the Book to a common word: worship none but God and take none as lords besides him; What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts]; Israel must tear down the standing stones of the Canaanite gods; A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken; God passes by and proclaims his name and attributes of mercy; A boundary is set round the holy mountain; whoever touches it dies; Whether one person (kin, descendants) bears another's sin [contrast between the texts]; Make no covenant with the inhabitants or their gods, who would be a snare; Do not offer sacrificial blood with leavened bread; fat not left until morning; No one shall appear before God empty-handed; and 21 more.

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts]; A place recognized as the house of God and gate of heaven; and 6 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand and incense altar: A cult object is hammered from a single piece of gold; Recipe of the holy anointing oil of myrrh, cinnamon, cane, cassia and olive oil; A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; A small gold-plated altar for burning incense before the veil; A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups; A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God; Two golden cherubim face each other with wings spread over the ark.

Only in Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath): The ark (tabut) returns, carried by angels, containing tranquility (sakina) and relics left by the family of Moses and Aaron; David kills Jalut (Goliath) and is given kingship and wisdom; Were it not for God checking people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted; 'How many a small band has overcome a large one by God's leave'; God chose the king and increased him in knowledge and stature, though he lacked wealth; The people object that the chosen king has no wealth and they have more right to kingship; Before battle the army is tested at a river: whoever drinks is not with the leader, except a handful scooped by hand; The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles [divergence between the texts]; What the ark contains [contrast between the texts]; David kills the Philistine giant [divergence between the texts]; A giant taunts Israel and is killed by a hero; A jar of manna preserved before the testimony for future generations; and 10 more.

matches.note: Exod: wəhinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat kaššāleg, a leprous hand, given so that the people will believe (ləmaʿan yaʾămînû). Q: takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾ, white 'without harm', which denies the disease, and given li-nuriyaka min āyātinā l-kubrā, a sign for Moses himself.

passages.text: וַיַּ֤עַן מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר וְהֵן֙ לֹֽא יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לִ֔י וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְע֖וּ בְּקֹלִ֑י כִּ֣י יֹֽאמְר֔וּ לֹֽא נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה
לְמַ֣עַן יַאֲמִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתָ֑ם אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב
וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ ע֗וֹד הָֽבֵא נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּבֵ֥א יָד֖וֹ בְּחֵיק֑וֹ וַיּ֣וֹצִאָ֔הּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה יָד֖וֹ מְצֹרַ֥עַת כַּשָּֽׁלֶג
وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخْرَىٰ
لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا ٱلْكُبْرَى

matches.label: Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips'
matches.note: Exod: speech trouble is an objection to the call, lōʾ ʾîš dəbārîm ʾānōkî ... kî kəbad-peh ûkəbad lāšôn ʾānōkî ... šəlaḥ-nāʾ bəyad-tišlāḥ, and God rebukes him, mî śām peh lāʾādām. Q: it is a prayer, rabbi shraḥ lī ṣadrī ... wa-ḥlul ʿuqdatan min lisānī yafqahū qawlī, granted at once, qad ūtīta suʾlaka yā Mūsā.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל יְהוָה֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָי֒ לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ דְּבָרִ֜ים אָנֹ֗כִי גַּ֤ם מִתְּמוֹל֙ גַּ֣ם מִשִּׁלְשֹׁ֔ם גַּ֛ם מֵאָ֥ז דַּבֶּרְךָ אֶל עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֧י כְבַד פֶּ֛ה וּכְבַ֥ד לָשׁ֖וֹן אָנֹֽכִי
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו מִ֣י שָׂ֣ם פֶּה֮ לָֽאָדָם֒ א֚וֹ מִֽי יָשׂ֣וּם אִלֵּ֔ם א֣וֹ חֵרֵ֔שׁ א֥וֹ פִקֵּ֖חַ א֣וֹ עִוֵּ֑ר הֲלֹ֥א אָנֹכִ֖י יְהוָֽה
וְעַתָּ֖ה לֵ֑ךְ וְאָנֹכִי֙ אֶֽהְיֶ֣ה עִם פִּ֔יךָ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּדַבֵּֽר
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى
وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى
وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى

matches.label: The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission
matches.note: Who initiates, and the mood. Exod: God imposes Aaron in anger, wayyiḥar-ʾap YHWH bəmōšeh ... hălōʾ ʾahărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wəhāyâ-hûʾ yihyeh-ləkā ləpeh wəʾattâ tihyeh-lô lēʾlōhîm. Q: Moses asks for him, wa-jʿal lī wazīran min ahlī Hārūna akhī ushdud bihi azrī wa-ashrikhu fī amrī, so that they may glorify God much (kay nusabbiḥaka kathīrā). No anger, and no 'as God'.

passages.text: וַיִּֽחַר אַ֨ף יְהוָ֜ה בְּמֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֨יךָ֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי דַבֵּ֥ר יְדַבֵּ֖ר ה֑וּא וְגַ֤ם הִנֵּה הוּא֙ יֹצֵ֣א לִקְרָאתֶ֔ךָ וְרָאֲךָ֖ וְשָׂמַ֥ח בְּלִבּֽוֹ
וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֖ים בְּפִ֑יו וְאָנֹכִ֗י אֶֽהְיֶ֤ה עִם פִּ֨יךָ֙ וְעִם פִּ֔יהוּ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֽׂוּן
וְדִבֶּר ה֥וּא לְךָ֖ אֶל הָעָ֑ם וְהָ֤יָה הוּא֙ יִֽהְיֶה לְּךָ֣ לְפֶ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶה לּ֥וֹ לֵֽאלֹהִֽים
وَٱجْعَل لِّى وَزِيرًا مِّنْ أَهْلِى
هَٰرُونَ أَخِى
ٱشْدُدْ بِهِۦٓ أَزْرِى

matches.label: A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff
matches.note: hašlîkēhû ʾarṣâ ... wayhî lənāḥāš wayyānos mōšeh mippānāyw ... šəlaḥ yādəkā weʾĕḥōz bizənābô; alqihā ... fa-idhā hiya ḥayyatun tasʿā, qāla khudhhā wa-lā takhaf sa-nuʿīduhā sīratahā l-ūlā: thrown down, it becomes a snake; he is told to take it and it turns back. Moses flees in Exod; in Q he is told 'do not fear'.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַשְׁלִיכֵ֣הוּ אַ֔רְצָה וַיַּשְׁלִיכֵ֥הוּ אַ֖רְצָה וַיְהִ֣י לְנָחָ֑שׁ וַיָּ֥נָס מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִפָּנָֽיו
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה שְׁלַח֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ וֶאֱחֹ֖ז בִּזְנָב֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיַּ֣חֲזֶק בּ֔וֹ וַיְהִ֥י לְמַטֶּ֖ה בְּכַפּֽוֹ
قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ
فَأَلْقَىٰهَا فَإِذَا هِىَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعَىٰ
قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Moses and Aaron, Noah, Ad, Thamud, the People of the Rass and the rained-upon town
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron, Noah, Ad, Thamud, the People of the Rass and the rained-upon town: The 'People of the Rass' (aṣḥāb al-rass, the well) named among destroyed peoples; Most unbelievers are like cattle, or even further astray; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; 'Do not go about after your heart and your eyes'; Ox knows its owner and the ass its master's crib, but Israel does not know (animals wiser than God's people); The sign the flood leaves for later generations [divergence between the texts]; The town that was rained on with an evil rain (Lot's) is passed by travelers; Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts]; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; The people mock God's messengers, despise his words and scoff at his prophets; All others perish; and 2 more.

matches.label: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed
matches.note: wa-jaʿalnā maʿahu akhāhu Hārūna wazīran ~ hălōʾ ʾAhărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wə-hāyâ hûʾ yihyeh lləkā lə-feh wə-ʾattâ tihyeh lô lēʾlōhîm: Aaron joins his brother. In Exodus God appoints him in anger (wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše) as Moses' 'mouth', with Moses 'as God' to him; in the Quran he is a helper (wazīr) given with the Book, and the 'as God' relation is absent.

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
leads.summary: 4 correspondences read side by side: 3 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' (weight 5.6); An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4). Pair score 40.5.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; and 12 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 36 more.

matches.label: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed
matches.note: God's answer to Moses' reluctance: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... hălōʾ ʾAhărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wə-ʾattâ tihyeh lô lēʾlōhîm (anger; Aaron as mouth, Moses as God to him) ~ qāla kallā fa-dhhabā bi-āyātinā innā maʿakum mustamiʿūna: no anger and no 'as God'; both are sent as equals (fa-dhhabā, dual).

passages.text: וַיִּֽחַר אַ֨ף יְהוָ֜ה בְּמֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֨יךָ֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי דַבֵּ֥ר יְדַבֵּ֖ר ה֑וּא וְגַ֤ם הִנֵּה הוּא֙ יֹצֵ֣א לִקְרָאתֶ֔ךָ וְרָאֲךָ֖ וְשָׂמַ֥ח בְּלִבּֽוֹ
וְדִבֶּר ה֥וּא לְךָ֖ אֶל הָעָ֑ם וְהָ֤יָה הוּא֙ יִֽהְיֶה לְּךָ֣ לְפֶ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶה לּ֥וֹ לֵֽאלֹהִֽים
وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

matches.label: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death
matches.note: Fear of being killed for the old killing: in Exodus God removes it by fact, kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā; in the Quran Moses raises it himself (wa-lahum ʿalayya dhanbun fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni), and God answers with his presence, 'kallā ... innā maʿakum mustamiʿūn'.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל מֹשֶׁה֙ בְּמִדְיָ֔ן לֵ֖ךְ שֻׁ֣ב מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּי מֵ֨תוּ֙ כָּל הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַֽמְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת נַפְשֶֽׁךָ
وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

matches.label: Moses' hand turned white as a sign
matches.note: wa-nazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāʾu li-n-nāẓirīna ~ wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: the white hand. In Exodus it is leprous (məṣōraʿat), shown to Moses at the bush and meant for the Israelites (4:8-9, 4:30); in the Quran it is simply 'white for the beholders', shown to Pharaoh and his court, with no disease.

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Salih, the rock-hewn houses of Thamud and the she-camel
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: How a people responds to a sign given to prove the messenger [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.

Only in Salih, the rock-hewn houses of Thamud and the she-camel: The people say the prophet is one of the bewitched and a mere human like them, and demand a sign; The prophet Ṣāliḥ is sent to the people of Thamūd; Thamūd hew houses out of the mountains, among gardens, springs and palms with tender spathes; Edom dwells in the clefts of the rock (sela) and thinks no one can bring it down; The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; The unbelievers demand: 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?'; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'.

וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ כִּֽי פָקַ֨ד יְהוָ֜ה אֶת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְכִ֤י רָאָה֙ אֶת עָנְיָ֔ם וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ
مَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُنَا فَأْتِ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6). Pair score 27.9.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; and 14 more.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed; Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts]; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; God addresses the hero with 'Fear not' in a vision; and 2 more.

וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה שְׁלַח֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ וֶאֱחֹ֖ז בִּזְנָב֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיַּ֣חֲזֶק בּ֔וֹ וַיְהִ֥י לְמַטֶּ֖ה בְּכַפּֽוֹ

sides.note: Moses flees from it; seizes it by the tail

passages.text: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

matches.label: The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל מֹשֶׁה֒ בְּלֶכְתְּךָ֙ לָשׁ֣וּב מִצְרַ֔יְמָה רְאֵ֗ה כָּל הַמֹּֽפְתִים֙ אֲשֶׁר שַׂ֣מְתִּי בְיָדֶ֔ךָ וַעֲשִׂיתָ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַאֲנִי֙ אֲחַזֵּ֣ק אֶת לִבּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א יְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת הָעָֽם
فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ
وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

sides.note: they denied them though their souls were convinced

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper
leads.summary: 4 correspondences read side by side: 4 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' (weight 5.6); An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4). Pair score 46.8.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; and 11 more.

Only in The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper: Moses says his brother Aaron is more eloquent of tongue and asks for him as a helper to confirm him; Moses is called from the tree on the right bank of the valley, in the blessed spot; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; Prophet lodges in 'the cave' on Horeb, the mountain of God; Where and how Moses comes to the place of his call [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; A shepherd tending flocks comes to the mountain of God and is called; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed.

matches.label: Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response
matches.note: As at Q 27:10: wa-yyānās Mōše mip-pānāyw ~ wallā mudbiran wa-lam yuʿaqqib; Exodus' command to seize the snake's tail (wə-ʾĕḥōz bi-znāvô) becomes yā Mūsā aqbil wa-lā takhaf innaka mina l-āminīn, 'come forward and do not fear, you are safe'.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַשְׁלִיכֵ֣הוּ אַ֔רְצָה וַיַּשְׁלִיכֵ֥הוּ אַ֖רְצָה וַיְהִ֣י לְנָחָ֑שׁ וַיָּ֥נָס מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִפָּנָֽיו
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה שְׁלַח֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ וֶאֱחֹ֖ז בִּזְנָב֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיַּ֣חֲזֶק בּ֔וֹ וַיְהִ֥י לְמַטֶּ֖ה בְּכַפּֽוֹ
وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقْبِلْ وَلَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْءَامِنِينَ

matches.label: Moses' hand turned white as a sign
matches.note: Two signs, not three, and no leprosy: Exodus gives staff, leprous hand (məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg), and a third sign held in reserve, Nile water turned to blood (wə-hāyû lə-dām bay-yabbāšet), meant for doubting Israelites; the Quran has fa-dhānika burhānāni min rabbika ilā Firʿawna wa-malaʾihi, two proofs aimed at Pharaoh, the hand white 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ), and adds 'draw your arm to your side against fear'.

passages.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ ע֗וֹד הָֽבֵא נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּבֵ֥א יָד֖וֹ בְּחֵיק֑וֹ וַיּ֣וֹצִאָ֔הּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה יָד֖וֹ מְצֹרַ֥עַת כַּשָּֽׁלֶג
וְהָיָה֙ אִם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לָ֔ךְ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וְהֶֽאֱמִ֔ינוּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֥ת הָאַחֲרֽוֹן

וְהָיָ֡ה אִם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֡ינוּ גַּם֩ לִשְׁנֵ֨י הָאֹת֜וֹת הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁמְעוּן֙ לְקֹלֶ֔ךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֙ מִמֵּימֵ֣י הַיְאֹ֔ר וְשָׁפַכְתָּ֖ הַיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וְהָי֤וּ הַמַּ֨יִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּקַּ֣ח מִן הַיְאֹ֔ר וְהָי֥וּ לְדָ֖ם בַּיַּבָּֽשֶׁת

ٱسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهْبِ فَذَٰنِكَ بُرْهَٰنَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

matches.label: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed
matches.note: Aaron's eloquence: in Exodus Moses says he is heavy of mouth, and God, angry, proposes Aaron himself: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... yādaʿtî kî dabbēr yədabbēr hûʾ ... wə-śamtā ʾet had-dəvārîm bə-fîw. In the Quran Moses proposes him, wa-akhī Hārūnu huwa afṣaḥu minnī lisānan fa-arsilhu maʿiya ridʾan yuṣaddiqunī, and God agrees without anger: sa-nashuddu ʿaḍudaka bi-akhīka. Aaron is a supporting witness (ridʾ, yuṣaddiqunī), not a mouth for Moses as God.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל יְהוָה֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָי֒ לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ דְּבָרִ֜ים אָנֹ֗כִי גַּ֤ם מִתְּמוֹל֙ גַּ֣ם מִשִּׁלְשֹׁ֔ם גַּ֛ם מֵאָ֥ז דַּבֶּרְךָ אֶל עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֧י כְבַד פֶּ֛ה וּכְבַ֥ד לָשׁ֖וֹן אָנֹֽכִי
וַיִּֽחַר אַ֨ף יְהוָ֜ה בְּמֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֨יךָ֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי דַבֵּ֥ר יְדַבֵּ֖ר ה֑וּא וְגַ֤ם הִנֵּה הוּא֙ יֹצֵ֣א לִקְרָאתֶ֔ךָ וְרָאֲךָ֖ וְשָׂמַ֥ח בְּלִבּֽוֹ
וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֖ים בְּפִ֑יו וְאָנֹכִ֗י אֶֽהְיֶ֤ה עִם פִּ֨יךָ֙ וְעִם פִּ֔יהוּ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֽׂוּן
وَأَخِى هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّى لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِىَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِىٓ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَٰنًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكُمَا ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ

matches.label: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death
matches.note: rabbi innī qataltu minhum nafsan fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni ~ kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā: the old killing as an obstacle to going back. In Exodus God removes it unasked, in the Quran Moses raises it at the call.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The king breaks his promise to release the people once a plague is lifted [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1). Pair score 11.8.

Only in Plagues 1-3: blood, frogs, lice: The dead frogs are piled in heaps and the land stinks; Egyptians dig around the Nile for drinkable water; Prophet lets the king choose when the plague should end, to prove God's power; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' [divergence between the texts]; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; How the defeated court magicians respond [divergence between the texts]; Prophet confronts the king at the river in the morning; The dust of the earth becomes lice on man and beast; Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts]; Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs; Nile water is turned to blood; and 3 more.

Only in Moses before Pharaoh: the laughing courtiers, the rivers beneath Pharaoh and the drowning: Each sign shown to Pharaoh's people was greater than the one before it; Pharaoh scorns Moses as contemptible, barely able to speak, without gold bracelets or attending angels; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh [divergence between the texts]; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh is the great tannin (crocodile/dragon) lying in the midst of his Nile channels; Pharaoh boasts to his people: is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me?; Who causes Pharaoh's refusal: God hardening his heart, or Pharaoh and his people themselves [divergence between the texts]; The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives [divergence between the texts]; King invests the hero with ring, linen and chariot; The king breaks his promise to release the people once a plague is lifted; Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips'; and 1 more.

matches.note: Pharaoh asks Moses to pray and breaks his word once relieved: wa-yiqrāʾ p̄arʿōh ... haʿtîrû ʾel YHWH wə-yāsēr haṣ-ṣəp̄arḏəʿîm ... wa-ʾăšalləḥâ ʾeṯ hā-ʿām; wa-yarʾ parʿōh kî hāyəṯâ hā-rəwāḥâ wə-haḵbēd ʾeṯ libbô vs. wa-qālū yā ayyuha s-sāḥiru dʿu lanā rabbaka bi-mā ʿahida ʿindaka innanā la-muhtadūn; fa-lammā kashafnā ʿanhumu l-ʿadhāba idhā hum yankuthūn. Changes: the speakers are Pharaoh's people, not Pharaoh alone; they address Moses as 'magician' (sāḥir); 'your Lord' (rabbaka) replaces 'YHWH'; the promise is to be guided (muhtadūn), not to release the people; and the relapse is breaking a pledge (nakth), with no heart-hardening (kibbēḏ lēḇ).

Only in Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues: Pharaoh's people are struck with years of drought and lack of fruits before the plagues; Enemies attribute their misfortune to the prophet as a bad omen (tatayyur); their omen is with God; The magicians' spell bewitches the people's eyes and terrifies them; The magicians offer the prophet to throw first; he tells them to throw; Pharaoh is said to have his own gods, whom Moses would make him abandon; One of the Egyptian plagues is a flood (tufan); The tyrant threatens to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify the converts; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [contrast between the texts]; Rulers fear that a people will leave the land, or drive them out of it [divergence between the texts]; The court magicians ask the king for a reward if they win and are promised closeness; Threatened believers say 'to our Lord we return' and pray for patience and to die as muslims; Pharaoh executes or threatens offenders by hanging, impaling or crucifixion; and 16 more.

matches.label: Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'
matches.note: The magicians' end. Exod: they fail at the lice and say ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm hiwʾ, but stay at court (they are struck by boils at 9:11), and Pharaoh's heart is hardened. Q: wa-ulqiya l-saḥaratu sājidīna qālū āmannā bi-rabbi l-ʿālamīna rabbi Mūsā wa-Hārūna. They convert at the first contest, are threatened with mutilation and crucifixion (la-uqaṭṭiʿanna aydiyakum wa-arjulakum min khilāfin thumma la-uṣallibannakum), and pray to die as muslims (wa-tawaffanā muslimīna). Grudging recognition becomes conversion and martyrdom.

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֱמֹ֣ר אֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֡ן קַ֣ח מַטְּךָ֣ וּנְטֵֽה יָדְךָ֩ עַל מֵימֵ֨י מִצְרַ֜יִם עַֽל נַהֲרֹתָ֣ם עַל יְאֹרֵיהֶ֣ם וְעַל אַגְמֵיהֶ֗ם וְעַ֛ל כָּל מִקְוֵ֥ה מֵימֵיהֶ֖ם וְיִֽהְיוּ דָ֑ם וְהָ֤יָה דָם֙ בְּכָל אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּבָעֵצִ֖ים וּבָאֲבָנִֽים

וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵן֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה וְאַהֲרֹ֜ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה וַיָּ֤רֶם בַּמַּטֶּה֙ וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת הַמַּ֨יִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּיְאֹ֔ר לְעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וּלְעֵינֵ֖י עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיֵּהָֽפְכ֛וּ כָּל הַמַּ֥יִם אֲשֶׁר בַּיְאֹ֖ר לְדָֽם

וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵ֨ן הַחַרְטֻמִּ֧ים בְּלָטֵיהֶ֛ם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶת הַכִּנִּ֖ים וְלֹ֣א יָכֹ֑לוּ וַתְּהִי֙ הַכִּנָּ֔ם בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָֽה

leads.title: Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs ↔ Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes (weight 6.7); Who causes Pharaoh's refusal: God hardening his heart, or Pharaoh and his people themselves (weight 6.3); God sends Moses and Aaron together, with his signs, to Pharaoh (weight 6.0); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6). Pair score 28.7.

Only in Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs: Hero is eighty (and his brother eighty-three) when they confront the king; God makes the prophet 'as God' to the king with his brother as his prophet; Wonders done so that Egypt shall know 'I am YHWH'; Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh turned away with his power/pillar (rukn) and called Moses 'a sorcerer or a madman'; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes [divergence between the texts]; An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents [divergence between the texts]; Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents; An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him; The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people [divergence between the texts]; and 1 more.

Only in Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith: Only some youths (dhurriyya) of Moses' people believed him, fearing Pharaoh; As he drowns Pharaoh declares faith in the God of the Israelites, too late; Pharaoh's body is saved from the sea to be a sign for those after him; Moses prays God to obliterate Pharaoh's wealth and harden their hearts so they do not believe until they see punishment; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; Moses and Aaron are told to make their people's houses in Egypt a qibla (place/direction of prayer); God's instruction about the Israelites' houses in Egypt before the exodus [divergence between the texts]; Threatened believers say 'to our Lord we return' and pray for patience and to die as muslims; Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites; Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows; Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows [divergence between the texts]; How Moses' own people in Egypt respond to his message [divergence between the texts]; and 6 more.

matches.note: The contest with Pharaoh's magicians, with the same verb 'throw' (alqā / hišlîk): qāla lahum mūsā alqū mā antum mulqūn ... inna llāha sa-yubṭiluhu vs wayyašlēk ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭēhû ... wayyaʿăśû gam-hēm ḥarṭummê miṣrayim bᵉlahăṭêhem kēn ... wayyiblaʿ maṭṭēh-ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭōtām. The actors change: in Exod Aaron throws first and his staff swallows theirs; in Q Moses speaks and invites the magicians to throw first, and God voids their magic.

וַיִּקְרָא֙ גַּם פַּרְעֹ֔ה לַֽחֲכָמִ֖ים וְלַֽמְכַשְּׁפִ֑ים וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֨וּ גַם הֵ֜ם חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֛יִם בְּלַהֲטֵיהֶ֖ם כֵּֽן

matches.label: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest
matches.note: Exod 7:11 wa-yyiqrāʾ gam Parʿōh la-ḥăkhāmîm wə-la-mkhaššəfîm, Pharaoh simply summons them and they repeat the sign with their secret arts (bə-lahăṭêhem). evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6). Pair score 21.1.

Only in Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs: Hero is eighty (and his brother eighty-three) when they confront the king; God makes the prophet 'as God' to the king with his brother as his prophet; Wonders done so that Egypt shall know 'I am YHWH'; Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh turned away with his power/pillar (rukn) and called Moses 'a sorcerer or a madman'; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes [divergence between the texts]; An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents [divergence between the texts]; Who causes Pharaoh's refusal: God hardening his heart, or Pharaoh and his people themselves; God sends Moses and Aaron together, with his signs, to Pharaoh; The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents; and 2 more.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed; Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts]; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; and 3 more.

matches.label: The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents
matches.note: Who throws the staff, and how. Exod: Aaron throws (wa-yyašlēkh ʾAhărōn ʾet-maṭṭēhû ... wa-yhî lə-tannîn); the magicians do the same (bə-lahăṭêhem kēn); and maṭṭēh-ʾAhărōn swallows their staffs (wa-yyivlaʿ). Q: Moses throws (fa-alqā ʿaṣāhu fa-idhā hiya thuʿbānun mubīnun); the magicians offer him the first throw (immā an tulqiya); their act is siḥr that 'bewitched the people's eyes' (saḥarū aʿyuna l-nāsi), and Moses' staff talqafu mā yaʾfikūna. Aaron drops out of the act; the magic is illusion.

leads.title: Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory ↔ Ha-Mim: the Forgiver; the throne-bearers pray for the believers
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The beings that carry God's throne, and what they do [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory: The heavenly creatures move straight ahead in every direction without turning; The heavenly creatures have straight legs with calves' hooves and human hands under their wings; A firmament gleaming like awesome ice/crystal is spread above the creatures' heads; A vision dated 'in the thirtieth year' without stated era; Fire like torches moves among the creatures and lightning flashes from it; Each heavenly creature has four faces: human, lion, ox and eagle; The center of the fire gleams like hashmal (amber/electrum); The heavens are opened and the prophet sees visions of God; The visionary hedges every description: 'the appearance of the likeness of...'; On the throne is 'a likeness as the appearance of a man'; The prophet is himself a priest or of priestly family; The radiance around the enthroned figure is like the rainbow in the cloud; and 13 more.

Only in Ha-Mim: the Forgiver; the throne-bearers pray for the believers: The damned say 'Lord, you caused us to die twice and gave us life twice; we confess our sins; is there a way out?'; The Day of the Approaching (al-azifa) when hearts reach the throats, choking; God as Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty (string of divine epithets); God casts the Spirit (al-ruh) of his command upon whom he wills of his servants to warn of the Day of Meeting; God knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal; In terror eyes swerve and hearts reach the throats; The angels who bear the Throne and those around it glorify God and ask forgiveness for the believers, praying they and their righteous kin enter Eden; Humans were dead, given life, will die and be given life again (two deaths, two lives); On the Day God asks 'Whose is the kingdom today?' and answers 'God's, the One, the Overpowering'; Formula: 'gracious and merciful, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love, relenting of evil'; Travel in the land and see the end of those who denied; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.
