leads.title: Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory ↔ Al-Najm: the star that sets, the mighty one on the horizon two bow-lengths away, and the Lote-Tree of the Boundary
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory: The heavenly creatures move straight ahead in every direction without turning; The heavenly creatures have straight legs with calves' hooves and human hands under their wings; A firmament gleaming like awesome ice/crystal is spread above the creatures' heads; A vision dated 'in the thirtieth year' without stated era; Fire like torches moves among the creatures and lightning flashes from it; Each heavenly creature has four faces: human, lion, ox and eagle; The center of the fire gleams like hashmal (amber/electrum); The heavens are opened and the prophet sees visions of God; The visionary hedges every description: 'the appearance of the likeness of...'; On the throne is 'a likeness as the appearance of a man'; The prophet is himself a priest or of priestly family; The radiance around the enthroned figure is like the rainbow in the cloud; and 14 more.

Only in Al-Najm: the star that sets, the mighty one on the horizon two bow-lengths away, and the Lote-Tree of the Boundary: The heart did not falsify what it saw; the gaze did not swerve nor transgress; When there covered the Lote-Tree that which covered it (an ineffable phenomenon); Oath 'By the star when it sets/falls (idha hawa)'; He saw him at a second descent by the Lote-Tree of the Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha), near the Garden of Refuge; The heavenly figure came within two bow-lengths or nearer (qaba qawsayn aw adna) and revealed to his servant; Leaders see God with a sapphire-like pavement under his feet; One mighty in power (shadid al-quwa) taught him, stood poised on the highest horizon, then drew near and descended; Your companion has not erred; he does not speak from desire; it is only revelation revealed; Whether a prophet speaks from his own heart or desire, or by revelation [contrast between the texts]; What or whom the visionaries saw: God himself or his messenger [divergence between the texts]; No human can see God's face and live; A tree whose fruit gives eternal life.

matches.label: He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord
matches.note: A prophet's vision of the divine described with deliberate distance. Ezekiel: dəmûṯ kə-marʾēh ʾāḏām ... kə-marʾēh haq-qešeṯ ʾăšer yihyeh ḇe-ʿānān ... hûʾ marʾēh dəmûṯ kəḇôḏ YHWH wā-ʾerʾeh wā-ʾeppōl ʿal pānāy (the likeness of the appearance of the glory, framed by a bow in the cloud). Quran: fa-kāna qāba qawsayni aw adnā ... mā kadhaba l-fuʾādu mā raʾā ... la-qad raʾā min āyāti rabbihi l-kubrā. Bow (qešeṯ / qaws, cognate) and seeing in both; Ezekiel falls on his face, while the Prophet's 'sight did not swerve' (mā zāgha l-baṣaru). The bow link is a lead only: the Quran's 'two bow-lengths' is a measure of distance.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory: The heavenly creatures move straight ahead in every direction without turning; The heavenly creatures have straight legs with calves' hooves and human hands under their wings; A firmament gleaming like awesome ice/crystal is spread above the creatures' heads; A vision dated 'in the thirtieth year' without stated era; Fire like torches moves among the creatures and lightning flashes from it; Each heavenly creature has four faces: human, lion, ox and eagle; The center of the fire gleams like hashmal (amber/electrum); The heavens are opened and the prophet sees visions of God; The visionary hedges every description: 'the appearance of the likeness of...'; On the throne is 'a likeness as the appearance of a man'; The prophet is himself a priest or of priestly family; The radiance around the enthroned figure is like the rainbow in the cloud; and 13 more.

Only in Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne: 'Ad were destroyed by a furious wind for seven nights and eight days, lying felled like hollow palm trunks; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears; That day eight (angels) bear the Throne of your Lord above them; At a single blast on the trumpet, the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing; Thamud were destroyed by the Overwhelming (al-tagiya, the Blast); Rhetorical opening: 'The Reality (al-haqqa)! What is the Reality? And what will make you know what the Reality is?'; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; The overturned city (al-mu'tafika, Sodom) God hurled down and covered with what covered it; A roaring cold wind (sarsar) on a day of continuous ill omen plucks men away like trunks of uprooted palms; The sky splits and is frail that day, and the angels are on its borders; When the Event (al-waqi'a) befalls, none can deny it: it abases and exalts; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed; and 3 more.

leads.title: Coals from between the cherubim; the wheels full of eyes; the glory leaves the temple ↔ The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The form, faces and number of wings of heavenly beings [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Each cherub or living creature has four faces (human, lion, ox/cherub, eagle), four wings and human hands under the wings (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in Coals from between the cherubim; the wheels full of eyes; the glory leaves the temple: Burning coals are taken from between the cherubim / wheels and scattered over the city; Above the firmament over the living creatures appears something like sapphire in the likeness of a throne; The sound of the cherubim's wings is heard like the voice of El Shaddai when he speaks; The wheels are called by the name 'galgal' ('whirl') in the prophet's hearing; The bodies, backs, hands, wings and wheels of the throne-creatures are full of eyes all around; A heavenly man clothed in linen with a scribe's writing kit at his waist; The spirit of the living creature is in the wheels, which move with them; Wheels gleaming like beryl, constructed as a wheel within a wheel, beside each creature; The divine glory leaves the temple in stages: from the cherub to the threshold, to the east gate, to the mountain east of the city; The glory of YHWH appears in the cloud; God addressed as enthroned (yoshev) on the cherubim.

Only in The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas: God made the angels messengers with wings in twos, threes and fours, adding to creation what he wills; To God ascends the good word, and righteous deeds raise it up; Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy; he calls his party to the blaze; The false gods do not own even the thin skin of a date-stone (qitmir); they cannot hear prayer and will disown it at the Resurrection; What God opens no one can shut, and what he withholds no one can release; What happens where fresh and salt water meet [divergence between the texts]; If God willed he could remove you and bring a new creation; God began man's creation from clay, then made his progeny from an extract of a despised fluid, then shaped him and breathed of his spirit; No one is granted long life or has his life shortened except it is in a Book; The life of this world is only amusement and play (lahw wa-la'ib); the abode of the hereafter is the true life; Sun and moon are subjected, each running to an appointed term; God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them; and 5 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Catalogue of bridal finery: embroidered cloth, tahash sandals, linen, silk, bracelets, necklace, nose-ring, earrings and a crown (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Jerusalem the exposed foundling, God's bride and the faithless harlot: An assembly stones the adulteress and hacks her with swords and burns her houses before many women; God gathers the adulteress's lovers, strips her naked before them and hands her over to be judged; The adorned bride trusts in her beauty and plays the harlot with every passer-by; Bride given a gold nose-ring and bracelets; King makes his son 'pass through the fire' after the abominations of the nations; Sons and daughters born to God are slaughtered and offered to idols as food; A newborn girl is cast into the open field unwashed, unsalted and unswaddled, with her navel cord uncut, loathed on the day of her birth; God spreads his garment-wing over the grown foundling, swears a covenant and takes the city as his wife, bathing, anointing, clothing and adorning her; Unlike other harlots, the city pays fees to her lovers instead of receiving them; Worship of other gods described as 'whoring after' them; God passes by the infant wallowing in her blood and says twice 'In your blood, live!'; Jerusalem's origin is Canaanite: 'your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite'; The unfaithful wife makes male images (tsalmei zakhar) from the gold and silver God gave her and fornicates with them; Political alliances with Egypt, Assyria and Chaldea pictured as harlotry with lovers ('big of flesh'); Man asked to spread his garment-wing over a woman as a sign of marriage.

Only in Entering houses, lowering the gaze, head-coverings, marriage and manumission: Do not enter others' houses until you have asked leave and greeted the household; if told to go back, go back; A father must not make his daughter a prostitute; Women should not strike their feet to make known their hidden ornaments (anklets); Freed slave must not be sent away empty-handed but furnished from flock, threshing floor and winepress; Believing men and women are told to lower their gaze and guard their private parts; Grant slaves who ask a written manumission contract (kitāba) and give them of God's wealth; Marry off the unmarried among you and your righteous slaves; God will enrich the poor; Believing women draw their head-coverings (khumur) over their bosoms and do not show adornment except to listed kin.

Only in The heirs of the Book, the Gardens of Eden and the cries of the damned: God made humans successors (khala'if) on the earth; Heirs of the Book are of three kinds: one who wrongs himself, one who is moderate, and one foremost in good deeds; The guilty, heads bowed before their Lord, beg to be returned to do good; God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; if they ceased, no one else could hold them; If God took people to task for what they earned he would not leave a creature on the earth's back, but he defers them to a set term; Paradise is the abode of permanence where no toil or weariness touches the blessed and grief is removed; The evil plot encompasses only its own authors; In hell the damned neither die nor live; The way (sunna) of God with those who passed before: you will find no change in God's way; Challenge to idolaters: show me what those besides God have created; Travel in the land and see the end of those who denied.

leads.title: Like mother like daughter; Sodom and Samaria her sisters; the everlasting covenant ↔ Lot and the destruction of his town
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The sin of Sodom was pride, surfeit of bread and careless ease, not strengthening the hand of the poor and needy (weight 6.3); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 5.2). Pair score 11.5.

Only in Like mother like daughter; Sodom and Samaria her sisters; the everlasting covenant: When God atones for her she will remember, be ashamed and never again open her mouth; Proverb 'like mother, like daughter'; God will restore the fortunes of Sodom and Samaria along with Jerusalem; Samaria (elder, on the left/north) and Sodom (younger, on the right/south) are Jerusalem's sisters, and she is worse than both; Jerusalem's origin is Canaanite: 'your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite'; God promises an everlasting covenant (berit olam) with his people; God swears 'As I live'.

Only in Lot and the destruction of his town: The host is troubled and helpless on account of the angelic guests, fearing for them; Lot's people approach men, cut off the road (highway robbery) and commit abominations in their assembly (nadi); Abraham's plea when told that the city of Lot will be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; How Lot receives the divine messengers [divergence between the texts]; God's messengers announce that they are sent to destroy the city; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom; A land will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, never inhabited; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10); The fate of Lot's wife; God appears as three men who visit the patriarch; Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'; and 1 more.

וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם מַדֻּ֛עַ לֹא נָשָׂ֥א הַבֵּ֖ן בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֑ב וְהַבֵּ֞ן מִשְׁפָּ֧ט וּצְדָקָ֣ה עָשָׂ֗ה אֵ֣ת כָּל חֻקּוֹתַ֥י שָׁמַ֛ר וַיַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם חָיֹ֥ה יִחְיֶֽה
הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא יִשָּׂ֣א בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב וְאָב֙ לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הַבֵּ֔ן צִדְקַ֤ת הַצַּדִּיק֙ עָלָ֣יו תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְרִשְׁעַ֥ת רשע הָרָשָׁ֖ע עָלָ֥יו תִּֽהְיֶֽה

قُلْ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبْغِى رَبًّا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُم مَّرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ

sides.note: Deut: lōʾ-yûmətû ʾāvôt ʿal-bānîm û-vānîm lōʾ-yûmətû ʿal-ʾāvôt ʾîš bə-ḥeṭʾô yûmātû, a court rule. Q applies it to the final reckoning: lā taziru wāziratun wizra ukhrā thumma ilā rabbikum marjiʿukum.

leads.title: Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance ↔ The primordial covenant ("Am I not your Lord?")
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: No one may excuse himself on judgment day because his ancestors associated partners (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance: Exhortation: cast away your transgressions and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; why will you die?; Test case of three generations: righteous father, violent son, and a grandson who sees his father's sins and does not imitate them; Whether one person can carry another's sin [divergence between the texts]; If the wicked turns from his sins, none of his transgressions will be remembered; if the righteous turns away, his righteousness is forgotten; Catalogue of the righteous man: no eating on the mountains, no idols, no adultery, no menstrual intercourse, no oppression, returns pledges, feeds the hungry, clothes the naked, no interest; Proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children's teeth are set on edge', abolished by God; Whether repentance has a time limit [divergence between the texts]; People complain 'the way of the Lord is not fair'; God answers that it is their ways that are unfair; God does not desire the death of the wicked but that he turn from his way and live; A cloak taken in pledge must be returned before sunset; 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; and 4 more.

Only in The primordial covenant ("Am I not your Lord?"): God takes all Adam's descendants from their loins and makes them testify 'Am I not your Lord?' ('Yes'); Covenant made with those present and with those not here today; Covenant made with those present and with those not here today [divergence between the texts]; The covenant is made with those alive today, not only with the fathers; The people are made witnesses against themselves to their choice; Unbelievers defend their practice as what they found their fathers doing.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Catalogue of the righteous man: no eating on the mountains, no idols, no adultery, no menstrual intercourse, no oppression, returns pledges, feeds the hungry, clothes the naked, no interest (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance: Exhortation: cast away your transgressions and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; why will you die?; Test case of three generations: righteous father, violent son, and a grandson who sees his father's sins and does not imitate them; Whether one person can carry another's sin [divergence between the texts]; No one may excuse himself on judgment day because his ancestors associated partners; If the wicked turns from his sins, none of his transgressions will be remembered; if the righteous turns away, his righteousness is forgotten; Proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children's teeth are set on edge', abolished by God; Whether repentance has a time limit [divergence between the texts]; People complain 'the way of the Lord is not fair'; God answers that it is their ways that are unfair; God does not desire the death of the wicked but that he turn from his way and live; A cloak taken in pledge must be returned before sunset; 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; and 4 more.

leads.title: Ezekiel's commission as 'son of man' to the rebellious house; he eats the scroll sweet as honey ↔ Ezekiel appointed watchman; bound and struck dumb in his house
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Israel called 'a rebellious house' (beit meri) (weight 6.7); A spirit enters the prophet and sets him on his feet (weight 6.7); The prophet sees 'the likeness of the glory of YHWH' as radiant fire enthroned (weight 6.3); The prophet must speak 'whether they hear or refuse' (weight 6.3); 'The hand of YHWH was upon' the prophet, bringing a vision or transport (weight 6.3). Pair score 32.2.

Only in Ezekiel's commission as 'son of man' to the rebellious house; he eats the scroll sweet as honey: Heavenly voice cries 'Blessed be the glory of YHWH from his place'; God makes the prophet's forehead as hard as diamond against a hard-faced people; Foreign peoples of strange speech would heed the prophet, but Israel will not; A hand is stretched out to the prophet holding a scroll; The prophet is made to eat a heavenly scroll; God addresses the prophet as 'son of man' (ben adam); The prophet lives among briers, thorns and scorpions, yet must not fear; The spirit lifts and carries the prophet away; After his vision the prophet sits stunned among the people for seven days; A great rushing sound of the creatures' wings and the wheels behind the prophet; The eaten scroll tastes sweet as honey in the prophet's mouth; A scroll written on front and back with laments, mourning and woe; and 5 more.

Only in Ezekiel appointed watchman; bound and struck dumb in his house: The glory seen by the river appears again to the prophet in a valley/plain; The prophet is told to shut himself in his house; If the watchman fails to warn the wicked, God requires their blood from him; Muteness imposed as a sign [divergence between the texts]; A righteous man who turns to iniquity dies and his former righteousness is not remembered; God appoints the prophet as a watchman (tsofeh) for the house of Israel; God makes the prophet's tongue cleave to his palate so he is mute except when God speaks; The prophet is sent as witness, bearer of good tidings and warner; The prophet falls on his face at the sight of the divine glory; Each person dies for his own sin.

leads.title: The city of blood; the dross in the furnace; no man in the breach ↔ Inheriting women, the dowry, and the forbidden degrees
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: List of forbidden close-kin unions ('uncovering nakedness') (weight 6.0); A man must not take his father's wife (uncover his father's skirt) (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.0.

Only in The city of blood; the dross in the furnace; no man in the breach: Catalogue of social, sexual and cultic sins in the city: contempt of parents, oppression of stranger, orphan and widow, slander, incest, bribery, interest; Israel has become dross: copper, tin, iron and lead in the furnace, gathered into Jerusalem to be melted by God's wrath; The land is not cleansed and not rained upon on the day of indignation; Princes are wolves tearing prey and prophets a roaring lion devouring souls; God seeks a man to build up the wall and stand in the breach before him for the land, and finds none; Priests do violence to the torah and fail to distinguish holy from profane and clean from unclean, hiding their eyes from the sabbaths; Jerusalem indicted as 'the city of bloodshed' (ir ha-damim) with a catalogue of its crimes; False prophets daub a flimsy wall with whitewash (tafel); God's storm, flood-rain and hailstones bring it down; Remove the dross from silver and a vessel comes out for the smith; remove the wicked and the throne is established; Prophet told to clap his hands, stamp his foot and cry 'Ah!' as a gesture of doom; Lending at interest or increase to a poor brother is forbidden; God executes justice for orphan and widow and loves the stranger.

Only in Inheriting women, the dowry, and the forbidden degrees: A husband exchanging one wife for another may not take back anything he gave, even a qinṭār; God wishes to lighten your burden, for the human was created weak; It is forbidden to inherit women against their will or to hold them back to recover gifts; One who cannot afford a free wife may marry a believing slave woman with her people's leave; Foster mothers and foster sisters by nursing are forbidden in marriage; A married slave woman who commits indecency receives half the punishment of a free woman; Man who lies with a slave woman designated to another man: inquiry and guilt offering, not death, because she is not free; The husband gives the bride her marriage gift (ṣaduqa, ajr) as her own; she may freely remit part; List of forbidden close-kin unions ('uncovering nakedness') [divergence between the texts]; Married women are forbidden except those one's right hand possesses (captives); Marrying two sisters [divergence between the texts]; A man may not marry his wife's sister as a rival while the wife lives; and 3 more.

leads.title: Gog of Magog invades the land dwelling at the navel of the earth ↔ The quake of the Hour and the proofs from embryo and rain
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: On that day a great earthquake shakes the land; fish, birds, beasts, creeping things and all humans quake before God, mountains are thrown down and every wall falls (weight 5.3). Pair score 5.3.

Only in Gog of Magog invades the land dwelling at the navel of the earth: The invader plots to attack a quiet people dwelling securely in unwalled villages without bars or gates, to seize plunder; Gog's coalition: Persia, Cush, Put, Gomer with all its hordes, Beth-togarmah from the far north, many peoples; God asks 'Are you the one of whom I spoke in former days through my servants the prophets?'; God turns the invader around and puts hooks in his jaws to drag him out with all his army; The invading host comes up like a storm, like a cloud covering the land; Every man's sword is turned against his brother in the enemy host; Gog is summoned 'after many days', 'in the latter years / end of days', against a land restored from the sword; Restored Israel dwells 'on the navel of the earth' (tabbur ha-arets); God judges Gog with pestilence, blood, torrential rain, hailstones, fire and sulfur; Sheba, Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish ask the invader 'Have you come to take plunder?'; Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince (nesi rosh) of Meshech and Tubal, an eschatological invader [divergence between the texts]; The final invader comes from the farthest recesses of the north (yarketei tsafon); and 10 more.

Only in The quake of the Hour and the proofs from embryo and rain: Some are returned to the most abject age so that after knowing they know nothing; The quake of the Hour: every nursing mother forgets her suckling, every pregnant one miscarries, people seem drunk though not drunk; Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped; God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews; Your dead shall live, their corpses rise; dwellers in the dust shall awake and sing; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

leads.title: Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds ↔ The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: After the first punishment God restores Israel's turn with wealth and sons (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds: God strikes the bow from the invader's left hand and makes the arrows drop from his right hand; The nations will know that Israel went into exile for its own iniquity because God hid his face, not because he was weak; The carrion-eaters are sated at God's table with horses, charioteers, warriors and all men of war; God sends fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands; God will no longer hide his face from Israel, for he has poured out his spirit on the house of Israel; Israel plunders those who plundered them and despoils those who despoiled them; God invites every bird and beast to his great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel to eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of princes, as of rams, lambs, goats and Bashan bulls, till drunk with blood; All Israel buries the dead for seven months to purify the land; appointed men search the land and mark every human bone with a sign (tsiyyun) for the buriers; Gog and his horde are buried in the Valley of the Travelers east of the sea, renamed Valley of Hamon-Gog; a city is named Hamonah; Israel's townsfolk burn the enemy weapons (shields, bows, arrows, clubs, spears) as fuel for seven years, cutting no wood from the forest; Strong bulls of Bashan encircle the sufferer; Slain enemies become a portion for jackals or food for beasts and birds; and 7 more.

Only in The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8): Israel addressed as descendants of those carried with Noah, who was a grateful servant; Divine warning 'if you return (to sin), we will return (to punishment)'; It is decreed in the Book that Israel will work corruption on earth twice; God takes his servant on a journey to show him some of his signs; God sends against Israel servants of his of great might who range through their homes; God carried his servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque; The enemy enters the sanctuary (masjid) a second time as the first and destroys all; Enemies roar in the sanctuary, hack its carved work with axes and burn it to the ground [divergence between the texts]; God gave Moses the Book as guidance for the Children of Israel; Enemies roar in the sanctuary, hack its carved work with axes and burn it to the ground.

Only in The glory of God returns to the temple: God's voice (or the sound of his coming) is like the sound of many waters; The divine glory returns to the temple from the east through the east gate; Kings' corpses or memorials (pigre malkehem) beside the temple defile God's holy name; The temple stands on the top of a (very high) mountain whose whole territory is most holy; The temple is called the place of God's throne and the soles of his feet, where he will dwell forever; The prophet is to describe the temple's plan so that Israel will be ashamed of its sins; Fear that the spirit of YHWH will carry the prophet off to an unknown place; The cloud and glory fill the sanctuary so that even the leader cannot enter; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain; The prophet falls on his face at the sight of the divine glory.

Only in Do not despair of mercy; the earth in God's grip; the throngs to hell and Garden: The angels are seen surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praise of their Lord; The blessed praise God who gave them the land (ard) as inheritance to settle in the Garden where they will; The Book (record) is laid down, the prophets and witnesses are brought, and judgment is passed with truth; Unbelievers are driven to hell in throngs (zumar) and the godfearing to the Garden in throngs; the gates open and the keepers address each; The keepers of the Garden greet the righteous 'Peace be upon you, you have been good; enter'; Lest a soul say 'Alas for my neglect of God' or 'If only I had another chance (karra)'; If you associate partners with God your deeds will come to nothing; At the first trumpet blast all in heaven and earth swoon (sa'iqa) except whom God wills; at the second they stand looking; On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth is in God's grip and the heavens folded in his right hand; Who holds the keys that open and shut [divergence between the texts]; The keepers of hell ask 'Did not messengers from among you come to you?'; To God belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth; and 5 more.

leads.title: The shut east gate, foreigners excluded, Levites and Zadokite priests ↔ Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter the sanctuary (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The shut east gate, foreigners excluded, Levites and Zadokite priests: The east gate stays shut forever because YHWH the God of Israel entered by it; The first of the dough (reshit arisot) is given to the priest so that blessing rests on the house; Levites who went astray after idols are demoted to gatekeepers and slaughterers, barred from priestly service; Priests stand as judges in disputes, judging by God's ordinances; Priests may neither shave their heads nor let their hair grow long, but must trim it; Priests serve in linen only, with no wool, and must not gird themselves with anything that causes sweat; Only the prince (nasi) may sit in the shut gate to eat bread before YHWH; Priestly tribe receives no land: 'I am your portion and inheritance'; Priest may defile himself only for close kin; Priests may not marry a harlot or divorcee; the high priest only a virgin of his people; Priests must take off their holy garments in special chambers before going out to the people, lest the garments transmit holiness; Priests must distinguish holy from profane and clean from unclean and teach the people; and 5 more.

Only in Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya: People of the Book who do not follow the true religion are fought until they pay the jizya, subdued; Polytheists are impure (najas) and may not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year; Gatekeepers stationed so that no one unclean enters the temple; Those counted impure are kept out of the sanctuary [divergence between the texts]; A large army must not claim the victory for itself [divergence between the texts]; City accepting peace becomes forced labor; one resisting has its males killed; The believers' pride in their great numbers avails nothing and the earth grows narrow for them (Hunayn); God supports the prophet with hosts (junud) the believers did not see; God reinforces the believers in battle with a thousand (or more) angels; God sends down his sakina (tranquility, cf. shekhinah) on the prophet and believers.

Only in The six executioners and the man in linen who marks the foreheads: The angelic agent returns and reports 'I have done as you commanded me'; Divine slaughter is to begin at God's sanctuary, with the elders before the temple; Six men (angelic executioners), each with a weapon of destruction, come from the north gate to slay the city; The destroyer (mashhit) passes over houses marked with blood; The reminder is in honored, exalted, purified scrolls in the hands of noble, righteous scribes (safara); A heavenly man clothed in linen with a scribe's writing kit at his waist; A mark on the faces or foreheads of the faithful [divergence between the texts]; Prophet falls on his face crying 'Ah Lord, will you destroy the whole remnant of Israel?'; The divine glory leaves the temple in stages: from the cherub to the threshold, to the east gate, to the mountain east of the city; Sinners say 'YHWH does not see us; YHWH has forsaken the land'.

Only in Covenant to send away foreign wives; assembly in the rain; list of offenders: The assembly sits trembling in the open square in the winter rains; Mixed marriages have already produced children, who are included in the dismissal; Community covenants to send away all foreign wives and their children; Named individuals are recorded as opposing the assembly's decision; Leader neither eats bread nor drinks water in mourning for the people's sin; Sons of the high priest are among those who married foreign wives; Named list of men who had married foreign wives; Leader makes the priests, Levites and all Israel swear to carry out the reform; Whoever fails to attend loses his property (herem) and is separated from the congregation; Leader prays and confesses weeping, prostrate before the house of God; 'There is still hope for Israel concerning this'; A tribunal of family heads examines each case at appointed times; and 1 more.

passages.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה נִֽכְרָת בְּרִ֣ית לֵ֠אלֹהֵינוּ לְהוֹצִ֨יא כָל נָשִׁ֜ים וְהַנּוֹלָ֤ד מֵהֶם֙ בַּעֲצַ֣ת אֲדֹנָ֔י וְהַחֲרֵדִ֖ים בְּמִצְוַ֣ת אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְכַתּוֹרָ֖ה יֵעָשֶֽׂה
וְעַתָּ֗ה תְּנ֥וּ תוֹדָ֛ה לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ רְצוֹנ֑וֹ וְהִבָּֽדְלוּ֙ מֵעַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמִן הַנָּשִׁ֖ים הַנָּכְרִיּֽוֹת

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتُ مُهَٰجِرَٰتٍ فَٱمْتَحِنُوهُنَّ ٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَٰنِهِنَّ فَإِنْ عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤْمِنَٰتٍ فَلَا تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى ٱلْكُفَّارِ لَا هُنَّ حِلٌّ لَّهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّ وَءَاتُوهُم مَّآ أَنفَقُوا۟ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ أَن تَنكِحُوهُنَّ إِذَآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ وَلَا تُمْسِكُوا۟ بِعِصَمِ ٱلْكَوَافِرِ وَسْـَٔلُوا۟ مَآ أَنفَقْتُمْ وَلْيَسْـَٔلُوا۟ مَآ أَنفَقُوا۟ ذَٰلِكُمْ حُكْمُ ٱللَّهِ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ
وَإِن فَاتَكُمْ شَىْءٌ مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُمْ إِلَى ٱلْكُفَّارِ فَعَاقَبْتُمْ فَـَٔاتُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ذَهَبَتْ أَزْوَٰجُهُم مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنفَقُوا۟ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنتُم بِهِۦ مُؤْمِنُونَ

leads.summary: 16 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A Mordecai appears among the leaders of the first return (weight 6.7); Twelve leaders head the return from exile (weight 6.7); Male and female singers among the household servants (weight 6.7); A family of temple servants is called 'sons of Sisera' (weight 6.7); The temple singers are the sons of Asaph (weight 6.7); Hereditary families of temple gatekeepers listed (weight 6.7); Families of 'the sons of Solomon's servants' among the returnees (weight 6.7); Those who cannot prove their descent are excluded from the priesthood as impure (weight 6.7); A written genealogical register is sought or found to verify descent (weight 6.7); A priestly family is named after the wife's father's house (weight 6.7); A ruling is deferred 'until a priest arises with Urim and Thummim' (weight 6.7); Priestly clans listed with their numbers (weight 6.3); Gifts of gold darics (darkemonim/adarkonim), silver minas and priestly tunics for the temple (weight 6.3); Stated census total disagrees with the sum of the listed subtotals (weight 6.3); Returnees listed by ancestral clan or by town with a number for each (weight 6.3); The netinim ('given ones'), temple servants of foreign origin, listed with priests and Levites (weight 6.0). Pair score 104.7.
Only in List of the returnees with Zerubbabel: Returnees' horses, mules, camels and donkeys are counted.

Only in Gates guarded; underpopulated city; the genealogical register of the first returnees found: City gates not to be opened until the sun is hot; A parallel list lacks the horses and mules counted in its source; The city is wide and large but the people few and houses unbuilt; An official is appointed because he is a faithful man who fears God more than many; A list repeated elsewhere with differing figures.

passages.text: (2:59) וְאֵ֗לֶּה הָֽעֹלִים֙ מִתֵּ֥ל מֶ֨לַח֙ תֵּ֣ל חַרְשָׁ֔א כְּר֥וּב אַדָּ֖ן אִמֵּ֑ר וְלֹ֣א יָֽכְל֗וּ לְהַגִּ֤יד בֵּית אֲבוֹתָם֙ וְזַרְעָ֔ם אִ֥ם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵֽם (2:60) בְּנֵי דְלָיָ֥ה בְנֵי טוֹבִיָּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י נְקוֹדָ֑א שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם (2:61) וּמִבְּנֵי֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים בְּנֵ֥י חֳבַיָּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י הַקּ֑וֹץ בְּנֵ֣י בַרְזִלַּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָ֠קַח מִבְּנ֞וֹת בַּרְזִלַּ֤י הַגִּלְעָדִי֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה וַיִּקָּרֵ֖א עַל שְׁמָֽם (2:62) אֵ֗לֶּה בִּקְשׁ֧וּ כְתָבָ֛ם הַמִּתְיַחְשִׂ֖ים וְלֹ֣א נִמְצָ֑אוּ וַֽיְגֹאֲל֖וּ מִן הַכְּהֻנָּֽה

sides.note: from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan, Immer

passages.text: (7:61) וְאֵ֗לֶּה הָֽעוֹלִים֙ מִתֵּ֥ל מֶ֨לַח֙ תֵּ֣ל חַרְשָׁ֔א כְּר֥וּב אַדּ֖וֹן וְאִמֵּ֑ר וְלֹ֣א יָכְל֗וּ לְהַגִּ֤יד בֵּית אֲבוֹתָם֙ וְזַרְעָ֔ם אִ֥ם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵֽם (7:62) בְּנֵי דְלָיָ֥ה בְנֵֽי טוֹבִיָּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י נְקוֹדָ֑א שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם (7:63) וּמִן הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים בְּנֵ֥י חֳבַיָּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י הַקּ֑וֹץ בְּנֵ֣י בַרְזִלַּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָ֠קַח מִבְּנ֞וֹת בַּרְזִלַּ֤י הַגִּלְעָדִי֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה וַיִּקָּרֵ֖א עַל שְׁמָֽם (7:64) אֵ֗לֶּה בִּקְשׁ֧וּ כְתָבָ֛ם הַמִּתְיַחְשִׂ֖ים וְלֹ֣א נִמְצָ֑א וַיְגֹֽאֲל֖וּ מִן הַכְּהֻנָּֽה

passages.text: אֵ֗לֶּה בִּקְשׁ֧וּ כְתָבָ֛ם הַמִּתְיַחְשִׂ֖ים וְלֹ֣א נִמְצָ֑אוּ וַֽיְגֹאֲל֖וּ מִן הַכְּהֻנָּֽה
וַיִּתֵּ֤ן אֱלֹהַי֙ אֶל לִבִּ֔י וָאֶקְבְּצָ֞ה אֶת הַחֹרִ֧ים וְאֶת הַסְּגָנִ֛ים וְאֶת הָעָ֖ם לְהִתְיַחֵ֑שׂ וָֽאֶמְצָ֗א סֵ֤פֶר הַיַּ֨חַשׂ֙ הָעוֹלִ֣ים בָּרִאשׁוֹנָ֔ה וָאֶמְצָ֖א כָּת֥וּב בּֽוֹ

leads.title: Ezra's priestly lineage and journey to Jerusalem ↔ 'Uzayr and the Messiah called sons of God; rabbis and monks as lords
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The standing of Ezra (ʿUzayr): scribe or son of God [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Ezra's priestly lineage and journey to Jerusalem: The journey from Babylon to Jerusalem takes four months, first to fifth month; The king grants the hero everything he asks; A priest's genealogy traced back to Aaron the chief priest; The scribe set his heart to seek (study) the Torah, to do it and to teach it; Hero called a skilled scribe (sofer mahir) in the Torah of Moses; Success attributed to 'the good hand of my God upon me'.

Only in 'Uzayr and the Messiah called sons of God; rabbis and monks as lords: Polemic: the Jews are said to call 'Uzayr (Ezra?) son of God; People of the Book took their rabbis (ahbar) and monks as lords besides God; Many rabbis and monks devour people's wealth wrongfully; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [response between the texts]; Opponents wish to put out God's light with their mouths, but God will perfect his light; Hoarded gold and silver are heated in hell and used to brand the hoarders' foreheads, sides and backs; Polemic against calling the Messiah son of God; God sent his messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion; A bribe blinds the clear-sighted and perverts the words of the righteous.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero blessed on leaving the vessel (weight 6.0); Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 5.8); Vessel comes to rest on a named mountain (weight 5.4); Deity decides to destroy humankind (weight 5.3); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 5.2); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.1); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Only in The Flood in Genesis: Birds released to find dry land; A sign in the sky commemorates the flood (bow, necklace); Exact dimensions of the vessel are specified; Hero's life or mission spans 950 years; Deity resolves or promises not to repeat the destruction; Destruction motivated by human wickedness or violence; Waters pour both from the sky and from springs of the earth; Deity or gods smell the offering; Hero offers sacrifice after leaving the vessel; Vessel sealed with pitch or bitumen; Hero singled out as righteous or pious; All others perish.

Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's opponents object that only the lowliest follow him; he refuses to drive the believers away; Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; and 22 more.

leads.title: Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest ↔ Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Deity creates by spoken command (Let there be...) (weight 5.8); God creates by saying to a thing 'Be' and it is (kun fa-yakun) (weight 5.3). Pair score 11.1.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Deity gives names to the elements it creates (day, night, heaven, earth, seas); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; The earth itself is commanded to bring forth plants or animals; Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Creation proceeds by dividing (light/darkness, waters above/below); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; and 26 more.

Only in Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God: Jews say the Christians stand on nothing, Christians say the same of the Jews; Claim that none enters paradise unless Jew or Christian, rebutted by surrender of the face to God; Believers told not to say 'ra'ina' (a word twisted by opponents) but 'unzurna'; God abrogates or causes to be forgotten a verse and brings a better or similar one (naskh); God swears by himself: to me every knee shall bow and every tongue swear; Whether God has or begets a son [contrast between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; From sunrise to sunset God's name is great among the nations and in every place incense and a pure offering are brought to his name; East and west belong to God; wherever you turn, there is the face of God; 'He spoke and it came to be; he commanded and it stood firm'; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks [divergence between the texts]; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks; and 1 more.

matches.label: The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq)
matches.note: Creation by splitting a unity. Gen: the rāqîaʿ divides waters from waters, wîhî mabdîl bên mayim lāmāyim. Q: heaven and earth themselves were one closed mass, kānatā ratqan fa-fataqnāhumā. What is divided differs: the waters in Gen, heaven from earth in Q.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יְהִ֥י רָקִ֖יעַ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַמָּ֑יִם וִיהִ֣י מַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין מַ֖יִם לָמָֽיִם
וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת הָרָקִיעַ֒ וַיַּבְדֵּ֗ל בֵּ֤ין הַמַּ֨יִם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לָרָקִ֔יעַ וּבֵ֣ין הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעַ֣ל לָרָקִ֑יעַ וַֽיְהִי כֵֽן
أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ

matches.label: God made every living thing from water
matches.note: yišrəṣû hammayim šereṣ nepeš ḥayyâ ... wəʾēt kol-nepeš haḥayyâ hārōmeśet ʾăšer šārəṣû hammayim; wa-jaʿalnā mina l-māʾi kulla shayʾin ḥayy: life comes from water (nepeš ḥayyâ / shayʾin ḥayy). In Gen the waters bring forth only sea creatures and birds, and land animals come from the earth (1:24); Q says every living thing.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יִשְׁרְצ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם שֶׁ֖רֶץ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֑ה וְעוֹף֙ יְעוֹפֵ֣ף עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ עַל פְּנֵ֖י רְקִ֥יעַ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם

וַיִּבְרָ֣א אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת הַתַּנִּינִ֖ם הַגְּדֹלִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת כָּל נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַֽחַיָּ֣ה הָֽרֹמֶ֡שֶׂת אֲשֶׁר֩ שָׁרְצ֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם לְמִֽינֵהֶ֗ם וְאֵ֨ת כָּל ע֤וֹף כָּנָף֙ לְמִינֵ֔הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי טֽוֹב
أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ

matches.label: Creation proceeds by dividing (light/darkness, waters above/below)

passages.text: וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת הָא֖וֹר כִּי ט֑וֹב וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל אֱלֹהִ֔ים בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֥ין הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ
וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת הָרָקִיעַ֒ וַיַּבְדֵּ֗ל בֵּ֤ין הַמַּ֨יִם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לָרָקִ֔יעַ וּבֵ֣ין הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעַ֣ל לָרָקִ֑יעַ וַֽיְהִי כֵֽן
וְלִמְשֹׁל֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם וּבַלַּ֔יְלָה וּֽלֲהַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֣ין הַחֹ֑שֶׁךְ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי טֽוֹב

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יְהִ֤י מְאֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַיּ֖וֹם וּבֵ֣ין הַלָּ֑יְלָה וְהָי֤וּ לְאֹתֹת֙ וּלְמ֣וֹעֲדִ֔ים וּלְיָמִ֖ים וְשָׁנִֽים

וְלִמְשֹׁל֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם וּבַלַּ֔יְלָה וּֽלֲהַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֣ין הַחֹ֑שֶׁךְ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי טֽוֹב

leads.title: Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest ↔ The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God made every living thing from water (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Deity gives names to the elements it creates (day, night, heaven, earth, seas); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; The earth itself is commanded to bring forth plants or animals; Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Creation proceeds by dividing (light/darkness, waters above/below); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; and 27 more.

Only in The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by wave upon wave and cloud above, darkness upon darkness, so one cannot see his own hand; The deeds of unbelievers are like a mirage in a plain that the thirsty takes for water until he reaches it and finds nothing, but finds God there; God is the light of the heavens and the earth; God's light is like a niche holding a lamp in a glass like a glittering star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of east nor west, whose oil almost glows untouched by fire: light upon light; God sends down hail from mountains in the sky; the flash of his lightning nearly takes away sight; In houses God allowed to be raised, men undistracted by trade glorify him morning and evening; God created every beast from water: some go on their bellies, some on two legs, some on four; Birds with outspread wings glorify God; each knows its prayer and praise; With God is the fountain of life; in his light we see light; A lamp fed directly by an olive tree [divergence between the texts]; A golden lampstand with seven lamps is flanked by two olive trees that pour golden oil through golden pipes; The mirage and the thirsty traveler [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

leads.title: Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest ↔ The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: What God does after creating in six days [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them (weight 5.8); A solid firmament (raqia) separates upper waters from lower waters (weight 5.6); Creation is completed in six days (weight 5.2); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7). Pair score 28.0.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Deity gives names to the elements it creates (day, night, heaven, earth, seas); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; The earth itself is commanded to bring forth plants or animals; Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Creation proceeds by dividing (light/darkness, waters above/below); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; and 23 more.

Only in The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations: God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently; God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage; Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?'; Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot); God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness; God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; God set constellations (buruj) in the sky and adorned it for beholders; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers; God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh); and 2 more.

matches.label: What God does after creating in six days
matches.note: After the six days: Gen 2:2 wa-yəkhal ʾĕlōhîm ba-yyôm haš-šəvîʿî məlaʾktô ... wa-yyišbōt ba-yyôm haš-šəvîʿî, God ceases or rests on the seventh day; Q 25:59 khalaqa s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa wa-mā baynahumā fī sittati ayyāmin thumma stawā ʿalā l-ʿarshi r-raḥmānu, God takes his seat on the Throne. There is no seventh day and no rest, and 25:58 adds al-ḥayy alladhī lā yamūt. cf. Q 50:38 (no weariness).

passages.text: וַיְכַ֤ל אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיִּשְׁבֹּת֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה

matches.note: jaʿala fīhā sirājan wa-qamaran munīran ~ ham-māʾôr hag-gādōl lə-memšelet hay-yôm wə-ʾet ham-māʾôr haq-qāṭōn: both avoid the sun's name and call it a light or lamp (māʾôr / sirāj); the Quran names the moon (qamar), Genesis does not.

Genesis divides upper from lower waters with a firmament; the Quran two seas side by side with a barrier (barzakh). Weak lead: shared idea of separation only.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Deity gives names to the elements it creates (day, night, heaven, earth, seas); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; The earth itself is commanded to bring forth plants or animals; Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Creation proceeds by dividing (light/darkness, waters above/below); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; and 26 more.

matches.label: The order of creating heaven and earth and the days allotted to each
matches.note: The order and the counting of the days. Gen: the firmament called šāmāyim on day 2 (yôm šēnî), dry land and plants on day 3, luminaries in the firmament on day 4, so heaven before dry earth, one work per day. Q: khalaqa l-arḍa fī yawmayni ... wa-qaddara fīhā aqwātahā fī arbaʿati ayyām ... thumma stawā ilā s-samāʾi wa-hiya dukhān ... fa-qaḍāhunna sabʿa samāwātin fī yawmayn. The earth is created first, its provisions in four days, and only then the seven heavens; the sums (2+4+2) are reckoned by the exegetes to six. There is no evening-and-morning formula, no seventh day, and the luminaries are 'lamps' of the lowest heaven.

matches.note: In the same breath as the creation of human pairs, opposite statements on likeness to God. Gen: naʿăśeh ʾāḏām bə-ṣalmēnû ki-ḏmûṯēnû ... zāḵār û-nəqēḇâ bārāʾ ʾōṯām. matches.label: The weekly holy day, and whether it rests on God's rest
matches.note: The weekly day without the creation rest. Genesis grounds the seventh day in God's rest: wa-yišbōṯ bay-yôm haš-šəḇîʿî ... wa-yəḇāreḵ ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ yôm haš-šəḇîʿî wa-yqaddēš ʾōṯô kî ḇô šāḇaṯ. The Quran's Friday (yawm al-jumuʿa, the day of assembly) has no rest and no creation basis: fa-ntashirū fī l-arḍ. This fits the Quran's denial that God rested (50:38).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The number of months with God is twelve, in God's book since the day he created heaven and earth (weight 6.7); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7). Pair score 11.4.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Deity gives names to the elements it creates (day, night, heaven, earth, seas); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; The earth itself is commanded to bring forth plants or animals; Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Creation proceeds by dividing (light/darkness, waters above/below); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; and 26 more.

Only in Twelve months and the ban on intercalation: God fixes the reckoning of months [divergence between the texts]; Four of the twelve months are sacred; God fixed all the boundaries of the earth and formed summer and winter; Postponing a sacred month (al-nasi', intercalation) is an increase in unbelief.

leads.title: The Table of Nations ↔ Hud and the monument-building people of Ad
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Nimrod, first mighty man, a mighty hunter before the LORD (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in The Table of Nations: First kingdom founded in Babel and Shinar; Founding of Nineveh and the Assyrian cities; The world's nations number about seventy; All nations listed as descendants of the three sons of the flood hero; In the days of Peleg the earth was divided; Humanity created from a male and a female and made into peoples (shu'ub) and tribes to know one another; the noblest is the most pious; Nations distinguished by land, language and clan; Philistines derived from Casluhim/Caphtorim (Crete).

Only in Hud and the monument-building people of Ad: The people of ʿĀd build a monument on every height and take fortresses (maṣāniʿ) hoping to live forever; Their graves (qirbam = qivram) are their houses forever, though they named lands after themselves; The prophet Hūd is sent to the people of ʿĀd; Builders seek to make a name for themselves and avoid dispersal; Building with baked bricks and bitumen instead of stone and mortar; Woe to the one who builds a city (Zion) with bloodshed and injustice; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal; The Day of YHWH: a coming day of divine judgment, terror and darkness; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger; The Prophet asks no wage for the message.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: All humanity once spoke one language (weight 6.7); Humankind was originally one (in speech or community) and then divided [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in The Tower of Babel: Babel explained from balal, to confuse; God scatters humanity over the earth; God confuses human language; God comes down to see what humans are doing; Builders seek to make a name for themselves and avoid dispersal; Why humans speak many languages [divergence between the texts]; Mankind once one, then divided [divergence between the texts]; Building with baked bricks and bitumen instead of stone and mortar; Humans build a tower whose top reaches heaven; Humans build a tower whose top reaches heaven [divergence between the texts]; God speaks in the plural (us, our) as if to a divine council.

matches.label: Humans build a tower whose top reaches heaven
matches.note: A tower toward heaven: Babel's builders, all humankind (hāvâ nivneh llānû ʿîr û-migdāl wə-rōʾšô vaš-šāmayim), want to make a name and not be scattered; God comes down to see, and scatters them. In the Quran one king orders it of his minister (fa-jʿal lī ṣarḥan laʿallī aṭṭaliʿu ilā ilāhi Mūsā wa-innī la-aẓunnuhu mina l-kādhibīna): the aim is to climb up and look at Moses' God, mockingly. The ending is drowning (fa-nabadhnāhum fī l-yamm), not dispersal. God's descent to inspect the tower (wa-yyēred YHWH lirʾōt) is reversed into Pharaoh's wish to ascend and inspect God.

The Quran has one objection about one man, inna fīhā Lūṭan, and the answer naḥnu aʿlamu bi-man fīhā la-nunajjiyannahu wa-ahlahu illā mraʾatahu. Concern for the city becomes concern for Lot, and there is no bargaining.

matches.note: A city spared for the sake of the righteous inside it. Genesis: ha-ʾap̄ tispeh ṣaddîq ʿim rāšāʿ ... wə-lōʾ ṯiśśāʾ lam-māqôm ləmaʿan ḥămiššîm haṣ-ṣaddîqim; lōʾ ʾašḥîṯ baʿăḇûr hā-ʿăśārâ (Abraham bargains; God would spare all for ten). The danger is a human army, not divine fire; no bargaining; and the righteous are to be separated out (tazayyul), not the cause of sparing everyone for ever.

matches.label: Who Abraham's visitors are
matches.note: Who comes: wa-la-qad jāʾat rusulunā ibrāhīma bi-l-bushrā vs wayyērāʾ ʾēlāyw YHWH ... wᵉhinnēh šᵉlōšāh ʾănāšîm. Gen has YHWH himself appear in the form of three men; Q has 'our messengers', with no number and no appearance of God.

passages.text: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵלֹנֵ֖י מַמְרֵ֑א וְה֛וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב פֶּֽתַח הָאֹ֖הֶל כְּחֹ֥ם הַיּֽוֹם

matches.label: Whether Abraham's heavenly guests eat the meal he serves
matches.note: Reversed: in Gen the guests eat (wayyittēn lipnêhem wᵉhûʾ-ʿōmēd ʿălêhem taḥat hāʿēṣ wayyōʾkēlû); in Q their hands do not reach the food (fa-lammā raʾā aydiyahum lā taṣilu ilayhi nakirahum). cf. Tob 12:19, Gen. Rab. 48:14, b. Bava Metzia 86b (angels only seem to eat), outside the canon.

matches.label: Who is afraid during the visit of the heavenly guests, and why
matches.note: Who is afraid and why: in Q Abraham is afraid because the guests will not eat (wa-awjasa minhum khīfatan qālū lā takhaf); in Gen it is Sarah who is afraid when caught laughing (wattᵉkaḥēš śārāh lēʾmōr lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî kî yārēʾāh).

passages.text: וַתְּכַחֵ֨שׁ שָׂרָ֧ה לֵאמֹ֛ר לֹ֥א צָחַ֖קְתִּי כִּ֣י יָרֵ֑אָה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לֹ֖א כִּ֥י צָחָֽקְתְּ

matches.label: When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered
matches.note: The order and the answer change: in Gen Sarah overhears the promise at the tent door and then laughs inwardly (wattiṣḥaq śārāh bᵉqirbāh), and God rebukes her (lāmmāh zeh ṣāḥăqāh śārāh), she denies it (lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî); in Q she is standing by and laughs first (wa-mraʾatuhu qāʾimatun fa-ḍaḥikat), then receives the tidings, with no rebuke and no denial. ṣḥq / ḍḥk are cognate.

matches.label: A divine messenger announces a son to a barren couple
matches.note: The promise of a son: fa-basharnāhā bi-isḥāqa wa-min warāʾi isḥāqa yaʿqūb vs šôb ʾāšûb ʾēlêkā kāʿēt ḥayyāh wᵉhinnēh-bēn lᵉśārāh ʾištekā. It is said to Sarah directly in Q, to Abraham in Gen (Sarah only overhears); Q names Isaac and adds Jacob after him; Gen names no child here and adds a date (lammôʿēd ... kāʿēt ḥayyāh).

matches.label: A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name
matches.note: wə-hinnēh-ḇēn lə-śārâ ʾišteḵā vs. wa-basharnāhu bi-Isḥāqa nabiyyan mina ṣ-ṣāliḥīn. The announcement of Isaac's birth. In Gen it comes four chapters before the Aqedah; in Q it comes after the sacrifice, as a further reward, and calls Isaac a prophet.

leads.finding: Who Abraham's visitors are

units.title: Three visitors at Mamre and the promise of Isaac
Abraham's honored guests, the barren old wife striking her face, the stones of clay for Lot's people; Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud and Noah

matches.label: Who Abraham's visitors are
matches.note: Who the visitors are. Genesis: wa-yērāʾ ʾēlâw YHWH bə-ʾēlōnê mamrēʾ ... wə-hinnēh šəlōšâ ʾănāšîm (YHWH appears, as three men; YHWH himself speaks in 18:13). Quran: ḍayfu ibrāhīma l-mukramīn, addressed as ayyuhā l-mursalūn (51:31): honored guests who are 'sent ones', no number, and God is not among them.

passages.text: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵלֹנֵ֖י מַמְרֵ֑א וְה֛וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב פֶּֽתַח הָאֹ֖הֶל כְּחֹ֥ם הַיּֽוֹם
וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים נִצָּבִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִפֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרְצָה
هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

matches.label: Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them
matches.note: The welcome. Genesis: Abraham runs to meet them (wa-yyāroṣ liqrāʾṯām), bows to the ground and begs ʾăḏōnāy ʾim nāʾ māṣāʾṯî ḥēn bə-ʿênêḵā, then wa-yəmahēr ʾaḇrāhām hā-ʾōhĕlâ ʾel śārâ. Quran: the guests speak first, fa-qālū salāman qāla salāmun qawmun munkarūn (Abraham returns the greeting and finds them strange), then fa-rāgha ilā ahlihi (he slipped off to his household). Same hurried move to the tent; the bow and the plea are absent, and Abraham's unease (munkarūn) is added.

passages.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים נִצָּבִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִפֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרְצָה
וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנָ֗י אִם נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ אַל נָ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר מֵעַ֥ל עַבְדֶּֽךָ
וַיְמַהֵ֧ר אַבְרָהָ֛ם הָאֹ֖הֱלָה אֶל שָׂרָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מַהֲרִ֞י שְׁלֹ֤שׁ סְאִים֙ קֶ֣מַח סֹ֔לֶת ל֖וּשִׁי וַעֲשִׂ֥י עֻגֽוֹת
إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ

matches.label: Whether Abraham's heavenly guests eat the meal
matches.note: Reversal: in Genesis the visitors eat: wə-hûʾ ʿōmēḏ ʿălêhem taḥaṯ hā-ʿēṣ wa-yyōʾḵēlû. In the Quran they do not: qāla a-lā taʾkulūn, fa-awjasa minhum khīfatan, qālū lā takhaf. The refusal to eat reveals that they are angels and frightens Abraham. cf. Tob 12:19, Gen. Rab. 48:14 and b. Bava Metzia 86b (the angels only seemed to eat), a solution to the same problem; not in the HB.

passages.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חֶמְאָ֜ה וְחָלָ֗ב וּבֶן הַבָּקָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא עֹמֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תַּ֥חַת הָעֵ֖ץ וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمٍ

matches.label: Sarah's reaction to the announcement of a son
matches.note: Sarah's reaction, changed from inner laughter to an open cry. Genesis: wat-tiṣḥaq śārâ bə-qirbāh lēʾmōr ʾaḥărê ḇəlōṯî ... wa-ʾḏōnî zāqēn; God asks lāmmâ zeh ṣāḥăqâ śārâ and she denies it out of fear (lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî kî yārēʾâ). Quran: fa-aqbalati mraʾatuhu fī ṣarratin fa-ṣakkat wajhahā wa-qālat ʿajūzun ʿaqīm (she came forward crying out, struck her face and said 'a barren old woman!'). The messengers answer ka-dhālika qāla rabbuki innahu huwa l-ḥakīmu l-ʿalīm: no rebuke, no denial, no laughter (ṣ-ḥ-q, the pun on Isaac's name, is gone).

passages.text: וַתִּצְחַ֥ק שָׂרָ֖ה בְּקִרְבָּ֣הּ לֵאמֹ֑ר אַחֲרֵ֤י בְלֹתִי֙ הָֽיְתָה לִּ֣י עֶדְנָ֔ה וַֽאדֹנִ֖י זָקֵֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל אַבְרָהָ֑ם לָ֣מָּה זֶּה֩ צָחֲקָ֨ה שָׂרָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר הַאַ֥ף אֻמְנָ֛ם אֵלֵ֖ד וַאֲנִ֥י זָקַֽנְתִּי
וַתְּכַחֵ֨שׁ שָׂרָ֧ה לֵאמֹ֛ר לֹ֥א צָחַ֖קְתִּי כִּ֣י יָרֵ֑אָה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לֹ֖א כִּ֥י צָחָֽקְתְּ
فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ فِى صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ
قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

matches.label: The answer given to the old woman's doubt
matches.note: The answer to the old woman's doubt: hă-yippālēʾ mē-YHWH dāḇār (is anything too wondrous for YHWH?, a rhetorical question by YHWH himself) vs. ka-dhālika qāla rabbuki innahu huwa l-ḥakīmu l-ʿalīm (thus said your Lord; he is the Wise, the Knowing, said by the messengers). Divine power becomes divine wisdom and knowledge, and the speaker is the angels quoting God.

passages.text: הֲיִפָּלֵ֥א מֵיְהוָ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר לַמּוֹעֵ֞ד אָשׁ֥וּב אֵלֶ֛יךָ כָּעֵ֥ת חַיָּ֖ה וּלְשָׂרָ֥ה בֵֽן
قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

matches.label: A tender calf is slaughtered and served to divine guests
matches.note: wa-yiqqaḥ ben bāqār raḵ wā-ṭôḇ ... wa-yiqqaḥ ḥemʾâ wə-ḥālāḇ û-ḇen hab-bāqār ... wa-yittēn lip̄nêhem vs. fa-jāʾa bi-ʿijlin samīnin fa-qarrabahu ilayhim. Genesis: a tender, good calf with curds and milk; Quran: a fat calf only.

passages.text: וְאֶל הַבָּקָ֖ר רָ֣ץ אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיִּקַּ֨ח בֶּן בָּקָ֜ר רַ֤ךְ וָטוֹב֙ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל הַנַּ֔עַר וַיְמַהֵ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת אֹתֽוֹ
וַיִּקַּ֨ח חֶמְאָ֜ה וְחָלָ֗ב וּבֶן הַבָּקָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא עֹמֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תַּ֥חַת הָעֵ֖ץ וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ
فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ

matches.label: A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name
matches.note: wə-hinnēh ḇēn lə-śārâ ʾištekā; lam-môʿēḏ ʾāšûḇ ʾēleḵā kā-ʿēṯ ḥayyâ û-lə-śārâ ḇēn vs. wa-bashsharūhu bi-ghulāmin ʿalīm. Genesis promises a son to Sarah with a set time; the Quran gives the good news to Abraham of 'a knowing boy', with no time and no name.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וֹב אָשׁ֤וּב אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה וְהִנֵּה בֵ֖ן לְשָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתֶּ֑ךָ וְשָׂרָ֥ה שֹׁמַ֛עַת פֶּ֥תַח הָאֹ֖הֶל וְה֥וּא אַחֲרָֽיו
הֲיִפָּלֵ֥א מֵיְהוָ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר לַמּוֹעֵ֞ד אָשׁ֥וּב אֵלֶ֛יךָ כָּעֵ֥ת חַיָּ֖ה וּלְשָׂרָ֥ה בֵֽן
فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمٍ

matches.label: Heavenly visitors eat a human meal

passages.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חֶמְאָ֜ה וְחָלָ֗ב וּבֶן הַבָּקָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא עֹמֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תַּ֥חַת הָעֵ֖ץ וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ

sides.note: curds, milk and calf: meat with milk, noted by rabbis

passages.text: فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ

sides.note: contrast: in the Quran the angels do not eat (Gen 18:8 they eat)

matches.label: The old wife overhears the promise of a son at the tent door and laughs

passages.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וֹב אָשׁ֤וּב אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה וְהִנֵּה בֵ֖ן לְשָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתֶּ֑ךָ וְשָׂרָ֥ה שֹׁמַ֛עַת פֶּ֥תַח הָאֹ֖הֶל וְה֥וּא אַחֲרָֽיו
וַתִּצְחַ֥ק שָׂרָ֖ה בְּקִרְבָּ֣הּ לֵאמֹ֑ר אַחֲרֵ֤י בְלֹתִי֙ הָֽיְתָה לִּ֣י עֶדְנָ֔ה וַֽאדֹנִ֖י זָקֵֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל אַבְרָהָ֑ם לָ֣מָּה זֶּה֩ צָחֲקָ֨ה שָׂרָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר הַאַ֥ף אֻמְנָ֛ם אֵלֵ֖ד וַאֲנִ֥י זָקַֽנְתִּי
فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ فِى صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ

leads.title: Three visitors at Mamre and the promise of Isaac ↔ Darkness and light, clay and two terms, and those who would not believe
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God appears as three men who visit the patriarch (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Three visitors at Mamre and the promise of Isaac: Child promised to a woman past childbearing age; The answer given to the old woman's doubt [divergence between the texts]; Heavenly visitors eat a human meal; Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age; Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age [divergence between the texts]; The aged father asks how he can have a son when his wife is barren and he is very old [divergence between the texts]; Who is afraid during the visit of the heavenly guests, and why [divergence between the texts]; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them [divergence between the texts]; Who Abraham's visitors are; Who Abraham's visitors are [divergence between the texts]; The patriarch tells his unknown guests 'we are afraid of you' [divergence between the texts]; Patriarch or matriarch laughs at the promise of a child in old age [divergence between the texts]; and 12 more.

Only in Darkness and light, clay and two terms, and those who would not believe: Had God sent an angel he would have made him a man; Even a book on parchment they could touch would be called magic; God destroyed earlier generations though he had established them more firmly and given them rain and rivers; Praise God who created heaven and earth and made the darknesses and the light; Earlier messengers were mocked, and what the mockers mocked surrounded them; God decreed a term (ajal) for each person, and another term named with him; Deniers demand that a treasure be sent down to the prophet or an angel come with him; Whether darkness is made by God or exists before creation [divergence between the texts]; The speaker too was 'pinched off from clay' (qoratsti), like a figure nipped from a lump of clay; 'I form light and create darkness, make peace and create evil (ra'); I YHWH do all these'; The listeners walk among the dwellings of generations God destroyed, a sign; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

matches.label: How Lot receives the heavenly guests
matches.note: Lot's response to the guests is reversed: in Gen he rises to meet them, bows and presses them to stay (wayyāqom liqrāʾtām wayyištaḥû ... wayyipṣar-bām mᵉʾōd ... wayyaʿaś lāhem mišteh); in Q he is distressed and helpless on their account (sīʾa bihim wa-ḍāqa bihim dharʿan wa-qāla hādhā yawmun ʿaṣīb).

passages.text: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ שְׁנֵ֨י הַמַּלְאָכִ֤ים סְדֹ֨מָה֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב וְל֖וֹט יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּשַֽׁעַר סְדֹ֑ם וַיַּרְא לוֹט֙ וַיָּ֣קָם לִקְרָאתָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה
וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הִנֶּ֣ה נָּא אֲדֹנַ֗י ס֣וּרוּ נָ֠א אֶל בֵּ֨ית עַבְדְּכֶ֤ם וְלִ֨ינוּ֙ וְרַחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֖ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֣ם לְדַרְכְּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֹּ֔א כִּ֥י בָרְח֖וֹב נָלִֽין
וַיִּפְצַר בָּ֣ם מְאֹ֔ד וַיָּסֻ֣רוּ אֵלָ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל בֵּית֑וֹ וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וּמַצּ֥וֹת אָפָ֖ה וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
وَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًا سِىٓءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا وَقَالَ هَٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ

matches.label: Lot's townspeople turn on him
matches.note: The townsmen besiege Lot's house: wa-jāʾahu qawmuhu yuhraʿūna ilayhi vs nāsabbû ʿal-habbayit minnaʿar wᵉʿad-zāqēn ... hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wᵉnēdʿāh ʾōtām. Their answer differs: in Gen they turn on Lot as an alien who plays the judge (hāʾeḥād bāʾ-lāgûr wayyišpōṭ šāpôṭ) and try to break the door; in Q they only say la-qad ʿalimta mā lanā fī banātika min ḥaqqin wa-innaka la-taʿlamu mā nurīd.

passages.text: טֶרֶם֮ יִשְׁכָּבוּ֒ וְאַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר אַנְשֵׁ֤י סְדֹם֙ נָסַ֣בּוּ עַל הַבַּ֔יִת מִנַּ֖עַר וְעַד זָקֵ֑ן כָּל הָעָ֖ם מִקָּצֶֽה
וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ אֶל לוֹט֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ אַיֵּ֧ה הָאֲנָשִׁ֛ים אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַלָּ֑יְלָה הוֹצִיאֵ֣ם אֵלֵ֔ינוּ וְנֵדְעָ֖ה אֹתָֽם
וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ גֶּשׁ הָ֗לְאָה וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ הָאֶחָ֤ד בָּֽא לָגוּר֙ וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֣ט שָׁפ֔וֹט עַתָּ֕ה נָרַ֥ע לְךָ֖ מֵהֶ֑ם וַיִּפְצְר֨וּ בָאִ֤ישׁ בְּלוֹט֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיִּגְּשׁ֖וּ לִשְׁבֹּ֥ר הַדָּֽלֶת

وَجَآءَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ بَنَاتِى هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِى ضَيْفِىٓ أَلَيْسَ مِنكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَّشِيدٌ
قَالُوا۟ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا لَنَا فِى بَنَاتِكَ مِنْ حَقٍّ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَعْلَمُ مَا نُرِيدُ

matches.label: What Lot says to the townsmen
matches.note: Lot offers his daughters: hāʾulāʾi banātī hunna aṭharu lakum fa-ttaqū llāha wa-lā tukhzūni fī ḍayfī a-laysa minkum rajulun rashīd vs ʾal-nāʾ ʾaḥay tārēʿû hinnēh-nāʾ lî šᵉtê bānôt ... wᵉʿăśû lāhen kaṭṭôb bᵉʿênêkem raq lāʾănāšîm hāʾēl ʾal-taʿăśû dābār. The terms differ: in Gen 'do to them as you please'; in Q 'they are purer for you', with an appeal to fear God and to right-minded men. Exegesis reads Q as lawful marriage.

passages.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אַל נָ֥א אַחַ֖י תָּרֵֽעוּ

הִנֵּה נָ֨א לִ֜י שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יָדְעוּ֙ אִ֔ישׁ אוֹצִֽיאָה נָּ֤א אֶתְהֶן֙ אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ן כַּטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם רַ֠ק לָֽאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵל֙ אַל תַּעֲשׂ֣וּ דָבָ֔ר כִּֽי עַל כֵּ֥ן בָּ֖אוּ בְּצֵ֥ל קֹרָתִֽי

وَجَآءَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ بَنَاتِى هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِى ضَيْفِىٓ أَلَيْسَ مِنكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَّشِيدٌ

matches.label: The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do
matches.note: The guests disclose their errand: yā lūṭu innā rusulu rabbika lan yaṣilū ilayka vs kî-mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet-hammāqôm hazzeh ... wayᵉšallᵉḥēnû YHWH lᵉšaḥătāh. In Gen the angels first pull Lot inside and strike the mob with blindness (hikkû bassanwērîm); in Q, where Lot wishes for strength or a strong support (law anna lī bikum quwwatan aw āwī ilā ruknin shadīd), only their word assures him.

passages.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֤וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֶת יָדָ֔ם וַיָּבִ֧יאוּ אֶת ל֛וֹט אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַבָּ֑יְתָה וְאֶת הַדֶּ֖לֶת סָגָֽרוּ
וְֽאֶת הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים אֲשֶׁר פֶּ֣תַח הַבַּ֗יִת הִכּוּ֙ בַּסַּנְוֵרִ֔ים מִקָּטֹ֖ן וְעַד גָּד֑וֹל וַיִּלְא֖וּ לִמְצֹ֥א הַפָּֽתַח
כִּֽי מַשְׁחִתִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ אֶת הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי גָֽדְלָ֤ה צַעֲקָתָם֙ אֶת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֥נוּ יְהוָ֖ה לְשַׁחֲתָֽהּ
قَالَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِى بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أَوْ ءَاوِىٓ إِلَىٰ رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ

قَالُوا۟ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكَ فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ

matches.label: When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls
matches.note: When they leave and when the blow falls: Q, by night, the destruction appointed for morning (bi-qiṭʿin mina l-layli ... inna mawʿidahumu ṣ-ṣubḥu a-laysa ṣ-ṣubḥu bi-qarīb); Gen, the angels hurry him at dawn (kᵉmô haššaḥar ʿālāh wayyāʾîṣû) and the fire falls once the sun has risen and Lot is in Zoar (haššemeš yāṣāʾ ʿal-hāʾāreṣ wᵉlôṭ bāʾ ṣōʿărāh).

passages.text: וּכְמוֹ֙ הַשַּׁ֣חַר עָלָ֔ה וַיָּאִ֥יצוּ הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים בְּל֣וֹט לֵאמֹ֑ר קוּם֩ קַ֨ח אֶֽת אִשְׁתְּךָ֜ וְאֶת שְׁתֵּ֤י בְנֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ הַנִּמְצָאֹ֔ת פֶּן תִּסָּפֶ֖ה בַּעֲוֺ֥ן הָעִֽיר
הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ יָצָ֣א עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ וְל֖וֹט בָּ֥א צֹֽעֲרָה
