matches.label: Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom
matches.note: Gen: Lot rises to meet them at the gate, bows, presses them to stay and bakes maṣṣôt. Q: Lot greets them coldly, innakum qawmun munkarūn ('you are strangers'). Hospitality is replaced by unease, as with Abraham.

passages.text: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ שְׁנֵ֨י הַמַּלְאָכִ֤ים סְדֹ֨מָה֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב וְל֖וֹט יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּשַֽׁעַר סְדֹ֑ם וַיַּרְא לוֹט֙ וַיָּ֣קָם לִקְרָאתָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה
וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הִנֶּ֣ה נָּא אֲדֹנַ֗י ס֣וּרוּ נָ֠א אֶל בֵּ֨ית עַבְדְּכֶ֤ם וְלִ֨ינוּ֙ וְרַחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֖ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֣ם לְדַרְכְּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֹּ֔א כִּ֥י בָרְח֖וֹב נָלִֽין
וַיִּפְצַר בָּ֣ם מְאֹ֔ד וַיָּסֻ֣רוּ אֵלָ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל בֵּית֑וֹ וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וּמַצּ֥וֹת אָפָ֖ה וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
فَلَمَّا جَآءَ ءَالَ لُوطٍ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ

matches.label: The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people
matches.note: Order reversed. Gen: first the mob (19:4-11), then the angels reveal kî-mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet-hammāqôm hazzeh (19:13). Q: the messengers state their mission and order the flight (15:63-66, dābira hāʾulāʾi maqṭūʿun muṣbiḥīn), and only then do the townsmen come (wa-jāʾa ahlu l-madīnati yastabshirūn).

passages.text: טֶרֶם֮ יִשְׁכָּבוּ֒ וְאַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר אַנְשֵׁ֤י סְדֹם֙ נָסַ֣בּוּ עַל הַבַּ֔יִת מִנַּ֖עַר וְעַד זָקֵ֑ן כָּל הָעָ֖ם מִקָּצֶֽה
וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ אֶל לוֹט֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ אַיֵּ֧ה הָאֲנָשִׁ֛ים אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַלָּ֑יְלָה הוֹצִיאֵ֣ם אֵלֵ֔ינוּ וְנֵדְעָ֖ה אֹתָֽם
וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים אֶל ל֗וֹט עֹ֚ד מִֽי לְךָ֣ פֹ֔ה חָתָן֙ וּבָנֶ֣יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר לְךָ֖ בָּעִ֑יר הוֹצֵ֖א מִן הַמָּקֽוֹם
قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ مُّجْرِمِينَ
قَالُوا۟ بَلْ جِئْنَٰكَ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ
وَأَتَيْنَٰكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَإِنَّا لَصَٰدِقُونَ

matches.label: Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests
matches.note: Gen: ʾal-nāʾ ʾaḥay tārēʿû hinnēh-nāʾ lî šətê bānôt ʾăšer lōʾ-yādəʿû ʾîš ... waʿăśû lāhen kaṭṭôb bəʿênêkem. Q: hāʾulāʾi ḍayfī fa-lā tafḍaḥūni wa-ttaqū llāha ... hāʾulāʾi banātī in kuntum fāʿilīn. Q keeps the offer but drops 'do with them as you please' and adds an appeal to fear God (Q's form is open to the later reading of marriage).

passages.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אַל נָ֥א אַחַ֖י תָּרֵֽעוּ

הִנֵּה נָ֨א לִ֜י שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יָדְעוּ֙ אִ֔ישׁ אוֹצִֽיאָה נָּ֤א אֶתְהֶן֙ אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ן כַּטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם רַ֠ק לָֽאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵל֙ אַל תַּעֲשׂ֣וּ דָבָ֔ר כִּֽי עַל כֵּ֥ן בָּ֖אוּ בְּצֵ֥ל קֹרָתִֽי
قَالَ إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ضَيْفِى فَلَا تَفْضَحُونِ
وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ
قَالَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ بَنَاتِىٓ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ

matches.label: Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place
matches.note: Gen: at dawn (kəmô haššaḥar ʿālâ) the angels drag the lingering Lot out by the hand; ʾal-tabbîṭ ʾaḥărêkā. Q: by night, fa-asri bi-ahlika bi-qiṭʿin mina l-layl wa-ttabiʿ adbārahum wa-lā yaltafit minkum aḥad: no hesitation, and Lot walks behind his family.

passages.text: וּכְמוֹ֙ הַשַּׁ֣חַר עָלָ֔ה וַיָּאִ֥יצוּ הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים בְּל֣וֹט לֵאמֹ֑ר קוּם֩ קַ֨ח אֶֽת אִשְׁתְּךָ֜ וְאֶת שְׁתֵּ֤י בְנֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ הַנִּמְצָאֹ֔ת פֶּן תִּסָּפֶ֖ה בַּעֲוֺ֥ן הָעִֽיר
וַֽיִּתְמַהְמָ֓הּ וַיַּחֲזִ֨קוּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים בְּיָד֣וֹ וּבְיַד אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ וּבְיַד֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י בְנֹתָ֔יו בְּחֶמְלַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַיֹּצִאֻ֥הוּ וַיַּנִּחֻ֖הוּ מִח֥וּץ לָעִֽיר
וַיְהִי֩ כְהוֹצִיאָ֨ם אֹתָ֜ם הַח֗וּצָה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הִמָּלֵ֣ט עַל נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ אַל תַּבִּ֣יט אַחֲרֶ֔יךָ וְאַֽל תַּעֲמֹ֖ד בְּכָל הַכִּכָּ֑ר הָהָ֥רָה הִמָּלֵ֖ט פֶּן תִּסָּפֶֽה
فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱتَّبِعْ أَدْبَٰرَهُمْ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ وَٱمْضُوا۟ حَيْثُ تُؤْمَرُونَ

matches.label: Lot's wife is among those who stay behind and perish
matches.note: Gen: her fate follows from her act, wattabbēṭ ʾištô mēʾaḥărāyw wattəhî nəṣîb melaḥ. Q: her fate is decreed in advance, qaddarnā innahā la-mina l-ghābirīn. There is no looking back and no pillar of salt.

passages.text: וַתַּבֵּ֥ט אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מֵאַחֲרָ֑יו וַתְּהִ֖י נְצִ֥יב מֶֽלַח
إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَآ إِنَّهَا لَمِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

matches.label: Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed
matches.note: Same hour and same overturning: haššemeš yāṣāʾ ʿal-hāʾāreṣ / fa-akhadhathumu ṣ-ṣayḥatu mushriqīn; wayyahăpōk ʾet-hehārîm hāʾēl / jaʿalnā ʿāliyahā sāfilahā. matches.label: The townsmen remind Lot they had forbidden him to receive outsiders
matches.note: hāʾeḥād bāʾ-lāgûr wayyišpōṭ šāpôṭ, the townsmen resent the sojourner judging them; a-wa-lam nanhaka ʿani l-ʿālamīn, they forbade him to take in outsiders. Both turn on Lot's status as an outsider to the town.

matches.label: A member of the hero's family is lost

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Pair score 11.5.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; Lot's family is saved at the time before dawn (bi-sahar) while a storm of stones (hasib) destroys the rest; and 40 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron, Noah, Ad, Thamud, the People of the Rass and the rained-upon town: The 'People of the Rass' (aṣḥāb al-rass, the well) named among destroyed peoples; Most unbelievers are like cattle, or even further astray; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission; 'Do not go about after your heart and your eyes'; Ox knows its owner and the ass its master's crib, but Israel does not know (animals wiser than God's people); The sign the flood leaves for later generations [divergence between the texts]; The town that was rained on with an evil rain (Lot's) is passed by travelers; Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts]; Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts]; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; The people mock God's messengers, despise his words and scoff at his prophets; All others perish; and 1 more.

matches.label: What the sin of Lot's townsmen was
matches.note: The sin: Genesis has one night's event, the townsmen demanding Lot's two guests, hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wə-nēdəʿâ ʾōtām; the Quran has a standing practice of the whole people, a-taʾtūna dh-dhukrāna mina l-ʿālamīna wa-tadharūna mā khalaqa lakum rabbukum min azwājikum. The Quran has no guests, angels or hospitality, and Lot preaches as 'their brother' and a trustworthy messenger (26:161-162), which Genesis' Lot never does.

matches.note: Messengers come to a doomed town. Gen: wa-yyāḇōʾû šənê ham-malʾāḵîm sədōmâ, two messengers (the third of Gen 18 stays behind). Q: idh arsalnā ilayhimu thnayni ... fa-ʿazzaznā bi-thālith, two messengers then a third. Lot alone urges his people (qûmû ṣəʾû min-ha-mmāqôm ha-zze) and is mocked (wa-yəhî ḵi-mṣaḥēq); the Quranic man from the city's edge urges yā-qawmi ttabiʿū l-mursalīn. Structural lead only, the town is unnamed in the Quran.

leads.summary: 5 correspondences read side by side: 3 deliberately changed, 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Who strikes the Sodom mob's eyes [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Lot's family is saved at the time before dawn (bi-sahar) while a storm of stones (hasib) destroys the rest (weight 6.7); The righteous man's warning is taken as a joke by his own relatives (weight 6.3); Attackers struck with blindness and cannot find the door (weight 6.3); What falls from heaven on Sodom [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Townsmen surround the house and demand the male guest for sexual abuse (weight 6.0); Hero's family saved with him [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.4); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Pair score 48.5.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 34 more.

Only in Refrains over 'Ad, Thamud's she-camel, Lot's guests and Pharaoh; everything by measure; the seat of truth: God's command is but one, like a blink of the eye; The guilty are dragged on their faces into the Fire: 'Taste the touch of Saqar'; The God-fearing are in gardens and a river, in a seat of truth with an all-powerful King; A single Cry (sayha) is sent and they become like the dry stubble of a pen-builder; When they solicited Lot's guests, God obliterated their eyes; 'The host will be routed and turn their backs' (applied to Badr); Everything they did is in the scriptures (zubur); every small and great thing is written down; God created everything by measure/decree (bi-qadar); 'Are your unbelievers better than those, or have you an immunity (bara'a) in the scriptures (zubur)?'; Supernatural being must leave before daybreak; Refrain: 'How then were my punishment and my warnings?' (fa-kayfa kana 'adhabi wa-nudhur); Refrain: 'We have made the Quran easy to remember; is there anyone who will remember?' (fa-hal min muddakir); and 5 more.

matches.label: Who strikes the Sodom mob's eyes
matches.note: The mob blinded at Lot's door. Genesis: ʾayyēh hā-ʾănāšîm ... hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wə-nēḏəʿāh ʾōṯām; the angels (hā-ʾănāšîm) strike them bas-sanwērîm and they weary themselves finding the door. Quran: wa-la-qad rāwadūhu ʿan ḍayfihi fa-ṭamasnā aʿyunahum fa-dhūqū ʿadhābī wa-nudhur (God says 'We blotted out their eyes'). The striking passes from the angel-guests to God himself, and the search for the door is dropped.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 41 more.

Only in Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne: 'Ad were destroyed by a furious wind for seven nights and eight days, lying felled like hollow palm trunks; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears; That day eight (angels) bear the Throne of your Lord above them; At a single blast on the trumpet, the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing; Thamud were destroyed by the Overwhelming (al-tagiya, the Blast); Rhetorical opening: 'The Reality (al-haqqa)! What is the Reality? And what will make you know what the Reality is?'; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne [divergence between the texts]; The overturned city (al-mu'tafika, Sodom) God hurled down and covered with what covered it; A roaring cold wind (sarsar) on a day of continuous ill omen plucks men away like trunks of uprooted palms; The sky splits and is frail that day, and the angels are on its borders; When the Event (al-waqi'a) befalls, none can deny it: it abases and exalts; and 4 more.

sides.note: Who is saved. Gen: bōʾ-ʾattāh wə-khol-bêtəkhā ʾel-hat-tēvāh; Nōaḥ û-vānāyw wə-ʾištô û-nəšê-vānāyw, his household. Q: fa-anjaynāhu wa-lladhīna maʿahu fī l-fulki, 'those with him', a community of believers rather than a family (cf. Q 11:46, where a son drowns).

leads.title: Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah ↔ The plot against the prophet and the worship of the pagans
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky' (weight 6.7); God will not punish a people while the prophet is among them or while they seek forgiveness (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; Lot's family is saved at the time before dawn (bi-sahar) while a storm of stones (hasib) destroys the rest; and 40 more.

Only in The plot against the prophet and the worship of the pagans: Fight them until there is no persecution (fitna) and religion is wholly God's; If unbelievers desist, what is past is forgiven; God separates the bad from the good, heaps the bad on one another and casts them into hell; The pagans' prayer at the House was only whistling and clapping; People dismiss the prophet: 'Is he not just a maker of parables (memashel meshalim)?'; Whether the righteous among a guilty people shield it from punishment [contrast between the texts]; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10); God's plotting (makr / kayd) outwits the schemers; none is safe from it but the losers; Unbelievers plot to confine, kill or expel the prophet, but God plots too; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal.

leads.title: Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman ↔ Adam, the angels and Iblis
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 3 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The first man names the animals (weight 6.7); The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden (weight 5.8); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6). Pair score 38.1.

Only in Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman: Eating the forbidden fruit is threatened with death; The first human is put in the garden to work and guard it; Man leaves father and mother and cleaves to his wife; they become one flesh; A mist or spring rises from the earth to water the ground; First couple naked and not ashamed; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; Forming a creature from earth and breathing life into it [divergence between the texts]; Four rivers in the Garden [divergence between the texts]; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The human condition on earth after the expulsion [divergence between the texts]; The office given to humans on earth at creation [divergence between the texts]; The tempter in the garden [divergence between the texts]; Whoever sheds human blood, by man shall his blood be shed, because humans bear God's image; and 7 more.

matches.label: The first man and the names of the creatures
matches.note: Who knows the names is reversed. Gen 2:19 wa-yyābēʾ ʾel hā-ʾādām lirʾôt mah yyiqrāʾ lô ... wa-yyiqrāʾ hā-ʾādām šēmôt: God brings the animals 'to see what he would call them' and the man invents the names; Q 2:31 wa-ʿallama ādama l-asmāʾa kullahā thumma ʿaraḍahum ʿalā l-malāʾikati: God teaches Adam all the names and displays the creatures to the angels as a test, ending innī aʿlamu ghayba s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ (2:33). Human initiative before an observing God becomes knowledge given by an all-knowing God, and the scene becomes a contest with the angels.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever (weight 4.4). Pair score 4.4.

Only in Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman: Eating the forbidden fruit is threatened with death; The first human is put in the garden to work and guard it; Man leaves father and mother and cleaves to his wife; they become one flesh; A mist or spring rises from the earth to water the ground; First couple naked and not ashamed; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; The first man names the animals; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; and 21 more.

Only in Call to worship the Creator; the challenge; paradise and the gnat: God is not ashamed to strike a parable of a gnat or something smaller; Fruits in paradise resemble those of earth: 'this is what we were given before'; A challenge to rivals to prove a divine claim [divergence between the texts]; God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; The people break the covenant God made with them; Humans were dead, given life, will die and be given life again (two deaths, two lives); God stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain; Hell's fire has men and stones as its fuel; The blessed have purified spouses (azwaj mutahhara) in paradise; God summons the coastlands and nations (and their gods) to a court trial to argue their case; God fashions seven heavens; Inimitability challenge: produce a surah like it, calling on your own witnesses (tahaddi); and 2 more.

leads.title: Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman ↔ One soul, the wombs, orphans' property and the bride-gift
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How the first woman was made [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); First woman made from the man's rib or side while he sleeps (weight 6.0); Humankind is created from a single soul, from which its mate was made to dwell with it (weight 5.6). Pair score 18.3.

Only in Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman: Eating the forbidden fruit is threatened with death; The first human is put in the garden to work and guard it; Man leaves father and mother and cleaves to his wife; they become one flesh; A mist or spring rises from the earth to water the ground; First couple naked and not ashamed; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; The first man names the animals; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; and 19 more.

Only in One soul, the wombs, orphans' property and the bride-gift: Those who devour orphans' property devour fire into their bellies; Fear God, by whom you ask of one another, and the wombs (kinship ties, al-arḥām); Kin, orphans and the poor present at the division of an estate are given something from it; Property is not handed to the feeble-minded (sufahāʾ); they are fed and clothed from it; Women as well as men receive a fixed share of what parents and kin leave; The husband gives the bride her marriage gift (ṣaduqa, ajr) as her own; she may freely remit part; God hears the cry of the oppressed widow and orphan and punishes measure for measure; Do not enter the fields of the fatherless, for their redeemer (go'el) is strong and will plead their cause; A man may marry two, three or four wives, or only one if he fears injustice; A man who seduces an unbetrothed virgin must marry her or pay the bride-price; Who receives the marriage payment [divergence between the texts]; Divine blessing: be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth; and 2 more.

matches.note: Gen 2:21-23 wa-yyappēl ... tardēmâ ... wa-yyiqqaḥ ʾaḥat mi-ṣṣalʿōtāyw ... wa-yyiben ... ʾet ha-ṣṣēlāʿ ... lĕ-ʾiššâ ... kî mē-ʾîš luqŏḥâ zōʾt: God puts the man to sleep and builds the woman from his rib; she is named 'woman' because taken from 'man'; Q 4:1 khalaqakum min nafsin wāḥidatin wa-khalaqa minhā zawjahā wa-baththa minhumā rijālan kathīran wa-nisāʾan: created from one soul, and from it its mate. Woman from the first human is kept; sleep, rib and the wordplay are left out, the first human is a gender-neutral 'soul' (nafs, grammatically feminine), and the address is to all people (yā ayyuhā n-nās).

matches.label: Four rivers in the Garden
matches.note: Four rivers in the Garden. Genesis: wə-nāhār yōṣēʾ mē-ʿēḏen ... wə-hāyâ lə-ʾarbāʿâ rāʾšîm: one river splits into four named geographic rivers, Pishon, Gihon, Ḥiddeqel, Pərāṯ, flowing to lands of gold and onyx. Quran: four rivers of four substances (water that does not go stale, milk, wine, purified honey), with no names or geography. cf. 2 Enoch 8:5 for rivers of honey, milk, oil and wine.

leads.title: Birth of Isaac and expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael ↔ Abraham's prayer at the sacred house (Surah 14:35-41)
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Abraham settles some of his offspring in a barren valley by God's sacred House [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Abraham thanks God for giving him Ishmael and Isaac in old age [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Abraham prays that the town be made secure and its people provided with fruits (weight 6.3). Pair score 19.7.

Only in Birth of Isaac and expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael: Mother lays her dying child under a bush and sits a bowshot away weeping; Slave-wife and her son expelled at the wife's demand; The outcast son grows up in the wilderness as an archer; A great feast on the day the child is weaned; God opens a woman's eyes to see a well in the desert that saves her child; Promised son born to aged parents at the appointed time; Whether Ishmael is with Abraham or sent away [contrast between the texts]; In labor the mother wishes she had died before this and been utterly forgotten; When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered; Mistreated slave-woman flees or is sent into the wilderness; Circumcision on the eighth day after birth; God promises to make the patriarch a great nation; and 3 more.

Only in Abraham's prayer at the sacred house (Surah 14:35-41): Abraham prays that he and his sons be kept from worshipping idols; Abraham prays that people's hearts yearn toward his offspring at the sanctuary; Abraham settles some of his offspring in a barren valley by God's sacred House; Abraham thanks God for giving him Ishmael and Isaac in old age; Abraham prayed for his father's forgiveness only by a promise, and disowned him when he proved God's enemy.

matches.label: Abraham settles some of his offspring in a barren valley by God's sacred House
matches.note: Expulsion becomes settlement. Gen: Sarah demands gārēš hāʾāmâ hazzōʾt wəʾet-bənāh kî lōʾ yîraš; Abraham, grieved, sends Hagar off with bread and a skin of water, and she wanders bəmidbar bəʾēr šābaʿ, then Paran. Q: Abraham himself says innī askantu min dhurriyyatī bi-wādin ghayri dhī zarʿin ʿinda baytika l-muḥarram li-yuqīmū ṣ-ṣalāh. Sarah's motive and the inheritance quarrel are gone, and a sanctuary is added.

passages.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם גָּרֵ֛שׁ הָאָמָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את וְאֶת בְּנָ֑הּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִירַשׁ֙ בֶּן הָאָמָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את עִם בְּנִ֖י עִם יִצְחָֽק

رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّىٓ أَسْكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِى بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِى زَرْعٍ عِندَ بَيْتِكَ ٱلْمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ وَٱرْزُقْهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ

matches.label: Abraham thanks God for giving him Ishmael and Isaac in old age
matches.note: Gen: the son of old age is Isaac alone (bēn lizqunāyw ... ben-məʾat šānâ), and Ishmael is set apart, kî bəyiṣḥāq yiqqārēʾ ləkā zāraʿ / gam ʾet-ben-hāʾāmâ ləgôy ʾăśîmennû. Q: Abraham thanks God for both as one gift of old age, wahaba lī ʿalā l-kibari Ismāʿīla wa-Isḥāq, Ishmael first.

matches.label: In labor the mother wishes she had died before this and been utterly forgotten
matches.note: Same sequence. A lone mother in a remote place despairs over death (ʾal-ʾerʾeh bəmôt hayyāled ... wattēbk / yā laytanī mittu qabla hādhā). A voice calls to her and says do not fear or grieve (wayyiqrāʾ malʾak ʾĕlōhîm ʾel-hāgār ... ʾal-tîrʾî / fa-nādāhā min taḥtihā allā taḥzanī). God provides water (wattēreʾ bəʾēr māyim / jaʿala rabbuki taḥtaki sariyyā). Changes: the voice comes 'from heaven' in Gen and 'from beneath her' in Q; Hagar fears for a living child, Maryam is in labor; Q adds the palm's dates.

matches.label: Whether Ishmael is with Abraham or sent away
matches.note: Gen 21:14 wa-yyiqqaḥ leḥem wĕ-ḥēmat mayim ... wĕ-ʾet ha-yyeled wa-yšallĕḥehā: Abraham sends Ishmael away with his mother, and only God's promise follows him (21:13 gam ʾet ben hā-ʾāmâ lĕ-gôy ʾăśîmennû); Q 2:125-128 ʿahidnā ilā ibrāhīma wa-ismāʿīla an ṭahhirā baytiya ... rabbanā wa-jʿalnā muslimayni laka: Ishmael is with Abraham as co-builder and co-petitioner, under the same covenant charge (ʿahidnā). matches.note: Placement of the 'test'. Gen opens with it, wə-hā-ʾĕlōhîm nissâ ʾeṯ-ʾaḇrāhām, so the reader knows from the start that it is a trial. Q names it only after the rescue: inna hādhā la-huwa l-balāʾu l-mubīn. Gen's closing reason, kî ʿattâ yāḏaʿtî kî-yərēʾ ʾĕlōhîm ʾattâ (now I know, 22:12), has no counterpart: in Q God does not come to know.

passages.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְהָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים נִסָּ֖ה אֶת אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַבְרָהָ֖ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי
إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْبَلَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْمُبِينُ

matches.label: God commands a father to sacrifice his son
matches.note: How the command comes. Gen: direct divine speech, qaḥ-nāʾ ʾeṯ-binḵā ... wə-lek-ləḵā ʾel-ʾereṣ ha-mmōriyyâ wə-haʿălēhû šām lə-ʿōlâ (a burnt offering at a named place). Q: a dream reported by the father, innī arā fī l-manāmi annī adhbaḥuka (I see in sleep that I slaughter you), with no place, no mountain and no ʿōlâ. Q's dhabaḥa is cognate with Hebrew zāḇaḥ, while Gen uses ʿōlâ and liš-ḥōṭ (22:10).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר קַח נָ֠א אֶת בִּנְךָ֨ אֶת יְחִֽידְךָ֤ אֲשֶׁר אָהַ֨בְתָּ֙ אֶת יִצְחָ֔ק וְלֶךְ לְךָ֔ אֶל אֶ֖רֶץ הַמֹּרִיָּ֑ה וְהַעֲלֵ֤הוּ שָׁם֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה עַ֚ל אַחַ֣ד הֶֽהָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ

matches.label: Who the son to be sacrificed is and how he is named
matches.note: Who the son is. Gen names him three times over: ʾeṯ-binḵā ʾeṯ-yəḥîḏəḵā ʾăšer-ʾāhaḇtā ʾeṯ-yiṣḥāq. Q has only bi-ghulāmin ḥalīm (a forbearing boy) and announces Isaac only after the episode, wa-basharnāhu bi-Isḥāqa nabiyyan mina ṣ-ṣāliḥīn (37:112). This leaves the victim unnamed, and many exegetes read him as Ishmael. The 'only' (yāḥîḏ) son of Gen is not said.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר קַח נָ֠א אֶת בִּנְךָ֨ אֶת יְחִֽידְךָ֤ אֲשֶׁר אָהַ֨בְתָּ֙ אֶת יִצְחָ֔ק וְלֶךְ לְךָ֔ אֶל אֶ֖רֶץ הַמֹּרִיָּ֑ה וְהַעֲלֵ֤הוּ שָׁם֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה עַ֚ל אַחַ֣ד הֶֽהָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ
فَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ حَلِيمٍ
وَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِإِسْحَٰقَ نَبِيًّا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

matches.label: What the son to be sacrificed knows and says
matches.note: Who speaks, and what the son knows. Gen: Isaac does not know. He asks hinnēh hā-ʾēš wə-hā-ʿēṣîm wə-ʾayyēh ha-śśeh lə-ʿōlâ, and Abraham gives the veiled answer ʾĕlōhîm yirʾeh-lô ha-śśeh ... bənî. Q: the father tells him openly and asks his view, fa-nẓur mādhā tarā, and the son consents, yā-abati fʿal mā tuʾmaru sa-tajidunī in shāʾa llāhu mina ṣ-ṣābirīn. The address pair ʾāḇî / bənî matches yā-abati / yā-bunayya. Isaac's silence becomes the son's active submission.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִצְחָ֜ק אֶל אַבְרָהָ֤ם אָבִיו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֔י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֶּ֣נִּֽי בְנִ֑י וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה הָאֵשׁ֙ וְהָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאַיֵּ֥ה הַשֶּׂ֖ה לְעֹלָֽה
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֱלֹהִ֞ים יִרְאֶה לּ֥וֹ הַשֶּׂ֛ה לְעֹלָ֖ה בְּנִ֑י וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם יַחְדָּֽו

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ

matches.label: The father lays the son down for the sacrifice
matches.note: The act. Gen: wood laid on Isaac, fire and knife, an altar built, wa-yyaʿăqōḏ ʾeṯ-yiṣḥāq bənô wa-yyāśem ʾōṯô ʿal-ha-mmizbēaḥ mi-mmaʿal lā-ʿēṣîm, knife raised. Q: fa-lammā aslamā wa-tallahu li-l-jabīn, both 'submitted' and he laid him on his brow. No binding (ʿăqēḏâ), no altar, no wood, no fire and no three-day journey. The decisive word is the dual aslamā (both of them submitted).

passages.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת עֲצֵ֣י הָעֹלָ֗ה וַיָּ֨שֶׂם֙ עַל יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת הָאֵ֖שׁ וְאֶת הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֑לֶת וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם יַחְדָּֽו

וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ אֶֽל הַמָּקוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֒ וַיִּ֨בֶן שָׁ֤ם אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֶת הָעֵצִ֑ים וַֽיַּעֲקֹד֙ אֶת יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם אֹתוֹ֙ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ מִמַּ֖עַל לָעֵצִֽים
וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת יָד֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֑לֶת לִשְׁחֹ֖ט אֶת בְּנֽוֹ
فَلَمَّآ أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُۥ لِلْجَبِينِ

matches.label: Who stops the sacrifice of the son, and why
matches.note: Who stops it, and why. Gen: wa-yyiqrāʾ ʾēlâw malʾaḵ YHWH min-ha-ššāmayim ... ʾaḇrāhām ʾaḇrāhām wa-yyōʾmer hinnēnî; ʾal-tišlaḥ yāḏəḵā ʾel-ha-nnaʿar, because Abraham fears God. Q: wa-nādaynāhu an yā-Ibrāhīmu qad ṣaddaqta r-ruʾyā. God calls in the first person plural, with no angel and no hinnēnî. The reason is that Abraham has already fulfilled the dream, not a prohibition.

passages.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֵלָ֜יו מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ מִן הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֣ם אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַל תִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל הַנַּ֔עַר וְאַל תַּ֥עַשׂ ל֖וֹ מְא֑וּמָּה כִּ֣י עַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי יְרֵ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ אַ֔תָּה וְלֹ֥א חָשַׂ֛כְתָּ אֶת בִּנְךָ֥ אֶת יְחִידְךָ֖ מִמֶּֽנִּי
وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ أَن يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَآ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

matches.label: What is offered in place of the son, and who provides it
matches.note: The substitute. Gen: Abraham looks up, sees ʾayil ʾaḥar neʾĕḥaz ba-ssəḇaḵ bə-qarnâw, and offers it ʿōlâ taḥaṯ bənô; he then names the place YHWH yirʾeh. Q: wa-fadaynāhu bi-dhibḥin ʿaẓīm. God himself ransoms (fadā) with a 'great sacrifice', the animal is unnamed, Abraham does not find it, and there is no place-name or temple-mount aetiology.

passages.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ וְהִנֵּה אַ֔יִל אַחַ֕ר נֶאֱחַ֥ז בַּסְּבַ֖ךְ בְּקַרְנָ֑יו וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אַבְרָהָם֙ וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת הָאַ֔יִל וַיַּעֲלֵ֥הוּ לְעֹלָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת בְּנֽוֹ
וַיִּקְרָ֧א אַבְרָהָ֛ם שֵֽׁם הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא יְהוָ֣ה יִרְאֶ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ יֵאָמֵ֣ר הַיּ֔וֹם בְּהַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה יֵרָאֶֽה
وَفَدَيْنَٰهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ

matches.label: The reward and blessing after the averted sacrifice
matches.note: The reward. Gen: bî nišbaʿtî nəʾum-YHWH ... bārēḵ ʾăḇāreḵḵā wə-harbâ ʾarbeh ʾeṯ-zarʿăḵā ... wə-yiraš zarʿăḵā ʾēṯ šaʿar ʾōyəḇâw wə-hiṯbārăḵû ḇə-zarʿăḵā kōl gôyê hā-ʾāreṣ, an oath and the unconditional blessing of the seed. Q: salāmun ʿalā Ibrāhīm ... wa-bāraknā ʿalayhi wa-ʿalā Isḥāqa wa-min dhurriyyatihimā muḥsinun wa-ẓālimun li-nafsihi mubīn. There is no oath and no conquest of enemy gates, and the offspring are explicitly mixed, some doing good and some wronging themselves.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בִּ֥י נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֗י יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וְלֹ֥א חָשַׂ֖כְתָּ אֶת בִּנְךָ֥ אֶת יְחִידֶֽךָ
כִּֽי בָרֵ֣ךְ אֲבָרֶכְךָ֗ וְהַרְבָּ֨ה אַרְבֶּ֤ה אֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּכוֹכְבֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְכַח֕וֹל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל שְׂפַ֣ת הַיָּ֑ם וְיִרַ֣שׁ זַרְעֲךָ֔ אֵ֖ת שַׁ֥עַר אֹיְבָֽיו
וְהִתְבָּרֲכ֣וּ בְזַרְעֲךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ עֵ֕קֶב אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ בְּקֹלִֽי
وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
وَبَٰرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌ وَظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ مُبِينٌ

matches.label: Father binds his son on the altar and lifts the knife

فَلَمَّآ أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُۥ لِلْجَبِينِ

leads.title: Abraham's servant finds Rebekah for Isaac ↔ Times of privacy, elderly women, eating in kin houses, leave from the messenger
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: On entering houses greet one another with a blessed greeting from God (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Abraham's servant finds Rebekah for Isaac: God sends his angel ahead to guide the journey; Departing bride blessed to become thousands of myriads; The bride is asked and consents to go ('I will go'); Son brings bride into his dead mother's tent and is comforted; Patriarch goes out to meditate (or pray) in the field at evening; A trusted servant is sent abroad to find a bride for the master's son; Hero asks God for a specific sign to identify the right person (who will offer water); Bride given a gold nose-ring and bracelets; Father insists his son's wife come from his own kin, not the local women; Bride covers herself with a veil on seeing the groom; Oath sworn by placing the hand under the thigh of the one demanding it; Descendants will possess the gate of their enemies; and 5 more.

Only in Times of privacy, elderly women, eating in kin houses, leave from the messenger: Do not address the messenger as you address one another, nor slip away without his leave; Elderly women past hope of marriage may lay aside their outer garments without displaying adornment; No blame on the blind, lame, sick or anyone eating in the houses of listed relatives or friends, together or apart; Slaves and children must ask permission at three times of undress: before dawn prayer, at noon and after the night prayer; Whether the blind and the lame may enter the house or share its table [contrast between the texts]; You may eat your fill in a neighbor's vineyard or pluck ears by hand, but not carry away or use a sickle; Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind; Creditor must wait outside for the pledge and return a poor man's cloak by sunset.

וַיְגָ֖רֶשׁ אֶת הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן עֵ֜דֶן אֶת הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֨רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת לִשְׁמֹ֕ר אֶת דֶּ֖רֶךְ עֵ֥ץ הַֽחַיִּֽים
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

matches.label: Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden
matches.note: Gen 3:15 wĕ-ʾêbâ ʾāšît bênkā û-bên hā-ʾiššâ û-bên zarʿăkā û-bên zarʿāh: enmity between serpent and woman and their offspring; Q 2:36 ihbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun: 'some of you enemies to others' among those sent down. The same decree of enmity (ʾêbâ / ʿaduww) at the expulsion, with the serpent gone.

passages.text: וְאֵיבָ֣ה אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: The human condition on earth after the expulsion
matches.note: Gen 3:17-19 ʾărûrâ hā-ʾădāmâ baʿăbûrekā bĕ-ʿiṣṣābôn tōʾkălennâ ... ʿad šûbĕkā ʾel hā-ʾădāmâ: cursed ground, toil and death; Q 2:36 wa-lakum fī l-arḍi mustaqarrun wa-matāʿun ilā ḥīn: on earth an abode and provision for a time. The curses on ground, woman and serpent are left out; the earth is a lodging and a time limit, not a curse.

passages.text: וּלְאָדָ֣ם אָמַ֗ר כִּֽי שָׁמַעְתָּ֮ לְק֣וֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ֒ וַתֹּ֨אכַל֙ מִן הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּיתִ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֲרוּרָ֤ה הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּֽעֲבוּרֶ֔ךָ בְּעִצָּבוֹן֙ תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ
בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance)
matches.note: The ending changes. Gen 3:12 hā-ʾiššâ ʾăšer nātattâ ʿimmādî hîʾ nātĕnâ-llî min hā-ʿēṣ wā-ʾōkēl: the man blames the woman (and God who gave her), with no repentance or pardon; Q 2:37 fa-talaqqā ādamu min rabbihi kalimātin fa-tāba ʿalayhi innahu huwa t-tawwābu r-raḥīm: Adam receives words and God turns to him in forgiveness before the descent. The Quran adds a reconciliation Genesis does not have.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה לִּ֥י מִן הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל
فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

matches.label: A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden
matches.note: Q 2:35 wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi sh-shajarata 'do not come near this tree' is God's own wording; in Genesis the extension is the woman's addition: Gen 3:3 lōʾ tōʾkĕlû mimmennû wĕ-lōʾ tiggĕʿû bô 'nor touch it', which God had not said (2:17).

passages.text: וּמִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן֒ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְלֹ֥א תִגְּע֖וּ בּ֑וֹ פֶּן תְּמֻתֽוּן
وَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

passages.text: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַנָּחָ֖שׁ אֶל הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה לֹֽא מ֖וֹת תְּמֻתֽוּן
כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע

sides.note: arum (cunning) puns on arummim (naked), 2:25

passages.text: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

sides.note: the tempter is al-shaytan, not a serpent

matches.label: God speaks in the plural (us, our) as if to a divine council

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע וְעַתָּ֣ה פֶּן יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם

sides.note: 'like one of us'

passages.text: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
وَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

leads.title: The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion ↔ Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent
leads.summary: 5 correspondences read side by side: 5 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Fig leaves sewn into coverings (weight 6.3); Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck (weight 6.3); Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked (weight 6.3); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); A tree whose fruit gives eternal life (weight 5.4). Pair score 68.9.

Only in The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion: Each accused shifts blame to another (man to woman, woman to serpent); First woman named as mother of all living; God heard walking in the garden in the breeze of the day; Humans gain divine knowledge and God fears they will also gain immortality; Woman punished with pain in childbirth and subordination to husband; The woman eats first and gives the fruit to her husband; Cherubim and a flaming turning sword guard the way to the tree of life; Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; God makes garments of skin for the first couple; God makes garments of skin for the first couple [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

Only in Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent: God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat; Whoever turned from God's reminder is raised blind on judgment day: as he forgot the signs, so he is forgotten; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays'; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; God commands the angels to prostrate to Adam; all do except Iblis, who refuses; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there.

Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Arabic.

matches.label: A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit
matches.note: Who tempts whom. Gen: wəhannāḥāš hāyâ ʿārûm ... wayyōʾmer ʾel-hāʾiššâ, a clever beast addressing the woman. Q: fa-waswasa ilayhi sh-shayṭānu qāla yā Ādamu, Satan, already marked as enemy after refusing to bow (inna hādhā ʿaduwwun laka wa-li-zawjik), addressing Adam. The serpent and the woman as first addressee drop out.

passages.text: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַנָּחָ֖שׁ אֶל הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה לֹֽא מ֖וֹת תְּמֻתֽוּן
وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ
فَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَٰذَا عَدُوٌّ لَّكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰٓ
فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ

matches.label: The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays'
matches.note: What the tree offers. Gen: knowledge, wihyîtem kēʾlōhîm yōdəʿê ṭôb wārāʿ; immortality belongs to a second tree that God guards, pen-yišlaḥ yādô wəlāqaḥ gam mēʿēṣ haḥayyîm wəʾākal wāḥay ləʿōlām. Q: the tempter names the forbidden tree itself shajarati l-khuldi wa-mulkin lā yablā. Gen's two trees merge into one, and the lure becomes eternal life and kingship, not godlike knowledge.

passages.text: כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע וְעַתָּ֣ה פֶּן יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם
فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ

matches.label: Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked
matches.note: wattōʾkal wattittēn gam-ləʾîšāh ... wayyōʾkal wattippāqaḥnâ ʿênê šənêhem wayyēdəʿû kî ʿêrummim hēm wayyitpərû ʿălēh təʾēnâ; fa-akalā minhā fa-badat lahumā sawʾātuhumā wa-ṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-janna. Same sequence: eating, exposed nakedness, sewing leaves. Changes: in Gen the woman eats first and hands it on, while Q has both eat and puts the blame on Adam (wa-ʿaṣā Ādamu rabbahu fa-ghawā); fig leaves become just 'leaves of the garden'.

passages.text: וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁ֡ה כִּ֣י טוֹב֩ הָעֵ֨ץ לְמַאֲכָ֜ל וְכִ֧י תַֽאֲוָה ה֣וּא לָעֵינַ֗יִם וְנֶחְמָ֤ד הָעֵץ֙ לְהַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַתִּקַּ֥ח מִפִּרְי֖וֹ וַתֹּאכַ֑ל וַתִּתֵּ֧ן גַּם לְאִישָׁ֛הּ עִמָּ֖הּ וַיֹּאכַֽל
וַתִּפָּקַ֨חְנָה֙ עֵינֵ֣י שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י עֵֽירֻמִּ֖ם הֵ֑ם וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ֙ עֲלֵ֣ה תְאֵנָ֔ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם חֲגֹרֹֽת

matches.label: Humans return to the earth they were taken from (and, in the Quran, are brought out of it again)
matches.note: Return to dust, read as the end or as a step. Genesis: ʿaḏ šûḇəḵā ʾel hā-ʾăḏāmâ ... kî ʿāp̄ār ʾattâ wə-ʾel ʿāp̄ār tāšûḇ (the sentence ends with the return to dust). Deniers in Q 50:3: a-idhā mitnā wa-kunnā turāban dhālika rajʿun baʿīd (when we are dust, that would be a far-fetched return), answered by 50:4 and by the rain-revived land, ka-dhālika l-khurūj (50:11). The 'return' (šûḇ / rajʿ) to dust in Genesis becomes, in the Quran, the disputed return from dust.

passages.text: בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב
أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا ذَٰلِكَ رَجْعٌۢ بَعِيدٌ

leads.title: The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion ↔ The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall
leads.summary: 10 correspondences read side by side: 8 deliberately changed, 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Which of the first couple is tempted and eats first [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); First humans expelled from the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?' (weight 6.3); Humans return to the earth they were taken from (and, in the Quran, are brought out of it again) [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck (weight 6.3); Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Fig leaves sewn into coverings (weight 6.3); Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked (weight 6.3); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden (weight 5.8). Pair score 94.8.

Only in The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion: Each accused shifts blame to another (man to woman, woman to serpent); First woman named as mother of all living; God heard walking in the garden in the breeze of the day; Humans gain divine knowledge and God fears they will also gain immortality; Woman punished with pain in childbirth and subordination to husband; The woman eats first and gives the fruit to her husband; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts]; Cherubim and a flaming turning sword guard the way to the tree of life; Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; God makes garments of skin for the first couple; and 12 more.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.

leads.finding: A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit

units.title: The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion
The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall

matches.label: A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit
matches.note: A different tempter. Gen: wə-han-nāḥāš hāyāh ʿārûm mik-kōl ḥayyat haś-śādeh, an animal speaking to the woman. Q: fa-waswasa lahumā l-shayṭānu, the devil already expelled in 7:13, whispering to both, and he swears an oath (wa-qāsamahumā innī lakumā la-mina l-nāṣiḥīna). There is no serpent and no curse to crawl on the belly (Gen 3:14).

passages.text: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַנָּחָ֖שׁ אֶל הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה לֹֽא מ֖וֹת תְּמֻתֽוּן
כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ
وَقَاسَمَهُمَآ إِنِّى لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

matches.label: The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals
matches.note: What the tempter promises. Gen: wi-hyîtem kē-ʾlōhîm yōdəʿê ṭôv wā-rāʿ, and God himself confirms the danger: hēn hā-ʾādām hāyāh kə-ʾaḥad mimmennû ... wā-ḥay lə-ʿōlām. Q: mā nahākumā rabbukumā ʿan hādhihi l-shajarati illā an takūnā malakayni aw takūnā mina l-khālidīna. 'Like gods knowing good and evil' becomes 'angels or immortals', a lie (bi-ghurūrin). Q has no divine admission that the humans have become 'like one of us'.

passages.text: כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע וְעַתָּ֣ה פֶּן יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

matches.label: Which of the first couple is tempted and eats first
matches.note: Who is tempted and eats first. Gen: the serpent talks to the woman (wa-yyōʾmer ʾel-hā-ʾiššāh), she eats first and gives to her husband (wat-tittēn gam-lə-ʾîšāh ʿimmāh wa-yyōʾkhal). Q uses the dual throughout: wa-zawjuka ... fa-kulā ... wa-lā taqrabā ... waswasa lahumā ... fa-lammā dhāqā l-shajarata. The couple acts together and the woman is not singled out.

passages.text: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל הַנָּחָ֑שׁ מִפְּרִ֥י עֵֽץ הַגָּ֖ן נֹאכֵֽל
וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁ֡ה כִּ֣י טוֹב֩ הָעֵ֨ץ לְמַאֲכָ֜ל וְכִ֧י תַֽאֲוָה ה֣וּא לָעֵינַ֗יִם וְנֶחְמָ֤ד הָעֵץ֙ לְהַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַתִּקַּ֥ח מִפִּרְי֖וֹ וַתֹּאכַ֑ל וַתִּתֵּ֧ן גַּם לְאִישָׁ֛הּ עִמָּ֖הּ וַיֹּאכַֽל
وَيَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ فَكُلَا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?'
matches.note: God's question. Gen: the couple hide (wa-yyitḥabbēʾ hā-ʾādām wə-ʾištô), God walks in the garden and calls ʾayyekkāh, then ha-min-hā-ʿēṣ ... ʾākhāltā. Q: wa-nādāhumā rabbuhumā a-lam anhakumā ʿan tilkumā l-shajarati wa-aqul lakumā inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduwwun mubīnun. No hiding and no walking God; the question is a reminder of a warning given.

passages.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶת ק֨וֹל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּגָּ֖ן לְר֣וּחַ הַיּ֑וֹם וַיִּתְחַבֵּ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם וְאִשְׁתּ֗וֹ מִפְּנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיִּקְרָ֛א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ אַיֶּֽכָּה
וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֚י הִגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עֵירֹ֖ם אָ֑תָּה הֲמִן הָעֵ֗ץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר צִוִּיתִ֛יךָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י אֲכָל מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אָכָֽלְתָּ

فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing
matches.note: The decisive reversal. Gen: hā-ʾiššāh ʾăšer nātattāh ʿimmādî hiwʾ nātənāh-llî; han-nāḥāš hiššîʾanî, the man blames the woman (and God), the woman the serpent. Q: qālā rabbanā ẓalamnā anfusanā wa-in lam taghfir lanā wa-tarḥamnā la-nakūnanna mina l-khāsirīna. Both confess together and ask forgiveness. Blame-shifting gives way to joint repentance, and the blame-shifter in Q is Iblis (fa-bi-mā aghwaytanī, 7:16).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה לִּ֥י מִן הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה הַנָּחָ֥שׁ הִשִּׁיאַ֖נִי וָאֹכֵֽל
قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَآ أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

matches.label: Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck
matches.note: Gen: wə-ʾêvāh ʾāšît bênkhā û-vên hā-ʾiššāh û-vên zarʿăkhā û-vên zarʿāh, enmity set by God between serpent and woman and their seed. Q: qāla hbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun, plural, a mutual enmity of those sent down (humans and Satan, 7:22 inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduww). There are no curses on the woman (childbirth, 3:16) or the ground (3:17-19).

passages.text: וְאֵיבָ֣ה אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב
قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: Humans return to the earth they were taken from (and, in the Quran, are brought out of it again)
matches.note: Gen: ʿad šûvəkhā ʾel-hā-ʾădāmāh kî mimmennāh luqqāḥtā kî-ʿāfār ʾattāh wə-ʾel-ʿāfār tāšûv, from dust and back to dust, as a curse. Q: fīhā taḥyawna wa-fīhā tamūtūna wa-minhā tukhrajūna. Q adds the third step, resurrection from the earth.

passages.text: בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב
قَالَ فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ

matches.label: First humans expelled from the garden
matches.note: Gen: wa-yšalləḥēhû ... wa-ygāreš ʾet-hā-ʾādām, with cherubim and the flaming sword guarding the tree of life, lest he eat and live forever. Q: ihbiṭū ... wa-lakum fī l-arḍi mustaqarrun wa-matāʿun ilā ḥīnin. A descent to a temporary home, with no guard, no tree of life and no fear of human immortality.

passages.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִגַּן עֵ֑דֶן לַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֻקַּ֖ח מִשָּֽׁם
וַיְגָ֖רֶשׁ אֶת הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן עֵ֜דֶן אֶת הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֨רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת לִשְׁמֹ֕ר אֶת דֶּ֖רֶךְ עֵ֥ץ הַֽחַיִּֽים

leads.title: The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion ↔ Children of Adam - clothing, Satan's enmity, what God forbids
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God makes garments of skin for the first couple (weight 6.7); God makes garments of skin for the first couple [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion: Each accused shifts blame to another (man to woman, woman to serpent); First woman named as mother of all living; God heard walking in the garden in the breeze of the day; Humans gain divine knowledge and God fears they will also gain immortality; Woman punished with pain in childbirth and subordination to husband; The woman eats first and gives the fruit to her husband; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts]; Cherubim and a flaming turning sword guard the way to the tree of life; Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts]; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; and 25 more.

Only in Children of Adam - clothing, Satan's enmity, what God forbids: Wear your adornment (clothing) at every place of prostration; Satan and his tribe see humans from where humans cannot see them; Satan pulled off the first couple's garments to show them their nakedness; Eat and drink but do not be excessive; God sends down clothing to cover nakedness, and the 'garment of piety' is better; God's adornments and good provisions are not forbidden to believers; Short list of what God truly forbids: indecencies open and hidden, sin, oppression, associating partners, false speech about God; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; Clothing at every altar or place of prostration; Nakedness must be covered at the place of worship; Every nation has a fixed term that cannot be advanced or delayed by an hour; Unbelievers defend their practice as what they found their fathers doing.

leads.title: Jacob's flight from Laban and the theft of the teraphim ↔ Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Brothers pursued and accused of theft (weight 5.8); Search proceeds through the others' bags before the youngest's (weight 5.8). Pair score 11.5.

Only in Jacob's flight from Laban and the theft of the teraphim: In a dream an angel shows the hero the striped and speckled he-goats mounting the flock; God commands the exile to return to the land of his fathers; Idols hidden in a camel saddle on which a woman sits, claiming menstruation; Pursuer warned by God in a dream not to harm the fugitive; Hero unknowingly pronounces death on whoever stole the object, though it is his loved one; Hero flees secretly with wives, children and flocks while the father-in-law is away shearing; Shepherd made to bear the loss of animals torn by beasts; Shepherd's speech of grievance: twenty years of heat, frost, sleeplessness and bearing losses; Daughter steals her father's household idols (teraphim); Employer changed the hero's wages ten times, but God thwarted him; Daughters complain their father sold them and consumed their bride-price; A standing stone (matsevah) set up and anointed with oil; and 2 more.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 107 more.

matches.label: Search proceeds through the others' bags before the youngest's
matches.note: Same pattern with roles reversed: the accused patriarch rashly names the penalty, ʿim ʾăšer timṣāʾ ʾet-ʾĕlōhêkā lōʾ yiḥyeh, and the search goes tent by tent and ends with Rachel; jazāʾuhu man wujida fī raḥlihi ... fa-badaʾa bi-awʿiyatihim. Rachel, mother of Joseph and Benjamin, really did steal (wattignōb rāḥēl, 31:19). Q 12:77, in saraqa fa-qad saraqa akhun lahu min qabl, fixes an earlier theft on the same maternal line; cf. later haggadic explanations, not in either text.

וַיָּבֹ֨א לָבָ֜ן בְּאֹ֥הֶל יַעֲקֹ֣ב וּבְאֹ֣הֶל לֵאָ֗ה וּבְאֹ֛הֶל שְׁתֵּ֥י הָאֲמָהֹ֖ת וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֑א וַיֵּצֵא֙ מֵאֹ֣הֶל לֵאָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּאֹ֥הֶל רָחֵֽל
וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל אָבִ֗יהָ אַל יִ֨חַר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י כִּ֣י ל֤וֹא אוּכַל֙ לָק֣וּם מִפָּנֶ֔יךָ כִּי דֶ֥רֶךְ נָשִׁ֖ים לִ֑י וַיְחַפֵּ֕שׂ וְלֹ֥א מָצָ֖א אֶת הַתְּרָפִֽים

matches.note: Gen 32:33 ʿal kēn lōʾ yōʾkĕlû bĕnê yiśrāʾēl ʾet gîd ha-nnāšeh ... kî nāgaʿ bĕ-kap yerek yaʿăqōb: the sons of Israel do not eat the sinew because the divine wrestler struck Jacob's thigh, a custom 'to this day'; Q 3:93 kullu ṭ-ṭaʿāmi kāna ḥillan li-banī isrāʾīla illā mā ḥarrama isrāʾīlu ʿalā nafsihi min qabli an tunazzala t-tawrātu: all food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel (Jacob) forbade himself before the Torah. A pre-Sinai food taboo tied to Jacob/Israel in both; in Genesis it comes from God's touch and binds the descendants, in the Quran Israel imposes it on himself, and the point is that the later Torah food laws were not original (fa-ʾtū bi-t-tawrāti fa-tlūhā).

אַלּֽוּף קֹ֛רַח אַלּ֥וּף גַּעְתָּ֖ם אַלּ֣וּף עֲמָלֵ֑ק אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֤י אֱלִיפַז֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֔וֹם אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י עָדָֽה
אֵ֖לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֣י הַחֹרִ֑י אַלּ֤וּף לוֹטָן֙ אַלּ֣וּף שׁוֹבָ֔ל אַלּ֥וּף צִבְע֖וֹן אַלּ֥וּף עֲנָֽה
וַיָּ֖מָת הֲדָ֑ד וַיִּהְיוּ֙ אַלּוּפֵ֣י אֱד֔וֹם אַלּ֥וּף תִּמְנָ֛ע אַלּ֥וּף עליה עַֽלְוָ֖ה אַלּ֥וּף יְתֵֽת
אַלּ֧וּף אָהֳלִיבָמָ֛ה אַלּ֥וּף אֵלָ֖ה אַלּ֥וּף פִּינֹֽן
אַלּ֥וּף קְנַ֛ז אַלּ֥וּף תֵּימָ֖ן אַלּ֣וּף מִבְצָֽר

leads.summary: 13 correspondences read side by side: 11 deliberately changed, 2 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero sold for a small sum of silver [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); One brother talks the others out of killing him [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A wild animal is blamed for the hero's death [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Father loves the hero more than his brothers [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Father himself sends the hero to his brothers [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Family prostrates before the hero, fulfilling the dream [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero bought by an Egyptian official [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero cast into a pit or well [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A wild animal is blamed for the hero's death (weight 6.0); Brothers bring the hero's garment with false blood (weight 6.0); A passing caravan takes the hero from the pit (weight 6.0); One brother talks the others out of killing him (weight 6.0); Father loves the hero more than his brothers (weight 6.0); Hero sold for a small sum of silver (weight 6.0); Dream of sun, moon and eleven stars bowing to the hero (weight 6.0); Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero (weight 6.0); Hero cast into a pit or well (weight 5.8); Hero bought by an Egyptian official (weight 5.8). Pair score 133.1.

Only in Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt: Brothers sit down to eat bread after casting their brother into the pit; Hero's story begins when he is seventeen; Young hero brings bad reports of his brothers to their father; An anonymous man finds the wandering hero in the field and directs him; Dream of the brothers' sheaves bowing to the hero's sheaf; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort; Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind; Father himself sends the hero to his brothers; Evidence presented with the formula 'Please recognize (haker na)' whose is this; Father gives the hero a special garment; Called by name, the hero answers 'Here I am' (hineni).

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 88 more.
