matches.label: Animals taken aboard in pairs
matches.note: fa-sluk fīhā min kullin zawjayni thnayni ~ šənayim mi-kkōl tāvîʾ ʾel hat-tēvâ ... zākhār û-nəqēvâ: two of every kind. The Quran omits the sevens of clean animals (Gen 7:2), which prepare Noah's sacrifice.

leads.title: The Flood (full read) ↔ Moses and Aaron, Noah, Ad, Thamud, the People of the Rass and the rained-upon town
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); All others perish (weight 5.0). Pair score 11.0.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; God regrets having made humankind and is grieved in his heart; God himself shuts the vessel's door behind the hero; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; A raven is sent out and does not return (goes to and fro); Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Vessel has several decks, a side door and a roof opening or window; God sends a wind (ruah) over the earth to make the waters subside; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; and 44 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron, Noah, Ad, Thamud, the People of the Rass and the rained-upon town: The 'People of the Rass' (aṣḥāb al-rass, the well) named among destroyed peoples; Most unbelievers are like cattle, or even further astray; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; 'Do not go about after your heart and your eyes'; Ox knows its owner and the ass its master's crib, but Israel does not know (animals wiser than God's people); The sign the flood leaves for later generations [divergence between the texts]; The town that was rained on with an evil rain (Lot's) is passed by travelers; Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts]; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; The people mock God's messengers, despise his words and scoff at his prophets; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities; and 1 more.

matches.note: wa-qawma Nūḥin lammā kadhdhabū r-rusula aghraqnāhum ~ wa-yyimmaḥ ʾet kol hay-yəqûm ... wa-yyiššāʾer ʾak Nōaḥ: Genesis wipes out 'all flesh' for corruption; the Quran drowns 'the people of Noah' because they denied the messengers (in the plural, rusul).

passages.text: וַיִּגְוַ֞ע כָּל בָּשָׂ֣ר הָרֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל הָאָ֗רֶץ בָּע֤וֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּבַ֣חַיָּ֔ה וּבְכָל הַשֶּׁ֖רֶץ הַשֹּׁרֵ֣ץ עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכֹ֖ל הָאָדָֽם

וַיִּ֜מַח אֶֽת כָּל הַיְק֣וּם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֗ה מֵאָדָ֤ם עַד בְּהֵמָה֙ עַד רֶ֨מֶשׂ֙ וְעַד ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּמָּח֖וּ מִן הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִשָּׁ֧אֶר אַךְ נֹ֛חַ וַֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָֽה
وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَّمَّا كَذَّبُوا۟ ٱلرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ ءَايَةً وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا

matches.note: Who speaks first. In Genesis Noah never addresses God: God speaks (wa-yyōʾmer ʾĕlōhîm lə-nōaḥ, 6:13; wa-yyōʾmer YHWH lə-nōaḥ bōʾ-ʾattâ, 7:1), and God 'remembers' him (wa-yyizkōr ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ-nōaḥ, 8:1). matches.label: What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer
matches.note: Who sets the flood in motion. Genesis: wa-yyōʾmer ʾĕlōhîm lə-nōaḥ qēṣ kol bāśār bāʾ ləp̄ānay kî mālʾâ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās (God decides, because of violence, and tells Noah). Quran: kadhdhabat qablahum qawmu nūḥin fa-kadhdhabū ʿabdanā wa-qālū majnūnun wa-zdujira, fa-daʿā rabbahu annī maghlūbun fa-ntaṣir (Noah's people call him mad and drive him off; Noah prays 'I am overcome, help me'; then the flood). Added in the Quran: Noah as rejected messenger and his prayer; absent: ḥāmās as the cause and God's regret (6:6).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ
كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ فَكَذَّبُوا۟ عَبْدَنَا وَقَالُوا۟ مَجْنُونٌ وَٱزْدُجِرَ
فَدَعَا رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَغْلُوبٌ فَٱنتَصِرْ

matches.label: How the ark is described
matches.note: The ark. Genesis: tēḇaṯ ʿăṣê-ḡōp̄er qinnîm ... wə-ḵāp̄artā ʾōṯāh ... ba-kkōp̄er, šəlōš mēʾôṯ ʾammâ ʾōreḵ (gopher wood, rooms, pitch, measured in cubits). Quran: wa-ḥamalnāhu ʿalā dhāti alwāḥin wa-dusur, tajrī bi-aʿyuninā (a thing of planks and fibres/nails, running under our eyes). No name 'ark', no dimensions; the stress moves from building to God's watching eyes.

passages.text: עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ תֵּבַ֣ת עֲצֵי גֹ֔פֶר קִנִּ֖ים תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֶת הַתֵּבָ֑ה וְכָֽפַרְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֛הּ מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ בַּכֹּֽפֶר
וְזֶ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֹתָ֑הּ שְׁלֹ֧שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אַמָּ֗ה אֹ֚רֶךְ הַתֵּבָ֔ה חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ רָחְבָּ֔הּ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אַמָּ֖ה קוֹמָתָֽהּ
وَحَمَلْنَٰهُ عَلَىٰ ذَاتِ أَلْوَٰحٍ وَدُسُرٍ
تَجْرِى بِأَعْيُنِنَا جَزَآءً لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ

matches.label: Waters pour both from the sky and from springs of the earth
matches.note: The flood from heaven and from the earth's springs, with cognate words: nibqəʿû kol maʿyənôṯ təhôm rabbâ wa-ʾărubbōṯ haš-šāmayim nip̄tāḥû vs. fa-fataḥnā abwāba s-samāʾi bi-māʾin munhamirin wa-fajjarnā l-arḍa ʿuyūnan (p-t-ḥ / f-t-ḥ 'opened'; maʿyənôṯ / ʿuyūn 'springs'). Changed agent: in Genesis the springs 'burst' and the windows 'were opened' (passive); in the Quran God speaks: 'We opened ... We made the earth burst'. Windows (ʾărubbôṯ) become gates (abwāb).

passages.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כָּֽל מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וַאֲרֻבֹּ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נִפְתָּֽחוּ

أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِى لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا

matches.label: Destruction motivated by human wickedness or violence
matches.note: Motive changed: Genesis gives moral corruption and violence (rabbāh rāʿat hā-ʾādām ... wa-ttimmālēʾ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās; hišḥît kol bāśār ʾet darkô). Q 71 gives rejection of the messenger and idolatry: rabbi innahum ʿaṣawnī ... wa-qālū lā tadharunna ālihatakum wa-lā tadharunna waddan wa-lā suwāʿan wa-lā yaghūtha wa-yaʿūqa wa-nasrā. Five named gods; Genesis names no god but YHWH/Elohim.

passages.text: וַיַּ֣רְא יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י רַבָּ֛ה רָעַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְכָל יֵ֨צֶר֙ מַחְשְׁבֹ֣ת לִבּ֔וֹ רַ֥ק רַ֖ע כָּל הַיּֽוֹם
וַתִּשָּׁחֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ חָמָֽס
וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֣ה נִשְׁחָ֑תָה כִּֽי הִשְׁחִ֧ית כָּל בָּשָׂ֛ר אֶת דַּרְכּ֖וֹ עַל הָאָֽרֶץ
قَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِى وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَن لَّمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارًا
وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا
وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا۟ كَثِيرًا وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلًا

matches.label: Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents
matches.note: Who calls for destruction is reversed: in Genesis God decides alone (wa-yyōʾmer YHWH ʾemḥeh ʾet hā-ʾādām; we-hinnî mašḥîtām ʾet hā-ʾāreṣ) and even regrets creating (wa-yyinnāḥem YHWH). In Q 71:26-27 Noah asks: rabbi lā tadhar ʿalā l-arḍi mina l-kāfirīna dayyāran, innaka in tadharhum yuḍillū ʿibādaka. There is no divine regret in the Quran.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה אֶמְחֶ֨ה אֶת הָאָדָ֤ם אֲשֶׁר בָּרָ֨אתִי֙ מֵעַל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה מֵֽאָדָם֙ עַד בְּהֵמָ֔ה עַד רֶ֖מֶשׂ וְעַד ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כִּ֥י נִחַ֖מְתִּי כִּ֥י עֲשִׂיתִֽם
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ
وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا
إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا۟ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا فَاجِرًا كَفَّارًا

matches.label: Seek forgiveness and repent, and God will send the sky down on you in abundant rain
matches.note: Rain reversed: in Genesis rain from opened sky is the destruction (wa-ʾărubbōt ha-ššāmayim niftāḥû, wa-yehî ha-ggešem ʿal hā-ʾāreṣ ʾarbāʿîm yôm). Noah in Q 71:10-11 promises rain as blessing if they repent: istaghfirū rabbakum ... yursili s-samāʾa ʿalaykum midrāran, then (71:25) mimmā khaṭīʾātihim ughriqū: the sky that could have blessed them drowns them.

passages.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כָּֽל מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וַאֲרֻבֹּ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נִפְתָּֽחוּ
וַֽיְהִ֥י הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָֽיְלָה
فَقُلْتُ ٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارًا
يُرْسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيْكُم مِّدْرَارًا

matches.label: Hero's family saved with him
matches.note: The saved are defined by faith, not by house: Gen 7:1 bōʾ ʾattāh we-kol bêtkā ʾel ha-ttēvāh kî ʾōtkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq. Q 71:28 rabbi ghfir lī wa-li-wālidayya wa-li-man dakhala baytiya muʾminan wa-li-l-muʾminīna wa-l-muʾmināt: whoever enters my house as a believer.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לְנֹ֔חַ בֹּֽא אַתָּ֥ה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ֖ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה כִּֽי אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה
וַיָּ֣בֹא נֹ֗חַ וּ֠בָנָיו וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וּנְשֵֽׁי בָנָ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה מִפְּנֵ֖י מֵ֥י הַמַּבּֽוּל
رَّبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِوَٰلِدَىَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِىَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًۢا

matches.label: Deity resolves or promises not to repeat the destruction
matches.note: Ending changed: Genesis ends with Noah's sacrifice and God's promise lōʾ ʾōsîf leqallēl ʿôd ʾet hā-ʾădāmāh ... we-lōʾ ʾōsîf ʿôd lehakkôt ʾet kol ḥay. Q 71 ends with the drowned sent on into fire (ughriqū fa-udkhilū nāran) and Noah's prayer of forgiveness and of destruction (wa-lā tazidi ẓ-ẓālimīna illā tabārā). No sacrifice, no covenant, no 'never again'.

passages.text: וַיִּ֥בֶן נֹ֛חַ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִכֹּ֣ל הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָע֣וֹף הַטָּהֹ֔ר וַיַּ֥עַל עֹלֹ֖ת בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

וַיָּ֣רַח יְהוָה֮ אֶת רֵ֣יחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל לִבּ֗וֹ לֹֽא אֹ֠סִף לְקַלֵּ֨ל ע֤וֹד אֶת הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּעֲב֣וּר הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣צֶר לֵ֧ב הָאָדָ֛ם רַ֖ע מִנְּעֻרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא אֹסִ֥ף ע֛וֹד לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת כָּל חַ֖י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִֽׂיתִי
مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا۟ فَأُدْخِلُوا۟ نَارًا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا۟ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارًا
رَّبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِوَٰلِدَىَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِىَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًۢا

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ
וַאֲנִ֗י הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא אֶת הַמַּבּ֥וּל מַ֨יִם֙ עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ לְשַׁחֵ֣ת כָּל בָּשָׂ֗ר אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ֙ ר֣וּחַ חַיִּ֔ים מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר בָּאָ֖רֶץ יִגְוָֽע
إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦٓ أَنْ أَنذِرْ قَوْمَكَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ

כֹּ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁמַת ר֨וּחַ חַיִּ֜ים בְּאַפָּ֗יו מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֶּחָֽרָבָ֖ה מֵֽתוּ

וַיִּ֜מַח אֶֽת כָּל הַיְק֣וּם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֗ה מֵאָדָ֤ם עַד בְּהֵמָה֙ עַד רֶ֨מֶשׂ֙ וְעַד ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּמָּח֖וּ מִן הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִשָּׁ֧אֶר אַךְ נֹ֛חַ וַֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָֽה
مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا۟ فَأُدْخِلُوا۟ نَارًا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا۟ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارًا
وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا

leads.title: Sons of God, daughters of men, and the Nephilim ↔ Creation not in jest; the unceasing angels and the argument from one God
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 answers the other.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Those called God's offspring are rather honored servants who do not speak before him [response between the texts] (weight 6.7); Divine beings take human women as wives (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in Sons of God, daughters of men, and the Nephilim: God limits human lifespan to 120 years; Giants or heroes (Nephilim) born from divine-human unions; Maidens of restrained glance whom no man or jinn has touched before them, like rubies and coral; Whether God has, begets or takes sons or other offspring [contrast between the texts].

Only in Creation not in jest; the unceasing angels and the argument from one God: God hurls the truth against falsehood and it shatters its skull, and falsehood vanishes; Those called God's offspring are rather honored servants who do not speak before him; Those with God glorify him night and day without tiring; God is not questioned about what he does, but they are questioned; Were there gods besides God in heaven and earth, both would have been ruined; In hell the damned neither die nor live; The host of heaven bows down to God; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth; Intercession avails only for whom God permits.

matches.label: Those called God's offspring are rather honored servants who do not speak before him
matches.note: Gen speaks of divine 'sons' who take human wives and father heroes, wayyirʾû bənê-hāʾĕlōhîm ʾet-bənôt hāʾādām ... wayyiqḥû lāhem nāšîm ... wəyālədû lāhem. Q rejects the very notion of offspring, wa-qālū ttakhadha r-Raḥmānu waladan subḥānahu bal ʿibādun mukramūn lā yasbiqūnahu bi-l-qawli wa-hum bi-amrihi yaʿmalūn. The heavenly beings are servants who act only on his command; they do not wed or beget.

Sanh 56a).

leads.title: Blessing of Noah, blood laws and the covenant of the bow ↔ Al-Qamar: the moon split, the dead like locusts, and Noah's ark of planks and fibres
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The sign left after the flood: the rainbow, or the ark [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Blessing of Noah, blood laws and the covenant of the bow: God requires the life of a human even from an animal that kills; God sees the bow in the cloud and remembers his covenant (the sign reminds the deity); God makes a covenant with humans and all living creatures; Eating animals permitted to humans after the flood; Whoever sheds human blood, by man shall his blood be shed, because humans bear God's image [divergence between the texts]; The same religion (din) was enjoined on Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and the Prophet: establish it and do not divide; Whoever sheds human blood, by man shall his blood be shed, because humans bear God's image; A sign in the sky commemorates the flood (bow, necklace); The sign the flood leaves for later generations [divergence between the texts]; Hero blessed on leaving the vessel; Humans given rule over animals; Deity resolves or promises not to repeat the destruction; and 3 more.

Only in Al-Qamar: the moon split, the dead like locusts, and Noah's ark of planks and fibres: God left the ark (or the event) as a sign: is there anyone who will remember?; Noah carried on a thing of planks and nails/fibres (dhat alwah wa-dusur), running under God's eyes; God opens the gates of heaven with pouring water and makes the earth burst with springs; the waters meet for a decreed matter; Noah, called a madman and driven off, prays 'I am overcome, so help me!'; Whenever they see a sign they turn away and say 'continuous/passing sorcery' (sihr mustamirr); What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer [divergence between the texts]; With downcast eyes they come out of the graves like scattered locusts, hastening to the caller; How the ark is described [divergence between the texts]; 'The Hour has drawn near and the moon is split' (inshaqqa l-qamar); God opens the windows or gates of heaven, for blessing or for the flood [contrast between the texts]; Refrain: 'How then were my punishment and my warnings?' (fa-kayfa kana 'adhabi wa-nudhur); Refrain: 'We have made the Quran easy to remember; is there anyone who will remember?' (fa-hal min muddakir); and 6 more.

matches.note: What remains as the flood's sign. Genesis: zōʾṯ ʾôṯ hab-bərîṯ ... ʾeṯ qaštî nāṯattî be-ʿānān (the rainbow as covenant sign that it will not happen again). Genesis' sign reassures that the flood will not return; the Quran's warns that punishment comes again (the refrain fa-kayfa kāna ʿadhābī wa-nudhur).

leads.title: The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes ↔ Rivalry, time and the slanderer
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes: The arrogant man's appetite is wide as Sheol and like Death never satisfied, gathering all nations; Woe to one who makes his neighbor drunk in order to gaze on his nakedness; The prophet stations himself on his watchpost to see what God will answer to his complaint; 'The righteous shall live by his faith (emunah)'; A series of 'woe' (hoy) taunt-sayings against an oppressor; The stone cries out from the wall and the beam answers from the woodwork; The vision is for an appointed time; though it tarry, wait for it, for it will surely come; Write the vision plainly on tablets so that a runner may read it; Woe to the one who says to wood 'Awake!' and to dumb stone 'Arise!'; there is no breath in it; The earth will be full of the knowledge of YHWH as the waters cover the sea; Peoples labor only for fire and nations weary themselves for nothing; 'Hush (has) before YHWH, all the earth', for he is in his holy temple or has roused himself; and 7 more.

Only in Rivalry, time and the slanderer: Knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin) and the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin): you will see hell; God's kindled fire rises over the hearts and is closed over them in extended columns; Oath by time or the afternoon (al-'asr): humankind is in loss; Rivalry in piling up (al-takathur) distracts people until they visit the graves; they will be asked about the pleasures; A fire is closed over the damned (mu'sada); Riches kept by their owner to his hurt, lost in a bad venture, so that his son has nothing in hand; Hell given proper names: Laza (scalp-stripper), Saqar (scorcher, leaves nothing), al-Hutama (the crusher), Hawiya (the abyss); Do not go about as a talebearer among your people; Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' (wa ma adraka ma) introducing an eschatological term.

leads.title: The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes ↔ Nearer than the jugular vein; the two recorders; driver and witness; Gehenna says 'Is there more?'; creation in six days without weariness
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God asks Gehenna 'Are you full?' and it answers 'Are there any more?' (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes: The arrogant man's appetite is wide as Sheol and like Death never satisfied, gathering all nations; Woe to one who makes his neighbor drunk in order to gaze on his nakedness; The prophet stations himself on his watchpost to see what God will answer to his complaint; 'The righteous shall live by his faith (emunah)'; A series of 'woe' (hoy) taunt-sayings against an oppressor; The stone cries out from the wall and the beam answers from the woodwork; The vision is for an appointed time; though it tarry, wait for it, for it will surely come; Write the vision plainly on tablets so that a runner may read it; Woe to the one who says to wood 'Awake!' and to dumb stone 'Arise!'; there is no breath in it; The earth will be full of the knowledge of YHWH as the waters cover the sea; Peoples labor only for fire and nations weary themselves for nothing; 'Hush (has) before YHWH, all the earth', for he is in his holy temple or has roused himself; and 7 more.

Only in Nearer than the jugular vein; the two recorders; driver and witness; Gehenna says 'Is there more?'; creation in six days without weariness: On the day the caller calls from a place near at hand, and they hear the Cry (al-sayha): the day of coming forth; The damned man's companion (qarin) disputes before God: 'Our Lord, I did not make him transgress'; The earth splits open from them and they hasten forth to the gathering; 'Enter it in peace': the day of eternity; they have what they wish and more (mazid) with God; The Garden is brought near to the God-fearing, not far off; God created the heavens and earth in six days and no weariness (lughub) touched him; Every soul comes with a driver (sa'iq) and a witness (shahid); The stupor (sakra) of death comes with the truth: 'this is what you tried to avoid'; Two receivers sit on the right and the left recording every word a person utters; At judgment the covering is removed from a person and his sight that day is sharp as iron; Four things are never satisfied: Sheol, the barren womb, earth not filled with water, and fire that never says 'Enough'; God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

leads.title: Hosea marries Gomer; the children Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi ↔ Zayd's wife, the seal of the prophets, and the prophet as a lamp
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: After Zayd ends his marriage, God marries his former wife to the prophet so believers may marry the ex-wives of adopted sons (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Hosea marries Gomer; the children Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi: God will avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu; The prophet's children receive symbolic names announcing judgment or salvation (Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi); God commands the prophet to marry a 'woman of harlotry' as a sign of the land's unfaithfulness; 'Not my people' becomes 'my people' and 'Not pitied' becomes 'pitied'; In the latter days Israel will return and seek YHWH and David their king; Israel called sons of God; Descendants promised to be as countless as the dust, stars or sand.

Only in Zayd's wife, the seal of the prophets, and the prophet as a lamp: The greeting of the righteous in the hereafter is 'Peace' (salam); Adopted sons are not one's sons; call them by their fathers' names, or as brothers in religion and clients; God and his angels bless (yusalluna 'ala) the prophet; believers are told to bless him and greet him with peace; A ruler or prophet marries the wife of a man under him [contrast between the texts]; Whether a man may marry his son's (or adopted son's) wife [divergence between the texts]; Muhammad is not the father of any of your men but the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets (khatam al-nabiyyin); The prophet is sent as witness, bearer of good tidings and warner; Glorify God in the evening, morning, afternoon and noon (set times of praise or prayer); The way (sunna) of God with those who passed before: you will find no change in God's way; God brings believers out of darknesses into light; false gods lead others from light into darkness.

Only in The luxuriant vine, the calves of Beth-aven, sow righteousness: Israel a luxuriant vine: the more fruit, the more altars and pillars; The idol-priests (kemarim) mourn as the calf is carried off as tribute to Assyria; Sow for yourselves righteousness, reap steadfast love, break up your fallow ground; Thorns and thistles grow up on their altars; Ephraim a trained heifer that loves to thresh, now yoked to plow; Israel's sin recalled as 'the days of Gibeah'; Bethel ('house of God') mocked as Beth-aven ('house of iniquity'); Infants dashed to pieces and pregnant women ripped open in war.

leads.title: The unfaithful wife and the new betrothal ↔ Female deities, Satan's vow, slit cattle ears, and Abraham the friend
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The faithless wife credits her lovers (the Baals) with her bread, water, wool, flax, oil and drink, not knowing God gave them (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The unfaithful wife and the new betrothal: God will allure his people into the wilderness and speak to her heart, as in the days of youth; Chain of responses: God answers the heavens, the heavens the earth, the earth grain-wine-oil, and they answer Jezreel; God betroths his people to himself forever in righteousness, justice, steadfast love, mercy and faithfulness; God will end the land's festivals, new moons and sabbaths; God hedges her way with thorns and a wall so she cannot find her lovers' paths; She will call God 'my husband (ishi)' and no longer 'my baal'; the names of the Baals removed from her mouth; The straying wife resolves 'I will go back to my first husband, for it was better then'; The unfaithful wife is threatened with being stripped naked as on the day she was born; The Valley of Achor ('trouble') becomes a door of hope; God's people portrayed as an adulterous wife who runs after lovers (the Baals); 'Not my people' becomes 'my people' and 'Not pitied' becomes 'pitied'; God makes a covenant of peace, banishing evil beasts so the flock can dwell securely in the wilderness and sleep in the forests.

Only in Female deities, Satan's vow, slit cattle ears, and Abraham the friend: Satan commands people to alter God's creation; Idolaters invoke only female beings besides God, and only a rebellious Satan; Salvation is not by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book: whoever does evil is requited; Cursed Satan vows to take an appointed share (naṣīb mafrūḍ) of God's servants; Satan commands people to slit the ears of cattle (a pagan dedication rite); Offerings, incense and libations to the 'Queen of Heaven'; Whoever does good, male or female, and believes, enters paradise; Abraham is called God's friend (ohev, 'lover'); God does not forgive associating partners with him (shirk) but forgives anything less; Not wronged by a date-stone's thread (fatīl) or groove (naqīr): proverbial minimal measures; Follow the religion (milla) of Abraham the ḥanīf, who was no idolater.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God expels Iblis as accursed (rajim) with a curse until the Day of Judgment (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Restoration of Jacob and the taunt over the king of Babylon (Helel son of Dawn): The proud one plans to ascend to heaven, raise his throne above the stars of El and make himself like Elyon; Reversal: Israel will take captive those who captured them and rule over their oppressors; The would-be god is brought down instead to Sheol, to the recesses of the pit (yarkete bor); Strangers (gerim) will join themselves to Israel and cleave to the house of Jacob; 'How you have fallen from heaven, Helel son of Shahar (Shining One, son of Dawn)!' - a star-figure cast down to earth; In the underworld maggots are spread beneath the dead king and worms are his covering; The mount of assembly (har mo'ed) in the recesses of the north (yarkete tsafon), seat of the gods; God cuts off from the enemy 'name and remnant, offspring and posterity'; Sheol below is stirred to meet the arriving tyrant; the shades and dead kings rise from their thrones to greet him: 'you too have become weak like us'; God sweeps the city with the broom of destruction, leaving it to hedgehogs and marshes; Mocking dirge (mashal) over a fallen tyrant: 'How the oppressor has ceased!'; The cypresses and cedars of Lebanon rejoice that no woodcutter comes up since the tyrant fell; and 8 more.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do; The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised; The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils; and 1 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: On that day neither wealth nor sons avail, only one who comes to God with a sound heart (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm: Speaker laments that in the noon of his days he must go to the gates of Sheol, deprived of the rest of his years; A psalm-like 'writing' (mikhtav) of the king composed when he was sick and recovered; My dwelling is pulled up like a shepherd's tent; I have rolled up my life like a weaver, he cuts me off from the loom; In distress the sufferer chirps like a swift or crane and moans like a dove; God has cast all the speaker's sins behind his back and held back his soul from the pit of destruction; The dead cannot praise God: no wonders for the dead, no hesed in the grave, no faithfulness in Abaddon; A dying person's plea to God for more life, and God's answer [contrast between the texts]; A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king; Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward); Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die'; Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping; Bequest (wasiyya) to parents and kin prescribed for one who leaves wealth; altering it is a sin; and 5 more.

Only in Abraham's argument against idols and his prayer: Abraham prays for 'a tongue of truthfulness' (good repute) among later generations; Abraham's creed: the God who created and guides me, feeds and gives drink, heals me when sick, causes me to die and revives me, and will forgive me; In hell the damned dispute with the gods they equated with God and wish for another chance; The deluded and all the hosts of Iblis are hurled headlong into hell; God wounds and binds up, strikes and his hands heal; Who sends sickness and who heals [divergence between the texts]; A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, favor rather than silver and gold; Abraham prayed for his father's forgiveness only by a promise, and disowned him when he proved God's enemy; Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols [divergence between the texts]; Wealth does not profit on the day of wrath; No man can ransom his brother or give God a ransom (kofer) for him; the redemption of life is too costly; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'; and 3 more.

leads.title: Comfort my people; a voice in the wilderness; to whom will you liken God ↔ Life like a crop, the abode of peace, darkened faces
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: All flesh is grass and its loyalty like the flower of the field; grass withers but the word of God stands forever (weight 6.3); Parable: worldly life is like vegetation fed by rain, adorned, then cut down overnight as if it never flourished (weight 6.3). Pair score 12.6.

Only in Comfort my people; a voice in the wilderness; to whom will you liken God: 'Comfort, comfort my people': Jerusalem's term of service is ended and she has received double for her sins; God tends his flock like a shepherd, gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them in his bosom; God brings out the starry host by number and calls each by name; none is missing; God sits enthroned above the circle (hug) of the earth; its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; Those who wait for YHWH renew strength, mount up with wings like eagles, run and not be weary; Nations are like a drop from a bucket and dust on the scales; Lebanon is not enough fuel nor its beasts enough for a burnt offering; A voice cries: 'In the wilderness clear the way of YHWH, make straight in the desert a highway for our God'; Who measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, marked off heaven with a span and weighed the mountains in scales?; God made everything grow in due weight and sends it down only in known measure; A double portion (k-p-l) from God [divergence between the texts]; On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth is in God's grip and the heavens folded in his right hand; A herald of good news (mevasseret Tsiyyon) goes up on a high mountain to announce 'Behold your God!'; and 17 more.

Only in Life like a crop, the abode of peace, darkened faces: The doers of good get the best reward 'and more' (ziyada); Paradise as the abode of peace (dār al-salām); The faces of evildoers are covered as with pieces of dark night; The destroyed are as if they had never lived in their land; Humans are like grass that flourishes in the morning and withers by evening; At judgment the associated 'partners' disown their worshipers: 'it was not us you worshiped'.

Only in Comfort my people; a voice in the wilderness; to whom will you liken God: 'Comfort, comfort my people': Jerusalem's term of service is ended and she has received double for her sins; God tends his flock like a shepherd, gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them in his bosom; God brings out the starry host by number and calls each by name; none is missing; God sits enthroned above the circle (hug) of the earth; its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; Those who wait for YHWH renew strength, mount up with wings like eagles, run and not be weary; Nations are like a drop from a bucket and dust on the scales; Lebanon is not enough fuel nor its beasts enough for a burnt offering; A voice cries: 'In the wilderness clear the way of YHWH, make straight in the desert a highway for our God'; Who measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, marked off heaven with a span and weighed the mountains in scales?; God made everything grow in due weight and sends it down only in known measure; A double portion (k-p-l) from God [divergence between the texts]; On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth is in God's grip and the heavens folded in his right hand; A herald of good news (mevasseret Tsiyyon) goes up on a high mountain to announce 'Behold your God!'; and 18 more.

Only in Sincerity, daybreak and mankind: God's unity and the two refuges: Refuge from the evil of darkness (or the moon) when it settles (ghasiq idha waqab); Refuge from the evil of an envier when he envies (evil eye); God is al-Samad (the Eternal Refuge, the solid one who needs nothing); Triple title: Lord of mankind, King of mankind, God of mankind; Refuge from the evil of the slinking whisperer (al-waswas al-khannas) who whispers in people's breasts, from jinn and humans; God does not beget and was not begotten; God does not beget and was not begotten [contrast between the texts]; Protection from the terror of the night, the arrow by day, the pestilence (dever) stalking in darkness and Qeteb that ravages at noon; Protective formula 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of...' (qul a'udhu bi-rabbi) against named evils; Refuge from the evil of those (women) who blow on knots (al-naffathat fi al-'uqad), i.e. knot-tying sorcery; Psalm used as protection against demons and harm (later amulet and 'song of plagues'); Cluster of divine epithets in sequence (e.g. the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne, the Glorious, doer of what he wills; or Lord, King, God of mankind); and 2 more.

matches.label: Human life like grass or plants that wither
matches.note: Life as withering plants, with a different counterweight. Isaiah: kol hab-bāśār ḥāṣîr wə-ḵol ḥasdô kə-ṣîṣ haś-śāḏeh; yāḇēš ḥāṣîr nāḇēl ṣîṣ û-ḏəḇar ʾĕlōhênû yāqûm lə-ʿôlām (against the grass stands God's word). Quran: ka-mathali ghaythin aʿjaba l-kuffāra nabātuhu thumma yahīju fa-tarāhu muṣfarran thumma yakūnu ḥuṭāman, wa-fī l-ākhirati ʿadhābun shadīdun wa-maghfiratun mina llāh (against the withering stands the hereafter, punishment or forgiveness). The Quran adds the farmer's pleasure in the growth and the list of what is passing: play, adornment, boasting, rivalry in wealth and children.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: None can change the words of God (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Comfort my people; a voice in the wilderness; to whom will you liken God: 'Comfort, comfort my people': Jerusalem's term of service is ended and she has received double for her sins; God tends his flock like a shepherd, gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them in his bosom; God brings out the starry host by number and calls each by name; none is missing; God sits enthroned above the circle (hug) of the earth; its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; Those who wait for YHWH renew strength, mount up with wings like eagles, run and not be weary; Nations are like a drop from a bucket and dust on the scales; Lebanon is not enough fuel nor its beasts enough for a burnt offering; A voice cries: 'In the wilderness clear the way of YHWH, make straight in the desert a highway for our God'; Who measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, marked off heaven with a span and weighed the mountains in scales?; God made everything grow in due weight and sends it down only in known measure; A double portion (k-p-l) from God [divergence between the texts]; On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth is in God's grip and the heavens folded in his right hand; A herald of good news (mevasseret Tsiyyon) goes up on a high mountain to announce 'Behold your God!'; and 18 more.

Only in Sworn oaths for a sign; even the dead speaking would not convince: Even if angels came down and the dead spoke to them, they would not believe; Most on earth follow only conjecture (ẓann) and guess; They swear solemnly they would believe if a sign came; Every prophet has enemies: devils of humans and jinn inspiring one another with gilded speech; Whether the dead may be consulted, or would persuade the living if they spoke [contrast between the texts]; Prophet commissioned to make the people's heart fat, ears heavy and eyes shut lest they understand and be healed [divergence between the texts]; Do not spread false reports or follow the majority to do wrong in court; Prophet commissioned to make the people's heart fat, ears heavy and eyes shut lest they understand and be healed.

matches.label: Who makes the hearers deaf, blind and closed of heart to the message
matches.note: Heavy ears, in the speakers' own mouth. Isa: God commands hašmēn lēḇ hā-ʿām ... wə-ʾoznâw hakbēd. Q: wa-qālū qulūbunā fī akinnatin ... wa-fī ādhāninā waqrun wa-min bayninā wa-baynika ḥijāb. The rejecters themselves boast of covered hearts and heavy ears (waqr ~ kāḇēḏ) as a refusal (fa-ʿmal innanā ʿāmilūn). The divine hardening becomes a self-declaration.

leads.title: The throne vision and the call of Isaiah ↔ Angels descend on the steadfast; repel evil with good; signs on the horizons
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Those with God glorify him night and day without tiring (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in The throne vision and the call of Isaiah: A seraph touches the prophet's lips with a burning coal from the altar, removing his guilt; Six-winged seraphim stand above God: two wings cover the face, two the feet, two for flying; Even the tenth that remains will be burned, like a felled terebinth or oak whose stump is the holy seed; At the heavenly voice the doorposts shake and the house fills with smoke; Prophet sees the Lord seated on a high and lifted-up throne, his train filling the temple; Heavenly beings call 'Holy, holy, holy is YHWH of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory'; God asks 'Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?' and the prophet volunteers 'Here am I, send me'; Prophet cries 'Woe is me, I am undone, a man of unclean lips' for having seen the King; The angels say: each of us has a known station; we are ranged in ranks; we glorify; God has not given the people a heart to know, eyes to see, ears to hear until today [divergence between the texts]; Hardening of the heart, ears and eyes of the hearers [divergence between the texts]; God is 'Lord of the mighty Throne' (rabb al-'arsh al-'azim); and 11 more.

Only in Angels descend on the steadfast; repel evil with good; signs on the horizons: Angels descend on those who say 'Our Lord is God' and stand firm: 'Fear not, grieve not, rejoice in the Garden'; Do not prostrate to the sun or the moon but to God who created them; Falsehood cannot approach the Book from before it or behind it; No fruit comes out of its sheath and no female conceives or gives birth but with God's knowledge; Given relief, man says 'This is mine; I do not think the Hour will come, and if returned to my Lord I will have the best with him'; On the Day God calls 'Where are my partners?', they answer 'We declare to you none of us is a witness'; The Quran is guidance and healing (shifa') for believers; for others deafness and blindness; 'We will show them our signs on the horizons and in themselves until it is clear to them that it is the truth'; Do not say 'I will repay evil'; wait for YHWH and he will save you; Doing good to an enemy, and what it brings [divergence between the texts]; Had it been revealed to a non-Arab (aʿjamī) reciting it, they would still not believe; When an evil prompting from Satan stirs you, seek refuge in God; and 13 more.

matches.label: Those with God glorify him night and day without tiring
matches.note: Heavenly beings praising God: wə-qārāʾ zeh ʾel zeh wə-ʾāmar qāḏôš qāḏôš qāḏôš YHWH ṣəḇāʾôṯ vs. fa-lladhīna ʿinda rabbika yusabbiḥūna lahu bi-l-layli wa-n-nahāri wa-hum lā yasʾamūn. Isaiah's seraphim cry to one another; the Quran's 'those with your Lord' praise night and day without weariness, set against men who are too proud (istakbarū) to prostrate. Unceasing praise is not stated in Isa 6; cf. 1 Enoch 39:12-13, Rev 4:8.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: In hell the damned neither die nor live (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Judgment by fire, ingathering of nations, the undying worm: From new moon to new moon and Sabbath to Sabbath all flesh comes to worship before God; The nations bring all Israel's brothers to Jerusalem as an offering on horses, chariots, litters, mules and dromedaries; God gathers all nations and tongues to come and see his glory; God will take some of the nations as priests and Levites; God comes in fire with chariots like a whirlwind to judge all flesh by fire and sword; Those who sanctify themselves for the gardens, following one in the middle, eat swine, abominations and mice; God sends survivors to distant nations (Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Tubal, Javan, the far islands) to declare his glory; Corpses of the rebels whose worm does not die and fire is not quenched, an abhorrence to all flesh; One of the blessed recalls a companion who denied the resurrection, looks down and sees him in the midst of hell; God creates new heavens and a new earth; the former things will not be remembered; The pig is unclean and forbidden.

Only in The heirs of the Book, the Gardens of Eden and the cries of the damned: God made humans successors (khala'if) on the earth; Heirs of the Book are of three kinds: one who wrongs himself, one who is moderate, and one foremost in good deeds; The guilty, heads bowed before their Lord, beg to be returned to do good; God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; if they ceased, no one else could hold them; If God took people to task for what they earned he would not leave a creature on the earth's back, but he defers them to a set term; Paradise is the abode of permanence where no toil or weariness touches the blessed and grief is removed; The evil plot encompasses only its own authors; In paradise the righteous are adorned with gold bracelets and pearls and wear silk; The way (sunna) of God with those who passed before: you will find no change in God's way; Challenge to idolaters: show me what those besides God have created; Travel in the land and see the end of those who denied.

leads.title: Heaven is my throne; sacrifice as abomination ↔ Ranks of the messengers and the Throne Verse
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God's throne in relation to heaven and earth [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Heaven is my throne; sacrifice as abomination: The faithful are hated and cast out by their own brothers for God's name's sake; God looks to the poor and contrite in spirit who trembles at his word; 'Heaven is my throne and earth my footstool: what house could you build for me?'; Hypocritical sacrifice is equated with crimes: slaughtering an ox is like killing a man, offering a lamb like breaking a dog's neck; A tumult from the city, a voice from the temple: the voice of YHWH repaying his enemies; Those who tremble at God's word (haredim) gather to the leader.

Only in Ranks of the messengers and the Throne Verse: God's footstool or seat (kursi) extends over the heavens and the earth; No compulsion in religion; Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes God; Whoever rejects false gods (taghut) and believes in God grasps the firmest handhold that never breaks; God does not slumber or sleep [divergence between the texts]; The guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps; A day comes with no trade, no friendship and no intercession; The temple as a house of rest for the ark and the footstool of God's feet; Jesus son of Mary given clear signs and supported with the holy spirit (ruh al-qudus); Israel's God is called 'the living God, enduring forever, whose kingdom shall never be destroyed'; God ranked some messengers above others; to some God spoke; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); and 4 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Fifth confession - you enticed me; fire shut up in my bones: The prophet complains 'You enticed (pittitani) me, YHWH, and I was enticed; you overpowered me and prevailed'; The prophet is full of God's wrath or word and is weary of holding it in; The persecuted prophet asks God to let him see vengeance on his enemies; Jeremiah's 'confessions': the prophet's personal laments and complaints to God about his mission and persecutors; 'Terror on every side' (magor missaviv); God celebrated as a warrior ('YHWH is a man of war').

Only in Closing confession and prayer: Prayer not to be laid with a burden (isr) like that laid on those before us; Prayer to be cleansed of hidden and unwitting faults (shegi'ot, nistarot); Believers make no distinction between any of the prophets (Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Moses, Jesus); 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's; 'We are the clay and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand'; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; God alone knows the hearts of all humans.

Only in Zedekiah's inquiry - the way of life and the way of death: The besieged king sends to ask the prophet to inquire of God, hoping God will do a wonder and make the enemy withdraw; The city is given into the hand of the king of Babylon who will burn it with fire; God himself fights against his own people with outstretched hand and mighty arm, turning their weapons back; Whoever stays in the city will die, but whoever goes out and surrenders to the besiegers will live, his life as spoil; God redeems 'with an outstretched arm' and great judgments; Judgment by the triad sword, famine and pestilence.

Only in Concerning the prophets - who has stood in the council of YHWH?: The prophet's heart is broken and all his bones shake; he is like a drunken man because of God's holy words; The prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery and strengthen evildoers; they have become like Sodom and Gomorrah; Whether a prophet has first-hand knowledge of the heavenly council [contrast between the texts]; Whether a prophet speaks from his own heart or desire, or by revelation [contrast between the texts]; The earth mourns and the heavens above grow dark because of God's decree; God gives his people poisoned water (mei rosh) to drink and wormwood to eat; 'Have you listened in the council (sod) of God, and limited wisdom to yourself?'; Prophets and priests heal the wound lightly, saying 'Peace, peace' when there is no peace; The storm of YHWH's fury goes out and whirls on the head of the wicked; in the latter days you will understand it; God enthroned with the host of heaven standing at his right and left deliberates; The tree of Zaqqum grows from the bottom of hell; its spathes are like the heads of devils; the damned fill their bellies and drink boiling water; God did not send the prophets who promise peace; they prophesy a lying vision, divination and the deceit of their heart.

Only in Near compromise, prayer times, the praised station, the spirit, the challenge and the demanded signs (Surah 17:73-100): Were angels walking the earth, God would have sent them an angel as messenger; The creator of heavens and earth is able to create the like of them (resurrection argument); The astray are gathered on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf; Opponents demand a spring gushing from the earth or a garden of palms and vines with rivers; Opponents demand that the prophet have a house of gold ornament; Opponents demand that the sky fall on them in pieces or God and the angels appear; Whenever the fire of hell abates, God increases its blaze; Even owning the treasuries of God's mercy, humans would hold back for fear of spending; Keep vigil (tahajjud) with recitation in part of the night as an extra devotion; The prophet may be raised to a 'praised station' (maqam mahmud), later read as intercession; Prayer: 'Lord, make my entrance and my exit true and grant me a helping authority'; Prayer is fixed from the sun's decline to the dark of night, with the dawn recitation; and 10 more.

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى فَٱكْتُبُوهُ وَلْيَكْتُب بَّيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌۢ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَلَا يَأْبَ كَاتِبٌ أَن يَكْتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ فَلْيَكْتُبْ وَلْيُمْلِلِ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلْيَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُۥ وَلَا يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْـًٔا فَإِن كَانَ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُۥ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱسْتَشْهِدُوا۟ شَهِيدَيْنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمْ فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَٱمْرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ وَلَا يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُوا۟ وَلَا تَسْـَٔمُوٓا۟ أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أَوْ كَبِيرًا إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلِهِۦ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَٰدَةِ وَأَدْنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَرْتَابُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا وَأَشْهِدُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُمْ وَلَا يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلَا شَهِيدٌ وَإِن تَفْعَلُوا۟ فَإِنَّهُۥ فُسُوقٌۢ بِكُمْ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God will give his people one heart and one way to fear him always (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Jeremiah buys his cousin's field at Anathoth during the siege: Sons and daughters passed through fire to Molech at the high places in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom; Deeds are put in an earthenware jar so they may last many days; God's eyes are open on all the ways of humanity to repay each by his deeds; Incense offered to Baal and libations to other gods on the roofs of houses; A field bought for seventeen shekels of silver; The prophet buys a family field during siege as a sign that land will again be bought; Siege ramps are raised against the city; The king will see the conquering king eye to eye and speak with him mouth to mouth; A land deed made in a sealed copy and an open copy, witnessed and the silver weighed; The prophet is confined in the court of the guard in the palace; Baruch son of Neriah, the prophet's scribe; God promises an everlasting covenant (berit olam) with his people; and 5 more.

leads.title: Baruch reads the scroll; Jehoiakim cuts it with a penknife and burns it; it is rewritten ↔ The Criterion sent down; charges of forgery and the prophet who eats in markets
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Who dictated and who wrote down a prophet's book [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Baruch reads the scroll; Jehoiakim cuts it with a penknife and burns it; it is rewritten: A destroyed sacred book is rewritten from dictation with many words added; The king cuts the prophetic scroll column by column with a scribe's knife and burns it in his brazier; The king's corpse will be cast out to heat by day and frost by night; The king will have no descendant sitting on David's throne; The king and his servants hear the words of judgment and do not tear their garments; Royal officials turn in fear to one another when the scroll is read to them; Sympathetic officials tell the prophet and his scribe to hide; Some officials beg the king not to burn the scroll; The prophet dictates God's words and a scribe writes them in a scroll; A prophetic scroll is read publicly in the temple on a fast day; Perhaps the people will turn from evil and God will relent of the disaster he planned; Baruch son of Neriah, the prophet's scribe.

Only in The Criterion sent down; charges of forgery and the prophet who eats in markets: Opponents object that the messenger eats food and walks in the markets, with no angel, treasure or garden; Opponents claim the prophet had old tales written down and dictated to him morning and evening, with others helping him; God gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion (al-furqān), a light and reminder; Opponents say the believers follow only a bewitched man (rajul mashur); Whether old tradition handed down from the ancients carries authority [contrast between the texts]; Those called God's offspring are rather honored servants who do not speak before him; Worshipping what can neither harm nor benefit you; The made idol cannot move from its place, speak or answer and save those who cry to it; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

matches.note: Who dictates to whom: in Jeremiah the prophet dictates and the scribe writes, wa-yyiktōv Bārûkh mip-pî Yirmyāhû ... mip-pîw yiqrāʾ ʾēlay ... wa-ʾănî kōtēv ʿal has-sēfer bad-dəyô; in the opponents' charge the prophet has old tales written down and they are dictated to him (iktatabahā fa-hiya tumlā ʿalayhi bukratan wa-aṣīlan), with helpers (aʿānahu ʿalayhi qawmun ākharūn). The Quran rejects the charge: it was sent down by the one who knows the secret (25:6).

وَقَالُوٓا۟ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ ٱكْتَتَبَهَا فَهِىَ تُمْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا

leads.title: Fall of Jerusalem; Zedekiah blinded at Riblah; Jeremiah freed; Ebed-melech promised safety ↔ Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The conqueror leaves the poorest people in the land as vinedressers and farmers (weight 6.7); Jerusalem is breached, captured and burned by the Babylonians (weight 6.7); The fleeing king is overtaken in the plains of Jericho (weight 6.7); Besieged king flees by night through a gate between the walls and is overtaken (weight 6.3); The captive king's sons are slaughtered before his eyes, then his eyes are put out (weight 6.3). Pair score 32.6.

Only in Fall of Jerusalem; Zedekiah blinded at Riblah; Jeremiah freed; Ebed-melech promised safety: The conquering Babylonian officers, named with their titles (Rab-saris, Rab-mag), sit in the city's Middle Gate; The foreign conqueror orders his officers to look after the prophet and do him no harm; A foreigner who helped the prophet is promised his life will be spared because he trusted God; Captive king taken with hooks and bound in bronze fetters to Babylon; Whoever surrenders to the enemy will live; his life shall be his booty.

Only in Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release: Precise numbers of deportees for each year of exile; A captive king is released after decades, changes his prison clothes and eats at the foreign king's table; A king 'lifts the head' of a prisoner, releasing and honoring him; The besiegers build a siege wall (dayeq) around the city; Famine becomes severe in the besieged city; there is no bread; The chief priest, second priest and officials are executed by the conqueror at Riblah; The king's mother is named in his regnal formula; The released captive king is given a throne above the other kings in Babylon; The temple of Jerusalem is burned and the city walls broken down; Seven princes or counselors who 'see the king's face' advise the king; A great cast-bronze 'sea' basin rests on twelve bronze oxen facing the four directions in threes; Two named bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, before the temple; and 2 more.

leads.title: My bowels, my bowels - the vision of uncreation ↔ Moses asks Pharaoh to hand over God's servants; the sea left parted; heaven did not weep
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether heaven and earth mourn a destroyed people [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Oracle against Babylon (I): Bel and Merodach shamed, the hammer of the earth broken: Israel a scattered sheep: first Assyria devoured it, last Babylon gnawed its bones; Babylon's gods Bel and Merodach are put to shame and its idols dismayed; Desert creatures or demons (tsiyyim, iyyim) and ostriches inhabit the ruined city; God opens his armory and brings out the weapons of his indignation; Babylon called the 'hammer of the whole earth' is broken; Babylon is a land of idols, mad over their terrors; God's people are lost sheep whose shepherds led them astray on the mountains; Babylon addressed by wordplay names: Merathaim ('double rebellion') and Pekod ('punishment'); Repay the city according to her deeds: do to her as she has done; Israel's iniquity will be sought and not found, for God pardons the remnant; Repeated 'A sword upon...' litany against every class of a city; A day of vengeance belonging to YHWH of hosts against his foes; and 11 more.

Only in Job's piety, the heavenly council and the first test: The verb 'bless' (barekh) used as a scribal euphemism for cursing God; Grown sons hold feasts in turn, each on his day, and invite their sisters; A great wind from the desert strikes the four corners of the house and it falls on the feasting children; God has set a protective hedge around the righteous man, his house and goods; 'Fire of God' falls from heaven and consumes flocks and servants; Messenger after messenger arrives while the last is still speaking, each the sole survivor of a disaster; 'I alone escaped to tell you'; 'Does he fear God for nothing?': piety suspected of being motivated by reward; The exemplary righteous man is a non-Israelite living in the land of Uz in the east; Father offers burnt offerings in case his children 'blessed' (cursed) God in their hearts; A blessed man has seven sons and three daughters; Mourner shaves his head and falls to the ground; and 15 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God's crafting of the human body, and what is said to follow from it [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews (weight 5.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Pair score 17.0.

Only in Job - 'Your hands fashioned me'; land of darkness: The sufferer reminds God that God's hands shaped him yet now destroy him; 'Have you eyes of flesh? Are your days like a mortal's days?'; God hunts the sufferer like a lion; The underworld as a land of darkness and deep shadow, without order, where light is like darkness; God created Adam 'with my two hands'; God creates you in your mothers' bellies creation after creation in three darknesses; Like a vanishing cloud, whoever goes down to Sheol does not come up; his place knows him no more; From dust, then a drop, then a clinging clot ('alaqa), then a child, then full strength, then old age; some die before; Have you seen what you emit? Do you create it, or are we the creator?; Sufferer wishes he had died in the womb or been a hidden stillborn; Human created in stages: a drop of sperm (nutfa), a clinging clot ('alaq/'alaqa), then shaped and proportioned; Human comes from dust and returns to dust.

Only in Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships: God called 'the best of creators' (aḥsan al-khāliqīn); Cattle are a lesson: God gives drink from what is in their bellies; A tree springing from Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Saynāʾ) yields oil and a relish for eaters; In the womb God makes the lump into bones and clothes the bones with flesh, then makes it another creation; At creation God fixed the weight of the wind, the measure of the waters, a decree for the rain and a way for the thunderbolt; Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped; God's eyes saw the speaker's unformed substance (golem); all his days were written in God's book before one of them existed; The speaker too was 'pinched off from clay' (qoratsti), like a figure nipped from a lump of clay; God fashions seven heavens.

leads.title: Eliphaz's first speech, the night vision ↔ The first of those who submit; canopies of fire; chambers above chambers
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The Book in paired repetitions (mathani) makes the skins of the godfearing shiver, then their skins and hearts soften (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Eliphaz's first speech, the night vision: God puts no trust in his servants and charges his angels with folly; Humans are dwellers in houses of clay founded in dust, crushed like a moth; The roaring lion's teeth are broken and its cubs scattered (image of the wicked's end); In a night vision a spirit glides past the seer's face and his hair bristles with terror; Revelation comes as 'a silence, and a voice' (demamah vaqol); 'Can a mortal be righteous before God, a man pure before his maker?'; God casts a deep sleep (tardemah) on a man; Friend's doctrine: no innocent man ever perished; those who plow iniquity reap it.

Only in The first of those who submit; canopies of fire; chambers above chambers: An Arabic Quran without any crookedness; The damned have canopies (zulal) of fire above them and below them; For the godfearing are lofty chambers with built chambers above them, beneath which rivers flow; God expands a person's breast (sharh al-sadr) to Islam so he is upon a light from his Lord; The punishment of hell envelops the damned from above them and from beneath their feet; Parable: a slave owned by quarreling partners versus a slave belonging wholly to one man; Humans are like grass that flourishes in the morning and withers by evening; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: One brother stays behind in Egypt (weight 6.0); Plan to store grain in the good years for the famine years (weight 6.0); A wild animal is blamed for the hero's death (weight 6.0); Their payment is secretly returned in their bags (weight 6.0); Hero asks the freed prisoner to mention him to the king (weight 6.0); Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode (weight 6.0); Birds eat bread from on top of the dreamer's head (weight 6.0); King dreams of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean, and seven green ears and seven dry (weight 6.0); Hero's cup is hidden in the youngest brother's bag (weight 6.0); One prisoner is restored, the other executed and his body exposed (weight 6.0); The freed prisoner remembers the hero and recommends him (weight 6.0); Brothers bring the hero's garment with false blood (weight 6.0); Two fellow prisoners dream of pressing wine and carrying bread (weight 6.0); A passing caravan takes the hero from the pit (weight 6.0); One brother talks the others out of killing him (weight 6.0); Hero reveals his identity to his brothers (weight 6.0); Father loves the hero more than his brothers (weight 6.0); God's favor rests on the hero while he is a slave or prisoner (weight 6.0); Father revives on hearing the hero lives (weight 6.0); The brothers themselves name the thief's penalty (weight 6.0); The freed prisoner forgets the hero for years (weight 6.0); A brother offers himself or another in place of the youngest (weight 6.0); Hero demands they bring their youngest brother (weight 6.0); Hero meets and embraces his father (weight 6.0); Hero refuses, citing loyalty to his master and to God (weight 6.0); Brothers come for grain and do not recognize the hero (weight 6.0); Hero sold for a small sum of silver (weight 6.0); Dream of sun, moon and eleven stars bowing to the hero (weight 6.0); Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero (weight 6.0); Hero cast into a pit or well (weight 5.8); A brother or the brothers give the father a pledge for the youngest (weight 5.8); Hero thrown into prison (weight 5.8); The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault (weight 5.8); Hero bought by an Egyptian official (weight 5.8); Family prostrates before the hero, fulfilling the dream (weight 5.8); The master's wife tries to seduce the hero (weight 5.8); The whole family moves to Egypt (weight 5.8); The father's eyesight fails (weight 5.8); Seduction attempt when the two are alone in the house (weight 5.8); Search proceeds through the others' bags before the youngest's (weight 5.8); Brothers pursued and accused of theft (weight 5.8); Hero placed over the land's storehouses or the kingdom (weight 5.6); Hero declares that God turned the brothers' deed to good (weight 5.6); Hero forgives his brothers (weight 5.6); Father refuses at first to send the youngest (weight 5.6); Hero attributes his dream interpretation to God (weight 5.4); The king's experts cannot interpret the dream (weight 5.3); Hero's beauty is remarked on (weight 4.9). Pair score 281.2.

Only in Joseph in Genesis (37, 39–50): After the father's death the brothers fear revenge; Grandfather crosses his hands to bless the younger first; Dream of the brothers' sheaves bowing to the hero's sheaf; Embalming in the Egyptian manner; Hero buys the people's land for the king during the famine; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort; Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind; Father himself sends the hero to his brothers; Father gives the hero a special garment; Hero accuses his brothers of being spies; Hero given an Egyptian priest's daughter as wife; Master entrusts his whole household to the hero; and 4 more.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 61 more.

Only in God commissions Joshua; Transjordan tribes pledged: People pledge to obey the successor as they obeyed his predecessor; rebels to die; Every place your foot treads will be yours, from the wilderness to the Euphrates; Three days of preparation before a decisive crossing or event; Formula: be strong and courageous, do not fear, God will not leave or forsake you; Leader charges his successor to be strong and courageous; Tribes settled east of the Jordan must lead the armed vanguard for their brothers.

Only in Signs for people of understanding; closing prayer: 'We heard a caller calling to faith: believe in your Lord'; God does not waste the work of any worker, male or female; you are of one another; Be patient, vie in patience, stand guard (rabitu); The heavens recount God's glory; day to day pours out speech without words or voice; 'Our Lord, you have not created this in vain'; Among the People of the Book an upright community recites God's signs through the night and prostrates; Those who remember God standing, sitting and on their sides and reflect on creation; Catalogue of signs: heavens and earth, alternation of night and day, ships, rain reviving dead earth, beasts, winds, clouds; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God casts great hailstones from heaven, killing more than the sword (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in Battle of Gibeon, hailstones, sun and moon stand still, five kings in the cave, southern campaign: Summary of a sweeping conquest of the whole south from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza; Captains put their feet on the necks of captured kings; Five kings form an alliance and are defeated together; God heeds the command of a man, a unique event; A king of Jerusalem bears a name with 'tsedeq' (Adoni-zedek, Melchizedek); Defeated kings hide in a cave, which is sealed with great stones; The army marches all night and attacks the enemy by surprise; Idiom: no one 'sharpened his tongue' against Israel; A lost source book is cited (the Book of Jashar); A captured enemy king is killed and hanged on a tree until sunset, then buried under stones; 'You did not throw when you threw, but God threw': the victory is God's act; God throws the enemy into confusion and panic before Israel; and 4 more.

Only in The companions of the elephant: God sends birds in flocks (tayran ababil) that pelt an army with stones of baked clay (sijjil), leaving them like devoured straw; God's action against the companions of the elephant (ashab al-fil), whose plot he made go astray; The angel of YHWH strikes 185,000 in the enemy camp in one night; at dawn all are corpses [divergence between the texts]; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant [divergence between the texts]; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant; The wicked are like chaff driven by the wind.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A man secretly takes from the goods devoted to God (herem) (weight 6.7); The army is defeated because of one member's hidden sin (weight 6.7); A man secretly takes from the goods devoted to God (herem) [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 20.1.

Only in Defeat at Ai and the trespass of Achan: The culprit is urged to 'give glory to God' by confessing; The sinner's children, animals and property are destroyed with him; Leader complains to God after a defeat: would that we had stayed where we were; Sin described as a sequence: I saw, I coveted, I took, I hid; Spies are sent ahead to scout a land for conquest; A great heap of stones is raised over an executed man, 'to this day'; Lot or Urim-Thummim cast to identify the guilty party (tamim); Leader and elders tear their clothes, fall on their faces and put dust on their heads; A place is named after an event that happened there, 'to this day'.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A destroyed city is made a perpetual ruin-mound (tel olam) (weight 6.7); The fate of a destroyed town: lasting ruin or revival [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Ambush and capture of Ai; altar and Torah inscribed on Mount Ebal: Leader holds out his javelin and does not lower his hand until victory is complete; A captured enemy king is killed and hanged on a tree until sunset, then buried under stones; Large stones plastered with lime and inscribed with the whole Torah after crossing; The whole law is read aloud before the assembly, including women, children and foreigners; Column of smoke from the city is the prearranged signal of the ambush; Blessing pronounced on Mount Gerizim and curse on Mount Ebal; A great heap of stones is raised over an executed man, 'to this day'; Altar of whole stones on which no iron tool is lifted; Feigned retreat draws defenders out while an ambush takes the city; Ban (herem): total destruction of a conquered population.

Only in The man who passed a ruined town: The sleeper is shown his donkey's bones assembled and clothed with flesh; After a century the sleeper's food and drink have not spoiled; A man passing a ruined town is made to die for a hundred years, then revived, thinking he slept a day or part of a day; The question whether God can make the dead live [divergence between the texts]; At the prophet's word there is a rattling; bones come together bone to bone, then sinews, flesh and skin cover them, but there is no breath.

וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ גִּדְע֜וֹן אֶת מִסְפַּ֧ר הַחֲל֛וֹם וְאֶת שִׁבְר֖וֹ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ אֶל מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ק֔וּמוּ כִּֽי נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה בְּיֶדְכֶ֖ם אֶת מַחֲנֵ֥ה מִדְיָֽן

Lev 11 forbids many species and treats contact with nəbēlâ as defiling (hannōgēaʿ bənibəlātāh yiṭmāʾ ... wəhāʾōkēl minnibəlātāh yəkabbēs bəgādāyw). Lev's carrion rule (purification, not a ban on eating) also differs from Q's maytah.

matches.label: Intercourse with a menstruating woman is forbidden
matches.note: Same verb of approach: Lev 18:19 wĕ-ʾel ʾiššâ bĕ-niddat ṭumʾātāh lōʾ tiqrab lĕ-gallôt ʿerwātāh; Q 2:222 qul huwa adhan fa-ʿtazilū n-nisāʾa fī l-maḥīḍi wa-lā taqrabūhunna ḥattā yaṭhurna (q-r-b in both). Leviticus calls it impurity (ṭumʾâ); the Quran calls menstruation 'a hurt' (adhan) and then gives positive permission when they are purified (fa-idhā taṭahharna fa-ʾtūhunna).

matches.label: List of forbidden close-kin unions ('uncovering nakedness')
matches.note: Lev 18:7-17 ʿerwat ... lōʾ tĕgallēh: mother, father's wife, sister and half-sister, granddaughter, aunts, uncle's wife, daughter-in-law, brother's wife, a woman with her daughter; Q 4:23 ḥurrimat ʿalaykum ummahātukum wa-banātukum wa-akhawātukum wa-ʿammātukum wa-khālātukum wa-banātu l-akhi wa-banātu l-ukhti wa-ummahātukumu llātī arḍaʿnakum wa-akhawātukum mina r-raḍāʿa ...: mothers, daughters, sisters, aunts, nieces, nursing mothers and milk sisters, mothers-in-law, stepdaughters, sons' wives. Shared core; the Quran adds daughters and nieces (not named in Lev 18) and milk kinship (absent from the HB), and drops the uncle's wife and the brother's wife (Lev 18:14, 16). Formula: 'uncover nakedness' vs 'forbidden to you'.

matches.note: Lev 23:27-32 wĕ-ʿinnîtem ʾet napšōtêkem ... kî kol ha-nnepeš ʾăšer lōʾ tĕʿunneh ... wĕ-nikrĕtâ ... mē-ʿereb ʿad ʿereb: one day of self-affliction on the tenth of the seventh month, from evening to evening, on pain of being cut off; Q 2:183-187 kutiba ʿalaykumu ṣ-ṣiyāmu ka-mā kutiba ʿalā lladhīna min qablikum ... ayyāman maʿdūdātin ... ḥattā yatabayyana lakumu l-khayṭu l-abyaḍu ... thumma atimmū ṣ-ṣiyāma ilā l-layl: a fast 'as prescribed for those before you', but for a whole month, from dawn to nightfall, with eating at night, and exemptions for the sick and traveller and ransom by feeding the poor (fidya). evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Redemption of land, interest-free loans, and Israelite bondmen: An impoverished Israelite sold to a brother serves as a hired worker, not a slave, until the jubilee; Houses in Levite cities can always be redeemed and their fields never sold; Do not rule over a fellow Israelite with harshness (perekh); Permanent slaves may be bought from surrounding nations and resident aliens and bequeathed; A house in a walled city can be redeemed only within a year and does not return at the jubilee; Freeing or buying back the enslaved [divergence between the texts]; Sold land returns to its ancestral owner in the jubilee; Israelite sold to a resident alien may be redeemed by kin or himself, priced by years to jubilee; Whose slaves or servants the Israelites are [contrast between the texts]; Israelites cannot be sold as slaves because they are God's servants whom he brought out of Egypt; Nearest kinsman (go'el) has the right and duty to redeem land and family.
