matches.note: What fat is exempt. Lev puts on the altar ha-ḥēlev ha-məkhasseh ʾet-haq-qerev wə-ʾēt kol-ha-ḥēlev ʾăšer ʿal-haq-qerev (the fat on the entrails) and ha-ʾalyāh təmîmāh lə-ʿummat he-ʿāṣeh (the fat tail by the backbone). Lev: nefeš kî tiššāvaʿ ləvaṭṭēʾ vi-śfātayim, a lamb or goat, if one cannot afford it two birds, and if not that, a tenth of an ephah of flour (wə-ʾim-lōʾ taggîaʿ yādô ... wə-ʾim-lōʾ taśśîg yādô). evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Son dishonors father, daughter rises against mother, daughter-in-law against mother-in-law; a man's enemies are his own household (weight 6.7); Son dishonors father, daughter rises against mother, daughter-in-law against mother-in-law; a man's enemies are his own household [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in No godly man left; who is a God like you?: 'Do not rejoice over me, my enemy: though I fall I shall rise; though I sit in darkness YHWH is my light'; The godly have vanished from the land like a vineyard after gleaning with no cluster to eat; God will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea; Trust no neighbor or friend; guard your mouth even from the wife in your bosom; God will show truth to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham as he swore to the fathers; Enemies bow down and lick the dust before the king or God; 'Lay your hand upon your mouth': gesture of appalled silence; Nations taunt 'Where is their God?'; God called the patriarch's shepherd all his life; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'.

Only in Al-Taghabun: forms made beautiful, the Day of Mutual Loss, enemies among wives and children, and the goodly loan: The Day of Gathering is the Day of Mutual Dispossession / Loss and Gain (yawm al-taghabun); Among your spouses and children are enemies to you, so beware of them; yet if you pardon and forgive, God is forgiving; Fear God as much as you are able (ma stata'tum); No calamity strikes except by God's leave; whoever believes, God guides his heart; Unbelievers rejected their messengers saying 'Shall mere humans guide us?'; God created you, and among you are unbelievers and believers; God shaped you and made your forms good (sawwarakum fa-ahsana suwarakum); The poor emigrants and the hosts who prefer others over themselves even in need; whoever is saved from his own greed succeeds; The Day of Gathering (yawm al-jam') when all humanity is assembled; one party to the Garden, one to the Blaze; Wealth and children are a trial (fitna); The prophet is not a guardian over people; his duty is only to deliver the message (al-balagh); God is the Rich (al-ghani) and you are the poor; the miser is miserly only against himself; and 5 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Cluster of divine epithets in sequence (e.g. the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne, the Glorious, doer of what he wills; or Lord, King, God of mankind) (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in The jealous and avenging God against Nineveh: God's way is in whirlwind and storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet; One who plots evil against YHWH comes out of the enemy city, a counselor of Belial (beliyya'al); YHWH is an avenging God (noqem), 'lord of wrath' (ba'al hemah), keeping anger for his enemies; God rebukes the sea and dries it up and makes all rivers fail; Bashan, Carmel and Lebanon wither; 'Who can stand before his indignation?': rhetorical question on the unendurable divine wrath; Command to destroy figured stones, molten images and high places of the land; God broke the bars of the yoke and made the people walk upright; God is a jealous God; God called rock, fortress, refuge, stronghold or tower of strength; At God's coming the earth quakes, heavens drip and mountains flow; Formula of divine attributes: slow to anger, abundant in mercy, visits iniquity to fourth generation; The poem is an alphabetic acrostic (lines or stanzas begin with successive letters); and 1 more.

Only in The constellations: the people of the ditch and the preserved tablet: The scripture is a glorious recitation inscribed on a preserved tablet (lawh mahfuz) in heaven; Oath by the sky possessing the constellations or towers (dhat al-buruj); The people of the ditch (ashab al-ukhdud) sit by a fire pit, watching what they do to believers, whose only offense was faith in God; The scripture is a glorious recitation inscribed on a preserved tablet (lawh mahfuz) in heaven [divergence between the texts]; Hero thrown into a fire or furnace by a king or people [divergence between the texts]; God originates creation and then repeats it (resurrection as re-creation); List of destroyed peoples or hosts (e.g. 'Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh) recalled as warning; Hero thrown into a fire or furnace by a king or people; A series of oaths by natural phenomena (dawn, night, day, sun, moon, sky, earth, stars, winds) opens or punctuates a passage.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Prohibition of intermarriage with the peoples of the land lest they turn sons to other gods [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3); Prohibition of intermarriage with the peoples of the land lest they turn sons to other gods (weight 5.4). Pair score 11.7.

Only in The sealed pledge (amanah) and its stipulations: Community pledges an annual third of a shekel for the temple service; The people enter into a curse and an oath to walk in God's Torah; Named list of those who sealed the covenant document; Pledge not to buy wares or grain from foreign traders on the Sabbath or holy day; Pledge: 'we will not forsake the house of our God'; A written covenant document (amanah) sealed by leaders; Seventh-year release (shemittah) of debts owed by a fellow Israelite; Gifts, firstfruits and holy portions assigned to the priests; Those who separate themselves from the impurity of the nations join the community; The land lies fallow in the seventh year for the poor and wild animals; Families cast lots for set times to bring wood for the altar fire; Ban on marrying outside the community and its criterion [divergence between the texts]; and 2 more.

Only in Contracts, pilgrim sanctity and the forbidden foods: The food of the People of the Book is lawful to believers and theirs to them; Fulfil your contracts and covenants (ʿuqūd); Sacrificial animals (hady) marked with garlands (qalāʾid) are inviolable; Believers may marry chaste women of the People of the Book; 'Today I have perfected your religion and completed my favor'; The sacred month and God's rites must not be profaned; Forbidden: the strangled, the beaten to death, the fallen and the gored animal; What trained hunting animals (dogs, birds of prey) catch is lawful, with God's name pronounced; Divination by shaking or drawing arrows (belomancy); Eating carrion or torn flesh is forbidden or defiling [divergence between the texts]; Seeking decisions by divining arrows (azlām) is forbidden; Flesh of an animal torn by a beast of prey is not to be eaten [divergence between the texts]; and 9 more.

leads.title: Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession ↔ Address to the Children of Israel
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: People of the Book cast God's book behind their backs (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession: God found Abraham's heart faithful (ne'eman) before him; God chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and renamed him Abraham; Call to bless God 'from everlasting to everlasting'; God's ordinances are those 'which a man shall do and live by them'; 'You give life to them all' - God sustains all creation; God gave his good spirit to instruct the people in the wilderness; Levites stand on a platform and cry out to God with a loud voice; A quarter of the day spent reading the Torah and a quarter confessing and bowing; God made known his holy Sabbath at Sinai; The seed of Israel separate themselves from all foreigners; Drowned enemies sink like a stone or like lead in mighty waters; Closing doxology: glory to your Lord, Lord of might, above what they describe; peace on the messengers; praise to God, Lord of the worlds; and 17 more.

Only in Address to the Children of Israel: If the people keep God's covenant, God keeps his covenant with them; God's choosing of Israel among the peoples [divergence between the texts]; On that day no soul will avail another, no intercession or ransom accepted, no help given; Refrain to the Children of Israel: 'remember my favor which I bestowed on you'; God rebukes the wicked who recites his statutes and covenant yet consorts with thieves and adulterers; Whether payment may substitute for a life [contrast between the texts]; Israel chosen as God's treasured people (am segullah) out of all peoples; No man can ransom his brother or give God a ransom (kofer) for him; the redemption of life is too costly; Each person dies for his own sin.

leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: People of the Book cast God's book behind their backs (weight 5.8); Israel killed the prophets who warned them (weight 5.1); People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain (weight 4.7). Pair score 15.6.

Only in Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession: God found Abraham's heart faithful (ne'eman) before him; God chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and renamed him Abraham; Call to bless God 'from everlasting to everlasting'; God's ordinances are those 'which a man shall do and live by them'; 'You give life to them all' - God sustains all creation; God gave his good spirit to instruct the people in the wilderness; Levites stand on a platform and cry out to God with a loud voice; A quarter of the day spent reading the Torah and a quarter confessing and bowing; God made known his holy Sabbath at Sinai; The seed of Israel separate themselves from all foreigners; Drowned enemies sink like a stone or like lead in mighty waters; Closing doxology: glory to your Lord, Lord of might, above what they describe; peace on the messengers; praise to God, Lord of the worlds; and 15 more.

Only in Polemic with the People of the Book: The love of the calf was made to sink (be drunk) into their hearts; If the next world is yours alone, wish for death: they never will; Enmity to Gabriel and Michael (Mikal) equated with enmity to God; Gabriel (Jibril) brings down the revelation upon the prophet's heart; Some wish to be granted a life of a thousand years; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Claim that the fire will touch them only for a few numbered days, rebutted; The idol is burned, ground to powder, scattered on water and the people made to drink it; Israel at the mountain says 'we hear and we disobey' (sami'na wa-'asayna); Woe to those who write the book with their own hands and say it is from God, for a small price; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; and 14 more.

Only in Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession: God found Abraham's heart faithful (ne'eman) before him; God chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and renamed him Abraham; Call to bless God 'from everlasting to everlasting'; God's ordinances are those 'which a man shall do and live by them'; 'You give life to them all' - God sustains all creation; God gave his good spirit to instruct the people in the wilderness; Levites stand on a platform and cry out to God with a loud voice; A quarter of the day spent reading the Torah and a quarter confessing and bowing; God made known his holy Sabbath at Sinai; The seed of Israel separate themselves from all foreigners; Drowned enemies sink like a stone or like lead in mighty waters; Closing doxology: glory to your Lord, Lord of might, above what they describe; peace on the messengers; praise to God, Lord of the worlds; and 17 more.

matches.label: What Korah's sin was, and why the earth swallowed him
matches.note: Korah's offence: Numbers has a religious revolt against Moses and Aaron, rav lākhem kî khol hā-ʿēdâ kullām qədōšîm ... û-maddûaʿ titnaśśəʾû ʿal qəhal YHWH, with Dathan, Abiram and 250 chieftains. The Quran has the wealth and arrogance of a single man of Moses' people: Qārūna kāna min qawmi Mūsā fa-baghā ʿalayhim wa-ātaynāhu mina l-kunūzi mā inna mafātiḥahu la-tanūʾu bi-l-ʿuṣbati, who boasts innamā ūtītuhu ʿalā ʿilmin ʿindī and parades in his finery. The Quran has no priesthood dispute, incense test or fellow rebels. cf. b. Sanh. 110a and b. Pes. 119a (Korah's wealth), outside the HB.

matches.note: Num 27:8-11 ʾîš kî yāmût û-bēn ʾên lô wĕ-haʿăbartem ʾet naḥălātô lĕ-bittô wĕ-ʾim ʾên lô bat ... lĕ-ʾeḥāyw ... la-ʾăḥê ʾābîw ... li-šʾērô ha-qqārōb: a chain of single heirs: son, else daughter, else brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; Q 4:11-12 li-dh-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi l-unthayayn ... wa-li-abawayhi li-kulli wāḥidin minhumā s-sudusu ... wa-lakum niṣfu mā taraka azwājukum: fixed fractional shares for several heirs at once, daughters with sons, parents, and spouses (absent from Num 27), siblings only for the kalāla. A sequence of exclusive heirs becomes a set of simultaneous shares. The Quran begins yūṣīkumu llāhu 'God charges you' (cf. ḥuqqat mišpāṭ, 27:11).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: No one put to death on the testimony of a single witness (weight 5.4). Pair score 5.4.

Only in Levitical cities, cities of refuge and the law of homicide: Murder distinguished from manslaughter by weapon (iron, stone, wood), enmity and intent; Manslayer may leave refuge only at the death of the high priest; Shed blood pollutes the land and only the killer's blood atones for it; Forty-eight cities with pasture-lands of measured cubits assigned to the Levites; No ransom (kofer) may be taken for a murderer's life; How many witnesses a charge requires [divergence between the texts]; A place of refuge for one who kills unintentionally [divergence between the texts]; The 'redeemer of blood' (go'el ha-dam) kills the murderer; Same law for the resident alien and the native; Whether payment may substitute for a life [contrast between the texts]; Six cities of refuge for the unintentional killer, three on each side of the Jordan.

Only in Indecency, four witnesses, and the limits of repentance: Women guilty of indecency are confined to houses until death or until God makes a way; Repentance is not accepted from one who repents only when death comes; Four witnesses are required to establish sexual indecency (fāḥisha); Offenders who repent and reform are to be left alone; Penalty for adultery or sexual indecency [contrast between the texts]; How sin committed in ignorance is forgiven [divergence between the texts]; God accepts repentance from those who do evil in ignorance and soon repent; Whether repentance has a time limit [divergence between the texts]; How many witnesses are required [divergence between the texts].

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether and how daughters inherit [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Daughters petition and win the right to inherit when there is no son (weight 5.8). Pair score 12.1.

Only in Marriage of heiresses within the tribe; colophon of Numbers: The Jubilee year considered in tribal land transfers; Daughters who inherit must marry within their father's tribe so land does not pass away; The marriage of fatherless girls is tied to their inheritance [divergence between the texts].

Only in The fixed shares of inheritance: Shares are distributed only after a bequest (waṣiyya) and debts are paid; Inheritance fixed in fractions (one half, a third, a quarter, a sixth, an eighth, two-thirds); Husband and wife inherit fixed shares from each other; Three named daughters (Jemimah, Keziah, Keren-happuch), the most beautiful in the land, inherit among their brothers; Who receives a double share of inheritance [divergence between the texts]; One who dies without parent or child (kalāla): brothers and sisters inherit fixed shares; A son (or brother) inherits the share of two daughters (or sisters); Rules for who inherits and in what order or share [divergence between the texts]; 'These are the bounds (hudud) of God; do not approach (or transgress) them'; Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

matches.note: Num 36:8 wĕ-kol bat yōrešet naḥălâ ... lĕ-ʾeḥād mi-mmišpaḥat maṭṭēh ʾābîhā tihyeh lĕ-ʾiššâ: an heiress must marry within her father's tribe so the land stays in it; Q 4:11-12: the shares go to persons (daughters, spouses, parents) with no tribal or land restriction, and a husband inherits from his wife (wa-lakum niṣfu mā taraka azwājukum), which would move property across lines.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Marriage of heiresses within the tribe; colophon of Numbers: The Jubilee year considered in tribal land transfers; Daughters who inherit must marry within their father's tribe so land does not pass away; Whether and how daughters inherit [divergence between the texts]; Daughters petition and win the right to inherit when there is no son.

Only in Orphan girls, reconciliation, the suspended wife, and justice against oneself: You will never be able to be equally just among wives, however eager; A wife who fears her husband's aversion may make a settlement with him; settlement is best; Whether separation of spouses is allowed or hated by God [contrast between the texts]; Form: 'They ask you for a ruling (yastaftūnaka); say: God gives you a ruling'; Do not leave a wife 'suspended' (kal-muʿallaqa), neither married nor free; Stand firm for justice as witnesses for God even against yourselves, parents and kin, rich or poor; Judge fairly, favoring neither the poor nor the great; Guardians must keep orphans' property intact and hand it over when they come of age; If God wills he takes you away and brings another people in your place.

matches.label: The marriage of fatherless girls is tied to their inheritance
matches.note: In both, a female orphan's inheritance is tied to her marriage. Num makes marriage within the father's clan a duty, so the naḥălāh does not pass to another tribe: ʾakh lə-mišpaḥat maṭṭēh ʾăvîhem tihyênāh lə-nāšîm. Q censures guardians who wish to marry orphan girls while withholding what is written for them: allātī lā tuʾtūnahunna mā kutiba lahunna wa-targhabūna an tankiḥūhunna.

leads.title: The suspected adulteress and the bitter water ↔ Lashes for fornication, four witnesses and the mutual cursing oath
leads.summary: 4 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed, 1 opposite ruling, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Adultery done in secret with no witness and not caught in the act (weight 6.7); Whether the husband who accuses his wife bears any liability [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7); How the case of a wife suspected of adultery is decided [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Who swears, and how, when a husband suspects his wife of adultery without witnesses [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Wife suspected of adultery drinks 'water of bitterness' as an ordeal (weight 6.7). Pair score 33.5.

Only in The suspected adulteress and the bitter water: Suspected wife's offering is barley flour without oil or frankincense, a 'meal offering of jealousy'; Ordeal curse: the guilty woman's belly swells and her thigh falls; Person responds to an imprecation with 'Amen, amen'; Holy water in an earthen vessel mixed with dust from the sanctuary floor; Husband who brings an ordeal accusation is free of guilt whatever the result; Woman cleared by the ordeal will bear children; A 'spirit of jealousy' comes over a husband who suspects his wife; Priest unbinds the accused woman's hair before God; Written curses are wiped into water that the accused then drinks; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; An oath before God settles a suspicion that cannot be proven.

Only in Lashes for fornication, four witnesses and the mutual cursing oath: The fornicating woman and man each receive a hundred lashes, witnessed by a party of believers; A fornicator may marry only a fornicator or an idolater; such marriage is forbidden to believers; A husband accusing his wife without witnesses swears four times by God and a fifth time invokes God's curse on himself if lying; she averts punishment by four counter-oaths and a fifth invoking God's wrath; Whoever accuses a chaste woman without four witnesses is flogged eighty lashes and his testimony is never accepted; Who is barred from marrying an unchaste woman [divergence between the texts]; Judges told to let no pity hold them back from carrying out a fixed punishment; How many lashes a flogging may have [contrast between the texts]; A man accused swears a curse-oath before the altar, and God judges guilty and innocent; The penalty for adultery or fornication [contrast between the texts]; The penalty for falsely accusing a woman of unchastity [divergence between the texts]; Husband who falsely accuses his bride is flogged, fined 100 silver, and may never divorce her; Adulterer and adulteress both put to death; and 3 more.

leads.finding: Who swears, and how, when a husband suspects his wife of adultery without witnesses

units.title: The suspected adulteress and the bitter water

matches.label: Who swears, and how, when a husband suspects his wife of adultery without witnesses
matches.note: Who swears: in Num 5 only the woman, made to swear by the priest (wə-hišbîaʿ ʾōtāh hak-kōhēn bi-švuʿat hā-ʾālâ), answering ʾāmēn ʾāmēn; in Q 24 the husband swears first, four times by God (arbaʿu shahādātin bi-llāh) and a fifth time that God's curse (laʿnat Allāh) be on him if he lies, then the wife swears four counter-oaths and a fifth calling God's wrath (ghaḍab Allāh) on herself. The curse falls on both parties, no priest is involved and there is no sanctuary rite.

passages.text: וְהִשְׁבִּ֨יעַ אֹתָ֜הּ הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְאָמַ֤ר אֶל הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אִם לֹ֨א שָׁכַ֥ב אִישׁ֙ אֹתָ֔ךְ וְאִם לֹ֥א שָׂטִ֛ית טֻמְאָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת אִישֵׁ֑ךְ הִנָּקִ֕י מִמֵּ֛י הַמָּרִ֥ים הַֽמְאָרֲרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

וְהִשְׁבִּ֨יעַ הַכֹּהֵ֥ן אֶֽת הָֽאִשָּׁה֮ בִּשְׁבֻעַ֣ת הָאָלָה֒ וְאָמַ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ לָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה יִתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה אוֹתָ֛ךְ לְאָלָ֥ה וְלִשְׁבֻעָ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ עַמֵּ֑ךְ בְּתֵ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אֶת יְרֵכֵךְ֙ נֹפֶ֔לֶת וְאֶת בִּטְנֵ֖ךְ צָבָֽה
וּ֠בָאוּ הַמַּ֨יִם הַמְאָרְרִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ בְּֽמֵעַ֔יִךְ לַצְבּ֥וֹת בֶּ֖טֶן וְלַנְפִּ֣ל יָרֵ֑ךְ וְאָמְרָ֥ה הָאִשָּׁ֖ה אָמֵ֥ן אָמֵֽן
وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْوَٰجَهُمْ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ شُهَدَآءُ إِلَّآ أَنفُسُهُمْ فَشَهَٰدَةُ أَحَدِهِمْ أَرْبَعُ شَهَٰدَٰتٍۭ بِٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
وَٱلْخَٰمِسَةُ أَنَّ لَعْنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
وَيَدْرَؤُا۟ عَنْهَا ٱلْعَذَابَ أَن تَشْهَدَ أَرْبَعَ شَهَٰدَٰتٍۭ بِٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ

matches.label: How the case of a wife suspected of adultery is decided
matches.note: Outcome: Num 5 lets the bitter water decide, with a physical sign on the guilty body (bə-tēt YHWH ʾet yərēkhēk nōfelet wə-ʾet biṭnēk ṣāvâ); in Q 24:8 the wife's oath alone averts the punishment (wa-yadraʾu ʿanhā l-ʿadhāba an tashhada), with no ordeal, water, dust or written curse, and the verdict is left to God.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The suspected adulteress and the bitter water: Suspected wife's offering is barley flour without oil or frankincense, a 'meal offering of jealousy'; Ordeal curse: the guilty woman's belly swells and her thigh falls; Person responds to an imprecation with 'Amen, amen'; Holy water in an earthen vessel mixed with dust from the sanctuary floor; Husband who brings an ordeal accusation is free of guilt whatever the result; Woman cleared by the ordeal will bear children; A 'spirit of jealousy' comes over a husband who suspects his wife; Priest unbinds the accused woman's hair before God; Written curses are wiped into water that the accused then drinks; Whether the husband who accuses his wife bears any liability [contrast between the texts]; Wife suspected of adultery drinks 'water of bitterness' as an ordeal; An oath before God settles a suspicion that cannot be proven; and 3 more.

leads.title: Agur's numerical sayings (leech, four wonders, four small wise creatures) ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The ant, a people without strength, prepares its food in summer (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Agur's numerical sayings (leech, four wonders, four small wise creatures): The adulteress eats, wipes her mouth and says 'I have done no wrong'; Pressing milk produces butter, pressing the nose produces blood, pressing anger produces strife (pun on af 'nose/anger'); Do not slander a slave to his master lest he curse you; Four small but wise creatures: ants storing food in summer, rock-badgers housed in rock, locusts with no king marching in ranks, the lizard in kings' palaces; Four stately in stride: the lion mightiest of beasts, the strutting rooster (zarzir), the he-goat, and a king with his army; Under four the earth trembles: a slave who becomes king, a fool sated with food, an unloved woman who marries, a maid who supplants her mistress; Catalogue of a corrupt 'generation' (dor): cursing parents, self-righteous yet unwashed, haughty, with sword-teeth devouring the poor; If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, put your hand on your mouth; The leech ('aluqah) has two daughters: 'Give, give!'; The locusts have no king yet all go out in ranks; The eye that mocks a father and scorns a mother will be pecked out by ravens of the valley and eaten by young vultures; Four wonders: the way of an eagle in the sky, a serpent on a rock, a ship in the sea, and a man with a young woman ('almah); and 4 more.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 22 more.

Only in Proverbs 6:20-35, commandment as lamp; adultery as fire in the bosom: 'The commandment is a lamp and the teaching (torah) is light; reproofs of discipline are the way of life'; Can a man carry fire in his bosom and his clothes not burn, or walk on coals and his feet not be scorched? So is adultery; A prostitute costs a loaf of bread, but another man's wife hunts the precious life; The jealous husband shows no mercy on the day of vengeance and will accept no ransom (kofer) or bribe for adultery; When you walk it will lead you, when you lie down it will watch over you, when you wake it will talk with you; A starving thief is not despised, yet when caught he repays sevenfold, giving all the wealth of his house; How far a child must obey father and mother [divergence between the texts]; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden; 'Hear, my son, your father's instruction and do not forsake your mother's teaching (torah)'; Bind the teachings around your neck (or fingers) and write them on the tablet of your heart; Warning against the 'strange woman' (ishah zarah / nokhriyyah) with smooth words.

leads.title: Proverbs 6:1-19, surety, the ant, the scoundrel, six things God hates ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: 'Go to the ant, sluggard': without chief or ruler she stores food in summer and harvest (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Proverbs 6:1-19, surety, the ant, the scoundrel, six things God hates: The worthless man (adam beliyya'al) winks with his eyes, scrapes with his feet and points with his fingers, sowing discord; Six things YHWH hates, seven an abomination: haughty eyes, lying tongue, hands shedding innocent blood, scheming heart, feet running to evil, false witness, sower of discord; Warning against striking hands as surety for a neighbor or stranger; free yourself without sleep like a gazelle from the hunter; 'A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands', and poverty comes like a vagabond, want like an armed man; Do not obey every contemptible swearer, backbiter going about with slander, hinderer of good, coarse and moreover 'zanim' (base-born, ignoble); Graded numerical saying ('One thing God spoke, two things I heard'; 'three, yes four').

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 22 more.

leads.title: Proverbs 8:22-31, Wisdom before and at creation ↔ The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations
leads.summary: 2 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness (weight 6.3); A solid firmament (raqia) separates upper waters from lower waters (weight 5.6). Pair score 11.9.

Only in Proverbs 8:22-31, Wisdom before and at creation: 'YHWH acquired (or created, qanani) me as the beginning (reshit) of his way, the first of his works of old'; Wisdom was beside God as an 'amon' (master craftsman, or nursling/child); Wisdom was brought forth (holalti, 'born in travail') when there were no deeps or springs, before mountains were sunk and hills existed; Wisdom's delight was with the sons of man (benei adam); Wisdom was 'installed' or 'woven' (nissakhti) from eternity, from the beginning, before the earth; Wisdom was God's delight day by day, playing (mesaheqet) before him always, playing in his inhabited world; Wisdom was present when God established the heavens, drew the circle on the deep, fixed the clouds, set the sea's limit and marked earth's foundations; Before creation there was no rain, plant or man to till the ground (when-not-yet opening); God sets a boundary the sea may not pass, so it will never again cover the earth; Earth built like a structure with measurements, measuring line, sunk bases and a cornerstone; God made all his works in wisdom; Before creation there is a dark watery deep (tehom) out of which the world is formed; and 2 more.

Only in The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations: God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently; God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage; Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?'; What God does after creating in six days [divergence between the texts]; Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot); God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; God set constellations (buruj) in the sky and adorned it for beholders; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them; God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers; God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky; and 5 more.

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ The Book made firm, the Throne on the water, the challenge of ten surahs
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God lays the beams of his upper chambers on the (heavenly) waters and waters the mountains from them (weight 6.7); All creatures look to God to give their food in due season; he opens his hand and they are satisfied (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 39 more.

Only in The Book made firm, the Throne on the water, the challenge of ten surahs: Every creature on earth has its provision from God, who knows its resting place and depository; Before creation God's throne was upon the water; On judgment day witnesses (al-ashhad) testify against those who lied about God; Those who want only this life are paid in full here and have nothing in the hereafter but fire; God created heaven and earth to test which of you is best in deeds; Deniers demand that a treasure be sent down to the prophet or an angel come with him; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; YHWH sat enthroned over the flood (mabbul); YHWH sits as king forever; Man calls on God lying, sitting or standing in distress, then passes on as if he had never prayed once relieved; Moses writes the Torah and gives it to the Levitical priests and elders; What is over the waters before or at creation: God's spirit, his throne or his voice [divergence between the texts]; Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?'; and 9 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God pours down rain, splits the earth and makes grain, grapes, olives, palms and pasture grow, as provision and sign (weight 5.6); God set firm mountains on the earth lest it sway with people (weight 5.6). Pair score 11.2.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 39 more.

Only in The command has come; cattle, rain, sea and stars as blessings (Surah 16:1-23): God sends down the angels with the spirit of his command upon whom he wills; Cattle were created for human warmth, food, burden-bearing and the beauty of herds coming and going; God made horses, mules and donkeys to ride and for adornment, and creates what you do not know; Man was created from a drop, yet he becomes an open adversary; The subjected sea gives fresh meat and ornaments to wear, and ships cleave it; Night, day, sun, moon and stars are subjected by God's command; If you counted God's blessings you could never number them; Your God is one God (ilahukum ilahun wahid); God made the stars for guidance in the darknesses of land and sea; The idols create nothing, are themselves created, and are dead, not living; Idols of wood and stone that cannot see, hear, eat or smell.

passages.text: מַשְׁקֶ֣ה הָ֭רִים מֵעֲלִיּוֹתָ֑יו מִפְּרִ֥י מַ֝עֲשֶׂ֗יךָ תִּשְׂבַּ֥ע הָאָֽרֶץ
מַצְמִ֤יחַ חָצִ֨יר לַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וְ֭עֵשֶׂב לַעֲבֹדַ֣ת הָאָדָ֑ם לְה֥וֹצִיא לֶ֝֗חֶם מִן הָאָֽרֶץ
וְיַ֤יִן יְשַׂמַּ֬ח לְֽבַב אֱנ֗וֹשׁ לְהַצְהִ֣יל פָּנִ֣ים מִשָּׁ֑מֶן וְ֝לֶ֗חֶם לְֽבַב אֱנ֥וֹשׁ יִסְעָֽד
هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً لَّكُم مِّنْهُ شَرَابٌ وَمِنْهُ شَجَرٌ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ
يُنۢبِتُ لَكُم بِهِ ٱلزَّرْعَ وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلنَّخِيلَ وَٱلْأَعْنَٰبَ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى سَخَّرَ ٱلْبَحْرَ لِتَأْكُلُوا۟ مِنْهُ لَحْمًا طَرِيًّا وَتَسْتَخْرِجُوا۟ مِنْهُ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلْفُلْكَ مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 40 more.

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God made the sun a radiance and the moon a light with measured stations, to count years and reckoning (weight 6.3); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). Pair score 15.5.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 38 more.

Only in Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship: The night is a sign: God strips (naslakh) the day from it and they are in darkness; A sign: God carried their offspring in the laden ship, and made for them similar things to ride; God measured stations (manazil) for the moon until it returns like an old dried palm-stalk; Asked to spend, unbelievers retort 'shall we feed one whom God could feed if he willed?'; God made the flood ship (or its survivors) a sign for all the worlds; The hero is saved with those with him in the laden ark (al-fulk al-mashḥūn); The sun comes forth like a bridegroom from his chamber and rejoices like a strong man to run his course; The sun runs to its resting place (mustaqarr); Sun and moon each swim in an orbit (falak); God created humans (and things) in pairs, male and female; Scoffers ask the prophet to hasten the punishment; it is held back only by an appointed term and will come suddenly.

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Qaf: wonder at the warner, the earth that consumes the dead, the sky without rifts and the destroyed peoples
leads.summary: 2 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Human comes from dust and returns to dust (weight 5.0); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). Pair score 9.4.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 39 more.

Only in Qaf: wonder at the warner, the earth that consumes the dead, the sky without rifts and the destroyed peoples: The companions of al-Rass (the well/pit), a destroyed people; Tall palm trees with spathes of layered dates (tal' nadid) as provision; The unbelievers marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves; God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead bodies, and with him is a preserving record; The people of Tubba' (the Himyarite kings of Yemen) as a destroyed people; God built the sky and adorned it, and it has no rifts (furuj); God was not wearied by creating the heavens and earth (polemic against divine rest); Earth built like a structure with measurements, measuring line, sunk bases and a cornerstone; Oath by the Quran itself ('By the wise Quran'); Humans return to the earth they were taken from (and, in the Quran, are brought out of it again) [divergence between the texts]; Shuʿayb is sent to the People of the Thicket (aṣḥāb al-ayka); Deniers ask 'When we are bones and fragments, shall we be raised as a new creation?'; and 4 more.

matches.note: Winds as God's agents: ʿōśeh malʾāḵâw rûḥôṯ məšārəṯâw ʾēš lōhēṭ vs. wa-dh-dhāriyāti dharwan fa-l-ḥāmilāti wiqran fa-l-jāriyāti yusran fa-l-muqassimāti amran. The psalm makes winds God's messengers; the Quran swears by winds (or angels) that scatter, carry and distribute the command. leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 3 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The sun and the moon run by exact reckoning (husban) (weight 6.7); All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n) (weight 6.7); Man created from ringing clay like pottery, the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire (marij min nar) (weight 6.7); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7). Pair score 24.8.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; God looks at the earth and it trembles, touches the mountains and they smoke; and 37 more.

Only in Al-Rahman: the Merciful taught the Quran; sun and moon by reckoning; clay and smokeless fire; the two seas and the barrier: God raised the sky and set the Balance: do not transgress in the balance; weigh with justice and do not skimp; Lord of the two easts and the two wests (the solstitial sunrises and sunsets); The Merciful (al-Rahman) taught the Quran, created man and taught him clear speech (bayan); From the two seas come pearls and coral (marjan); A creation litany with a refrain after every line [divergence between the texts]; The text addresses jinn and humans together in the dual ('you two', al-thaqalan, 'the two weighty ones'); Earth and heavens will perish and wear out like a garment, changed like clothing, but God remains the same; Just weights and measures, and the ground given for them [divergence between the texts]; Refrain repeated 31 times: 'Which then of the bounties of your Lord will you two (jinn and humans) deny?'; Ships running on the sea like landmarks/mountains are a sign; God could still the wind and leave them motionless or wreck them; The star (or herb, najm) and the tree prostrate themselves to God; All on earth perish; there remains the Face of your Lord, possessor of majesty and honor; and 6 more.

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God makes the night cover the day (weight 6.3); God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky (weight 5.4); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). Pair score 20.9.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 37 more.

Only in Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection: Parable: good land yields its plants by God's leave, bad land yields only scantily; Call on God humbly and in secret / not aloud; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A felled tree sprouts again at the scent of water, but a man dies and does not rise [contrast between the texts]; God sends rain on the desert where no human lives, to make grass sprout; Creation is completed in six days; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh).

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Those sent forth: the refrain of woe
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 40 more.

Only in Those sent forth: the refrain of woe: Humans created from a despised fluid placed in a secure lodging (the womb) for a known term; On that day the damned do not speak and are not permitted to offer excuses; The earth is made a receptacle (kifat) that holds the living and the dead; Hell throws sparks as huge as castles, like yellow (or black) camels; The damned are led to a shadow of three branches that gives no shade nor protects from the flame; Every verse ends with the same response ('for his steadfast love is forever'), an antiphonal litany; In paradise the shades are close and the fruit clusters hang low within reach; Stars and constellations (kesilim) give no light, the sun is dark at its rising and the moon does not shine; Refrain 'Woe that day to the deniers' (waylun yawma'idhin lil-mukadhdhibin) repeated through a surah; At the end the sky is split, cleft or opened (infatarat, inshaqqat, furijat); At the end the mountains become a heap of running sand, are blown away, set in motion or turn into a mirage; God set the mountains as pegs or firm anchors (awtad, rawasi) for the earth; and 2 more.

leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr) (weight 6.3); God pours down rain, splits the earth and makes grain, grapes, olives, palms and pasture grow, as provision and sign (weight 5.6). Pair score 11.9.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 39 more.

Only in The great tiding: signs of creation and the day of sorting: On the day the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks; none speaks except whom the Merciful permits and who says what is right; Transgressors abide in hell for ages (ahqaban); On the day the unbeliever says 'Would that I were dust!'; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven [divergence between the texts]; Hell (or the Lord) lies in wait (mirsad) as a watch-post for the transgressors; Paradise has full-breasted companions of equal age (kawa'ib atrab); The righteous drink sealed pure wine (rahiq makhtum) whose seal is musk; God created seven heavens in layers (sab' samawat tibaqan) or built seven strong (heavens) above humans; The Spirit and the angels, or the angels with the coming Lord, stand rank upon rank (saffan saffa) on judgment day; The sun is made a lamp (siraj), a blazing lamp, and the moon a light (nur) within the heavens; God has counted everything by number and recorded it in a book; and 9 more.

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: East and west belong to God; wherever you turn, there is the face of God (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo: Darkness is not dark to God; night shines like day, darkness and light are alike; 'YHWH, you have searched me and known me': God knows sitting and rising, thoughts from afar, every word before it is spoken; Nowhere to flee God's spirit: if I ascend to heaven you are there, if I make my bed in Sheol you are there; 'Do I not hate those who hate you, YHWH? I hate them with perfect hatred'; 'If I take the wings of the dawn (shahar) and dwell at the far end of the sea, even there your hand leads me'; No soul dies except by God's leave at a term written (kitaban mu'ajjalan); Speaker was made in secret and embroidered (ruqqamti) in the depths of the earth; No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves but it is in a Book before God brings it into being; Nothing wet or dry but is in a clear book; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near [divergence between the texts]; God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead bodies, and with him is a preserving record; and 15 more.

matches.label: God formed the kidneys and wove (knit) the speaker in his mother's womb
matches.note: tə-sukkēnî bə-ḇeṭen ʾimmî ... ʾăšer-ʿuśśêṯî ḇa-ssēṯer ruqqamtî bə-taḥtiyyôṯ ʾāreṣ vs. yakhluqukum fī buṭūni ummahātikum khalqan min baʿdi khalqin fī ẓulumātin thalāth: God forms the embryo stage by stage in a hidden place. The psalm's 'in secret' and 'the depths of the earth' match the Quran's 'three darknesses'.

passages.text: כִּֽי אַ֭תָּה קָנִ֣יתָ כִלְיֹתָ֑י תְּ֝סֻכֵּ֗נִי בְּבֶ֣טֶן אִמִּֽי
לֹא נִכְחַ֥ד עָצְמִ֗י מִ֫מֶּ֥ךָּ אֲשֶׁר עֻשֵּׂ֥יתִי בַסֵּ֑תֶר רֻ֝קַּ֗מְתִּי בְּֽתַחְתִּיּ֥וֹת אָֽרֶץ

خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَٰحِدَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ ثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَزْوَٰجٍ يَخْلُقُكُمْ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ خَلْقًا مِّنۢ بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ فِى ظُلُمَٰتٍ ثَلَٰثٍ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لَهُ ٱلْمُلْكُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَأَنَّىٰ تُصْرَفُونَ

leads.title: Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo ↔ Qaf: wonder at the warner, the earth that consumes the dead, the sky without rifts and the destroyed peoples
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead bodies, and with him is a preserving record (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo: Darkness is not dark to God; night shines like day, darkness and light are alike; 'YHWH, you have searched me and known me': God knows sitting and rising, thoughts from afar, every word before it is spoken; Nowhere to flee God's spirit: if I ascend to heaven you are there, if I make my bed in Sheol you are there; 'Do I not hate those who hate you, YHWH? I hate them with perfect hatred'; 'If I take the wings of the dawn (shahar) and dwell at the far end of the sea, even there your hand leads me'; No soul dies except by God's leave at a term written (kitaban mu'ajjalan); Speaker was made in secret and embroidered (ruqqamti) in the depths of the earth; No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves but it is in a Book before God brings it into being; Nothing wet or dry but is in a clear book; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near [divergence between the texts]; If the sea were ink for God's words it would run dry before they ran out, even with another sea; and 15 more.

Only in Qaf: wonder at the warner, the earth that consumes the dead, the sky without rifts and the destroyed peoples: The companions of al-Rass (the well/pit), a destroyed people; Tall palm trees with spathes of layered dates (tal' nadid) as provision; The unbelievers marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves; The people of Tubba' (the Himyarite kings of Yemen) as a destroyed people; God built the sky and adorned it, and it has no rifts (furuj); God was not wearied by creating the heavens and earth (polemic against divine rest); Earth built like a structure with measurements, measuring line, sunk bases and a cornerstone; Oath by the Quran itself ('By the wise Quran'); Humans return to the earth they were taken from (and, in the Quran, are brought out of it again) [divergence between the texts]; Shuʿayb is sent to the People of the Thicket (aṣḥāb al-ayka); Deniers ask 'When we are bones and fragments, shall we be raised as a new creation?'; God set the mountains as pegs or firm anchors (awtad, rawasi) for the earth; and 5 more.

matches.label: God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near
matches.note: God knows thought and speech. Ps 139: bantâ lə-rēʿî mē-rāḥôq (you understand my thought from afar); kî ʾên millâ bi-lšônî hēn YHWH yāḏaʿtā ḵullāh (no word on my tongue that you do not know). Quran: naʿlamu mā tuwaswisu bihi nafsuhu wa-naḥnu aqrabu ilayhi min ḥabli l-warīd; mā yalfiẓu min qawlin illā ladayhi raqībun ʿatīd. 'From afar' becomes 'nearer than the jugular vein', and God's knowledge of every word is backed by an angelic recorder.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The righteous does not slander with his tongue or take up reproach against his neighbor (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Psalm 15 - who may dwell on your holy mountain: The righteous keeps his oath even to his own hurt and does not change; Entrance liturgy: 'Who may dwell on your holy mountain?' answered by a list of ethical qualifications; God shows no partiality and takes no bribe; Do not charge interest to the poor of my people; Psalm superscription ascribes the poem to David (le-david).

Only in The affair of the lie (ifk) against a chaste woman: The wealthy must not swear to stop giving to kin, the poor and emigrants, but pardon and overlook; A band spreads a lie (ifk) against a chaste believing woman; the community is rebuked for not dismissing it; Corrupt women are for corrupt men and good women for good men; Whoever accuses a chaste woman without four witnesses is flogged eighty lashes and his testimony is never accepted; On judgment day tongues, hands and feet testify against people; Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all offenses; Do not spread false reports or follow the majority to do wrong in court; Do not go about as a talebearer among your people.

leads.title: Psalm 150, everything that breathes, praise Yah ↔ Daughters of God, all things glorify him, bones and dust, the cursed tree (Surah 17:40-60)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: 'Let everything that has breath (neshamah) praise Yah' (weight 6.7); 'Let everything that has breath (neshamah) praise Yah' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in Psalm 150, everything that breathes, praise Yah: Catalogue of instruments for praise: shofar, harp, lyre, timbrel, dance, strings, pipe (ugav), sounding and clashing cymbals; God praised in his sanctuary and in the firmament (raqia) of his might; God's name praised with dance (mahol), timbrel and lyre; Blow the shofar at the new moon and at the full moon (keseh) on our feast day; A doxology ('Blessed be YHWH ... Amen and amen') closes one of the five books of Psalms; The cultic cry 'Hallelu-Yah' (praise Yah) closes or opens a psalm.

Only in Daughters of God, all things glorify him, bones and dust, the cursed tree (Surah 17:40-60): Answer to the deniers: even if you were stone or iron, the one who made you first will raise you; Every town will be destroyed or severely punished before the Day of Resurrection, as inscribed in the Book; Those whom the polytheists invoke themselves seek a means (wasila) of nearness to God; When the prophet recites, God places a hidden veil between him and those who deny the hereafter; The prophet's vision and the cursed tree in the Quran are made a trial for people; If there were other gods they would seek a way to the Lord of the Throne; Opponents say the believers follow only a bewitched man (rajul mashur); Satan stirs up enmity (nazagha) between brothers or among people; Thamud's most wretched one rises; the messenger warns 'God's she-camel and her drinking'; they hamstring her and God crushes them; The seven heavens, the earth and everything in them glorify God, though humans do not understand their praise; God ranked some messengers above others; to some God spoke; God gave David the Psalms (Zabur); and 5 more.

leads.title: Psalm 16 - YHWH my portion; not abandoned to Sheol ↔ Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God shows the path of life; fullness of joy in his presence, pleasures at his right hand forever (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Psalm 16 - YHWH my portion; not abandoned to Sheol: I have set YHWH always before me; he is at my right hand; Obscure reference to 'the holy ones who are in the land' and 'the mighty ones'; My kidneys (inner self) instruct me in the night; God will not abandon the speaker's soul to Sheol nor let his faithful one see the pit; The measuring lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; a goodly inheritance; The speaker will not pour the blood libations of other gods' followers nor take their names on his lips; YHWH is my allotted portion and my cup; you hold my lot; Superscription contains an obscure musical or liturgical term (neginot, nehilot, sheminit, gittit, alamot, shiggayon, maskil, miktam, shoshannim...); Psalm superscription ascribes the poem to David (le-david).

Only in Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden: In paradise they have the flesh of fowl as they desire; Immortal youths (wildan mukhalladun) circulate with goblets, ewers and a cup from a flowing spring; God created (the companions) anew and made them virgins, loving, of equal age; The Foremost are a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later; In paradise they hear no idle talk or sin, only the saying 'Peace, peace'; The Companions of the Right are among thornless lote trees (sidr makhdud) and layered talh (acacia/banana) with extended shade and poured water; Humanity sorted into three classes: Companions of the Right, Companions of the Left, and the Foremost (al-sabiqun) brought near; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; The earth is shaken violently and the mountains crumbled into scattered dust (haba'); Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; Abundant fruit in paradise, neither cut off (seasonless) nor forbidden; Into how many groups humankind is sorted at the end [divergence between the texts]; and 11 more.

leads.title: Psalm 17 - prayer of the innocent; shadow of your wings ↔ Kindness to parents, thirty months of bearing and weaning, the prayer at forty and the son who says 'Uff'

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The damned are told: you used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them; today you are repaid with humiliation (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Psalm 17 - prayer of the innocent; shadow of your wings: On waking the speaker will be satisfied with seeing God's form (temunah); God has tried the speaker's heart, visited him by night and refined him and found nothing; The worldly men whose portion is in this life fill their belly and leave their surplus to their children; God guards his people as the pupil (apple) of his eye; Taking refuge under the wings of God; The enemy is like a lion that tears the speaker's soul or lurks in ambush; Call to God to arise (qumah YHWH) and save or judge; Psalm superscription ascribes the poem to David (le-david).

Only in Kindness to parents, thirty months of bearing and weaning, the prayer at forty and the son who says 'Uff': God enjoins humans to be good to their parents; On reaching full strength at forty, a man prays to be grateful for favor on himself and his parents and for righteous offspring; A son says 'Uff!' to his parents who plead with him, scorning resurrection as 'tales of the ancients'; His mother bore him with hardship and delivered him with hardship; bearing and weaning take thirty months; The mother's pain in bearing children: penalty, or ground of gratitude [divergence between the texts]; For all there are degrees (darajat) according to what they did; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; A son who rejects his parents: the charge and the penalty [divergence between the texts]; Stubborn and rebellious son, glutton and drunkard, stoned by the men of his city; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal.

leads.title: Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany ↔ The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God is called the speaker's lamp who lights his darkness (weight 6.3); God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven (weight 5.8). Pair score 12.1.

Only in Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany: God makes darkness his hiding place and dark waters and clouds his canopy; The king gives thanks for God's deliverance from all his enemies (song also in 2 Sam 22); At God's rebuke the channels of the sea are seen and the foundations of the world laid bare; 'Who is God except YHWH, and who is a rock besides our God?'; God reaches from on high and draws the sufferer out of many waters; Enemies beaten fine as dust and trampled like mire of the streets; Foreigners come cringing and trembling to submit to the king; God answers the distressed when he calls and removes the evil; God hears the cry from his (heavenly) temple; God shows himself loyal to the loyal and crooked to the crooked; God rides on a cherub and flies on the wings of the wind; God trains the king's hands for war so his arms bend a bow of bronze; and 13 more.

Only in The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by wave upon wave and cloud above, darkness upon darkness, so one cannot see his own hand; The deeds of unbelievers are like a mirage in a plain that the thirsty takes for water until he reaches it and finds nothing, but finds God there; God is the light of the heavens and the earth; God's light is like a niche holding a lamp in a glass like a glittering star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of east nor west, whose oil almost glows untouched by fire: light upon light; God sends down hail from mountains in the sky; the flash of his lightning nearly takes away sight; In houses God allowed to be raised, men undistracted by trade glorify him morning and evening; God created every beast from water: some go on their bellies, some on two legs, some on four; Birds with outspread wings glorify God; each knows its prayer and praise; With God is the fountain of life; in his light we see light; A lamp fed directly by an olive tree [divergence between the texts]; A golden lampstand with seven lamps is flanked by two olive trees that pour golden oil through golden pipes; The mirage and the thirsty traveler [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: YHWH sat enthroned over the flood (mabbul); YHWH sits as king forever (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Psalm 29 - the voice of YHWH over the waters: In his temple all say 'Glory!'; The voice of YHWH hews out flames of fire (lightning); Sevenfold refrain 'the voice of YHWH' (qol YHWH) as thunder over waters, cedars, fire, desert; The sons of gods (benei elim) are summoned to ascribe glory and strength to YHWH; The voice of YHWH breaks the cedars of Lebanon and makes Lebanon and Sirion skip like calves and young wild oxen; The voice of YHWH makes the hinds writhe in labor and strips the forests bare; The voice of YHWH shakes the wilderness of Kadesh; The voice of YHWH thunders over the many waters; The thunder glorifies God with his praise, and the angels too in awe of him [divergence between the texts]; God gave David the Psalms (Zabur); Thunder is the roaring voice of God; God's strength for the people like the horns of the wild ox (re'em); and 1 more.

Only in The Book made firm, the Throne on the water, the challenge of ten surahs: Every creature on earth has its provision from God, who knows its resting place and depository; Before creation God's throne was upon the water; On judgment day witnesses (al-ashhad) testify against those who lied about God; Those who want only this life are paid in full here and have nothing in the hereafter but fire; God created heaven and earth to test which of you is best in deeds; Deniers demand that a treasure be sent down to the prophet or an angel come with him; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; Man calls on God lying, sitting or standing in distress, then passes on as if he had never prayed once relieved; Moses writes the Torah and gives it to the Levitical priests and elders; God lays the beams of his upper chambers on the (heavenly) waters and waters the mountains from them; What is over the waters before or at creation: God's spirit, his throne or his voice [divergence between the texts]; All creatures look to God to give their food in due season; he opens his hand and they are satisfied; and 10 more.

leads.title: Psalm 33 - by the word of YHWH the heavens were made ↔ Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: 'He spoke and it came to be; he commanded and it stood firm' (weight 6.3); Deity creates by spoken command (Let there be...) (weight 5.8); God creates by saying to a thing 'Be' and it is (kun fa-yakun) (weight 5.3). Pair score 17.4.

Only in Psalm 33 - by the word of YHWH the heavens were made: God frustrates the counsel of the nations; his own counsel stands forever; By the word of YHWH the heavens were made and all their host by the breath of his mouth; No king is saved by a great army; the horse is a vain hope for victory; God gathers the waters of the sea as a heap and puts the deeps in storehouses; God, who fashions the hearts of all and observes all their deeds, looks down from his dwelling; Psalm in Book I lacking any superscription; God looks down from heaven on humankind to see if any seek him; Praise with lyre and ten-stringed harp (nevel asor); Beatitude formula 'Happy (ashrei) is the man who...'; Call to sing a new song (shir hadash) to God.

Only in Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God: Jews say the Christians stand on nothing, Christians say the same of the Jews; Claim that none enters paradise unless Jew or Christian, rebutted by surrender of the face to God; Believers told not to say 'ra'ina' (a word twisted by opponents) but 'unzurna'; God abrogates or causes to be forgotten a verse and brings a better or similar one (naskh); God swears by himself: to me every knee shall bow and every tongue swear; Whether God has or begets a son [contrast between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; From sunrise to sunset God's name is great among the nations and in every place incense and a pure offering are brought to his name; East and west belong to God; wherever you turn, there is the face of God; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks [divergence between the texts]; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks; Denial that God has taken a son (walad).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
