Only in Psalm 45 - royal wedding song: The foreign bride is told: 'Hear, daughter, forget your people and your father's house'; The daughter of Tyre and the rich of the people seek the bride's favor with gifts; The king (or his throne) is addressed as 'elohim': 'your throne, O God, is forever and ever'; God anointed the king with the oil of gladness above his companions; The king is fairer than the sons of men; grace is poured on his lips; The king girds his sword on his thigh and rides victoriously for truth and righteousness; his arrows are sharp; The king's garments are fragrant with myrrh, aloes and cassia; music from ivory palaces; The princess is all glorious within, in gold-woven robes, led to the king with her virgin companions; The queen (shegal) stands at the king's right hand in gold of Ophir; Instead of your fathers shall be your sons; you will make them princes in all the earth; The poet's tongue is the pen of a ready scribe; A love song (shir yedidot) for the king's wedding to a foreign princess; and 3 more.

Only in The prophet's wives, the people of the House, and the believers men and women: The prophet's wives are given the choice between worldly adornment (with release and gift) and God and the hereafter; God wishes to remove impurity from you, people of the House (ahl al-bayt), and purify you thoroughly; The prophet's wives will receive double punishment for open indecency and double reward for obedience; Paired list of male and female believers (muslims, believers, devout, truthful, patient, humble, charitable, fasting, chaste, remembering) promised equal reward; Each person dies for his own sin.

leads.title: Psalm 75, I set firm its pillars; the cup in YHWH's hand ↔ The Opening (al-Fatiha)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God is king or master of the Day of Judgment (yawm al-din) (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Psalm 75, I set firm its pillars; the cup in YHWH's hand: God declares 'When I seize the appointed time (mo'ed) I will judge with equity'; The earth is shaken violently and the mountains crumbled into scattered dust (haba'); The arrogant are warned not to lift up their horn; God cuts off the horns of the wicked and exalts those of the righteous; Hymn of reversals: the barren bears seven, the mighty broken, the poor raised from the dung-heap; God is judge: he puts down one and lifts up another; The world set upon pillars belonging to God; A psalm quotes a first-person oracle of God; Psalm heading names a tune or melody to which it is sung (e.g. 'Do not destroy', 'Dove of distant terebinths', 'Lilies'); The wicked should drink of the wrath (cup) of Shaddai.

Only in The Opening (al-Fatiha): Text or act opened with the formula 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate'; Three ways contrasted: those God favored, those under wrath, and those gone astray; Communal confession 'You alone we worship, you alone we ask for help'; Praise (hamd) belongs to God, Lord of the worlds (rabb al-alamin); Contrast of the way of the righteous, which God knows, and the way of the wicked, which perishes [divergence between the texts]; God called al-Rahman and al-Rahim (the Merciful, the Compassionate), paired names from the root r-h-m (womb, mercy); Contrast of the way of the righteous, which God knows, and the way of the wicked, which perishes; Prayer to be guided on the straight path (al-sirat al-mustaqim).

leads.title: Psalm 75, I set firm its pillars; the cup in YHWH's hand ↔ Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The earth is shaken violently and the mountains crumbled into scattered dust (haba') (weight 6.7); Hymn of reversals: the barren bears seven, the mighty broken, the poor raised from the dung-heap (weight 6.0); God is judge: he puts down one and lifts up another (weight 5.8). Pair score 18.5.

Only in Psalm 75, I set firm its pillars; the cup in YHWH's hand: God declares 'When I seize the appointed time (mo'ed) I will judge with equity'; God is king or master of the Day of Judgment (yawm al-din); The arrogant are warned not to lift up their horn; God cuts off the horns of the wicked and exalts those of the righteous; The world set upon pillars belonging to God; A psalm quotes a first-person oracle of God; Psalm heading names a tune or melody to which it is sung (e.g. 'Do not destroy', 'Dove of distant terebinths', 'Lilies'); The wicked should drink of the wrath (cup) of Shaddai.

Only in Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden: In paradise they have the flesh of fowl as they desire; Immortal youths (wildan mukhalladun) circulate with goblets, ewers and a cup from a flowing spring; God created (the companions) anew and made them virgins, loving, of equal age; The Foremost are a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later; In paradise they hear no idle talk or sin, only the saying 'Peace, peace'; The Companions of the Right are among thornless lote trees (sidr makhdud) and layered talh (acacia/banana) with extended shade and poured water; Humanity sorted into three classes: Companions of the Right, Companions of the Left, and the Foremost (al-sabiqun) brought near; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; Abundant fruit in paradise, neither cut off (seasonless) nor forbidden; Into how many groups humankind is sorted at the end [divergence between the texts]; Paradise drink from which they suffer no headache nor intoxication; and 9 more.

Only in Psalm 76, God's lair in Salem where he broke the flaming arrows: At God's rebuke the enemy warriors sleep their last sleep, horse and chariot stunned; Jerusalem called Salem (Shalem); Song of Zion: God dwells in Zion/Salem and breaks the weapons of war there; Foreign kings bring gifts or tribute to God's temple in Jerusalem; A priest-king of Salem brings bread and wine and blesses the patriarch; God makes wars cease to the end of the earth, breaks the bow, snaps the spear and burns the chariots; Resheph and Qeteb (plague deities/demons) sent as God's arrows.

Only in The fig and the olive, Mount Sinai and the secure city: Humankind created in the best of forms (ahsan taqwim), then returned to the lowest of the low, except the believers; Humankind created in the best of forms (ahsan taqwim), then returned to the lowest of the low, except the believers [divergence between the texts]; Hero challenges God: shall the judge of all the earth not do justice? leads.title: Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David ↔ Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus
leads.summary: 14 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Swarms (arov) of insects or wild beasts fill the houses of Egypt (weight 6.3); Moses was given nine clear signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Egypt is called 'the tents of Ham' or 'the land of Ham' (weight 6.3); A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus (weight 6.0); Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs (weight 6.0); Water brought out of a rock by the leader's rod (weight 6.0); God kills every firstborn of the land, from the king's heir to the lowest servant and cattle (weight 6.0); God rains bread from heaven to feed the people in the desert (weight 6.0); Quail come up in the evening and cover the camp (weight 6.0); God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven (weight 5.8); Nile water is turned to blood (weight 5.8); Psalm retells Israel's sacred history (patriarchs, Egypt, wilderness, conquest) as instruction or praise (weight 5.6); Locusts brought by an east wind devour all vegetation left after the hail (weight 5.6); God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night (weight 5.1). Pair score 82.6.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 27 more.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 19 more.

leads.title: Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David ↔ Moses' nine signs, the drowning of Pharaoh, the Quran sent in portions (Surah 17:101-111)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses was given nine clear signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 10.8.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 39 more.

Only in Moses' nine signs, the drowning of Pharaoh, the Quran sent in portions (Surah 17:101-111): Call on God as Allah or as al-Rahman: to him belong the most beautiful names; After Pharaoh's drowning Israel is told to dwell in the land; at the last promise they are gathered in a mixed crowd; Do not be loud in prayer nor too quiet; seek a way between; The prophet answers the accusing king: 'I think you are doomed'; Those given knowledge before fall on their chins prostrate and weeping when the scripture is recited; Moses was given nine clear signs; Do not be loud in prayer nor too quiet; seek a way between [contrast between the texts]; The scripture is sent down in portions so the prophet recites it to people at intervals; Those given knowledge before fall on their chins prostrate and weeping when the scripture is recited [divergence between the texts]; Those who do not prostrate when the scripture is recited to them are rebuked (a prostration verse); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives [divergence between the texts]; The people weep on hearing the words of the Torah; and 2 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Prophet stretches his staff over the sea and God splits it with a strong east wind (weight 6.0); Manna, unknown food from heaven (weight 6.0); God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night (weight 5.1); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 21.6.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 37 more.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; and 14 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Enemies roar in the sanctuary, hack its carved work with axes and burn it to the ground [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Enemies roar in the sanctuary, hack its carved work with axes and burn it to the ground (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.3.

Only in Psalm 79, the nations have come into your inheritance: Prayer that God not remember against us the iniquities of former generations; Bodies of God's servants left as food for birds and beasts; blood poured like water around Jerusalem with none to bury; Vengeance multiplied sevenfold (or seventy-sevenfold); Israel called the flock of God's pasture; Prayer 'Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you'; Lament question 'How long, O God?' / 'Why have you rejected us forever?'; Nations taunt 'Where is their God?'; Communal lament over national disaster, asking why God has rejected his people; Heading assigns the psalm to a Levitical singer or guild (Jeduthun, Asaph, sons of Korah, Heman, Ethan).

Only in The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8): Israel addressed as descendants of those carried with Noah, who was a grateful servant; Divine warning 'if you return (to sin), we will return (to punishment)'; It is decreed in the Book that Israel will work corruption on earth twice; God takes his servant on a journey to show him some of his signs; God sends against Israel servants of his of great might who range through their homes; God carried his servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque; After the first punishment God restores Israel's turn with wealth and sons; The enemy enters the sanctuary (masjid) a second time as the first and destroys all; God gave Moses the Book as guidance for the Children of Israel.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Elias (Ilyas) rebukes his people: 'Will you call on Ba'l and forsake the best of creators?' (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Moses and Aaron; Elias against Ba'l: The prophet's name appears in variant form ('Il Yasin') for rhyme; A single prophet of YHWH stands against 450 prophets of Baal and 400 of Asherah; How the people respond to the prophet's challenge over Baal [divergence between the texts]; A prophet challenges the people who worship Baal [divergence between the texts]; Aaron's standing before God [divergence between the texts]; Who is named as saved and credited at the deliverance from Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Refrain 'We left for him among later generations: Peace upon X... thus we reward those who do good'; Israel serves the Baals and the Ashtaroth/Asherahs; The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives.

Only in A cleansing fountain, the end of prophecy, and the struck shepherd: A fountain is opened for the house of David and Jerusalem to cleanse sin and menstrual impurity (niddah); Prophets wear a hairy mantle (adderet se'ar) as a mark of office, here to deceive; Disclaimer: 'I am no prophet; I am a tiller of the soil'; If anyone still prophesies, his own father and mother will pierce him through for speaking falsely in God's name; In that day God cuts off the names of idols and removes the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land; 'Awake, sword, against my shepherd, the man who is my fellow; strike the shepherd and the sheep will scatter'; Two-thirds perish and one third is brought through fire, refined like silver and tested like gold; Asked about the wounds 'between your hands', the man says 'I was struck in the house of my friends (lovers)'; Command to destroy figured stones, molten images and high places of the land; Mutual declaration: Israel avows YHWH as God, YHWH avows Israel as his treasured people.

(qul a'udhu bi-rabbi) against named evils; Refuge from the evil of those (women) who blow on knots (al-naffathat fi al-'uqad), i.e. knot-tying sorcery; Psalm used as protection against demons and harm (later amulet and 'song of plagues'); Cluster of divine epithets in sequence (e.g. the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne, the Glorious, doer of what he wills; or Lord, King, God of mankind); and 2 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A lamp fed directly by an olive tree [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A golden lampstand with seven lamps is flanked by two olive trees that pour golden oil through golden pipes (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in Fifth vision, the lampstand, the two olive trees and Zerubbabel: The headstone is brought out with shouts of 'Grace, grace to it'; 'Who has despised the day of small things?' (small beginnings of the rebuilding); 'Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you become a plain'; 'Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit', says YHWH; The angel rouses the prophet like a man woken from sleep before the vision; Two 'sons of oil' (anointed ones) stand by the Lord of all the earth; 'The eyes of YHWH run to and fro through all the earth'; A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups.

leads.title: Eighth vision, four chariots between bronze mountains ↔ Those sent forth: the refrain of woe
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Eighth vision, four chariots between bronze mountains: Four chariots come out from between two mountains of bronze; The chariots are the four winds (spirits) of heaven that go out after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth; The horses going to the north country have set God's spirit at rest there; Horses of different colors (red, sorrel, white, black, dappled) are sent out by God through the earth; A heavenly being reports he has been roaming to and fro on the earth.

Only in Those sent forth: the refrain of woe: Humans created from a despised fluid placed in a secure lodging (the womb) for a known term; On that day the damned do not speak and are not permitted to offer excuses; The earth is made a receptacle (kifat) that holds the living and the dead; Hell throws sparks as huge as castles, like yellow (or black) camels; The damned are led to a shadow of three branches that gives no shade nor protects from the flame; Every verse ends with the same response ('for his steadfast love is forever'), an antiphonal litany; In paradise the shades are close and the fruit clusters hang low within reach; Stars and constellations (kesilim) give no light, the sun is dark at its rising and the moon does not shine; Refrain 'Woe that day to the deniers' (waylun yawma'idhin lil-mukadhdhibin) repeated through a surah; At the end the sky is split, cleft or opened (infatarat, inshaqqat, furijat); At the end the mountains become a heap of running sand, are blown away, set in motion or turn into a mirage; God set the mountains as pegs or firm anchors (awtad, rawasi) for the earth; and 2 more.

leads.title: Noah's challenge to his people ↔ Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi
leads.summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood (weight 6.3); Why God destroyed a generation or a people (weight 6.3); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood (weight 5.2); Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger (weight 4.8); The Prophet asks no wage for the message (weight 4.6); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 31.7.

Only in Noah's challenge to his people: Prophet challenges the idolaters to call their partners and plot against him without delay; Leader protests he never took so much as a donkey from anyone; A seer faced with payment or worldly gain [contrast between the texts]; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear.

Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's opponents object that only the lowliest follow him; he refuses to drive the believers away; Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; and 23 more.

passages.text: وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ نُوحٍ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَٰقَوْمِ إِن كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكُم مَّقَامِى وَتَذْكِيرِى بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ فَأَجْمِعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَآءَكُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً ثُمَّ ٱقْضُوٓا۟ إِلَىَّ وَلَا تُنظِرُونِ
فَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَمَا سَأَلْتُكُم مِّنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

sides.note: Noah before the flood: in Gen he says nothing to anyone and simply obeys (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer ṣiwwāh ʾōtô ʾĕlōhîm kēn ʿāśāh); in Q he preaches and challenges his people: yā qawmi in kāna kabura ʿalaykum maqāmī wa-tadhkīrī bi-āyāti llāhi ... fa-ajmiʿū amrakum wa-shurakāʾakum. Q adds the speech.

passages.text: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنِّى لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ

sides.note: Noah and his people before the flood: Gen records no word from Noah, only obedience (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer-ṣiwwāhû YHWH); Q adds a long debate, innī lakum nadhīrun mubīnun an lā taʿbudū illā llāha, with the chiefs' replies (mā narāka illā basharan mithlanā) and their mockery while he builds (sakhirū minhu).

matches.label: Why God destroyed a generation or a people

passages.text: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ خَلَٰٓئِفَ وَأَغْرَقْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

sides.note: Why the generation drowns: in Q because they rejected the messenger (wa-aghraqnā lladhīna kadhdhabū bi-āyātinā); in Gen because the earth was full of violence and corruption (wattimmālēʾ hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās ... kî-hišḥît kol-bāśār ʾet-darkô). Moral corruption becomes rejection of a prophet.

passages.text: فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ
وَٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

sides.note: Why they drown: Gen, the earth full of violence (kî-mālᵉʾāh hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās mippᵉnêhem); Q, rejecting the messenger and doing wrong (lladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), after Noah's preaching. In Gen all flesh perishes (qēṣ kol-bāśār); in Q 'Noah's people'.

leads.title: Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil ↔ Abraham's guests and the destruction of Lot's people (Surah 15:51-77)
leads.summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place (weight 6.3); Lot's wife is among those who stay behind and perish (weight 6.3); Stones of baked clay (sijjil), in layers, each marked by the Lord, rain on the town (weight 6.3); Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom (weight 6.0); Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests (weight 6.0); Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed (weight 5.6). Pair score 36.4.

Only in Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil: The angels tell Lot the destruction is appointed for the morning: 'is not the morning near?'; Lot wishes he had strength or a strong support to take refuge in; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city; What Lot says to the townsmen; How Lot receives the heavenly guests [divergence between the texts]; When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls [divergence between the texts]; Lot's townspeople turn on him; What falls from heaven on Sodom; A land will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, never inhabited; The fate of Lot's wife; God casts great hailstones from heaven, killing more than the sword; and 2 more.

Only in Abraham's guests and the destruction of Lot's people (Surah 15:51-77): The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people; The rescued family leaves by night, the leader following behind them; God swears by the prophet's life (la-'amruka); The patriarch tells his unknown guests 'we are afraid of you'; The ruins of the destroyed towns lie on a road still traveled; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; The doomed people are seized by the Shout (al-sayha) at dawn or sunrise; Do not despair of God's mercy (rawh / rahma); only unbelievers or the astray despair; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 9 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom (weight 6.0); A land will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, never inhabited (weight 6.0); The fate of Lot's wife (weight 5.8); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 5.2); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Only in Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil: The angels tell Lot the destruction is appointed for the morning: 'is not the morning near?'; Lot wishes he had strength or a strong support to take refuge in; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city; What Lot says to the townsmen; How Lot receives the heavenly guests [divergence between the texts]; When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls [divergence between the texts]; Lot's townspeople turn on him; What falls from heaven on Sodom; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place; Lot's wife is among those who stay behind and perish; Stones of baked clay (sijjil), in layers, each marked by the Lord, rain on the town; and 3 more.

Only in Lot and the destruction of his town: The host is troubled and helpless on account of the angelic guests, fearing for them; Lot's people approach men, cut off the road (highway robbery) and commit abominations in their assembly (nadi); Abraham's plea when told that the city of Lot will be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; How Lot receives the divine messengers [divergence between the texts]; God's messengers announce that they are sent to destroy the city; The sin of Sodom was pride, surfeit of bread and careless ease, not strengthening the hand of the poor and needy; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10); God appears as three men who visit the patriarch; Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A specific sign marks the moment to board (weight 6.3); The flood waters are hot or boiling (weight 6.0); A member of the hero's family is lost (weight 5.8); Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 5.8); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood (weight 5.2); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 5.2); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's opponents object that only the lowliest follow him; he refuses to drive the believers away; Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; and 22 more.

Only in Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven: God forbids the prophet to address him on behalf of those who did wrong: they will be drowned; The flood hero prays to be landed at a blessed landing place; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; When and from where the flood waters come [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts]; Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts]; Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts]; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga').

leads.title: Salih, the she-camel and the Shout ↔ Shu'ayb - measures, the prayer that commands, the clan
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A people is destroyed by the Shout / Blast (al-sayha) (weight 6.7); Refrain 'away with...' (bu'dan li-) the destroyed people (weight 6.0); The destroyed are as if they had never lived in their land (weight 5.8); Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings (weight 5.6); Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him' (weight 5.2). Pair score 29.2.

Only in Salih, the she-camel and the Shout: The people tell their prophet he had been their hope before this; After the crime the people are given three days' enjoyment in their homes before destruction; The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; Unbelievers defend their practice as what they found their fathers doing; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

Only in Shu'ayb - measures, the prayer that commands, the clan: The people mock: 'Does your prayer command you that we abandon our fathers' gods or our way with our wealth?'; The prophet does not wish to do himself what he forbids them; he wants only reform; What God leaves you (baqiyyat Allah) is better than dishonest gain; Only the prophet's clan keeps the people from stoning him; Prophet tells deniers 'Wait, I too am waiting'; Roll call of destroyed peoples: Noah's, Ad, Thamud, Abraham's people, Midian and the overturned cities; Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded.

leads.title: Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50) ↔ Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72)
leads.summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 6.3); Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him (weight 6.3); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 5.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Pair score 34.4.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; God expels Iblis as accursed (rajim) with a curse until the Day of Judgment; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils.

Only in Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72): Whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the hereafter and further astray; On judgment day every people is called with its leader (imam); God lets Iblis incite humans with his voice, his cavalry and infantry, sharing their wealth and children; Threat: God could send a storm of stones on land or a shattering wind at sea; Whoever is given his book in his right hand has an easy reckoning; whoever is given it behind his back cries for destruction; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [contrast between the texts]; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [divergence between the texts]; God honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea and preferred them above much of creation; The devil argues he is better than man because he was made of fire and man of clay; The earth opens its mouth and swallows rebels alive into Sheol.

passages.text: فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

passages.text: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍ

leads.title: Exodus, the calf and the wilderness ↔ Twelve tribes, twelve springs, and the word changed at the gate
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Twelve springs in the wilderness [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word (weight 6.3); Prophet strikes a rock and water flows out for the people (weight 6.3); Oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees (weight 6.0); God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night (weight 5.1). Pair score 29.9.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; and 13 more.

Only in Twelve tribes, twelve springs, and the word changed at the gate: Twelve springs gush from the struck rock, one drinking place for each tribe; Among Moses' people is a community that guides by the truth and acts justly by it; Prophet strikes a rock and water flows out for the people [divergence between the texts]; Manna and quail are followed by a punishment from God [divergence between the texts]; The wrongdoers replace the word they were told with another, and a plague falls from heaven; Twelve sons of the patriarch listed by their mothers; Quail come up in the evening and cover the camp.

passages.text: وَإِذِ ٱسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْحَجَرَ فَٱنفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ مِن رِّزْقِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ

sides.note: Exod 15:27 wa-yyābōʾû ʾêlimâ wĕ-šām šĕtêm ʿeśrēh ʿênōt mayim wĕ-šibʿîm tĕmārîm: twelve springs at the oasis of Elim; Q 2:60 fa-nfajarat minhu thnatā ʿashrata ʿaynan qad ʿalima kullu unāsin mashrabahum: twelve springs (cognate numeral + ʿayin) burst from the struck rock, one per tribe. The Elim springs are moved into the rock miracle; the seventy palms are dropped.

passages.text: وَقَطَّعْنَٰهُمُ ٱثْنَتَىْ عَشْرَةَ أَسْبَاطًا أُمَمًا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱسْتَسْقَىٰهُ قَوْمُهُۥٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْحَجَرَ فَٱنۢبَجَسَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْغَمَٰمَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ

sides.note: Twelve springs: fa-nbajasat minhu thnatā ʿashrata ʿaynan qad ʿalima kullu unāsin mashrabahum vs šᵉtêm ʿeśrēh ʿênōt mayim wᵉšibʿîm tᵉmārîm (ʿayn = ʿayin). Elim's natural oasis becomes the miracle of the struck rock, and the twelve springs are tied to the twelve tribes (ithnatay ʿashrata asbāṭan; asbāṭ = šᵉbāṭîm); the seventy palms are dropped.

leads.summary: 8 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Pharaoh threatens the converted magicians with cutting off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifixion (on palm trunks) (weight 6.7); The magicians' ropes and staffs appear by sorcery to be moving like snakes (weight 6.7); Condemned believers tell the tyrant 'decree what you will; you can only decree for this worldly life' (weight 6.7); The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron (weight 6.3); King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' (weight 6.3); The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents (weight 6.0); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' (weight 5.4); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1). Pair score 49.2.

Only in Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians: The contest with the magicians is set for a festival day (yawm al-zīna) at forenoon with the people assembled; From the earth humans were created, into it they return, and from it they are brought forth again; Formula: 'Peace be on whoever follows the guidance'; Pharaoh asks about the fate of former generations; the answer: their knowledge is with God in a book; The prophets are told to speak to the tyrant with gentle words, that he may take heed or fear; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' [divergence between the texts]; God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents [divergence between the texts]; In hell the damned neither die nor live; The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people [divergence between the texts]; and 3 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 35 more.

passages.text: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

matches.label: The fate of Lot's wife

passages.text: إِلَّا عَجُوزًا فِى ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

sides.note: illā ʿajūzan fī l-ghābirīna ~ wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ: the one family member lost. Genesis names her Lot's wife and says why (she looked back) and how (pillar of salt); the Quran says only 'an old woman among those who stayed behind', with no looking back and no salt.

passages.text: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَٰهَا مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

sides.note: Who decides the wife's fate: Genesis gives her own act, the warning ʾal tabbîṭ ʾaḥărêkā and wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ; the Quran gives God's decree, illā mraʾatahu qaddarnāhā mina l-ghābirīna, 'we decreed her among those who stayed behind', with no looking back and no salt.

leads.title: Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains ↔ Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1). Pair score 28.1.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 38 more.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; God addresses the hero with 'Fear not' in a vision; and 2 more.

leads.finding: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs

units.title: Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs

matches.label: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs

passages.text: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

sides.note: Pharaoh's response to the sign: Exod 7:13 wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh wə-lōʾ šāmaʿ ʾălēhem ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart hardened as God foretold (God hardens it himself at 14:4, 14:8); Q 26:49 has no hardening and no divine agency, only Pharaoh's rage: āmantum lahu qabla an ādhana lakum innahu la-kabīrukumu lladhī ʿallamakumu s-siḥra, with a threat of amputation and crucifixion.

passages.text: وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

sides.note: Why Egypt refuses: Exod 8:15 the magicians admit ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm hîʾ, yet wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh ... ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart is hardened as God foretold; Q 27:14 wa-jaḥadū bihā wa-staiqanathā anfusuhum ẓulman wa-ʿuluwwan, they rejected the signs though inwardly convinced, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. Refusal by God's design becomes knowing, self-chosen denial.

matches.label: Moses' hand turned white as a sign

passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

sides.note: wa-nazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāʾu li-n-nāẓirīna ~ wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: the white hand. In Exodus it is leprous (məṣōraʿat), shown to Moses at the bush and meant for the Israelites (4:8-9, 4:30); in the Quran it is simply 'white for the beholders', shown to Pharaoh and his court, with no disease.

passages.text: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

sides.note: wa-adkhil yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾin ~ hāvēʾ nāʾ yādəkā bə-ḥêqekā ... wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: hand into the bosom (jayb / ḥêq) and out white. The Quran's 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ) excludes exactly what Exodus says, that the hand was leprous (məṣōraʿat), and needs no second step of restoring it (4:7).

matches.label: Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign

passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ
وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

sides.note: into his bosom (jayb), white without evil

matches.label: A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff

passages.text: فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ
وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

matches.label: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest

passages.text: قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ
قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ

sides.note: fa-lammā jāʾathum āyātunā mubṣiratan qālū hādhā siḥrun mubīnun ~ wa-yyiqrāʾ gam Parʿōh la-ḥăkhāmîm wə-la-mkhaššəfîm wa-yyaʿăśû gam hēm ... bə-lahăṭêhem kēn: Pharaoh's side treats the signs as magic; Exodus shows it by having the magicians copy them, the Quran by having Pharaoh's people call them 'clear sorcery'.

leads.finding: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death

units.title: Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper

matches.label: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death

passages.text: وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

sides.note: Fear of being killed for the old killing: in Exodus God removes it by fact, kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā; in the Quran Moses raises it himself (wa-lahum ʿalayya dhanbun fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni), and God answers with his presence, 'kallā ... innā maʿakum mustamiʿūn'.

passages.text: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى قَتَلْتُ مِنْهُمْ نَفْسًا فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ

sides.note: rabbi innī qataltu minhum nafsan fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni ~ kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā: the old killing as an obstacle to going back. In Exodus God removes it unasked, in the Quran Moses raises it at the call.

matches.label: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed

passages.text: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

sides.note: God's answer to Moses' reluctance: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... hălōʾ ʾAhărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wə-ʾattâ tihyeh lô lēʾlōhîm (anger; Aaron as mouth, Moses as God to him) ~ qāla kallā fa-dhhabā bi-āyātinā innā maʿakum mustamiʿūna: no anger and no 'as God'; both are sent as equals (fa-dhhabā, dual).

passages.text: وَأَخِى هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّى لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِىَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِىٓ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَٰنًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكُمَا ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ

sides.note: Aaron's eloquence: in Exodus Moses says he is heavy of mouth, and God, angry, proposes Aaron himself: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... yādaʿtî kî dabbēr yədabbēr hûʾ ... wə-śamtā ʾet had-dəvārîm bə-fîw. In the Quran Moses proposes him, wa-akhī Hārūnu huwa afṣaḥu minnī lisānan fa-arsilhu maʿiya ridʾan yuṣaddiqunī, and God agrees without anger: sa-nashuddu ʿaḍudaka bi-akhīka. Aaron is a supporting witness (ridʾ, yuṣaddiqunī), not a mouth for Moses as God.

matches.label: Moses' hand turned white as a sign

passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

sides.note: wa-nazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāʾu li-n-nāẓirīna ~ wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: the white hand. In Exodus it is leprous (məṣōraʿat), shown to Moses at the bush and meant for the Israelites (4:8-9, 4:30); in the Quran it is simply 'white for the beholders', shown to Pharaoh and his court, with no disease.

passages.text: ٱسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهْبِ فَذَٰنِكَ بُرْهَٰنَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

sides.note: Two signs, not three, and no leprosy: Exodus gives staff, leprous hand (məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg), and a third sign held in reserve, Nile water turned to blood (wə-hāyû lə-dām bay-yabbāšet), meant for doubting Israelites; the Quran has fa-dhānika burhānāni min rabbika ilā Firʿawna wa-malaʾihi, two proofs aimed at Pharaoh, the hand white 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ), and adds 'draw your arm to your side against fear'.

matches.label: Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign

passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

ٱسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهْبِ فَذَٰنِكَ بُرْهَٰنَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

sides.note: two proofs (burhānān); 'draw your arm to your side against fear'

matches.label: Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips'

passages.text: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ

Only in The annunciation and the mission of Jesus: Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils; Child makes birds from clay that come alive; Jesus asks 'Who are my helpers to God?' and the disciples (hawariyyun) answer 'We are God's helpers'; They plotted, and God plotted; God is the best of plotters; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil; Jesus heals the born-blind and the leper and raises the dead by God's leave; The likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam, created from dust by 'Be'; Jesus comes confirming the Torah and making lawful some of what was forbidden; God says to Jesus 'I will take you (mutawaffika) and raise you to myself and purify you'; Jesus tells people what they eat and store in their houses; Jesus announced as a word (kalima) from God, named the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; Prophet is taken up alive to heaven in a whirlwind; God sent down the Torah (al-Tawrat) and the Gospel (al-Injil) before as guidance.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Youths (ghilman) like hidden pearls go round serving them (weight 6.7); The blessed recline on couches set in rows (or face to face) (weight 6.7); Abundant fruit in paradise from which the blessed eat (weight 6.0); The blessed are paired with wide-eyed maidens (hur 'in) (weight 6.0); The effects of wine and of the cup: mockery, madness, or none [contrast between the texts] (weight 5.8). Pair score 31.1.

Only in The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges: The blessed question each other and recall that they used to be fearful among their families, and God saved them from the scorching wind (samum); In paradise they pass a cup to one another in which is no idle talk (laghw) or sin; If they saw a fragment of the sky falling they would say 'heaped-up clouds'; Glorify God when you rise, in the night, and at the retreat of the stars (dawn); Do they have a ladder (sullam) by which they eavesdrop on heaven? Let their listener bring clear proof; 'Be patient for your Lord's judgment, for you are under our eyes'; Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Did they create the heavens and earth?; Do they possess the Unseen (al-ghayb) so they write it down?; Dream of a ladder or stairway reaching heaven with angels ascending and descending; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; A ladder (sullam / sullām) reaching from earth to heaven [divergence between the texts]; Believers' offspring who followed them in faith are joined with them in paradise, without loss of reward; each is pledged for what he earned; and 9 more.

Only in Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden: In paradise they have the flesh of fowl as they desire; Immortal youths (wildan mukhalladun) circulate with goblets, ewers and a cup from a flowing spring; God created (the companions) anew and made them virgins, loving, of equal age; The Foremost are a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later; In paradise they hear no idle talk or sin, only the saying 'Peace, peace'; The Companions of the Right are among thornless lote trees (sidr makhdud) and layered talh (acacia/banana) with extended shade and poured water; Humanity sorted into three classes: Companions of the Right, Companions of the Left, and the Foremost (al-sabiqun) brought near; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; The earth is shaken violently and the mountains crumbled into scattered dust (haba'); Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; Abundant fruit in paradise, neither cut off (seasonless) nor forbidden; Into how many groups humankind is sorted at the end [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.

Only in The recited commandments (the Quranic decalogue): List of commandments introduced 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you'; Lest you say scripture was sent only to two groups before us; This is my straight path; follow it and not other ways that scatter you; God gave Moses the book complete and detailing everything; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; Stand firm for justice as witnesses for God even against yourselves, parents and kin, rich or poor; Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness [divergence between the texts]; Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left; I set before you life and death, blessing and curse: choose life; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness.

وَلَا تَقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَوْلَٰدَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَٰقٍ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْـًٔا كَبِيرًا
وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ ٱلزِّنَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةً وَسَآءَ سَبِيلًا

leads.title: The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall ↔ Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50)
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 6.3); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 5.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Pair score 28.2.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; and 17 more.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; God expels Iblis as accursed (rajim) with a curse until the Day of Judgment; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils.

leads.summary: 9 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans (weight 6.7); Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck (weight 6.3); Fig leaves sewn into coverings (weight 6.3); Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked (weight 6.3); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6). Pair score 55.7.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?' [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

Only in Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent: God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat; Whoever turned from God's reminder is raised blind on judgment day: as he forgot the signs, so he is forgotten; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays'; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts]; God commands the angels to prostrate to Adam; all do except Iblis, who refuses; Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts]; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays' [divergence between the texts]; A tree whose fruit gives eternal life.

passages.text: قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

sides.note: Gen: wə-ʾêvāh ʾāšît bênkhā û-vên hā-ʾiššāh û-vên zarʿăkhā û-vên zarʿāh, enmity set by God between serpent and woman and their seed. Q: qāla hbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun, plural, a mutual enmity of those sent down (humans and Satan, 7:22 inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduww). There are no curses on the woman (childbirth, 3:16) or the ground (3:17-19).

passages.text: قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

sides.note: wəʾêbâ ʾāšît bênkā ûbên hāʾiššâ ûbên zarʿăkā ûbên zarʿāh ... wayəšalləḥēhû ... waygāreš ʾet-hāʾādām; qāla hbiṭā minhā jamīʿan baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduww. Enmity and expulsion. Gen's enmity is between serpent and woman and their seed, and the way back is barred by cherubim. Q's enmity is among those sent down, and Q adds a promise of guidance, fa-immā yaʾtiyannakum minnī hudan fa-mani ttabaʿa hudāya fa-lā yaḍillu wa-lā yashqā.

passages.text: فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

sides.note: A different tempter. Gen: wə-han-nāḥāš hāyāh ʿārûm mik-kōl ḥayyat haś-śādeh, an animal speaking to the woman. Q: fa-waswasa lahumā l-shayṭānu, the devil already expelled in 7:13, whispering to both, and he swears an oath (wa-qāsamahumā innī lakumā la-mina l-nāṣiḥīna). There is no serpent and no curse to crawl on the belly (Gen 3:14).

فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ

sides.note: Who tempts whom. Gen: wəhannāḥāš hāyâ ʿārûm ... wayyōʾmer ʾel-hāʾiššâ, a clever beast addressing the woman. leads.title: Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection ↔ The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky (weight 5.4); After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh) (weight 5.2); Creation is completed in six days (weight 5.2); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). Only in Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection: Parable: good land yields its plants by God's leave, bad land yields only scantily; Call on God humbly and in secret / not aloud; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A felled tree sprouts again at the scent of water, but a man dies and does not rise [contrast between the texts]; God makes the night cover the day; God sends rain on the desert where no human lives, to make grass sprout.

passages.text: فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ
قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ نَحْنُ ٱلْمُلْقِينَ
قَالَ أَلْقُوا۟ فَلَمَّآ أَلْقَوْا۟ سَحَرُوٓا۟ أَعْيُنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ وَجَآءُو بِسِحْرٍ عَظِيمٍ

sides.note: Who throws the staff, and how. Exod: Aaron throws (wa-yyašlēkh ʾAhărōn ʾet-maṭṭēhû ... wa-yhî lə-tannîn); the magicians do the same (bə-lahăṭêhem kēn); and maṭṭēh-ʾAhărōn swallows their staffs (wa-yyivlaʿ). Q: Moses throws (fa-alqā ʿaṣāhu fa-idhā hiya thuʿbānun mubīnun); the magicians offer him the first throw (immā an tulqiya); their act is siḥr that 'bewitched the people's eyes' (saḥarū aʿyuna l-nāsi), and Moses' staff talqafu mā yaʾfikūna. Aaron drops out of the act; the magic is illusion.

passages.text: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا۟ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ
وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَٰحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ

sides.note: Exod: Aaron's staff (wayyašlēk ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭēhû ... wayhî lətannîn), and the magicians really do the same, wayyaʿăśû gam-hēm ḥarṭummê miṣrayim bəlahăṭêhem kēn ... wayyihyû lətannînim, before wayyiblaʿ maṭṭēh-ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭōtām. Q: Moses' staff (alqi mā fī yamīnika talqaf mā ṣanaʿū), and the magicians' ropes and staffs only seem to move, yukhayyalu ilayhi min siḥrihim annahā tasʿā. The actor and the reality of the rival magic both change.

passages.text: وَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سَٰجِدِينَ
قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
رَبِّ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ

matches.label: Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me'

حَقِيقٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَن لَّآ أَقُولَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِبَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعِىَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ

sides.note: The sender's title and the demand. Exod: kōh-ʾāmar YHWH ʾĕlōhê Yiśrāʾēl šallaḥ ʾet-ʿammî wə-yāḥōggû lî bam-midbār; ʾĕlōhê hā-ʿivrîm niqrāʾ ʿālênû, God of Israel and of the Hebrews, with a pretext of a three-day festival or sacrifice. Q: yā Firʿawnu innī rasūlun min rabbi l-ʿālamīna ... fa-arsil maʿiya banī Isrāʾīla. 'The Lord of the worlds', with no festival or three-day journey, and 'the Children of Israel' instead of 'my people'. Pharaoh's 'who is YHWH?' (mî YHWH, 5:2) becomes in fa-ʾti bihā in kunta mina l-ṣādiqīn.

sides.note: Title and purpose change. Q: innā rasūlā rabbika, 'messengers of your Lord', Pharaoh's own Lord, and the purpose is release from oppression, fa-arsil maʿanā banī Isrāʾīla wa-lā tuʿadhdhibhum. Q adds wa-s-salāmu ʿalā mani ttabaʿa l-hudā.

فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمُ ٱلرِّجْزَ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ هُم بَٰلِغُوهُ إِذَا هُمْ يَنكُثُونَ

sides.note: Who hardens the heart. Exod: first Pharaoh (wa-yyakhbēd Parʿōh ʾet-libbô gam bap-paʿam haz-zōʾt), then God (wa-yḥazzēq YHWH ʾet-lēv Parʿōh, 9:12). passages.text: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ

וּלְגֻבְרִ֤ין גִּבָּֽרֵי חַ֨יִל֙ דִּ֣י בְחַיְלֵ֔הּ אֲמַר֙ לְכַפָּתָ֔ה לְשַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ לְמִרְמֵ֕א לְאַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא

בֵּאדַ֜יִן קְרֵ֣ב נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר לִתְרַע֮ אַתּ֣וּן נוּרָ֣א יָקִֽדְתָּא֒ עָנֵ֣ה וְאָמַ֗ר שַׁדְרַ֨ךְ מֵישַׁ֧ךְ וַעֲבֵד נְג֛וֹ עַבְד֛וֹהִי דִּֽי אֱלָהָ֥א עליא עִלָּאָ֖ה פֻּ֣קוּ וֶאֱת֑וֹ בֵּאדַ֣יִן נָֽפְקִ֗ין שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֛ךְ וַעֲבֵ֥ד נְג֖וֹ מִן גּ֥וֹא נוּרָֽא

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֡שׁ לְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר עָמְד֨וּ עָלָ֜יו הַאַתֶּ֣ם תְּרִיב֣וּן לַבַּ֗עַל אִם אַתֶּם֙ תּוֹשִׁיע֣וּן אוֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥יב ל֛וֹ יוּמַ֖ת עַד הַבֹּ֑קֶר אִם אֱלֹהִ֥ים הוּא֙ יָ֣רֶב ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת מִזְבְּחֽוֹ
וַיִּקְרָא ל֥וֹ בַיּוֹם הַה֖וּא יְרֻבַּ֣עַל לֵאמֹ֑ר יָ֤רֶב בּוֹ֙ הַבַּ֔עַל כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת מִזְבְּחֽוֹ

sides.note: The same argument from the idol's helplessness: ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreb lô kî nātaṣ ʾet-mizbəḥô, 'if he is a god let him contend for himself'; bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fa-sʾalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūn, 'ask them, if they can speak'. In Judg the idolatrous father Joash says it to protect his son; in Q Abraham says it to shame the people, and they are turned on their heads (nukisū ʿalā ruʾūsihim).

passages.text: (6:25) וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֨עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת (6:26) וּבָנִ֨יתָ מִזְבֵּ֜חַ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ עַ֣ל רֹ֧אשׁ הַמָּע֛וֹז הַזֶּ֖ה בַּמַּֽעֲרָכָ֑ה וְלָֽקַחְתָּ֙ אֶת הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהַעֲלִ֣יתָ עוֹלָ֔ה בַּעֲצֵ֥י הָאֲשֵׁרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּכְרֹֽת (6:27) וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה (6:28) וַיַּשְׁכִּ֜ימוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֤ה נֻתַּץ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַבַּ֔עַל וְהָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו כֹּרָ֑תָה וְאֵת֙ הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֹֽעֲלָ֔ה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ הַבָּנֽוּי

וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֨עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת

וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה

leads.summary: 9 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Waters pour both from the sky and from springs of the earth (weight 6.0); Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 5.8); Vessel comes to rest on a named mountain (weight 5.4); Hero singled out as righteous or pious (weight 5.3); Deity decides to destroy humankind (weight 5.3); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 5.2); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.1); All others perish (weight 5.0); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 47.6.

Only in Noah in the Quran: Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; Vessel described by its planks and fastenings; A specific sign marks the moment to board; Hero blessed on leaving the vessel; The flood waters are hot or boiling; Hero's life or mission spans 950 years; People mock the hero while he builds the vessel; A member of the hero's family is lost; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; God regrets having made humankind and is grieved in his heart; God himself shuts the vessel's door behind the hero; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; A raven is sent out and does not return (goes to and fro); Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Vessel has several decks, a side door and a roof opening or window; God sends a wind (ruah) over the earth to make the waters subside; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; and 37 more.

passages.text: وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا ٱلْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا وَٱتَّخِذُوا۟ مِن مَّقَامِ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ مُصَلًّى وَعَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْعَٰكِفِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ

وَإِذَا جَآءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْنِ أَوِ ٱلْخَوْفِ أَذَاعُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ وَإِلَىٰٓ أُو۟لِى ٱلْأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ لَعَلِمَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَنۢبِطُونَهُۥ مِنْهُمْ وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ لَٱتَّبَعْتُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
